## Estimate for creating a subscription

<a id="opIdestimate_for_creating_a_subscription"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/customers/string/create_subscription_for_items_estimate' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /customers/{customer-id}/create_subscription_for_items_estimate`

Generates an estimate without creating a subscription. This endpoint can be called when you want to preview details of a new subscription before actually creating one.  
The following conditions must be met or **tax calculation** is ignored:

* The `taxability` [attribute](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#taxability) for the customer is `true`.
* `shipping_address` is passed when needed for tax calculation.

```yaml
null
```

## Create a quote for subscription creation

<a id="opIdcreate_a_quote_for_a_new_subscription_items"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/customers/string/create_subscription_quote_for_items' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /customers/{customer-id}/create_subscription_quote_for_items`

Create a quote for new subscription line items of a customer.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

## List customer entitlements

<a id="opIdlist_customer_entitlements"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/customers/string/customer_entitlements' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /customers/{customer-id}/customer_entitlements`

**Tip**

To retrieve subscription entitlements for a specific subscription, use the [List subscription entitlements API](/docs/api/subscription_entitlements/list-subscription-entitlements).

Returns a list of `customer_entitlement` objects for the specified customer. The entitlements returned are for *active* subscriptions only. Specifically, these are subscriptions with a [status](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object#status) of `active` or `non_renewing`.  
Pagination  
[Pagination](/docs/api/list-ops#pagination) works differently for this endpoint than other List endpoints in the Billing API. In other list endpoints, the `limit` parameter sets the limit on the total number of objects returned in the response. However, in this endpoint, the `limit` parameter defines the number of features for which the `customer_entitlement` objects are returned. For example, if `limit` = n, then all `customer_entitlement` objects for up to n features are returned.

Let's look at an example:

#### Features {#pagination-content}

Consider the following three features defined in Chargebee for a project management software:

* User Licenses
* Support Level
* Xero Integration

The `feature` objects are listed below:

##### Feature 1

```js

{
    "feature": {
        "id": "user-licenses",
        "name": "User Licenses",
        "description": "Maximum number of user licenses allowed.",
        "status": "active",
        "type": "quantity",
        "unit": "licence",
        "levels": [
            {
                "name": "3 licences",
                "value": "3",
                "is_unlimited": false,
                "level": 1
            },
            {
                "name": "10 licences",
                "value": "10",
                "is_unlimited": false,
                "level": 2
            },
            {
                "name": "25 licences",
                "value": "25",
                "is_unlimited": false,
                "level": 3
            },
            {
                "name": "Unlimited licence",
                "value": "Unlimited",
                "is_unlimited": true,
                "level": 4
            }
        ],
        "object": "feature"
    }
}

```

##### Feature 2

```js

{
    "feature": {
        "id": "support-level",
        "name": "Support Level",
        "description": "Level of support offered.",
        "status": "active",
        "type": "custom",
        "levels": [
            {
                "name": "Email",
                "value": "Email",
                "is_unlimited": false,
                "level": 1
            },
            {
                "name": "Chat",
                "value": "Chat",
                "is_unlimited": false,
                "level": 2
            },
            {
                "name": "Calls",
                "value": "Calls",
                "is_unlimited": false,
                "level": 3
            }
        ],
        "object": "feature"
    }
}

```

##### Feature 3

```js

{
    "feature": {
        "id": "xero-integration",
        "name": "Xero Integration",
        "description": "Integrate your Chargebee site with Xero",
        "status": "active",
        "type": "switch",
        "object": "feature"
    }
}

```

##### Subscriptions

Now consider that a customer `c1` has two subscriptions: `s1` and `s2`.

##### Subscription entitlements

Consider the following subscription entitlements for `s1` and `s2`:  

| Subscription id |    Feature Name    | Entitlement Value |
|-----------------|--------------------|-------------------|
| `s1`            | `User Licenses`    | `3`               |
| `s1`            | `Support Level`    | `Email`           |
| `s2`            | `User Licenses`    | `10`              |
| `s2`            | `Support Level`    | `Chat`            |
| `s2`            | `Xero Integration` | `true`            |

##### API responses

API calls to this endpoint work as follows:

###### First call

Consider the first call with `limit` set to `2`.

```js

GET /api/v2/customers/c1/customer_entitlements?limit=2

```

###### Response

```js

{
    "list": [
        {
            "customer_entitlement": {
                "customer_id": "c1",
                "subscription_id": "s1",
                "feature_id": "user-licenses",
                "value": "3",
                "name": "3 licences",
                "is_enabled": true,
                "object": "customer_entitlement"
            }
        },
        {
            "customer_entitlement": {
                "customer_id": "c1",
                "subscription_id": "s2",
                "feature_id": "xero-integration",
                "value": "true",
                "name": "Available",
                "is_enabled": true,
                "object": "customer_entitlement"
            }
        },
        {
            "customer_entitlement": {
                "customer_id": "c1",
                "subscription_id": "s2",
                "feature_id": "user-licenses",
                "value": "10",
                "name": "10 licences",
                "is_enabled": true,
                "object": "customer_entitlement"
            }
        }
    ],
    "next_offset": "2"
}

```

Since `limit` = `2`, the API returns the `customer_entitlement` for two features: **User Licenses** and **Xero Integration**. Three objects are returned, corresponding to rows 1, 3, and 5 in the table above.

###### Second call

We now retrieve the next page of the list in the second call by setting `offset` to the value of `next_offset` obtained from the previous response.

```js

    GET /api/v2/customers/c1/customer_entitlements?limit=2&offset=2

```

###### Response

```js

{
    "list": [
        {
            "customer_entitlement": {
                "customer_id": "c1",
                "subscription_id": "s1",
                "feature_id": "support-level",
                "value": "Email",
                "name": "Email",
                "is_enabled": true,
                "object": "customer_entitlement"
            }
        },
        {
            "customer_entitlement": {
                "customer_id": "c1",
                "subscription_id": "s2",
                "feature_id": "support-level",
                "value": "Chat",
                "name": "Chat",
                "is_enabled": true,
                "object": "customer_entitlement"
            }
        }
    ]
}

```

Although `limit` = `2`, the `customer_entitlement` objects for only one more feature, namely, Support Level are returned because the remaining were covered in the previous page. No more `customer_entitlement` objects remain for the customer, as indicated by the absence of the `next_offset` attribute in the response. The returned objects in this last call correspond to rows 2 and 4 in the table above.

Update a differential price using a `differential_price_id`

.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

<h3 id="update-a-differential-price-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|
|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|differential-price-id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» item_price_id|body|string|true|The id of the item price (`addon`<br>or `charge`<br>) whose price should change according to the plan-item it is applied to.<br>|
|» price|body|integer(int64)|false|The differential price. If the pricing model of the `item_price_id`<br>is `tiered`<br>, `volume`<br>, or `stairstep`<br>, pass `tiers`<br>instead of this.<br>|
|» price_in_decimal|body|string|false|The price of the item when the pricing_model is `flat_fee`.<br>When the pricing model is `per_unit`<br>, it is the price per unit quantity of the item. Not applicable for the other pricing models. The value is in decimal and in major units of the currency. Also, this is only applicable when [multi-decimal pricing](/docs/api/currencies)<br>is enabled.<br>|
|» parent_periods|body|object|false|Parameters for parent_periods<br>|
|» » period_unit|body|[string]|true|none|
|» » period|body|[[object]]|false|The billing period of the plan in `period_unit`<br>s. For example, a 6 month plan has `period`<br>as 6 and `period_unit`<br>as `month`.  <br>**Note**<br>For a [charge-item price](/docs/api/item_prices),<br><br>* When `parent_periods[period_unit]` and `parent_periods[period]` values are **passed** , then the [price](/docs/api/differential_prices/create-a-differential-price#price) is applied to a **specific** billing frequency of the plan-item.<br>* When `parent_periods[period_unit]` and `parent_periods[period]` values are **not passed** , then the [price](/docs/api/differential_prices/create-a-differential-price#price) is applied to **all** billing frequencies of the plan-item.<br>* When parent_periods\[period_unit\] is **passed** (eg. month) and the `parent_periods[period]` value is **not passed** , then the price is applied to all `parent_periods[period_unit]` (eg. monthly) frequencies of the plan-item. Updating or deleting the [price](/docs/api/differential_prices/create-a-differential-price#price) after creation will impact all of its related plan-item frequencies.<br>|
|» tiers|body|object|false|Parameters for tiers<br>|
|» » starting_unit|body|[integer(int32)]|false|The lower limit of a range of units for the tier<br>|
|» » ending_unit|body|[integer(int32)]|false|The upper limit of a range of units for the tier<br>|
|» » price|body|[integer(int64)]|false|The per-unit price for the tier when the `pricing_model`<br>is `tiered`<br>or `volume`<br>; the total cost for the item price when the `pricing_model`<br>is `stairstep`.<br>The value is in the [minor unit of the currency](/docs/api/currencies)<br>.<br>|
|» » starting_unit_in_decimal|body|[string]|false|The decimal representation of the lowest value of quantity in this tier. This is zero for the lowest tier. For all other tiers, it is the same as `ending_unit_in_decimal`<br>of the next lower tier. Returned only when the `pricing_model`<br>is `tiered`<br>, `volume`<br>or `stairstep`<br>and [multi-decimal pricing](/docs/api/currencies)<br>is enabled.<br>|
|» » ending_unit_in_decimal|body|[string]|false|The decimal representation of the highest value of quantity in this tier. This attribute is not applicable for the highest tier. For all other tiers, it must be equal to the `starting_unit_in_decimal`<br>of the next higher tier. Returned only when the `pricing_model`<br>is `tiered`<br>, `volume`<br>or `stairstep`<br>and [multi-decimal pricing](/docs/api/currencies)<br>is enabled.<br>|
|» » price_in_decimal|body|[string]|false|The decimal representation of the per-unit price for the tier when the `pricing_model`<br>is `tiered`<br>or `volume`.<br>When the `pricing_model`<br>is `stairstep`<br>, it is the decimal representation of the total price for the addon. The value is in major units of the currency. Returned when the plan is quantity-based and [multi-decimal pricing](/docs/api/currencies)<br>is enabled.<br>|
|» » pricing_type|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » package_size|body|[integer(int32)]|false|Package size for the tier when pricing type is `package`.<br>Specify the number of units that make up one package. For example, if 1000 API hits are grouped into a single package, set the package size to 1000.<br>|

<h1 id="chargebee-api-disputes">disputes</h1>

This resource represents a [dispute](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/payments/2.0/others/chargeback) raised against a payment collected on your site.

## Retrieve A Dispute

<a id="opIdretrieve_a_dispute"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/disputes/string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /disputes/{dispute-id}`

Retrieves a dispute identified by its unique id.

Use this operation to check the current [`status`](/docs/api/disputes/dispute-object#status) of a dispute, the amount under dispute, and the transaction and customer it relates to. To find disputes when you don't have the dispute id, use the [List disputes](/docs/api/disputes/list-disputes) operation.


<h3 id="retrieve-a-dispute-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|dispute-id|path|string|true|none|

## List Disputes

<a id="opIdlist_disputes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/disputes' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /disputes`

Lists the disputes raised against the transactions on your site, with the most recently created dispute first.

Use the filter parameters to narrow the list to the disputes you want to act on. For example, filter on `status` to work through the disputes that are still open, or on `customer_id` to review every dispute raised by one customer.

This operation does not support a `sort_by` parameter. The results are always ordered by `created_at` in descending order.


<h3 id="list-disputes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|limit|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of resources to be returned.<br>|
|offset|query|string|false|Determines your position in the list for pagination. To ensure that the next page is retrieved correctly, always set `offset`<br>to the value of `next_offset`<br>obtained in the previous iteration of the API call.<br>|
|id|query|object|false|optional, string filter<br><br>Uniquely identifies the dispute.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, starts_with, in, not_in<br><br>**Example →**<br>*id\[is\] = "dspt_16BdDXSlbu4uV1Ee6"*<br>|
|status|query|object|false|optional, enumerated string filter<br><br>The current state of the dispute. Possible values are : initiated, funds_withdrawn, in_review, cancelled, lost, won.<br><br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, in, not_in<br><br>**Example →**<br>*status\[is\] = "initiated"*<br>|
|type|query|object|false|optional, enumerated string filter<br><br>The nature of the dispute raised against the payment. Possible values are : chargeback, inquiry.<br><br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, in, not_in<br><br>**Example →**<br>*type\[is\] = "chargeback"*<br>|
|customer_id|query|object|false|optional, string filter<br><br>Identifier of the customer whose payment was disputed.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, starts_with, in, not_in<br><br>**Example →**<br>*customer_id\[is\] = "4gmiXbsjdm"*<br>|
|transaction_id|query|object|false|optional, string filter<br><br>Identifier of the transaction that was disputed.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, starts_with, in, not_in<br><br>**Example →**<br>*transaction_id\[is\] = "txn_16BdDXSlbu4uV1Ee6"*<br>|
|amount|query|object|false|optional, in cents filter<br><br>To filter based on the amount under dispute.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, lt, lte, gt, gte, between<br><br>**Example →**<br>*amount\[gt\] = "1200"*<br>|
|created_at|query|object|false|optional, timestamp(UTC) in seconds filter<br><br>To filter based on the time at which the dispute was created. Use this filter when listing disputes for better query performance.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>after, before, on, between<br><br>**Example →**<br>*created_at\[after\] = "1435054328"*<br>|

<h1 id="chargebee-api-einvoices">einvoices</h1>

An e-invoice record associated with an invoice or credit note.

## List e-invoices

<a id="opIdlist_e-invoices"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/einvoices' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /einvoices`

Returns a list of e-invoices. You can filter by id, reference id, updated at, invoice id, or credit note id.


<h3 id="list-e-invoices-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|limit|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of resources to be returned.<br>|
|offset|query|string|false|Determines your position in the list for pagination. To ensure that the next page is retrieved correctly, always set `offset`<br>to the value of `next_offset`<br>obtained in the previous iteration of the API call.<br>|
|id|query|object|false|optional, string filter<br><br>The unique id for the e-invoice.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, in<br><br>**Example →**<br>*id\[is\] = "HmaT0avT2mtbTL3mR"*<br>|
|reference_id|query|object|false|optional, string filter<br><br>Identifier returned by the connected e-invoicing provider for this submission.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, in<br><br>**Example →**<br>*reference_id\[is\] = "einvoice_ref_123"*<br>|
|updated_at|query|object|false|optional, timestamp(UTC) in seconds filter<br><br>Filter e-invoices based on `updated_at`. Useful for downstream delta sync.<br>It is advisable when using this filter, to pass the `sort_by`<br>input parameter as `updated_at`<br>for a faster response.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>after, before, on, between<br><br>**Example →**<br>*updated_at\[after\] = "1243545465"*<br>|
|sort_by|query|object|false|optional, string filter<br><br>Sorts based on the specified attribute.<br>**Supported attributes :**<br>updated_at<br><br>**Supported sort-orders :**<br>asc, desc<br><br>**Example →**<br>*sort_by\[desc\] = "updated_at"*<br><br>This will sort the result based on the 'updated_at' attribute in descending (latest first) order.<br>When omitted, the list defaults to `updated_at` descending (with `id` as tiebreaker).<br>|
|invoice_id|query|string|false|Filter e-invoices belonging to the invoice with this id.  <br>**Constraints**<br><br>* Query parameter (`invoice_id={invoice_id}`), not an operator filter (`invoice_id[is]`).<br>* Cannot be sent together with `credit_note_id`; the API returns an error if both are passed.<br>|
|credit_note_id|query|string|false|Filter e-invoices belonging to the credit note with this id.  <br>**Constraints**<br><br>* Query parameter (`credit_note_id={credit_note_id}`), not an operator filter (`credit_note_id[is]`).<br>* Cannot be sent together with `invoice_id`; the API returns an error if both are passed.<br>|

<h1 id="chargebee-api-entitlements">entitlements</h1>

## Manage entitlements for a feature

<a id="opIdupsert_or_remove_entitlements_for_a_feature"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/entitlements' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /entitlements`

Create, update, or remove a set of `entitlement`s for a feature.

The behavior depends on the specified `action`. It tries to create, update, or delete `entitlement` objects. If any of the entitlement objects fail to process, the entire operation stops with an error, and no entitlements are processed. In essence, the request processes either all the provided entitlements or none of them.

### Grandfathering in entitlements {#grandfathering}

> **Early Access**
>
> Grandfathering in entitlements is in early access. Write to [eap@chargebee.com](mailto:eap@chargebee.com) to get this enabled.

By default, this operation impacts all [subscriptions](/docs/api/subscriptions) that contain the item or item price. However, if you set `apply_grandfathering` to `true`, the existing subscriptions are not impacted by the change.

#### Example

Consider the following example:

##### On January 1st

* You have a [plan price](/docs/api/item_prices/item_price-object#item_type) (`id`: `premium-monthly-usd`) entitled to a [feature](/docs/api/features) (`user_licenses`) at [value](/docs/api/features/feature-object#levels) `10`.
* You have a subscription (`id`: `AzZjAiTl1btqS2lEj`) that contains the plan price (`premium-monthly-usd`).

##### On January 2nd

* Using this API operation, you change the entitlement level of the plan price `premium-monthly-usd` for the `user_licenses` feature to `value` `20`. You also set `apply_grandfathering` to `true`.
* After the API operation completes, you [create a new subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items) (`id`: `6oqNGUlMd9Yn4Ui`) that contains the same plan price (`premium-monthly-usd`).
* The existing subscription (`id`: `AzZjAiTl1btqS2lEj`) is [grandfathered in](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grandfather_clause), so it continues to be entitled to `user_licenses` at `value` `10`. The new subscription (`id`: `6oqNGUlMd9Yn4Ui`) is entitled to `user_licenses` at `value` `20`.

##### On January 3rd

* Using this API operation, you change the entitlement level of the plan price `premium-monthly-usd` for the `user_licenses` feature to `value` `30`. You also set `apply_grandfathering` to `false`.
* After the API operation completes, you create another subscription (`id`: `99CRh8UgMXTq77tl`) that contains the same plan price (`premium-monthly-usd`).
* Because grandfathering was not enabled, all three subscriptions (`AzZjAiTl1btqS2lEj`, `6oqNGUlMd9Yn4Ui`, and `99CRh8UgMXTq77tl`) are now entitled to `user_licenses` at `value` `30`.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

<h3 id="manage-entitlements-for-a-feature-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|

|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» action|body|string|true|The specific action to be performed for each `entitlement`<br>specified.<br><br>* upsert -<br>  If the `entitlement`<br>  already exists for the `feature_id`<br>  and `entity_id`<br>  combination, the `value`<br>  of the `entitlement`<br>  is updated. If it doesn't exist, a new `entitlement`<br>  is created.<br>* remove -<br>  Deletes the `entitlement`<br>  for the `feature_id`<br>  and `entity_id`<br>  combination, if it exists.<br>|

The `entitlement` is created regardless.<br>|
|» » feature_id|body|[string]|true|The unique identifier of the `feature` to which the entity gains entitlement.<br>|
|» » entity_type|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » value|body|[string]|false|The level of entitlement that the entity has towards the feature. The possible values depend on the value of `feature.type`<br>:<br><br>* When `feature.type` is `quantity` and:<br><br>* If `feature.levels[is_unlimited]` is not `true` for any one of `feature.levels[]`, then the value can be any one of `feature.levels[value][]`.<br><br>* If `feature.levels[is_unlimited]` is `true` for one of the `feature.levels[]`, then the value can be:<br><br>  * any one of `feature.levels[value][]`<br>  * or it can be `unlimited` (case-insensitive), indicating unlimited entitlement.<br>* When `type` is `range` and:<br><br>* If `feature.levels[is_unlimited]` is not `true` for any one of `feature.levels[]`, then the value can be any whole number between `levels[value][0]` and `levels[value][1]` (inclusive).<br><br>* If `feature.levels[is_unlimited]` is `true` for one of the `feature.levels[]`, then the value can be:<br><br>  * any whole number equal to or greater than `levels[value][0]`<br>  * or it can be `unlimited` (case-insensitive), indicating unlimited entitlement.<br>* When `type` is `custom`, then the value can be any one of `feature.levels[value][]`.<br><br>* When `type` is `switch`, then the value is set as `available` or `true`.<br><br>|
|» » apply_grandfathering|body|[boolean]|false|**Early Access**<br><br>[Grandfathering support](/docs/api/entitlements) for entitlements is in early access. Write to [eap@chargebee.com](mailto:eap@chargebee.com) to get this enabled.<br><br>Determines whether to [grandfather in](/docs/api/entitlements) existing subscriptions affected by this entitlement.<br><br>* `true`: Existing subscriptions that contain this entity as one of the [subscription items](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object#subscription_items), are not mapped to this value of the entitlement; their currently mapped value for this entitlement are retained. New subscriptions created in the future that contain this entity, or existing subscriptions updated in the future to include this entity, are mapped to this value of the entitlement.<br>* `false`: All subscriptions that contain this entity are mapped to this version of the entitlement.<br>|

<h1 id="chargebee-api-estimates">estimates</h1>

During the process of signing up customers to subscriptions, use the Estimates API to evaluate the details of the purchase before actually signing them up.

## Estimate for creating a customer and subscription

<a id="opIdestimate_for_creating_a_customer_and_subscription"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/estimates/create_subscription_for_items' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /estimates/create_subscription_for_items`

Generates an estimate for creating a subscription when the customer does not exist in Chargebee. This estimate API can be called when the customer has not yet signed up and you want to preview how a new subscription would look like for them.  
**Note:**
Estimate operations do not make any changes in Chargebee; hence this API does not create an actual `customer`
or `subscription`
record.

The response contains one or more of the following objects:

* `subscription_estimate`: The subscription details like the status of the subscription (such as `in_trial` or `active`), next billing date, and so on.
* `invoice_estimate`:The details of the immediate invoice, if there is one. If the subscription is created in `trial`/`future` states, `invoice_estimate` is unavailable as no immediate invoice is generated.
* `next_invoice_estimate`:This is returned when an immediate invoice is not generated. It contains the details of the invoice that will be generated on the next billing date of the subscription.
* `unbilled_charge_estimates`: This contains the details of charges that have not been invoiced. This is returned only if the `invoice_immediately` parameter is set to `false`.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

## Create a payment schedule estimate

<a id="opIdestimates_for_payment_schedules"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/estimates/payment_schedules' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /estimates/payment_schedules`

Generates an estimate without creating a payment schedule. This endpoint can be called when you want to preview details of a new payment schedule before actually creating one.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

<h3 id="create-a-payment-schedule-estimate-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|
|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» scheme_id|body|string|true|The unique identifier for the `payment_schedule_scheme`.<br>This identifier is used to retrieve the payment schedule scheme, which is then applied to calculate the amount and date for the specified number of payment schedules.<br>|
|» amount|body|integer(int64)|false|Defines the payment schedule amount set for an invoice. If this is not provided, the total `invoice.amount_due`<br>is used. This value is mandatory in case `invoice_id`<br>is not provided.<br>|
|» invoice_id|body|string|false|Unique identifier of the invoice.<br>|
|» payment_schedule_start_date|body|integer(unix-time)|false|The date from which the payment schedule will start. This is applicable only when invoice_id is not provided. If `invoice_id`<br>is provided, we will consider `invoice.due_date`<br>.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|chargebee-event-email|all-disabled|
|chargebee-event-webhook|all-disabled|

## Create invoice for items estimate

<a id="opIdcreate_invoice_for_items_estimate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/estimates/create_invoice_for_items' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /estimates/create_invoice_for_items`

This endpoint creates an invoice estimate for non-recurring items.

You can optionally override the line item name and description displayed on the invoice for charge-item prices and one-time charges. These overrides are reflected in the returned invoice estimate.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

<h3 id="create-invoice-for-items-estimate-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|
|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» currency_code|body|string|false|The currency code (ISO 4217 format) of the invoice amount.<br>|
|» invoice_note|body|string|false|A note for this particular invoice. This, and [all other notes](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#notes)<br>for the invoice are displayed on the PDF invoice sent to the customer.<br>|
|» remove_general_note|body|boolean|false|Set as `true`<br>to remove the [**general note**](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/invoice_notes.html#adding-general-notes)<br>from this invoice.<br>|
|» coupon_ids|body|[string]|false|List of Coupons to be added.<br>|
|» authorization_transaction_id|body|string|false|Authorization transaction to be captured.<br>|
|» payment_source_id|body|string|false|Payment source to be used for this payment.<br>|
|» auto_collection|body|string|false|The customer level auto collection will be override if specified.<br><br>* on - Whenever an invoice is created, an automatic attempt will be made to charge.<br>* off - Whenever an invoice is created as payment due.<br>|
|» invoice_date|body|integer(unix-time)|false|The document date displayed on the invoice PDF. By default, it is the date of creation of the invoice or, when Metered Billing is enabled, it can be the date of closing the invoice. Provide this value to backdate the invoice (set the invoice date to a value in the past). Backdating an invoice is done for reasons such as booking revenue for a previous date or when the non-recurring charge is effective as of a past date.<br>`taxes`<br>and<br>`line_item_taxes`<br>are computed based on the tax configuration as of this date. The date should not be more than one calendar month into the past. For example, if today is 13th January, then you cannot pass a value that is earlier than 13th December.<br>|
|» invoice|body|object|false|Parameters for invoice<br>|
|» » customer_id|body|string|false|Identifier of the customer for which this invoice needs to be created.<br>|
|» » subscription_id|body|string|false|Identifier of the subscription for which this invoice needs to be created. Should be specified if 'customer_id' is not specified.(not applicable for consolidated invoice)<br>|
|» » po_number|body|string|false|Purchase Order Number for this invoice.<br>|
|» shipping_address|body|object|false|Parameters for shipping_address<br>|
|» » first_name|body|string|false|The first name of the contact.<br>|
|» » last_name|body|string|false|The last name of the contact.<br>|
|» » email|body|string(email)|false|The email address.<br>|
|» » company|body|string|false|The company name.<br>|
|» » phone|body|string|false|The phone number.<br>|
|» » line1|body|string|false|Address line 1<br>|
|» » line2|body|string|false|Address line 2<br>|
|» » line3|body|string|false|Address line 3<br>|
|» » city|body|string|false|The name of the city.<br>|
|» » state_code|body|string|false|The [ISO 3166-2 state/province code](https://www.iso.org/obp/ui/#search/code)<br>without the country prefix. Currently supported for USA, Canada and India. ## Gift subscription estimate for items

<a id="opIdgift_subscription_estimate_for_items"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/estimates/gift_subscription_for_items' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /estimates/gift_subscription_for_items`

This endpoint generates an estimate for a subscription that is intended to be a gift. The estimate provides details about the gift sender, gift recipient, address details of the recipient, and the type and details of subscription items included in the gift.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

## Estimate for updating a subscription

<a id="opIdestimate_for_updating_a_subscription"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/estimates/update_subscription_for_items' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /estimates/update_subscription_for_items`

Returns an estimate for updating a subscription.

In the response,

* [subscription_estimate](/docs/api/estimates/estimate-object): The details of the changed subscription such as `status`, next billing date, and so on.
* [invoice_estimate](/docs/api/estimates/estimate-object):The details of the immediate invoice, if it is generated. An immediate invoice is not generated when:
  * `end_of_term` parameter is true
  * `prorate` parameter is `false`
  * No changes are made to the plan item prices or addon item prices in `subscription_items`.
  * For changes such as [quantity downgrades](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/proration.html#proration-mechanism_plan-quantity-downgrade-paid-invoice).
* [next_invoice_estimate](/docs/api/estimates/estimate-object):The details of the invoice to be generated later (if any) on the occasion that no immediate invoice has been generated.
* [credit_note_estimates](/docs/api/estimates/estimate-object):The list of credit notes (if any) generated during this operation.
* [unbilled_charge_estimates](/docs/api/estimates/estimate-object): The details of charges that have not been invoiced. This is returned only if the `invoice_immediately` parameter is set to `false`.

The following conditions must be met or **tax calculation** is ignored:

* The `taxability` [attribute](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#taxability) for the customer is `true`.
* Necessary parameters for tax calculation such as the following are passed: `billing_address`, `shipping_address`, `customer[vat_number]`


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|

|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|
|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» changes_scheduled_at|body|integer(unix-time)|false|When `change_option` is set to `specific_date`, then set the date/time at which the subscription change is to happen or has happened.  <br>**Constraints**<br><br>* Do not pass this parameter along with `reactivate_from`.<br>* The `changes_scheduled_at` parameter does not apply to `auto_collection`, `shipping_address`, and `po_number`; these parameters take effect **immediately** when scheduling a subscription update.  <br>**Backdated changes**<br><br>`changes_scheduled_at`can be set to a value in the past. This is called backdating the subscription change and is performed when the subscription change has already been provisioned but its billing has been delayed. Backdating is allowed only when the following prerequisites are met:<br><br>* Backdating must be enabled for subscription change operations.<br>* Only the following changes can be backdated:<br>  * Changes in the recurring items or their prices.<br>  * Addition of non-recurring items.<br>* Subscription `status` is `active`, `cancelled`, or `non_renewing`.<br>* The current day of the month does not exceed the limit set in Chargebee for backdating subscription change. This limit is typically the day of the month by which the accounting for the previous month must be closed.<br>* The date is on or after `current_term_start`.<br>* The date is on or after the last date/time any of the following changes were made:<br>  * Changes in the recurring items or their prices.<br>  * Addition of non-recurring items.<br>* The date is not more than duration X into the past where X is the billing period of the plan. For example, if the period of the plan in the subscription is 2 months and today is 14th April, `changes_scheduled_at` cannot be earlier than 14th February.<br>|
|» change_option|body|string|false|Specifies the effective date for the subscription change.<br><br>* end_of_term - The change is carried out at the end of the current billing cycle of the subscription.<br>* specific_date - Executes the change on a specified date. The change occurs as of the date/time defined in `changes_scheduled_at`.<br>* immediately - The change is carried out immediately.<br>|
|» mandatory_items_to_remove|body|[string]|false|Item ids of [mandatorily attached addons](/docs/api/attached_items)<br>that are to be removed from the subscription.<br>|
|» replace_items_list|body|boolean|false|If `true`<br>then the existing `subscription_items`<br>list for the subscription is replaced by the one provided. If `false`<br>then the provided `subscription_items`<br>list gets added to the existing list.<br>|
|» invoice_date|body|integer(unix-time)|false|The document date displayed on the invoice PDF. The default value is the current date. Provide this value to backdate the invoice. Backdating an invoice is done for reasons such as booking revenue for a previous date or when the subscription is effective as of a past date. Moreover, if `create_pending_invoices`<br>is set to `true`<br>, and if the site is configured to set invoice dates to date of closing, then upon invoice closure, this date is changed to the invoice closing date. taxes and line_item_taxes are computed based on the tax configuration as of `invoice_date`.<br>When passing this parameter, the following prerequisites must be met:<br><br>* `invoice_date` must be in the past.<br>* `invoice_date` is not more than one calendar month into the past. For example, if today is 13th January, then you cannot pass a value that is earlier than 13th December.<br>* It is not earlier than `changes_scheduled_at`, `reactivate_from`, or `trial_end`.<br>* `invoice_immediately` is `true`. .<br>|
|» billing_cycles|body|integer(int32)|false|Billing cycles set for plan-item price is used by default.<br>|
|» terms_to_charge|body|integer(int32)|false|The number of subscription billing cycles to [invoice in advance](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/advance-invoices.html).<br>If a new term is started for the subscription due to this API call, then `terms_to_charge`<br>is inclusive of this new term. See description for the `force_term_reset`<br>parameter to learn more about when a subscription term is reset.<br>|
|» reactivate_from|body|integer(unix-time)|false|If the subscription `status`<br>is `cancelled`<br>and it is being reactivated via this operation, this is the date/time at which the subscription should be reactivated.<br>**Note:**<br>It is recommended not to pass this parameter along with `changed_scheduled_at`.<br>`reactivate_from`<br>can be backdated (set to a value in the past). Use backdating when the subscription has been reactivated already but its billing has been delayed. Backdating is allowed only when the following prerequisites are met:<br><br>* Backdating must be enabled for subscription reactivation operations.<br>* The current day of the month does not exceed the limit set in Chargebee for backdating subscription change. This limit is the day of the month by which the accounting for the previous month must be closed.<br>* The date is on or after the last date/time any of the product catalog items of the subscription were changed.<br>* The date is not more than duration X into the past where X is the billing period of the plan. For example, if the period of the plan in the subscription is 2 months and today is 14th April, `changes_scheduled_at` cannot be earlier than 14th February. .<br>|
|» billing_alignment_mode|body|string|false|Override the [billing alignment mode](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/calendar-billing.html#alignment-of-billing-date)<br>chosen for the site for calendar billing. Only applicable when using calendar billing.<br><br>* immediate - Subscription period will be aligned with the configured billing date immediately, with credits or charges raised accordingly..<br>* delayed - Subscription period will be aligned with the configured billing date at the next renewal.<br>|
|» coupon_ids|body|[string]|false|List of coupons to be applied to this subscription. You can provide coupon ids or [coupon codes](/docs/api/coupon_codes)<br>.<br>|
|» replace_coupon_list|body|boolean|false|If `true`<br>then the existing `coupon_ids`<br>list for the subscription is replaced by the one provided. If `false`<br>then the provided list gets added to the existing `coupon_ids`<br>.<br>|
|» prorate|body|boolean|false|* When `true`: [Prorated credits or charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/proration.html#proration-mechanism) are created as applicable for this change.<br>* When `false`: The subscription is changed without creating any credits or charges.<br>* When not provided, the value configured in the [site settings](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/proration.html#proration-for-subscription-change) is considered.<br><br>**Caveat**<br><br>For further changes within the same billing term, when `prorate` is set to `true`, **credits** are **not created** when **all** the conditions below hold true:<br><br>An immediate previous change was made<br><br>* with `prorate` set to `false` and<br>* no changes were made to the subscription's billing term and<br>* a change was made to either the subscription's items or their prices.<br>|
|» end_of_term|body|boolean|false|**Deprecated**<br><br>* Use `change_option` instead.<br>* If you pass this parameter along with `change_option`, then `change_option` wins.<br><br>Set this to true if you want the update to be applied at the end of the current subscription billing cycle.<br>|
|» force_term_reset|body|boolean|false|Say the subscription has the renewal date as 28th of every month. When the plan-item price of the subscription is set to one that has the same billing period as the current plan-item price, the subscription change does not change the term. In other words, the subscription still renews on the 28th. Passing this parameter as `true`<br>will have the subscription reset its term to the current date (provided `end_of_term`<br>is false).<br>**Note**:<br>When the new plan-item price has a billing period different from the current plan-item price of the subscription, the term is always reset, regardless of the value passed for this parameter.<br>|
|» reactivate|body|boolean|false|Applicable only for `cancelled`<br>subscriptions. When passed as `true`<br>, the canceled subscription is activated; otherwise subscription changes are made without changing its `status`.<br>If not passed, subscription will be activated only if `subscription_items`<br>is passed.<br>|
|» include_delayed_charges|body|boolean|false|If true, all the unbilled charges will be included for the invoice estimate.<br>|
|» use_existing_balances|body|boolean|false|The generated invoice_estimate/next_invoice_estimate will include all the balances - Promotional Credits, Refundable Credits, and Excess Payments - if any. If you don't want these balances to be included you can specify 'false' for the parameter *use_existing_balances*<br>.<br>|
|» invoice_immediately|body|boolean|false|If there are charges raised immediately for the subscription, this parameter specifies whether those charges are to be invoiced immediately or added to [unbilled charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/unbilled-charges.html).<br>The default value is as per the [site settings](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/unbilled-charges.html#configuration)<br>.  <br>**Note:**<br>`invoice_immediately`<br>only affects charges that are raised at the time of execution of this API call. Any charges scheduled to be raised in the future are not affected by this parameter.<br><br>.<br>|
|» invoice_usages|body|boolean|false|Setting this attribute to `true` will invoice the overages for the metered item during subscription changes<br>.<br>|
|» subscription|body|object|false|Parameters for subscription<br>|
|» » id|body|string|true|A unique and immutable identifier for the subscription. If not provided, it is autogenerated.<br>|
|» » start_date|body|integer(unix-time)|false|The new start date of a `future`<br>subscription. Applicable only for `future`<br>subscriptions.<br>|
|» » trial_end|body|integer(unix-time)|false|The time at which the trial has ended or will end for the subscription. This is only allowed when the subscription `status`<br>is `future`<br>, `in_trial`<br>, or `cancelled`.<br>Also, the value must not be earlier than `changes_scheduled_at`<br>or `start_date`.<br>**Note** :<br>This parameter can be backdated (set to a value in the past) only when the subscription is in `cancelled`<br>or `in_trial`<br>`status`.<br>Do this to keep a record of when the trial ended in case it ended at some point in the past. When `trial_end`<br>is backdated, the subscription immediately goes into `active`<br>or `non_renewing`<br>status.<br>|
|» » auto_collection|body|string|false|Defines whether payments need to be collected automatically for this subscription. Overrides customer's auto-collection property.<br><br>* off - Automatic collection of charges will not be made for this subscription. Use this for offline payments.<br>* on - Whenever an invoice is created for this subscription, an automatic charge will be attempted on the payment method available.<br>|
|» » offline_payment_method|body|string|false|The preferred offline payment method for the subscription.<br><br>* uk_automated_bank_transfer - UK Automated Bank Transfer<br>* jp_automated_bank_transfer - JP Automated Bank Transfer<br>* bank_transfer - Bank Transfer<br>* us_automated_bank_transfer - US Automated Bank Transfer<br>* boleto - Boleto<br>* no_preference - No Preference<br>* sepa_credit - SEPA Credit<br>* mx_automated_bank_transfer - MX Automated Bank Transfer<br>* ach_credit - ACH Credit<br>* custom - Custom<br>* eu_automated_bank_transfer - EU Automated Bank Transfer<br>* cash - Cash<br>* check - Check<br>|
|» » free_period|body|integer(int32)|false|The period of time by which the first term of the subscription is to be extended free-of-charge. The value must be in multiples of free_period_unit.<br>|

Whenever the subscription has a trial period, this attribute (parameter) is returned (required) and specifies the operation to be carried out for the subscription once the trial ends.<br><br>* activate_subscription - The subscription activates and charges are raised for non-metered items.<br>* cancel_subscription - The subscription cancels.<br>* plan_default -<br>  The action [configured for the site](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/trial_periods_hidden.html#how-to-define-the-end-of-trial-actions-for-subscriptions)<br>  at the time when the trial ends, takes effect.<br>* site_default -<br>  This is the default value. <h1 id="chargebee-api-events">events</h1>

### Introduction When important changes occur on your Chargebee site, they are recorded as events.

## List events

<a id="opIdlist_events"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/events' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /events`

Retrieves list of events.


<h3 id="list-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|limit|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of resources to be returned.<br>|
|offset|query|string|false|Determines your position in the list for pagination. To ensure that the next page is retrieved correctly, always set `offset`<br>to the value of `next_offset`<br>obtained in the previous iteration of the API call.<br>|
|id|query|object|false|optional, string filter<br><br>Uniquely identifies a event.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, starts_with, in, not_in<br><br>**Example →**<br>*id\[is\] = "8ndk0hbKm"*<br>|
|webhook_status|query|object|false|optional, enumerated string filter<br><br>Returns the events (occurred in the past 6 days) which has this status in any of the events' webhooks.<br>**Note**:<br>To retrieve events which have occurred before the 6 day period, use the occurred_at(start_time/end_time) attribute. Possible values are : not_configured, scheduled, succeeded, re_scheduled, failed, skipped, not_applicable.<br><br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, in, not_in<br><br>**Example →**<br>*webhook_status\[is\] = "succeeded"*<br>|

## Retrieve an event

<a id="opIdretrieve_an_event"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/events/string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /events/{event-id}`

Retrieves a specific event identified by a unique event identifier.  
**Note:**
Only events that are less than 90 days old will be retrieved.


<h3 id="retrieve-an-event-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|event-id|path|string|true|none|

<h1 id="chargebee-api-exports">exports</h1>

Export resource represents an export job and contains the status of the job and the download URL, if the job is successfully completed.

## Export customers

<a id="opIdexport_customers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/exports/customers' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /exports/customers`

This API triggers export of customer data. The exported zip file contains CSV files with customer-related data.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

|» » » is|body|string|false|* `in_progress` - Transaction is being processed by the gateway. This typically happens for [direct debit transactions](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/direct-debit-payments.html) or, in case of cards, refund transactions. Such transactions can take 2-7 days to complete, depending on the gateway and payment method.<br>* `success` - The transaction is successful.<br>* `voided` - The transaction got voided or authorization expired at gateway.<br>* `failure` - Transaction failed. ## Export Subscription Ramps

<a id="opIdexport_subscription_ramps"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/exports/ramps' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /exports/ramps`

Starts an export job for [subscription ramps](/docs/api/ramps) data. The exported zip file contains CSV files with ramp-related data.  

### Best practice

For a full data export, use filters to export in batches, as suggested in the samples below.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

<h3 id="export-subscription-ramps-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|
|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» export_type|body|string|false|Determines the format of the data. Returns the export type based on the selected value.<br><br>* data - Provides the full set of data for the subscription ramps in multiple `.csv` files.<br>* import_friendly_data - Provides a `.csv` file whose columns match the [`ramp`](/docs/api/ramps/ramp-object) schema. This file format can be readily imported through the UI by using [Bulk Operations](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/bulk-operations.html).<br>|
|» ramp|body|object|false|Parameters for ramp<br>|
|» » status|body|object|false|The execution status of the ramp. Use this filter to export ramps in a specific status, such as `scheduled`<br>, `succeeded`<br>, `failed`<br>, or `draft`.<br>|
|» » » in|body|string|false|* `scheduled` - Status of the subscription schedule on creation. <br>* `succeeded` - The execution status of the schedule if success. <br>* `failed` - The execution status of the schedule if failed. <br>* `draft` - Status of the subscription schedule considering as draft|
|» » » is|body|string|false|* `scheduled` - Status of the subscription schedule on creation. <br>* `succeeded` - The execution status of the schedule if success. <br>* `failed` - The execution status of the schedule if failed. <br>* `draft` - Status of the subscription schedule considering as draft|
|» » subscription_id|body|object|false|The ID of the subscription for which the ramp was created. Use this filter to export ramps that belong to specific subscriptions.<br>|
|» » » in|body|string|false|none|
|» » » is|body|string|false|none|
|» » effective_from|body|object|false|To filter based on `effective_from`<br>, the time when the changes defined in the ramp are applied to the subscription by executing the ramp.<br>|
|» » » after|body|string(unix-time)|false|none|
|» » » before|body|string(unix-time)|false|none|
|» » » on|body|string(unix-time)|false|none|
|» » » between|body|string|false|none|
|» » updated_at|body|object|false|To filter based on `updated_at`.<br>This attribute will be present only if the resource has been updated after 2016-09-28. It is advisable when using this filter, to pass the `sort_by`<br>input parameter as `updated_at`<br>for a faster response. [Learn more](/docs/api/exports) about the best practice before performing full export.<br>|
|» » » after|body|string(unix-time)|false|none|
|» » » before|body|string(unix-time)|false|none|
|» » » on|body|string(unix-time)|false|none|
|» » » between|body|string|false|none|

## Export differential price

<a id="opIdexport_differential_price"></a>

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/exports/differential_prices' \

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

```

`POST /exports/differential_prices`

This API triggers export of differential price data. The exported zip file contains CSV files with differential price-related data.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

<h3 id="export-differential-price-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» item_id|body|object|false|optional, string filter<br><br>Item Id of Addon / Charge item price for which differential pricing is applied to.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, starts_with, in, not_in<br><br>**Example →**<br>*item_id\[is\] = "day-pass"*<br>|
|» » is|body|string|false|none|

|» » » is|body|string|false|none|
|» » » is_not|body|string|false|none|

|» » » in|body|string|false|none|

For example, this would be the id of the *Standard*<br>or *Enterprise*<br>plans-items mentioned in the [examples above](/docs/api/differential_prices)<br>.<br>|

## Export invoices

<a id="opIdexport_invoices"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/exports/invoices' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /exports/invoices`

This API triggers export of invoice data. The exported zip file contains CSV files with invoice-related data.

### Invoice Export Best Practice

For a full export, Chargebee recommends exporting data in batches by using date filters. The table below provides examples of how to set the filters:  

|                 **Scenario**                  |                        **Filter Example**                        |                **Description**                |
|-----------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| Export invoices updated after January 1, 2024 | *invoice\[updated_at\]\[after\] = "1704067200"*                  | Export invoices from January 1, 2024 onwards. |
| Export invoices for 2023                      | *invoice\[updated_at\]\[between\] = "\[1672531200,1704067199\]"* | Export all invoices for the year 2023.        |
| Export invoices for 2022                      | *invoice\[updated_at\]\[between\] = "\[1640995200,1672531199\]"* | Export all invoices for the year 2022.        |

If the export still fails, further reduce the date range, for example:  

|            **Scenario**            |                        **Filter Example**                        |                           **Description**                            |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Export for the second half of 2024 | *invoice\[updated_at\]\[after\] = "1717200000"*                  | Export invoices are updated after June 1, 2024.                      |
| Export for the first half of 2024  | *invoice\[updated_at\]\[between\] = "\[1704067200,1717199999\]"* | Export invoices updated between January 1, 2024, and May 31, 2024.   |
| Export for the second half of 2023 | *invoice\[updated_at\]\[between\] = "\[1685577600,1704067199\]"* | Export invoices updated between June 1, 2023, and December 31, 2023. |
| Export for the first half of 2023  | *invoice\[updated_at\]\[between\] = "\[1672531200,1685577599\]"* | Export invoices updated between January 1, 2023, and May 31, 2023.   |

**Note**

The date ranges in the examples above are just suggestions; you can adjust the date window to fit your specific needs. If an export fails due to large data volume, reduce the date window further and retry the export.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

## Retrieve an export

<a id="opIdretrieve_an_export"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/exports/string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /exports/{export-id}`

This API gets the status of the export job initiated by the Exports API. If the export job is completed, the downloads resource will also be obtained in the API response. The returned URL in the downloads resource is secure and can be downloaded. The URL expires after 4 hours. Please note that this is a public URL, and can be downloaded by anyone with whom it's shared.

**Note:** In case the export is in Failed or In-process state, then the downloads resource will not be available.


<h3 id="retrieve-an-export-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|export-id|path|string|true|none|

## Export deferred revenue reports

<a id="opIdexport_deferred_revenue_reports"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/exports/deferred_revenue' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /exports/deferred_revenue`

**Important:**
This report is deprecated. Therefore, the endpoint is also deprecated.

This API triggers export for the Deferred Revenue Report.

**Note:**
This API call is asynchronous.
You need to check if this operation has completed by checking if the export status is **completed**

function provided as an instance method in the library.

|» » taxability|body|object|false|Specifies if the customer is liable for tax. Possible values are : taxable, exempt, zero_rated.<br>|
|» » » is|body|string|false|* `taxable` - Computes tax for the customer based on the [site configuration](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/tax.html). In some cases, depending on the region, shipping_address is needed. If not provided, then billing_address is used to compute tax. If that's not available either, the tax is taken as zero.<br>* `exempt` -<br>  * Customer is exempted from tax. When using Chargebee's native [Taxes](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/tax.html) feature or when using the [TaxJar integration](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/taxjar.html), no other action is needed.<br>  * However, when using our [Avalara integration](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/avalara.html), optionally, specify `entity_code` or `exempt_number` attributes if you use Chargebee's [AvaTax for Sales](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/avalara.html#configuring-tax-exemption) or specify `exemption_details` attribute if you use [Chargebee's AvaTax for Communications](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/avatax-for-communication.html) integration. Tax may still be applied by Avalara for certain values of `entity_code`/`exempt_number`/`exemption_details` based on the state/region/province of the taxable address.<br>* `zero_rated` - With [Chargebee Taxes](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/tax.html), otherwise taxable line items for the customer are taxed at 0%. These line items have `is_taxed` set to `true`, the tax rate and tax amount set to `0`, and `tax_exempt_reason` set to `zero_rated`. Unlike `exempt`, this option follows the taxable tax path at a zero rate.<br>|
|» » » is_not|body|string|false|* `taxable` - Computes tax for the customer based on the [site configuration](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/tax.html). In some cases, depending on the region, shipping_address is needed. If not provided, then billing_address is used to compute tax. If that's not available either, the tax is taken as zero.<br>* `exempt` -<br>  * Customer is exempted from tax. `POST /exports/revenue_recognition`

**Important:**

|» » » is|body|string|false|* `taxable` - Computes tax for the customer based on the [site configuration](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/tax.html). If that's not available either, the tax is taken as zero.<br>* `exempt` -<br>  * Customer is exempted from tax. When using Chargebee's native [Taxes](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/tax.html) feature or when using the [TaxJar integration](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/taxjar.html), no other action is needed.<br>  * However, when using our [Avalara integration](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/avalara.html), optionally, specify `entity_code` or `exempt_number` attributes if you use Chargebee's [AvaTax for Sales](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/avalara.html#configuring-tax-exemption) or specify `exemption_details` attribute if you use [Chargebee's AvaTax for Communications](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/avatax-for-communication.html) integration. Tax may still be applied by Avalara for certain values of `entity_code`/`exempt_number`/`exemption_details` based on the state/region/province of the taxable address.<br>* `zero_rated` - With [Chargebee Taxes](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/tax.html), otherwise taxable line items for the customer are taxed at 0%. ## Export credit notes

<a id="opIdexport_credit_notes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/exports/credit_notes' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /exports/credit_notes`

This API triggers export of credit note data. The exported zip file contains CSV files with credit note-related data.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

<h3 id="export-credit-notes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|

## Export coupons

<a id="opIdexport_coupons"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/exports/coupons' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /exports/coupons`

This API triggers export of coupon data. The exported zip file contains CSV files with coupon-related data.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

## Export subscriptions

<a id="opIdexport_subscriptions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/exports/subscriptions' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /exports/subscriptions`

This API triggers export of subscription data. The exported zip file contains CSV files with subscription-related data.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

<h3 id="export-subscriptions-parameters">Parameters</h3>
