<h1 id="chargebee-api-ledgeraccountbalances">ledger_account_balances</h1>

Credit Grants ------------- A credit grant is a quantified allocation of credits given to a subscription through a configured [item price](/docs/api/item_prices) or via the [allocate](/docs/api/ledger_operations/allocate) operation, consumed over time through ledger operations.

## Update the overdraft limit

<a id="opIdupdate_overdraft_limit"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/ledger_account_balances/update_overdraft_limit' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /ledger_account_balances/update_overdraft_limit`

Updates the [overdraft limit](/docs/api/ledger_account_balances#overdraft_balance_limit) for a subscription and credit unit.

By default, the overdraft limit for a credit unit is a single, site-wide value applied to every subscription. Use this operation to manually override that default for one `subscription_id`-`unit_id` pair --- for example, to raise the ceiling for a trusted high-value customer, or to let customers self-configure their own spending limit after credits are granted.  
**Behavior**

* Applies the new limit synchronously and returns the outcome in the same response --- there's no pending or asynchronous state.
* Rejects the request immediately if the new limit is below what's already committed (`used_amount` + `hold_amount`) on the active overdraft balance. The limit isn't scheduled or retried later; the caller must resubmit once the balance permits it.
* Requires that an overdraft balance already exists for the subscription and credit unit.
* Leaves the [`provisioned_balance`](/docs/api/ledger_account_balances#provisioned_balance) and the site-level default untouched. Other subscriptions on the same credit unit continue to use the site default until they get their own override.  
**Usage**

Use this operation to raise or lower the overdraft ceiling for a specific subscription without changing the site-wide default --- for instance, extending more runway to an enterprise customer, or letting an end customer raise their own limit after receiving promotional credits.

The response echoes the `subscription_id`, `unit_id`, and `change_reason` inputs, and returns the resulting [`overdraft_balance`](/docs/api/ledger_account_balances#overdraft_balance) snapshot as well.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

<h3 id="update-the-overdraft-limit-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|
|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» subscription_id|body|string|true|A unique, immutable identifier for the [subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object#id) whose overdraft limit is being changed.<br>|
|» unit_id|body|string|true|Identifier of the [credit unit](/docs/api/credit_units) linked to the subscription. For example, a credit unit id such as `ai_credits`.  <br>**Prerequisites**<br><br>An [overdraft balance](/docs/api/ledger_account_balances#overdraft_balance) must already exist for this `(subscription_id, unit_id)` pair.<br>|
|» is_unlimited|body|boolean|true|Whether the overdraft limit for this credit unit is unlimited.  <br>**Behavior**<br><br>* When `true`, requests unlimited overdraft and [`limit`](#limit) must not be passed.<br>* When `false`, requests a finite overdraft and [`limit`](#limit) is required.<br>|
|» limit|body|string|false|The new maximum overdraft allowed for this credit unit.<br>Pass this value as a decimal string.  <br>**Required if**<br><br>[`is_unlimited`](#is_unlimited) is `false`.  <br>**Constraints**<br><br>* Must not be passed when [`is_unlimited`](#is_unlimited) is `true`.<br>* Must be zero or a positive value; negative values are not allowed.<br>* Maximum supported value: `9999999999999999999999999.9999999999` (up to 25 digits before the decimal and up to 10 digits after).<br>* Must be greater than or equal to the sum of `used_amount` and `hold_amount` on the active [overdraft balance](/docs/api/ledger_account_balances#overdraft_balance). Any limit that would drop below the already committed amount is rejected.<br>|
|» change_reason|body|string|false|The reason for this overdraft limit change, for your reference. Recorded for audit purposes.<br>|

<h1 id="chargebee-api-ledgeroperations">ledger_operations</h1>

A ledger operation represents a single action recorded in the ledger that results in a state change.

## Release authorization

<a id="opIdrelease_authorization"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/ledger_operations/release_authorization' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /ledger_operations/release_authorization`

The release_authorization operation releases previously held credits back to the usable balance, effectively canceling an existing authorization (hold).  
**API Behavior**

* Reverses an earlier `authorize` operation.
* Moves credits from held (reserved) → usable balance.
* No consumption occurs as part of this operation.
* Always releases the entire remaining held amount; partial releases are not supported.
* Once released, the hold is considered closed.  
**Requirements**

Requires the `authorization_id` of the original authorize request.  
**Business Use Cases**

Cancellation flows
When an authorized action is no longer needed.

Failure recovery
Downstream processing fails after authorization.

Timeout handling
Manual alternative to auto-release on hold expiry.  
**Usage**

Ensures held credits are fully returned to the usable balance, preventing funds from remaining locked.

The response returns `ledger_operations` (and, for compatibility, a deprecated singular `ledger_operation`), the updated `ledger_account_balance`, the affected `grant_blocks`, and the `ledger_entries` recorded by this operation.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

<h3 id="release-authorization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|
|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» authorization_id|body|string|true|Identifier of the original `authorize` operation whose hold is being released.  <br>**Behavior**<br><br>* Must reference a valid and active hold created via an `authorize` request.<br>* Must match the `ledger_operation_id` used in the original `authorize` call.<br>|
|» id|body|string|false|Optional client-supplied identifier for this release_authorization operation.  <br>**Behavior**<br><br>* When provided, must uniquely identify this operation across the entire ledger.<br>* Should not conflict with any other operation, regardless of type.<br>|
|» ledger_operation_timestamp|body|integer(unix-time)|true|Unix timestamp (in seconds) representing when the release_authorization occurred in the upstream system.  <br>**Usage**<br><br>* Used for period attribution, grace-period eligibility, and reporting accuracy.  <br>**Note**<br><br>Late or out-of-order submissions appear in arrival order, while attribution and eligibility logic rely on `ledger_operation_timestamp`.<br>|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Optional opaque JSON object carrying additional business context.  <br>**Behavior**<br><br>* Stored as-is and returned verbatim by the system.<br>* Not interpreted, validated, or indexed by the system.<br>|

## Capture

<a id="opIdcapture"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/ledger_operations/capture' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /ledger_operations/capture`

The capture operation immediately consumes credits for a completed action.  
**Behavior**

* Credits are directly moved from usable → consumed.
* No intermediate hold or reservation is created.  
**Usage**

Ideal for simple, immediate consumption scenarios where there is no need for multi-step confirmation or concurrency control.

The response returns `ledger_operations` (and, for compatibility, a deprecated singular `ledger_operation`), the updated `ledger_account_balance`, the affected `grant_blocks`, and the `ledger_entries` recorded by this operation.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

## Allocate

<a id="opIdallocate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/ledger_operations/allocate' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /ledger_operations/allocate`

The allocate operation allocates credit grants to a subscription's provisioned balance.  
**Behavior**

* Allocates the specified `amount` to the subscription's provisioned balance for the given `unit_id`.
* Creates one [grant block](/docs/api/grant_blocks) to track the credit-grant lifecycle, including balance, holds, expiry, and rollover.
* Creates a [ledger operation](/docs/api/ledger_operations) of type `allocation` to record the movement of credit grants.  
**Usage**

Use this operation to allocate ad-hoc credit grants to a subscription --- for example, to reward subscribers with bonus credit grants or compensate for service disruptions.

The response returns the created `ledger_operations`, the updated `ledger_account_balance`, the created `grant_blocks`, and the `ledger_entries` recorded by this operation.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

<h3 id="allocate-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|
|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» subscription_id|body|string|true|A unique, immutable identifier for the [subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object#id) to which the allocated credit grants are applied.<br>|
|» unit_id|body|string|true|Identifier of the credit unit for which credit grants are allocated. For example, a credit unit id such as `ai_credits`.<br>|
|» id|body|string|false|Optional client-supplied identifier for this allocate operation.  <br>**Behavior**<br><br>* When provided, must uniquely identify this operation across the entire ledger.<br>* Should not conflict with any other operation, regardless of type.<br>* Reusing the same value is treated as a replay of the original allocation rather than a conflict, so a retry does not create a second grant block.  <br>**Constraints**<br><br>* Maximum length: 50 characters.  <br>**Default value**<br><br>* When omitted, Chargebee generates an identifier for the operation.  <br>**Usage**<br><br>* Supply a value that you can reproduce, such as your own allocation reference, and send that same value when retrying after an unexpected response.<br>|
|» amount|body|string|true|The number of credit grants to allocate as part of this operation.<br>Pass this value as a decimal string.  <br>**Constraints**<br><br>Maximum supported value: `9999999999999999999999999.9999999999` (up to 25 digits before the decimal and up to 10 digits after).  <br>**Behavior**<br><br>* Must be a positive value greater than zero.<br>* Allocated to the subscription's provisioned balance for the given `unit_id`.  <br>**Example**<br><br>If `amount = "500"`, then 500 credit grants are added to the subscription's total as well as usable balance and recorded as a new grant block.<br>|
|» effective_from|body|integer(unix-time)|false|Optional Unix timestamp (in seconds) at which the allocated credit grants become usable. Sets [`effective_from`](/docs/api/grant_blocks#effective_from) on the grant block created by this allocation.  <br>**Behavior**<br><br>* When set to a future timestamp, the grant block is created with [`status`](/docs/api/grant_blocks#status) `scheduled` and its credit grants stay out of the usable balance until that time.<br>* At `effective_from`, the grant block becomes `available` and its credit grants are included in the usable balance.  <br>**Default value**<br><br>* When omitted, the credit grants become usable at the time of the request.  <br>**Note**<br><br>`effective_from` is inclusive. A capture operation with a timestamp exactly equal to `effective_from` is eligible to consume credit grants from this grant block.<br>|
|» expires_at|body|integer(unix-time)|true|Unix timestamp (in seconds) at which the allocated credit grants expire and become unavailable for consumption.  <br>**Behavior**<br><br>* Once expired, the remaining balance in the associated grant block moves to `expired_amount`.  <br>**Constraints**<br><br>* `expires_at` must be a future timestamp.<br>|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Optional opaque JSON object carrying additional business context for this allocation.  <br>**Behavior**<br><br>* Stored as-is and returned verbatim by the system.<br>* Not interpreted, validated, or indexed by the system.<br>|

## Authorize

<a id="opIdauthorize"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/ledger_operations/authorize' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /ledger_operations/authorize`

Reserves credit grants at the time of request for later finalization via `capture_authorization` or `release_authorization`.

Use this operation when the final amount is unknown while a job is in progress, or when multiple concurrent operations or users draw from the same credit pool. Authorization holds credits during an operation so concurrent requests cannot spend the same held credits. When the job begins, credits move from the usable balance to a held state. When the job completes, `capture_authorization` converts the captured amount from held credits into consumed credits and releases any unused held credits.  
**API Behavior**

* Moves credits from usable balance → held (reserved) state.
* No consumption occurs at this stage; only reservation.
* Final state is determined later:
  * `capture_authorization`: converts held credits into consumed.
* `release_authorization`: returns held credits to usable balance.  
**Reserved Credits Behavior**

* Held credits are not consumable by other operations.
* Held credits are not counted as used until captured.
* Unreleased holds are automatically returned to usable balance upon expiry.

**Use Cases**

* Concurrency control
* Prevents concurrent operations from spending the same held credits.
* Ensures credits are reserved for a specific flow while other requests see reduced availability.
* The final captured amount may be unknown while a job is in progress, but the authorize request still requires an `amount` to reserve credits. Authorization holds those credits until the job completes.

Two-step workflows
Supports "check now, finalize later" flows. When the job begins, authorization reserves credits. When the job completes, `capture_authorization` uses the original `authorization_id`, converts only the captured amount into consumed credits, and releases any unused held credits.

The response returns `ledger_operations` (and, for compatibility, a deprecated singular `ledger_operation`), the updated `ledger_account_balance`, the affected `grant_blocks`, and the `ledger_entries` recorded by this operation.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

<h3 id="authorize-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|
|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» id|body|string|false|Optional client-supplied identifier for this authorize operation.  <br>**Behavior**<br><br>* When provided, must uniquely identify this operation across the entire ledger.<br>* Should not conflict with any other operation, regardless of type.  <br>**Usage**<br><br>* Identifies the specific reservation of credits created by this request.<br>* Used as the reference for subsequent operations:<br>  * `capture_authorization`: to finalize (consume) the held credits.<br>  * `release_authorization`: to release the held credits back to usable balance.<br>|
|» subscription_id|body|string|true|A unique, immutable identifier for the [subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object#id) against which credit grants are tracked.<br>|
|» unit_id|body|string|true|Identifier of the credit unit for which credit grants are tracked. For example, a credit unit id such as `ai_credits`.<br>|
|» amount|body|string|true|The number of credit grants to reserve from the usable balance. While held, this amount is unavailable for other operations, helping prevent concurrent requests from spending the same credits.<br>Pass this value as a decimal string.  <br>**Constraints**<br><br>Maximum supported value: `9999999999999999999999999.9999999999` (up to 25 digits before the decimal and up to 10 digits after).  <br>**Behavior**<br><br>* On `authorize`, this amount is moved from `usable_balance` to `hold_amount`. It is not consumed yet.<br>* The held amount can later be:<br>  * Captured via `capture_authorization`.<br>  * Released via `release_authorization`.<br>* Auto-released when the hold expires.  <br>**Example**<br><br>If `amount = "50"`, the ledger reserves 50 credits immediately, if available. A later `capture_authorization` can consume all or part of that hold. Any unused remainder is released back to the usable balance.<br>|
|» ledger_operation_timestamp|body|integer(unix-time)|true|Unix timestamp (in seconds) representing when the business operation occurred in the upstream system.  <br>**Usage**<br><br>Used for period attribution, grace-period eligibility, and reporting accuracy.  <br>**Note**<br><br>Late or out-of-order submissions appear in arrival order, while attribution and eligibility logic rely on `ledger_operation_timestamp`.  <br>**Constraints**<br><br>* The `ledger_operation_timestamp` must be within the last 10 minutes from the time of the request.<br>* Grant blocks outside their active window (including those in the grace period) are not eligible for authorization and are excluded from balance checks for this ledger operation.<br>|
|» auto_release_timestamp|body|integer(unix-time)|false|Unix timestamp (in seconds) indicating when an unfinalized hold will be automatically released back to the usable balance.  <br>**Behavior**<br><br>* Applies only to authorize operations.<br>* If not explicitly provided, the system assigns a default expiry. Defaults to approximately 10 minutes after the authorize request is processed.  <br>**Usage**<br><br>Ensures held credits are not locked indefinitely by abandoned or unfinalized authorizations.  <br>**Note**<br><br>* By default, the value reflects what is provided in the request.<br>* If the specified timestamp exceeds the end of the block's grace period, it is adjusted (clamped) to the grace period end and returned in the response.<br>|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Optional opaque JSON object carrying additional business context  <br>**Behavior**<br><br>* Stored as-is and returned verbatim by the system.<br>* Not interpreted, validated, or indexed by the system.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|chargebee-event-actions|all-disabled|
|chargebee-event-email|all-disabled|
|chargebee-event-webhook|all-disabled|

<h3 id="list-ledger-operations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|

|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|

## Capture authorization

<a id="opIdcapture_authorization"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/ledger_operations/capture_authorization' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /ledger_operations/capture_authorization`

The capture_authorization operation finalizes a previously created hold by converting reserved credits into consumed credits.  
**API Behavior**

* Completes an earlier authorize operation.
* Moves credits from held (reserved) → consumed (debited).
* Any unused portion of the hold is automatically released back to the usable balance.
* Once fully captured (and remainder released, if any), the hold is considered closed.  
**Requirement**

Requires the `authorization_id` (i.e., the `ledger_operation_id` of the original authorize operation).  
**Note**

* In case of a partial capture (where the amount held in the authorize call is greater than the amount in the capture call), the remaining held credits are released via a separate internal release operation.
* This internal operation is not included in the immediate response, but is visible via the list operations API.
* The internal release will have a different `ledger_operation_id` (system-generated), but will share the same `authorization_id` as the capture operation for correlation.

The response returns `ledger_operations` (and, for compatibility, a deprecated singular `ledger_operation`), the updated `ledger_account_balance`, the affected `grant_blocks`, and the `ledger_entries` recorded by this operation.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

<h3 id="capture-authorization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|
|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» authorization_id|body|string|true|Identifier of the original `authorize` operation whose hold is being captured.  <br>**Behavior**<br><br>* Must reference a valid and active hold created via an `authorize` request.<br>* Must match the `ledger_operation_id` used in the original `authorize` call.<br>|
|» id|body|string|false|Optional client-supplied identifier for this capture_authorization operation.  <br>**Behavior**<br><br>* When provided, must uniquely identify this operation across the entire ledger.<br>* Should not conflict with any other operation, regardless of type.<br>|
|» amount|body|string|true|The number of credits to finalize as consumption from a previously authorized (held) amount.<br>Pass this value as a decimal string.  <br>**Constraints**<br><br>Maximum supported value: `9999999999999999999999999.9999999999` (up to 25 digits before the decimal and up to 10 digits after).  <br>**Behavior**<br><br>* Must be less than or equal to the current held amount for the specified authorization_id.<br>* The specified amount is moved from held → consumed.  <br>**Constraints**<br><br>Cannot exceed the total credits currently on hold for the authorization.  <br>**Example**<br><br>Step 1: Authorize (hold created): `amount = "100"` results in 100 credits moved from usable to held.<br><br>Step 2: Capture authorization (partial consumption): `amount = "70"` results in 70 credits moved from held to consumed; remaining 30 credits auto-released back to usable balance (via internal release operation)  <br>**Ledger Effect Summary**<br><br>* Consumed: 70<br>* Released: 30<br>* Remaining Hold: 0 (hold closed)<br>|
|» ledger_operation_timestamp|body|integer(unix-time)|true|Unix timestamp (in seconds) representing when the capture_authorization occurred in the upstream system.  <br>**Usage**<br><br>Used for period attribution, grace-period eligibility, and reporting accuracy.  <br>**Note**<br><br>Late or out-of-order submissions appear in arrival order, while attribution and eligibility logic rely on `ledger_operation_timestamp`.<br>|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Optional opaque JSON object carrying additional business context.  <br>**Behavior**<br><br>* Stored as-is and returned verbatim by the system.<br>* Not interpreted, validated, or indexed by the system.<br>|

## Reactivate a metered feature

<a id="opIdreactivate_a_metered_feature"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/metered_features/string/reactivate_command' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /metered_features/{metered-feature-id}/reactivate_command`

Restores a previously archived metered feature `status` back to `active`.

The sample responses show metered features with and without group-by attributes.  
**Availability**

Support for adding `GROUP BY` to metered features and retrieving usage grouped by attributes is an upcoming capability and is not generally available yet. It will be made available in the coming weeks.  

### Prerequisites \& Constraints

* The metered feature `status` must be `archived`.  

### Impacts

**Metered feature**  
* The metered feature `status` is changed to `active`.
* The meter `status` is changed to `active`.
* The meter's `query` and `column_definitions` remain unchanged. When `query` includes a `GROUP BY` clause, `group_by` also remains unchanged.  
**Entitlements and subscription entitlements**  
* New [entitlements](/docs/api/entitlements) and [subscription entitlements](/docs/api/subscription_entitlements) can be created for the feature when it's reactivated.

## Create a metered feature

<a id="opIdcreate_a_metered_feature"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/metered_features' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /metered_features`

Creates a metered feature.

Use `query` to define how Chargebee measures usage for the metered feature. The result is a single aggregate across all matching usage events. To report grouped usage, include attributes in a `GROUP BY` clause. Each distinct set of values forms one usage group. These attributes are the metered feature's group-by attributes.  
**Availability**

Support for adding `GROUP BY` to metered features and retrieving usage grouped by attributes is an upcoming capability and is not generally available yet. It will be made available in the coming weeks.  

### Use Cases

##### Create a metered feature with grouped usage

Use group-by attributes when customers need to view how usage is distributed across properties such as GPU type and region.

For example, the following query measures completed GPU hours and groups them by `gpu_type` and `region`:

```sql
SELECT SUM(hours)
FROM events
WHERE status = 'completed'
GROUP BY gpu_type, region;
```

Chargebee creates a separate usage group for each distinct set of `gpu_type` and `region` values. For example:

```text
gpu_type = "h100", region = "us-east"  60 hours
gpu_type = "a100", region = "eu-west"  40 hours
```

These groups can be displayed in [Retrieve usage summary for a subscription](/docs/api/usage_summary/retrieve-usage-summary-for-a-subscription) and [Retrieve usages for an invoice as PDF](/docs/api/usages/retrieve-usages-for-an-invoice-as-pdf). Subscription billing uses the overall aggregate of 100 hours.

**Null and empty group-by attribute values**

Chargebee stores usage in the null group in the following cases:

* Usage recorded before the group-by attribute was added to the metered feature's `GROUP BY` clause. For example, if `region` is added to the `GROUP BY` clause later, usage recorded before `region` was added belongs to the null group for `region`.
* Events that do not contain the group-by attribute. For example, an event without `region` belongs to the null group.
* Events where the group-by attribute is JSON `null`, such as `"region": null`.
* Events where the attribute is the exact string `"null"`, irrespective of capitalization, such as `"region": "null"`, `"region": "NULL"`, or `"region": "nULL"`.

The comparison with `"null"` is case-insensitive, but the entire value must match. Chargebee does not remove leading or trailing whitespace. Therefore, `"region": " null"` and `"region": "null "` remain separate string groups.

An explicit empty string is also kept separate. For example, `"region": ""` belongs to the empty-string group and not the null group.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

<h3 id="create-a-metered-feature-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|
|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|A case-sensitive name for the metered feature. For example: `API Calls`, `Input Tokens`.<br>|
|» description|body|string|false|A brief description of the metered feature.<br>|
|» feature_unit|body|string|true|Unit of measure for the metered feature, in singular form. It is pluralized automatically as needed. For example, `request` or `token`.<br>|
|» query|body|string|true|The SQL query used to calculate usage from [`usage_event`](/docs/api/usage_events) properties. For example: `SELECT SUM(api_calls) FROM events WHERE status = 'completed'`.<br><br>To group usage by attribute values, include a `GROUP BY` clause. Each distinct set of group-by attribute values forms a separate usage group. For example: `SELECT SUM(hours) FROM events WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY gpu_type, region`. The response returns the group-by attribute names in [`group_by`](/docs/api/metered_features/metered-feature-object#group_by), in the same order.  <br>**Availability**<br><br>Support for adding `GROUP BY` to metered features and retrieving usage grouped by attributes is an upcoming capability and is not generally available yet. It will be made available in the coming weeks.  <br>**Constraints**<br><br>* Properties used in the aggregate expression or `WHERE` clause must be listed in `column_definitions.column_name`.<br>* A group-by attribute used only in the `GROUP BY` clause does not require a `column_definitions` entry. Its value is treated as a string.<br>* The `GROUP BY` clause can contain up to 5 group-by attributes.<br>* Exact duplicate group-by attribute names are not allowed. Names are case-sensitive, so `region, region` is invalid, while `region, Region` identifies two different attributes.  <br>**Usage reporting and subscription billing**<br><br>For a metered feature whose `query` includes a `GROUP BY` clause, grouped usage is available in [Retrieve usage summary for a subscription](/docs/api/usage_summary/retrieve-usage-summary-for-a-subscription) and [Retrieve usages for an invoice as PDF](/docs/api/usages/retrieve-usages-for-an-invoice-as-pdf). These groups are for reporting only. Subscription billing uses the overall aggregate for the metered feature and does not bill each group separately.<br><br>For example, a `SUM` query can return 60 hours for `region=us-east` and 40 hours for `region=eu-west`. The reporting operations can display both groups. Subscription billing uses the overall aggregate of 100 hours.<br>|
|» column_definitions|body|object|false|Definitions of the columns or properties referenced by the `query`.<br>|
|» » column_name|body|[string]|true|Name of the column or property used in the `query`.  <br>**Constraint**:<br><br>* Must be one of the [`properties`](/docs/api/usage_events#properties) of a [`usage_event`](/docs/api/usage_events) object in Chargebee.<br>|
|» » data_type|body|[string]|true|none|

|chargebee-event-email|all-disabled|

## Archive a metered feature

<a id="opIdarchive_a_metered_feature"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/metered_features/string/archive_command' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /metered_features/{metered-feature-id}/archive_command`

Archives a metered [feature](/docs/api/metered_features) and its associated [meter](/docs/api/meters).

The sample responses show metered features with and without group-by attributes.  
**Availability**

Support for adding `GROUP BY` to metered features and retrieving usage grouped by attributes is an upcoming capability and is not generally available yet. It will be made available in the coming weeks.  

### Prerequisites \& Constraints

* The metered feature must be `active`.  

### Impacts

**Entitlements and subscription entitlements**  
* New entitlements and subscription entitlements cannot be created for the feature when it's archived.
* Pre-existing entitlements and subscription entitlements remain effective.  
**Feature and meter**  
* The feature and meter `status` are changed to `archived`.
* The meter's `query` and `column_definitions` remain unchanged. When `query` includes a `GROUP BY` clause, `group_by` also remains unchanged.


<h3 id="archive-a-metered-feature-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|
|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|metered-feature-id|path|string|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|

|chargebee-event-email|all-disabled|
|chargebee-event-webhook|all-disabled|

## One time purchase

<a id="opIdone_time_purchase"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/non_subscriptions/{non-subscription-app-id}/one_time_purchase' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /non_subscriptions/{non-subscription-app-id}/one_time_purchase`

This API is used to sync consumable, non-consumable, and non-renewing product payments in Chargebee.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

<h3 id="one-time-purchase-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|
|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|non-subscription-app-id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» receipt|body|string|true|**Google Play Store** :<br>The purchase `token`<br>taken from the Android device after successful creation of the in-app purchase.<br><br>**Apple App Store** :<br>The Base64 encoded [App Store in-app purchase receipt](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/storekit/original_api_for_in-app_purchase/validating_receipts_with_the_app_store?language=objc#overview)<br>taken from the Apple device after successful creation of the in-app purchase.<br>|
|» product|body|object|false|Parameters for product<br>|
|» » id|body|string|true|**Google Play Store** : The unique identifier of the product purchased. The value of this parameter is the `productId` or `sku` received from the [Google Play Store](https://developers.google.com/android-publisher/api-ref/rest/v3/inappproducts/get).  <br>**Note:**<br>The `max chars`<br>limit is `95`<br>for the Google Play Store.<br><br>**Apple App Store** : The [unique identifier](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/storekit/product/id/) (created in [App Store Connect](https://appstoreconnect.apple.com/login)) of the product purchased.<br>|
|» » currency_code|body|string|true|**Google Play Store** :<br>This parameter is **not applicable**<br>to the **Google Play Store**.<br>If the value is passed, it will return a validation error.<br><br>**Apple App Store**:<br>The currency code (ISO 4217 format) for the product.<br>|
|» » price|body|integer(int32)|true|**Google Play Store** :<br>This parameter is **not applicable**<br>to the **Google Play Store**.<br>If the value is passed, it will return a validation error.<br><br>**Apple App Store** :<br>The price paid by the customer for this product. The unit [depends on the type of currency](/docs/api/getting-started).<br>Provide either this or `product[price_in_decimal]`<br>.<br>|
|» » type|body|string|true|The type of product for one time purchase.<br><br>* consumable - This value represents a type of one-time purchase that provides users with in-app benefits or effects that can be consumed or depleted over time, such as lives, gems, boosts, or digital tips. Once consumed, the purchased item is no longer available and must be repurchased to obtain its benefits again.<br>* non_consumable - The value represents a type of in-app purchase that provides a permanent benefit to the user and can be purchased once without expiration. This type of purchase is typically used to offer premium features or content that enhance the user experience of the app, such as additional filters or cosmetic items in a game.<br>* non_renewing_subscription - The value represents a type of subscription that grants access to services or content for a limited period of time, such as a season pass to in-game content. Unlike other subscription models, this type of subscription does not renew automatically and requires people to purchase a new subscription once it concludes to continue accessing the content or services.<br>|
|» » name|body|string|false|**Google Play Store** :<br>The name (created in [Play Store Console](https://play.google.com/console/about/)<br>) of the product purchased. If not passed then the `product[id]`<br>will be considered as the value of `product[name]`.<br><br>**Apple App Store** :<br>The name (created in [App Store Connect](https://appstoreconnect.apple.com/login)<br>) of the product purchased.<br>|
|» » price_in_decimal|body|string|false|**Google Play Store** :<br>This parameter is **not applicable** to the **Google Play Store**. If the value is passed, it will return a validation error.<br><br>**Apple App Store** : The price paid by the customer for the product. The value is in decimal and in major units of the currency. Provide either this or `product[price]`.<br>|
|» customer|body|object|false|Parameters for customer<br>|
|» » id|body|string|false|**Google Play Store** :<br>The unique [id](/docs/api/customers/create-a-customer#id)<br>in Chargebee for the customer who made this purchase via Google Play Store. If not provided, a random unique ID generated for the purchase token will be the `customer[id]`.<br>If the customer record is not found in Chargebee, it is created.<br><br>**Apple App Store** :<br>The unique [id](/docs/api/customers/create-a-customer#id)<br>in Chargebee for the customer who made this purchase. If not provided, the value is considered to be [original_transaction_id](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appstorereceipts/original_transaction_id?language=objc)<br>(the transaction identifier at Apple, of the original purchase). If the customer record is not found in Chargebee, it is created.<br>|
|» » email|body|string(email)|false|The email address of the customer who made the purchase.<br>|
|» » first_name|body|string|false|The first name of the customer who made the purchase.<br>|
|» » last_name|body|string|false|The last name of the customer who made the purchase.<br>|

|chargebee-event-email|all-disabled|
|chargebee-event-webhook|all-disabled|

|» » type|non_consumable|
|» » type|non_renewing_subscription|

<h1 id="chargebee-api-offerevents">offer_events</h1>

Offer events are used to record and list user interactions with personalized offers.

## Create an offer event

<a id="opIdcreate_an_offer_event"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/offer_events' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /offer_events`

The Create Offer Event API records user interactions with an offer for tracking and analytics purposes.

Use this API to log user-triggered engagement events such as:

* `viewed` - when an offer is displayed to the user.
* `dismissed` - when the user closes or ignores the offer. These events are essential for accurate offer performance reporting and funnel analysis. Make sure to send them as they happen.

**Note:** System-driven events like accepted and fulfilled are captured automatically by the growth system through fulfillment workflows. You do not need to post these.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

<h3 id="create-an-offer-event-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|
|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» personalized_offer_id|body|string|true|The ID of the personalized offer the event pertains to.<br>|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of engagement event to be recorded.<br><br>* dismissed - Logged when the user closes or ignores the offer without accepting<br>* viewed - Logged when the user's UI renders or displays the offer<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|chargebee-event-actions|all-disabled|

<h1 id="chargebee-api-offerfulfillments">offer_fulfillments</h1>

Offer fulfillment allows you to initiate, update, and retrieve the lifecycle of an offer fulfillment, after a personalized offer has been accepted.

## Create an offer fulfillment

<a id="opIdcreate_an_offer_fulfillment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/offer_fulfillments' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /offer_fulfillments`

This API notifies that a user has accepted an offer, logs an accepted event immediately for reporting, and triggers a backend processing depending on the offer's processing_type.
You can call this API when a user accepts an offer (e.g., the user clicked Accept Offer or a similar confirmation).
This API will record an accepted event as soon as the API is called and initiate the appropriate fulfillment mechanism according to `processing_type`:

* `billing_update`: Initiates subscription or billing record updates (e.g., applying a discount or changing a plan) asynchronously.
* `checkout`: Returns a `hosted_page` object in the response, which contains a URL to render the hosted checkout flow.
* `url_redirect`: Returns a redirect_url. You are responsible for managing fulfillment on your end and must call the Update Offer Fulfillment API to report either completion or failure.
* `webhook`: Sends a webhook, and you must also manage fulfillment on your end. Be sure to call the Update Offer Fulfillment API to report completion or failure.
* `email`: Sends an email containing the offer details as configured. You are responsible for handling fulfillment on your side and must call the Update Offer Fulfillment API to report completion or failure. You can poll the Retrieve Offer Fulfillment endpoint for final status on `billing_update` and `checkout flows`. Upon actual fulfillment completion, the system logs a `fulfilled` event and sends notifications (webhook, Slack, email, Segment) as configured.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

<h3 id="create-an-offer-fulfillment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|
|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» personalized_offer_id|body|string|true|ID of the personalized offer that was accepted.<br>|
|» option_id|body|string|true|ID of the Offer Option that the user accepted.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|chargebee-event-email|all-disabled|

## Update an offer fulfillment

<a id="opIdupdate_an_offer_fulfillment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/offer_fulfillments/string' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /offer_fulfillments/{offer-fulfillment-id}`

This API is used to update the status of offer fulfillment for the processing types `url_redirect`, `webhook` and `email` as Chargebee cannot automatically fulfill these offers.

If `status = failed`, you must include a `failure_reason` to explain why the fulfillment did not succeed. The system logs a `fulfilled` event when `status = completed` or a `failed` event when `status = failed`.

**Note** : If the offer fulfillment is not marked as completed or failed within 7 days, Chargebee will mark the offer fulfillment as failed with the error code as `external_fulfillment_failed`.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|
|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|offer-fulfillment-id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» id|body|string|true|ID of the fulfillment that is being updated.<br>|
|» status|body|string|true|Final state of the fulfillment.<br><br>* failed - Pass this if the fulfillment is failed.<br>* completed - Pass this if the fulfillment is completed.<br>|
|» failure_reason|body|string|false|Explanation for failure; required when `status`<br>= `failed`<br>.<br>|

<h1 id="chargebee-api-omnichannelsubscriptionitems">omnichannel_subscription_items</h1>

Represents a product entitlement (item) within an [`omnichannel_subscription`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscriptions) purchased on Apple App Store or Google Play Store.

## List scheduled changes for omnichannel subscription item

<a id="opIdlist_scheduled_changes_for_omnichannel_subscription_item"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/omnichannel_subscription_items/string/scheduled_changes' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /omnichannel_subscription_items/{omnichannel-subscription-item-id}/scheduled_changes`

Returns scheduled changes for the specified `omnichannel_subscription_item`.

Scheduled changes are created when the store will apply a product or pause change later (typically at term end), for example:

* **Apple App Store** : Scheduled **downgrade** within the same subscription group.
* **Google Play Store** : Product changes using the **`DEFERRED`** replacement mode. Immediate changes (`CHARGE_PRORATED_PRICE`) do **not** create a scheduled-change resource.

Use this API when [`has_scheduled_changes`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_items/omnichannel_subscription_item-object#has_scheduled_changes) is `true`. See also [`omnichannel_subscription_item_scheduled_change`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_item_scheduled_changes) and [omnichannel events](/docs/api/omnichannel_events).

<h1 id="chargebee-api-omnichannelsubscriptions">omnichannel_subscriptions</h1>

Represents a subscription purchased and managed in an external app marketplace (`apple_app_store` or `google_play_store`), normalized into Chargebee's omnichannel model.

## Move an omnichannel subscription

<a id="opIdmove_an_omnichannel_subscription"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/omnichannel_subscriptions/string/move' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /omnichannel_subscriptions/{omnichannel-subscription-id}/move`

Moves an `omnichannel_subscription` to another customer in Chargebee.

### Prerequisites

* The target customer must already exist in Chargebee (or be creatable via your usual customer APIs before calling this operation).
* The omnichannel subscription must already be recorded in Chargebee.

### Impacts

* Updates the omnichannel subscription's `customer_id` and related records to the target customer.
* Triggers the [`omnichannel_subscription_moved_in`](/docs/api/events/webhook/omnichannel_subscription_moved_in) webhook with the new customer details.

This operation does **not** change the underlying Apple or Google purchase; it only reassigns ownership inside Chargebee.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

<h3 id="move-an-omnichannel-subscription-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|
|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|omnichannel-subscription-id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» to_customer_id|body|string|true|Specifies the unique ID of the `customer`<br>resource to which the subscription will be moved.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|chargebee-event-actions|all-disabled|
|chargebee-event-email|all-disabled|
|chargebee-event-webhook|all-disabled|

## Retrieve an omnichannel subscription

<a id="opIdretrieve_an_omnichannel_subscription"></a>

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/omnichannel_subscriptions/string' \

## List omnichannel transactions of an omnichannel subscription

<a id="opIdlist_omnichannel_transactions_of_an_omnichannel_subscription"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/omnichannel_subscriptions/string/omnichannel_transactions' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /omnichannel_subscriptions/{omnichannel-subscription-id}/omnichannel_transactions`

Returns the list of [`omnichannel_transaction`](/docs/api/omnichannel_transactions) objects associated with the specified `omnichannel_subscription`, including the initial purchase and subsequent renewals when available.

**Apple App Store** : Each transaction's `id_at_source` is the App Store **Transaction ID** . Price and `transacted_at` are typically present.

**Google Play Store** : Each transaction's `id_at_source` is the Google Play **Order ID** (typically `GPA....`), which differs from the parent subscription's purchase-token `id_at_source`. Price and `transacted_at` may be present depending on the data available from Google for that transaction.


<h3 id="list-omnichannel-transactions-of-an-omnichannel-subscription-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|omnichannel-subscription-id|path|string|true|none|
|limit|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of resources to be returned.<br>|
|offset|query|string|false|Determines your position in the list for pagination. To ensure that the next page is retrieved correctly, always set `offset`<br>to the value of `next_offset`<br>obtained in the previous iteration of the API call.<br>|

## List omnichannel subscriptions

<a id="opIdlist_omnichannel_subscriptions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/omnichannel_subscriptions' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /omnichannel_subscriptions`

Returns a list of `omnichannel_subscription` objects. Filter by Chargebee `id`, store-native `id_at_source`, `customer_id`, `source`, purchase/update timestamps, or nested item attributes.

**Apple App Store** : Filter `id_at_source` with the original purchase **Transaction ID**.

**Google Play Store** : Filter `id_at_source` with the subscription **purchase token** . Google may issue a new token after certain subscription changes; Chargebee updates `id_at_source` to the latest token, so use the current token when filtering.


<h3 id="list-omnichannel-subscriptions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|limit|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of resources to be returned.<br>|
|offset|query|string|false|Determines your position in the list for pagination. To ensure that the next page is retrieved correctly, always set `offset`<br>to the value of `next_offset`<br>obtained in the previous iteration of the API call.<br>|
|source|query|object|false|optional, enumerated string filter<br><br>To filter based on OmnichannelSubscription Source. Possible values are : apple_app_store, google_play_store.<br><br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, in, not_in<br><br>**Example →**<br>*source\[is_not\] = "apple_app_store"*<br>|
|customer_id|query|object|false|optional, string filter<br><br>Chargebee Customer External Identifier.<br><br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, starts_with, in, not_in<br><br>**Example →**<br>*customer_id\[is\] = "8gsnbYfsMLds"*<br>|
|id|query|object|false|optional, string filter<br><br>A unique and immutable identifier for the omnichannel subscription.<br><br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, starts_with, in, not_in<br><br>**Example →**<br>*id\[is\] = "os_1mG9tGuVIecbkzR"*<br>|
|id_at_source|query|object|false|optional, string filter<br><br>The identifier of the subscription in the [`source`](omnichannel_subscriptions#omnichannel_subscriptions_source).<br><br>**Apple App Store** : The original purchase **Transaction ID**.<br><br>**Google Play Store** : The subscription **purchase token** . Google may issue a new token after certain subscription changes; Chargebee updates `id_at_source` to the latest token.<br><br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, starts_with, in, not_in<br><br>**Example →**<br>*id_at_source\[is\] = "2000000123456789"*<br>|
|updated_at|query|object|false|optional, timestamp(UTC) in seconds filter<br><br>Timestamp (UTC) indicating when the subscription was last updated.<br><br>**Supported operators :**<br>after, before, on, between<br><br>**Example →**<br>*updated_at\[after\] = "1777902633"*<br>|
|purchased_at|query|object|false|optional, timestamp(UTC) in seconds filter<br><br>Timestamp (UTC) when the subscription was originally purchased in the respective marketplace (initial purchase).<br><br>**Supported operators :**<br>after, before, on, between<br><br>**Example →**<br>*purchased_at\[after\] = "1777559357"*<br>|
|sort_by|query|object|false|optional, string filter<br><br>Sorts based on the specified attribute.<br>**Supported attributes :**<br>created_at, updated_at<br><br>**Supported sort-orders :**<br>asc, desc<br><br>**Example →**<br>*sort_by\[asc\] = "created_at"*<br><br>This will sort the result based on the 'created_at' attribute in ascending(earliest first) order.<br>|
|omnichannel_subscription_item|query|object|false|Parameters for omnichannel_subscription_item<br>|

<a id="opIdlist_orders"></a>

curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/orders' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

```

`GET /orders`

This API is used to retrieve a list of all the available orders.


<h3 id="list-orders-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|id|query|object|false|optional, string filter<br><br>Uniquely identifies the order. It is the api identifier for the order.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, starts_with, in, not_in<br><br>**Example →**<br>*id\[is\] = "890"*<br>|
|invoice_id|query|object|false|optional, string filter<br><br>The invoice number which acts as an identifier for invoice and is generated sequentially.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, starts_with, in, not_in<br><br>**Example →**<br>*invoice_id\[is\] = "INVOICE_982"*<br>|

Possible values are : new, processing, complete, cancelled, voided, queued, awaiting_shipment, on_hold, delivered, shipped, partially_delivered, returned.<br><br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, in, not_in<br><br>**Example →**<br>*status\[is\] = "queued"*<br>|

null

Orders are generated by Chargebee in cancelled state.<br>* product_not_required - Product not required.<br>* payment_declined - Payment declined.<br>* product_not_available - Product not available.<br>* third_party_cancellation - Third party cancellation.<br>|
|» shipped_at|body|integer(unix-time)|false|The time at which the order was shipped.<br>|
|» delivered_at|body|integer(unix-time)|false|The time at which the order was delivered.<br>|

|» tracking_id|body|string|false|The tracking id of the order.<br>|
|» shipment_carrier|body|string|false|The carrier used to ship the goods to the customer. Ex:- FedEx.<br>|
|» fulfillment_status|body|string|false|The fulfillment status of an order as reflected in the shipping/order management application. Typical statuses include Shipped,Awaiting Shipment,Not fulfilled etc;.<br>|

Applicable only if you are using Chargebee's legacy order management system<br>* complete - Order has been processed successfully. Applicable only if you are using Chargebee's legacy order management system<br>* shipped - The order has moved from order management system to a shipping system.<br>* processing - Order is being processed. Applicable only if you are using Chargebee's legacy order management system<br>* queued - Order is yet to be processed by any system, these are scheduled orders created by Chargebee<br>* on_hold - The order is paused from being processed.<br>* new - Order has been created. Applicable only if you are using Chargebee's legacy order management system.<br>* returned - The order has been returned after delivery.<br>* delivered - The order has been delivered to the customer.<br>* awaiting_shipment - The order has been picked up by an integration system, and synced to a shipping management platform<br>* cancelled - Order has been cancelled. Applicable only if you are using Chargebee's legacy order management system<br>* partially_delivered - The order has been partially delivered to the customer.<br>|

`POST /orders/{order-id}/delete`

Deletes only [Imported Order](/docs/api/orders/import-an-order)
.Delete does not happen if the order was refunded. It goes through if order refund was initiated and is in "refund_due" state.


<h3 id="delete-an-imported-order-parameters">Parameters</h3>

## Create a payment intent

<a id="opIdcreate_a_payment_intent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/payment_intents' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /payment_intents`

Creates a PaymentIntent object. This is to be used with Chargebee.js API to complete the 3DS flow for new or stored cards.

While creating, specify the appropriate gateway account and amount. Exact amount can be estimated using our [Estimate API](/docs/api/estimates).

#### Customer resource lookup and creation

When [customer[id]](/docs/api/payment_intents/create-a-payment-intent#customer_id) is provided for this operation, it is looked up by Chargebee, and if found, the payment_intent is created for it. If not found, the `payment_intent` is created without any customer association and will be available for any customer.

##### Multiple business entities

If multiple [business entities](/docs/api/advanced-features) are created for the site, the customer resource lookup and creation happen within the [context](/docs/api/advanced-features) of the business entity [specified](/docs/api/advanced-features#mbe-header-main) in this API call. If no business entity is specified, the customer resource lookup is performed within the [site context](/docs/api/advanced-features), and if not found, the resource is created for the [default business entity](/docs/api/advanced-features) of the site.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

<h3 id="create-a-payment-intent-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|
|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» business_entity_id|body|string|false|Sets the [context]() for this operation to the [business entity](/docs/api/advanced-features) specified. Applicable only when multiple business entities have been created for the site. When this parameter is provided, the operation is able to read/write data associated only to the business entity specified. When not provided, the operation can read/write data for the entire site.  <br>**Note**<br><br>An alternative way of passing this parameter is by means of a [custom HTTP header](/docs/api/advanced-features).  <br>**See also**<br>[Customer resource lookup and creation.](/docs/api/payment_intents)<br>|
|» brand_id|body|string|false|The unique ID of the [brand](/docs/api/brands) this payment intent should be linked to. Applicable only when multiple brands have been created for the site. An alternative way of passing this parameter is by means of the `chargebee-brand-id` custom HTTP header; when both are provided, they must specify the same brand.  <br>**Default behavior**<br><br>* When not provided, the payment intent is linked to the brand of the customer it is created for, or to the default brand defined for the site when no customer is specified.<br>|

<h1 id="chargebee-api-paymentscheduleschemes">payment_schedule_schemes</h1>

Payment schedules for an invoice refer to a payment structure where the `amount_due` on an invoice is divided into smaller, more manageable parts, each of which is paid over a specified period.

## Retrieve a payment schedule scheme

<a id="opIdretrieve_a_payment_schedule_scheme"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/payment_schedule_schemes/string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /payment_schedule_schemes/{payment-schedule-scheme-id}`

This endpoint retrieves an existing payment schedule.


<h3 id="retrieve-a-payment-schedule-scheme-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|payment-schedule-scheme-id|path|string|true|none|

## List payment schedule schemes

<a id="opIdlist_payment_schedule_schemes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/payment_schedule_schemes' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /payment_schedule_schemes`

Returns a list of payment schedule schemes that match **all** the specified filter conditions. The list is sorted by `id` in descending order. Use `limit` and `offset` to paginate through the results.


<h3 id="list-payment-schedule-schemes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|limit|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of resources to be returned.<br>|
|offset|query|string|false|Determines your position in the list for pagination. To ensure that the next page is retrieved correctly, always set `offset`<br>to the value of `next_offset`<br>obtained in the previous iteration of the API call.<br>|
|id|query|object|false|optional, string filter<br><br>An auto-generated unique identifier for the payment schedule scheme.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, starts_with, in, not_in<br><br>**Example →**<br>*id\[is\] = "scheme-id"*<br>|
|updated_at|query|object|false|optional, timestamp(UTC) in seconds filter<br><br>To filter based on `updated_at`.<br>This attribute will be present only if the resource has been updated after 2016-09-28.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>after, before, on, between<br><br>**Example →**<br>*updated_at\[after\] = "1435054328"*<br>|
