This attribute is only applicable when `duration_type`<br>is `one_time`<br>and when the [feature is enabled](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/reporting.html#dashboards_flexible-mrr-calculation)<br>in Chargebee. Also, If the [site-level setting](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/reporting.html#chart_flexible-mrr-calculation)<br>is to exclude one-time discounts from MRR calculations, this value is always returned `false`<br>.<br>|

<h1 id="chargebee-api-products">products</h1>

## Update a product

<a id="opIdupdate_a_product"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/products/string' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /products/{product-id}`

This API allows you to update specific product details.

The following table will help you to understand the status of the mapped [item](/docs/api/items/item-object#status) and [item_price](/docs/api/item_prices/item_price-object#status) after passing product [status](/docs/api/products/update-a-product#status) value during product updation.  

|-------------------------------------|--------------------------------|
| **Product Status**(Input parameter) | **Item and Item Price Status** |
| **active**                          | **active**                     |
| **inactive**                        | **archived**                   |



> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

<h3 id="update-a-product-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|
|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|product-id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|A unique internal name for the product. This is only visible in Chargebee.<br>|
|» external_name|body|string|false|The unique name that appears for each product to the end user.<br>|
|» description|body|string|false|Description of the product.<br>|
|» status|body|string|false|Status of the product. Refer to the [table](/docs/api/products/update-a-product)<br>for more information.<br><br>* active - The active products are visible on the storefront, subscription, or checkout.<br>* inactive - The inactive products are not visible on the storefront, subscription, or checkout.<br>|
|» sku|body|string|false|A unique identifier code a seller assigns to each product or item. Retailers and merchants use SKUs to keep track of inventory and sales data and help organize products within a store or warehouse. SKUs can include a combination of letters, numbers, and symbols and can vary in length depending on the seller's needs.<br>|
|» shippable|body|boolean|false|Whether a product is shippable or not. Pass the value as `true`<br>if it is a shippable physical product, else pass the value as `false`<br>.<br>|
|» metadata|body|object|false|A collection of key-value pairs that provides extra information about the product.  <br>**Note:**<br>There's a character limit of 65,535.<br><br>[Learn more](/docs/api/advanced-features#metadata)<br>.<br>|

|chargebee-event-email|all-disabled|
|chargebee-event-webhook|all-disabled|

|» status|inactive|

## Delete a product

<a id="opIddelete_a_product"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/products/string/delete' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /products/{product-id}/delete`

This API deletes a product and changes the delete attribute value to `true`
. Deletion of a product is not allowed if there are `active`
or `archived`
variants under the product or if there are items mapped to the product. Once deleted, the `name`
of the product can be reused.

|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|
|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|product-id|path|string|true|none|

## List products

<a id="opIdlist_products"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/products' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /products`

This API retrieves the list of products that are `active`
or `inactive`
. Use `include_deleted`
parameter to include deleted products with `active`
and `inactive`
products.


<h3 id="list-products-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|limit|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of resources to be returned.<br>|
|offset|query|string|false|Determines your position in the list for pagination. To ensure that the next page is retrieved correctly, always set `offset`<br>to the value of `next_offset`<br>obtained in the previous iteration of the API call.<br>|
|include_deleted|query|boolean|false|If set to `true`<br>, it includes the deleted products in the API response.<br>|
|id|query|object|false|optional, string filter<br><br>Filter product based on their [id](/docs/api/products)<br>.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, starts_with, in, not_in<br><br>**Example →**<br>*id\[is\] = "basic"*<br>|
|name|query|object|false|optional, string filter<br><br>Filter product based on their `name`<br>s.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, starts_with, in, not_in<br><br>**Example →**<br>*name\[is\] = "basic"*<br>|
|status|query|object|false|optional, enumerated string filter<br><br>Filter product based on their `status`.<br>Possible values are : active, inactive.<br><br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, in, not_in<br><br>**Example →**<br>*status\[is\] = "basic"*<br>|
|shippable|query|object|false|optional, boolean filter<br><br>Filter product based on whether it is shippable or not. Possible values are : *true, false*<br><br>**Supported operators :**<br>is<br><br>**Example →**<br>*shippable\[is\] = "true"*<br>|
|has_variant|query|object|false|optional, boolean filter<br><br>Filter product based on whether it has variants or not. Possible values are : *true, false*<br><br>**Supported operators :**<br>is<br><br>**Example →**<br>*has_variant\[is\] = "true"*<br>|
|created_at|query|object|false|optional, timestamp(UTC) in seconds filter<br><br>Filter product based on their `created time`<br>.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>after, before, on, between<br><br>**Example →**<br>*created_at\[after\] = "1243545465"*<br>|
|updated_at|query|object|false|optional, timestamp(UTC) in seconds filter<br><br>Filter product based on their `updated time`<br>.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>after, before, on, between<br><br>**Example →**<br>*updated_at\[after\] = "1243545465"*<br>|
|sort_by|query|object|false|optional, string filter<br><br>Sorts based on the specified attribute.<br>**Supported attributes :**<br>name, id, created_at, updated_at<br><br>**Supported sort-orders :**<br>asc, desc<br><br>**Example →**<br>*sort_by\[asc\] = "name"*<br><br>This will sort the result based on the 'name' attribute in ascending(earliest first) order.<br>|

## Create a product variant

<a id="opIdcreate_a_product_variant"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/products/string/variants' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /products/{product-id}/variants`

This API is used for creating a new product variant.
The following table will help you to understand the state of the variant `status` after passing [status](/docs/api/variants/create-a-product-variant#status) value during variant creation.

* **Parameter Value** column holds possible inputs to the `variant.status`.

* **Product Status** column states the status of the associated product.

* **Variant Status** column states the value of the variant status once the variant is created.

|------------------------------|--------------------|--------------------|
| **Parameter Value**          | **Product Status** | **Variant Status** |
| No value passed              | **active**         | **active**         |
| No value passed              | **inactive**       | **inactive**       |
| Value passed as **active**   | **active**         | **active**         |
| Value passed as **inactive** | **active**         | **inactive**       |
| Value passed as **active**   | **inactive**       | **not allowed**    |
| Value passed as **inactive** | **inactive**       | **inactive**       |



> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

<h3 id="create-a-product-variant-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|
|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|product-id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» id|body|string|false|The immutable unique identifier of a product variant. If not passed, it will get autogenerated.<br>|
|» name|body|string|true|This is a unique name that appears for each product variant to the end user.<br>|
|» external_name|body|string|false|The unique name that appears for each product variant to the end user.<br>|
|» description|body|string|false|A detailed description of this product variant.<br>|
|» sku|body|string|false|A unique identifier code a seller assigns to each product variant. Retailers and merchants use SKUs to keep track of inventory and sales data and help organize products within a store or warehouse. SKUs can include a combination of letters, numbers, and symbols and can vary in length depending on the seller's needs.<br>|
|» metadata|body|object|false|A collection of key-value pairs that provides extra information about the product.  <br>**Note:**<br>There's a character limit of 65,535.<br><br>[Learn more](/docs/api/advanced-features#metadata)<br>.<br>|
|» status|body|string|false|Status of the product variant. Refer to the [table](/docs/api/variants/create-a-product-variant)<br>for more information.<br><br>* active - The active product variants are visible on the storefront, subscription, or checkout.<br>* inactive - The inactive product variants are not visible on the storefront, subscription, or checkout.<br>|
|» option_values|body|object|false|List of product variants option values.<br>|
|» » name|body|[string]|true|Name of the option values.<br>|
|» » value|body|[string]|true|Pass values of the `option_values`<br>|

|---|---|
|chargebee-event-actions|all-disabled|
|chargebee-event-email|all-disabled|
|chargebee-event-webhook|all-disabled|

|» status|inactive|

## Deduct promotional credits

<a id="opIddeduct_promotional_credits"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/promotional_credits/deduct' \

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

```

`POST /promotional_credits/deduct`

This API call can be used to deduct promotional credits for a customer. [Learn more about Promotional Credits](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/credit-notes.html#creating-promotional-credits).

For example, if a customer has a credit balance of $20, if you pass the **amount** as $5, then the customer's credit balance would become $15.

If you do not pass any amount as the input parameter then, it will deduct the whole available amount from the credit balance.

```yaml
null
```

<h1 id="chargebee-api-purchases">purchases</h1>

The `purchase` resource represents a collection of [item prices](/docs/api/item_prices) bought together.

## Create a purchase

<a id="opIdcreate_a_purchase"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/purchases' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /purchases`

Creates a `purchase` resource. A purchase can contain one or more of the following:

* subscriptions (a [subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions) resource consists of item prices such that at least one of the item prices belongs to an [item](/docs/api/items) of `type` `plan`.)
* group of one-time charges (aka [charge item prices](/docs/api/item_prices))

When you call this API, the invoices for the subscription(s) and one-time charge(s) are created immediately and not left [unbilled](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items#invoice_immediately)
. The exception is a subscription group whose subscription starts in trial, which is possible when trial support for purchases is enabled for the site. No charges are raised for such a group until the trial ends. When no group in the purchase raises charges, no invoice is created and `purchase.invoice_ids` is empty.  
**Note**

Providing `shipping_addresses[]` is required when the [Orders feature](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/orders.html#configuration_step-1-configure-site-wide-settings) has been enabled.

### Specifying `purchase_item` groups

When creating a purchase, you must specify the *group* or `index` to which each item price belongs. You can do this by setting the `purchase_items[index]` for each item price. Item prices with the same `purchase_items[index]` belong to the same group.
The grouping of item prices allows you to specify the `discounts[]` applicable for each group and indicate which item prices should be added to any subscriptions you want to create. Groups can be one of two types:

* Subscription groups
* One-time charge groups

The following subsections describe the types of groups in detail.  
**Note**

You can specify up to 10 groups,

* with a recommended subscription group of 5. To increase this limit to a maximum of 8, contact eap@chargebee.com.
* with a maximum of 10 one-time charge groups by default.

The total limit for group items for a single purchase is 60.

#### Subscription groups

To create a subscription, specify a *subscription group* . A subscription [group](/docs/api/purchases) is a group of item prices that contains exactly one item price of `type` `plan`. Multi-plan subscriptions are not supported: a group cannot contain more than one plan item price. To create multiple subscriptions, provide multiple subscription groups. Plans in different groups can belong to different [item families](/docs/api/item_families). When item families are enabled, item prices in one group must belong to the same item family as that group's plan.  
**Note**

A subscription group can have up to 20 non-plan item prices. To increase this limit to a maximum of 60, contact eap@chargebee.com.

#### Custom Fields

Purchase API supports custom fields of Subscriptions, use the following format to specify custom fields in Purchase API: **`subscription_info[custom_field]`**.

#### One-time charge groups

A one-time charge [group](/docs/api/purchases) is a group of charge item prices (i.e. item prices belonging to items of `type` `charge`). Charge item prices can be added to subscription groups as well. The charges within and across each one-time group must be unique.  
**Note**

* A one-time charge group can have up to 20 item prices. To increase this limit to a maximum of 60, contact eap@chargebee.com.
* A charge item price can only be added to a single one-time charge group. However, it can be part of multiple [subscription groups](/docs/api/purchases).

### Applying discounts

Discounts, both [manual discounts](/docs/api/discounts) and [coupons](/docs/api/coupons), can be applied to groups by specifying the `discounts[]` array. You cannot target one item price in a group. A manual discount applies to the invoice for the group. A coupon with [apply_on](/docs/api/coupons/coupon-object#apply_on) set to `invoice_amount` applies to the invoice `sub_total`. A coupon configured for specific item prices applies only to those item prices.

The following table describes the method of application based on whether `discounts[index][i]` is provided:  

|                      |                                                                                                                                                                   **`discounts[index][i]` is provided**                                                                                                                                                                    |                                                                                                                                                                                                                 **`discounts[index][i]` is not provided**                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Coupons**          | * The coupon is applied exclusively to the invoice for group `i`. * The coupon is applied exclusively to the invoice created immediately upon invoking this API. * If group `i` is a [subscription group](/docs/api/purchases), then the coupon is applied to invoices for subscription renewals based on coupon attributes such as `duration_type` and `max_redemptions`. | * The coupon must have [apply_on](/docs/api/coupons/coupon-object#apply_on) set to `invoice_amount`. A coupon configured for specific item prices is rejected unless you pass `discounts[index][i]`. * The coupon is applied to the first invoice only, irrespective of [coupon.duration_type](/docs/api/coupons/coupon-object#duration_type) or [coupon.max_redemptions](/docs/api/coupons/coupon-object#max_redemptions). * The coupon is not applied to later invoices. |
| **Manual discounts** | * The manual discount is applied exclusively to the invoice for group `i`. * The manual discount is applied exclusively to the invoice created immediately upon invoking this API. * The manual discount is not applied to subsequent invoices, such as those generated upon subscription renewal.                                                                         | * The manual discount is applied only to the first invoice for the purchase. * The manual discount is not applied to later invoices.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

**Note**

For a subscription group whose subscription is in trial, no invoice is created for the group when this API is invoked. A discount with `discounts[index][i]` set to that group is kept on the subscription and applied when the subscription is first invoiced. A discount without `discounts[index][i]` applies only to the first invoice, so it cannot be passed when the purchase creates no invoice.

### Limitations

Item prices in a subscription group are validated the same way as in [Create a subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items). This operation also has the following limitations.

#### Item prices

* A subscription group contains exactly one item price of `type` `plan`. You cannot create one subscription with more than one plan item price. Multi-plan subscriptions are not supported.
* Plans in different subscription groups can belong to different [item families](/docs/api/item_families). When item families are enabled, item prices in one group must belong to the same item family as that group's plan.
* You cannot set a service period for a charge. This operation has no equivalent of [subscription_items[service_period_days]](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items#subscription_items_service_period_days).

#### Subscriptions

* You cannot set [free_period](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items#free_period).
* You cannot set [start_date](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items#start_date). Each subscription starts immediately. A group can start in trial only when trial support for purchases is enabled and you set `subscription_info[trial_end]`.
* [Calendar billing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/calendar-billing.html#alignment-of-billing-date) settings for the site apply. You cannot override them with [billing_alignment_mode](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items#billing_alignment_mode).
* Each subscription uses the customer's [auto_collection](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#auto_collection). You cannot override it for the subscription.
* Only the current term is charged. You cannot set [terms_to_charge](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items#terms_to_charge).
* You cannot create [ramps](/docs/api/ramps) or schedule a subscription change in this request. After the subscriptions are created, use [Create a subscription ramp](/docs/api/ramps/create-a-ramp) or [Update a subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items).
* The `purchase` resource cannot be changed after it is created. Update each subscription with the subscription operations.

#### Multiple business entities

This operation does not accept [business_entity_id](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items#business_entity_id). Calling it on a site where [multiple business entities](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/mbe.html) are enabled returns an error.

#### Invoices

* When the purchase raises invoiceable charges and [consolidated invoicing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html) is enabled for the customer, Chargebee consolidates those charges. Subscription differences can still produce more than one invoice. When consolidated invoicing is disabled, each subscription gets its own invoice. A trial-only purchase, where every subscription group starts in trial and no one-time charges are raised, creates no invoice and `purchase.invoice_ids` is empty.
* Invoices for subscriptions and one-time charges are created immediately and are not left [unbilled](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items#invoice_immediately). A subscription group that starts in trial is the exception: no charges are raised for that group until the trial ends.
* This operation does not accept a net-term parameter. Net terms already set on the customer still apply. When those terms are greater than zero, the invoice is posted and payment collection waits until the due date. When the terms are zero and the customer's [auto_collection](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#auto_collection) is `on`, Chargebee attempts to collect payment while closing the invoice. The operation fails if the customer has no valid payment method, or if collection fails. When `auto_collection` is `off`, the invoice is closed with payment due.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

## Estimates for purchase

<a id="opIdestimates_for_purchase"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/purchases/estimate' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /purchases/estimate`

Returns an estimate for creating a `purchase` resource. The operation works exactly like [Create a purchase](/docs/api/purchases/create-a-purchase), except that only an [estimate](/docs/api/estimates) resource is returned without an actual `purchase` resource being created. The limitations of that operation apply here as well, including the error returned when [multiple business entities](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/mbe.html) are enabled for the site.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

|» subscription_info|body|object|false|Parameters for subscription_info<br>|
|» » index|body|[integer(int32)]|true|The index or identifier of the [group](/docs/api/purchases)<br>to which this subscription information belongs. This must be a value from the `purchase_items[index]`<br>array and the group must be a [subscription group](/docs/api/purchases)<br>.<br>|
|» » subscription_id|body|[string]|false|When specifying a [subscription group](/docs/api/purchases)<br>, this is the unique identifier of the [subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions)<br>to be created. This value must be unique for each subscription group.<br>|
|» » billing_cycles|body|[integer(int32)]|false|The number of billing cycles the subscription runs before canceling. If not provided, then the billing cycles [set for the plan-item price](/docs/api/item_prices/item_price-object#billing_cycles)<br>is used.<br>|
|» » contract_term_billing_cycle_on_renewal|body|[integer(int32)]|false|Number of billing cycles the new contract term should run for, on contract renewal. The default value is the same as `billing_cycles`<br>or a custom value depending on the [site configuration](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/contract-terms.html#configuring-contract-terms)<br>.<br>|
|» » trial_end|body|[integer(unix-time)]|false|End of the trial period for the subscription estimated for the [subscription group](/docs/api/purchases). This overrides the trial period set for the plan-item price. The value must be in the future, or set it to `0` to have no trial period.  <br>**Prerequisites**<br><br>* Trial support for purchases must be enabled for the site. Contact [Chargebee Support](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/kb/getting-started/how-to-contact-chargebees-support-team?utm_source=docs_api&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=support) to enable it.  <br>**Note**<br><br>* Charges for the group are not included in the invoice estimate while its subscription is in trial, so a charge-item price cannot be added to the group.<br>* When no group in the purchase raises charges, the invoice estimate is empty and discounts without `discounts[index]` cannot be passed.<br>|
|» » start_date|body|[integer(unix-time)]|false|none|
|» contract_terms|body|object|false|Parameters for contract_terms<br>|
|» » index|body|[integer(int32)]|true|The index number of the subscription/one-time group to which the item price is added. Provide a unique number between `0`<br>and `9`<br>(inclusive) for each group that is to be created. To increase this limit, contact Chargebee Support<br>|
|» » action_at_term_end|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » cancellation_cutoff_period|body|[integer(int32)]|false|The number of days before [`contract_end`](/docs/api/contract_terms/contract_term-object#contract_end)<br>, during which the customer is barred from canceling the contract term. The customer is allowed to cancel the contract term via the Self-Serve Portal only before this period. This allows you to have sufficient time for processing the contract term closure.<br>|

<h1 id="chargebee-api-quotes">quotes</h1>

A quote is an estimate of the invoice with the charges likely to occur when customers buy an item.

## Edit a quote for subscription update

<a id="opIdedit_update_subscription_quote_for_items"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/quotes/string/edit_update_subscription_quote_for_items' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /quotes/{quote-id}/edit_update_subscription_quote_for_items`

Edits a quote for updating a subscription.  

### Impacts

**#### Quote and related resources**  
If the quote is for a scheduled change, then the following resources are updated:

* When [Ramps](ramps) are disabled, the `quote` and the [`quoted_subscription`](quoted_subscriptions) are updated.
* When [Ramps](ramps) are enabled with compatibility mode, the `quote`, the [`quoted_ramp`](quoted_ramps), and the [`quoted_subscription`](quoted_subscriptions) are updated.

For more details, see [Ramps API compatibility mode](subscriptions#ramps-compat-mode).


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

<h3 id="edit-a-quote-for-subscription-update-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|
|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|quote-id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» notes|body|string|false|Notes specific to this quote that you want customers to see on the quote PDF.<br>|
|» expires_at|body|integer(unix-time)|false|Quotes will be valid till this date. After this quote will be marked as closed.<br>|
|» mandatory_items_to_remove|body|[string]|false|Item ids of [mandatorily attached addons](/docs/api/attached_items)<br>that are to be removed from the subscription.<br>|
|» replace_items_list|body|boolean|false|If `true`<br>then the existing `subscription_items`<br>list for the subscription is replaced by the one provided. If `false`<br>then the provided `subscription_items`<br>list gets added to the existing list.<br>|
|» billing_cycles|body|integer(int32)|false|Billing cycles set for plan-item price is used by default.<br>|
|» terms_to_charge|body|integer(int32)|false|The number of subscription billing cycles to [invoice in advance](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/advance-invoices.html).<br>If a new term is started for the subscription due to this API call, then `terms_to_charge`<br>is inclusive of this new term. See description for the `force_term_reset`<br>parameter to learn more about when a subscription term is reset.<br>|
|» reactivate_from|body|integer(unix-time)|false|If the subscription `status`<br>is `cancelled`<br>and it is being reactivated via this operation, this is the date/time at which the subscription should be reactivated.<br>**Note:**<br>It is recommended not to pass this parameter along with `changed_scheduled_at`.<br>`reactivate_from`<br>can be backdated (set to a value in the past). Use backdating when the subscription has been reactivated already but its billing has been delayed. Backdating is allowed only when the following prerequisites are met:<br><br>* Backdating must be enabled for subscription reactivation operations.<br>* The current day of the month does not exceed the limit set in Chargebee for backdating subscription change. This limit is the day of the month by which the accounting for the previous month must be closed.<br>* The date is on or after the last date/time any of the product catalog items of the subscription were changed.<br>* The date is not more than duration X into the past where X is the billing period of the plan. For example, if the period of the plan in the subscription is 2 months and today is 14th April, `changes_scheduled_at` cannot be earlier than 14th February. .<br>|
|» billing_alignment_mode|body|string|false|Override the [billing alignment mode](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/calendar-billing.html#alignment-of-billing-date)<br>chosen for the site for calendar billing. Only applicable when using calendar billing.<br><br>* immediate - Subscription period will be aligned with the configured billing date immediately, with credits or charges raised accordingly..<br>* delayed - Subscription period will be aligned with the configured billing date at the next renewal.<br>|
|» coupon_ids|body|[string]|false|The list of [IDs](/docs/api/coupons/coupon-object#id) of the coupons to be applied. [Coupon codes](/docs/api/coupon_codes) are also supported.  <br>**Note**<br><br>Not applicable when Chargebee CPQ is enabled. Use `coupons[]` array instead.<br>|
|» replace_coupon_list|body|boolean|false|Should be true if the existing coupons should be replaced with the ones that are being passed.<br>|
|» change_option|body|string|false|When the quote is converted, this attribute determines the date/time as of when the subscription change is to be carried out.<br><br>* specific_date -<br>  The change is carried out as of the date specified under `changes_scheduled_at`<br>  .<br>* immediately - The change is carried out immediately.<br>|
|» changes_scheduled_at|body|integer(unix-time)|false|When `change_option` is set to `specific_date`, then set the date-time at which the subscription change is to happen or has happened.  <br>**Constraints**<br><br>* Do not pass this parameter along with `reactivate_from`.<br>* The `changes_scheduled_at` parameter does not apply to `auto_collection`, `shipping_address`, and `po_number`; these parameters take effect **immediately** when scheduling a subscription update.  <br>**Backdated changes**<br><br>`changes_scheduled_at`can be set to a value in the past. This is called backdating the subscription change and is performed when the subscription change has already been provisioned but its billing has been delayed. Backdating is allowed only when the following prerequisites are met:<br><br>* Backdating must be [enabled](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/backdating#configuring-backdated-subscription-actions-and-invoicing) for subscription change operations.<br>* Only the following changes can be backdated:<br>  * Changes in the recurring items or their prices.<br>  * Addition of non-recurring items.<br>* Subscription `status` is `active`, `cancelled`, or `non_renewing`.<br>* The current day of the month does not exceed the limit set in Chargebee for backdating subscription change. This limit is typically the day of the month by which the accounting for the previous month must be closed.<br>* The date is on or after `current_term_start`.<br>* The date is on or after the last date/time any of the following changes were made:<br>  * Changes in the recurring items or their prices.<br>* Addition of non-recurring items.  <br>**Renewing a fixed-term subscription through Chargebee CPQ**<br><br>For Chargebee CPQ, set `change_option` to `specific_date` and set `changes_scheduled_at` to the current subscription's end timestamp (UTC, in seconds). That timestamp is the start of the new term. When the subscription has an active contract term, use the contract end. The API accepts only that exact value. Also set `subscription_items[start_date]` to the same timestamp and `subscription_items[end_date]` to the end of the new term. The subscription must have remaining billing cycles, and its `status` must be `active`, `non_renewing`, or `paused`.<br>|
|» force_term_reset|body|boolean|false|Applicable for 'Active' \& 'Non Renewing' states alone. Generally, subscription's term will be reset (i.e current term is ended and a new term starts immediately) when a new plan having different billing frequency is specified in the input. For all the other cases, the subscription's term will remain intact. Now for this later scenario, if you want to force a term reset you can specify this param as 'true'.<br>**Note**:<br>Specifying this value as 'false' has no impact on the default behaviour.<br>|
|» reactivate|body|boolean|false|Applicable only for cancelled subscriptions. Once this is passed as true, cancelled subscription will become active; otherwise subscription changes will be made but the subscription state will remain cancelled. If not passed, subscription will be activated only if there is any change in subscription data.<br>|

|» » start_date|body|[integer(unix-time)]|false|Specifies the start date for the coupon. The period of the coupon, as specified by the `start_date` and `end_date` determines the [ramp(s)](/docs/api/quoted_ramps) it will be part of.  <br>**Note**<br><br>The parameter applies only when Chargebee CPQ is enabled. To request access, contact [Chargebee Support](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/kb/getting-started/how-to-contact-chargebees-support-team?utm_source=docs_api&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=support).<br>|
|» » end_date|body|[integer(unix-time)]|false|Specifies the end date for the coupon. The period of the coupon, as specified by the `start_date` and `end_date` determines the [ramp(s)](/docs/api/quoted_ramps) it will be part of.  <br>**Note**<br><br>The parameter applies only when Chargebee CPQ is enabled. To request access, contact [Chargebee Support](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/kb/getting-started/how-to-contact-chargebees-support-team?utm_source=docs_api&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=support).<br>|
|» entitlement_overrides|body|object|false|The set of entitlement overrides to apply on this quote. Each entry targets a feature for an entity on the quote. Overrides are always upserted.<br>|
|» » feature_id|body|[string]|false|The `id` of the `feature` for which the entitlement override is being set.<br>|
|» » entity_id|body|[string]|false|The `id` of the entity on the quote (for example, a `plan_price`, `addon_price`, or `charge_price` handle from the quote context) whose entitlement is being overridden.<br>|
|» » entity_type|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » value|body|[string]|false|The level of entitlement that the item has towards the feature. The possible values depend on the value of `feature.type`<br>:<br><br>* When `feature.type` is `custom`: The value can be any one of `levels[].value`.<br><br>* When `feature.type` is `switch`: This value is `true` when the feature is available; it is `false` when the feature is unavailable.<br><br>* When `feature.type` is `quantity`:<br><br>* When `levels[].is_unlimited` is not `true`: The value can be any one of `levels[].value`.<br><br>* When `levels[].is_unlimited` is `true`: The value can also be any one of `levels[].value` or it can be `unlimited` (case-insensitive), indicating unlimited entitlement.<br><br>* When `feature.type` is `range`:<br><br>* When `levels[].is_unlimited` is not `true`: The value can be any whole number between `levels[0].value` and `levels[1].value` (inclusive).<br><br>* When `levels[].is_unlimited` is `true`: The value can be any whole number equal to or greater than `levels[0].value` or it can be `unlimited` (case-insensitive), indicating unlimited entitlement.<br><br>|
|» » is_enabled|body|[boolean]|false|Specifies whether the entitlement for the feature is enabled (`true`) or disabled (`false`) for the entity on the quote.<br>|
|» » start_date|body|[integer(unix-time)]|false|Start date (UTC timestamp) of the entitlement override for the item on the quote. Used with `end_date` for ramp-scoped entitlements.<br>|
|» » end_date|body|[integer(unix-time)]|false|End date (UTC timestamp) of the entitlement override for the item on the quote. Used with `start_date` for ramp-scoped entitlements.<br>|

|date|query|object|false|optional, timestamp(UTC) in seconds filter<br><br>Creation date of the quote. Typically this is the date on which quote is generated.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>after, before, on, between<br><br>**Example →**<br>*date\[on\] = "1435054328"*<br>|

## Convert a quote

<a id="opIdconvert_a_quote"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/quotes/string/convert' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /quotes/{quote-id}/convert`

This API is to convert a quote to an invoice.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

<h3 id="convert-a-quote-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|
|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|quote-id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» invoice_date|body|integer(unix-time)|false|The document date displayed on the invoice PDF. Provide this value to backdate the invoice. Backdating an invoice is done for reasons such as booking revenue for a previous date or when the subscription is effective as of a past date. When not provided, the value is the same as current date. Moreover, if the invoice is created as `pending`<br>, and if the site is configured to set invoice dates to date of closing, then upon invoice closure, this date is changed to the invoice closing date. `taxes`<br>and `line_item_taxes`<br>are computed based on the tax configuration as of `invoice_date`.<br>When passing this parameter, the following prerequisites must be met:<br><br>* `invoice_date` must be in the past.<br>* `invoice_date` is not more than one calendar month into the past. For example, if today is 13th January, then you cannot pass a value that is earlier than 13th December.<br>* The date is not earlier than `quoted_subscription.start_date` or `quoted_subscription.changes_scheduled_at` (whichever is applicable).<br>* `invoice_immediately` must be `true`. .<br>|
|» invoice_immediately|body|boolean|false|If there are charges raised immediately for the subscription, this parameter specifies whether those charges are to be invoiced immediately or added to [unbilled charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/unbilled-charges.html).<br>The default value is as per the [site settings](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/unbilled-charges.html#configuration)<br>.  <br>**Note:**<br>`invoice_immediately`<br>only affects charges that are raised at the time of execution of this API call. Any charges scheduled to be raised in the future are not affected by this parameter.<br><br>.<br>|
|» create_pending_invoices|body|boolean|false|This attribute is set to `true`<br>automatically for the subscription when it has one or more `metered`<br>items. However, when there are no `metered`<br>items, you can pass this parameter as `true`<br>to force all invoices (except the first) to be created as `pending`.<br>This is useful in the following scenarios:<br><br>* When you manage metered billing at your end by calculating usage-based charges yourself and add them to the subscription as [one-time charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/charges.html).<br>* When your workflow involves inspecting all charges before you close invoices.<br><br>**Note:**<br><br>* You must enable [Metered Billing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing) for this parameter to be acceptable.<br>* To create the first invoice also as `pending`, pass `first_invoice_pending` as `true`.<br><br>.<br>|
|» first_invoice_pending|body|boolean|false|Non-metered items are billed at the beginning of a billing cycle while metered items are billed at the end. Consequently, the first invoice of the subscription contains only the non-metered items.<br><br>By passing this parameter as `true`, you create the first invoice as `pending` allowing you to add the previous term's metered charges to it before closing. This is useful when the subscription is moved to Chargebee from a different billing system. As applicable to all `pending` invoices, this invoice is also [closed automatically](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing#configuring-metered-billing) or via an [API call](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice).  <br>**Note:**<br><br>This parameter is passed only when there are metered items in the subscription or when `create_pending_invoices` is `true`.<br><br>.<br>|
|» subscription|body|object|false|Parameters for subscription<br>|
|» » id|body|string|false|Applicable only for create subscription quote.<br>|
|» » auto_collection|body|string|false|Applicable only for create subscription quote.<br><br>* off - Automatic collection of charges will not be made for this subscription. Use this for offline payments.<br>* on - Whenever an invoice is created for this subscription, an automatic charge will be attempted on the payment method available.<br>|
|» » po_number|body|string|false|Purchase order number for this subscription.<br>|
|» » auto_close_invoices|body|boolean|false|When [auto-closing of invoices](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing#configuring-metered-billing)<br>is enabled for the site, you can pass this parameter as `false`<br>to prevent the automatic closing of invoices for this subscription. The value passed here takes precedence over the value stored at the [customer level](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#auto_close_invoices)<br>.<br>|

|chargebee-event-email|all-disabled|
|chargebee-event-webhook|all-disabled|

|» » auto_collection|off|

|quoted_subscription|[QuotedSubscription](#schemaquotedsubscription)|false|none|Resource object representing quoted_subscription<br>|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
BasicAuth
</aside>

## Edit a quote for subscription creation

<a id="opIdedit_create_subscription_quote_for_items"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/quotes/string/edit_create_subscription_quote_for_items' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /quotes/{quote-id}/edit_create_subscription_quote_for_items`

Changes the quote produced for creating a new subscription items


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

## Create a quote for subscription update

<a id="opIdcreate_a_quote_for_update_subscription_items"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/quotes/update_subscription_quote_for_items' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /quotes/update_subscription_quote_for_items`

Creates a quote for updating a subscription. Use this endpoint for amendments, and for renewals when Chargebee CPQ is enabled.

* **Amendment:** Changes the subscription within its current term, for example adding items or changing quantities or prices.
* **Renewal:** With Chargebee CPQ, continues a fixed-term subscription into its next term. Set the dates for the new term using `change_option`, `changes_scheduled_at`, and each item's `start_date` and `end_date`. See the renewal note under `changes_scheduled_at`, and `start_date` and `end_date` under `subscription_items`.  

### Impacts

**#### Quote and related resources**  
If the quote is for a scheduled change, then the following resources are created:

* When [Ramps](/docs/api/ramps) are disabled, a `quote` and a [`quoted_subscription`](/docs/api/quoted_subscriptions) are created.
* When [Ramps](/docs/api/ramps) are enabled with compatibility mode, a `quote`, a [`quoted_ramp`](/docs/api/quoted_ramps), and a [`quoted_subscription`](/docs/api/quoted_subscriptions) are created.

For more details, see [Ramps API compatibility mode](/docs/api/subscriptions#ramps-compat-mode).


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

|» reactivate_from|body|integer(unix-time)|false|If the subscription `status`<br>is `cancelled`<br>and it is being reactivated via this operation, this is the date/time at which the subscription should be reactivated.<br>**Note:**<br>It is recommended not to pass this parameter along with `changed_scheduled_at`.<br>`reactivate_from`<br>can be backdated (set to a value in the past). Use backdating when the subscription has been reactivated already but its billing has been delayed. Backdating is allowed only when the following prerequisites are met:<br><br>* Backdating must be enabled for subscription reactivation operations.<br>* The current day of the month does not exceed the limit set in Chargebee for backdating subscription change. This limit is the day of the month by which the accounting for the previous month must be closed.<br>* The date is on or after the last date/time any of the product catalog items of the subscription were changed.<br>* The date is not more than duration X into the past where X is the billing period of the plan. For example, if the period of the plan in the subscription is 2 months and today is 14th April, `changes_scheduled_at` cannot be earlier than 14th February. .<br>|
|» billing_alignment_mode|body|string|false|Override the [billing alignment mode](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/calendar-billing.html#alignment-of-billing-date)<br>chosen for the site for calendar billing. This is called backdating the subscription change and is performed when the subscription change has already been provisioned but its billing has been delayed. Backdating is allowed only when the following prerequisites are met:<br><br>* Backdating must be [enabled](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/backdating#configuring-backdated-subscription-actions-and-invoicing) for subscription change operations.<br>* Only the following changes can be backdated:<br>  * Changes in the recurring items or their prices.<br>  * Addition of non-recurring items.<br>* Subscription `status` is `active`, `cancelled`, or `non_renewing`.<br>* The current day of the month does not exceed the limit set in Chargebee for backdating subscription change. This limit is typically the day of the month by which the accounting for the previous month must be closed.<br>* The date is on or after `current_term_start`.<br>* The date is on or after the last date/time any of the following changes were made:<br>  * Changes in the recurring items or their prices.<br>* Addition of non-recurring items.  <br>**Renewing a fixed-term subscription through Chargebee CPQ**<br><br>For Chargebee CPQ, set `change_option` to `specific_date` and set `changes_scheduled_at` to the current subscription's end timestamp (UTC, in seconds). Also set `subscription_items[start_date]` to the same timestamp and `subscription_items[end_date]` to the end of the new term. The subscription must have remaining billing cycles, and its `status` must be `active`, `non_renewing`, or `paused`.<br>|

## List quote line groups

<a id="opIdlist_quote_line_groups"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/quotes/string/quote_line_groups' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /quotes/{quote-id}/quote_line_groups`

This API retrieves all the quote line groups and lineitems for a quote.


<h3 id="list-quote-line-groups-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|quote-id|path|string|true|none|
|limit|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of resources to be returned.<br>|
|offset|query|string|false|Determines your position in the list for pagination. To ensure that the next page is retrieved correctly, always set `offset`<br>to the value of `next_offset`<br>obtained in the previous iteration of the API call.<br>|

## Retrieve a quote as PDF

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/quotes/string/pdf' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /quotes/{quote-id}/pdf`

Retrieves the quote as a PDF. The returned URL is secure, allows download and expires in 60 minutes.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

## List Quote Entitlements

<a id="opIdlist_quote_entitlements"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/quotes/string/quote_entitlements' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /quotes/{quote-id}/quote_entitlements`

Retrieves the list of `quote_entitlements` for the [quote](/docs/api/quotes).


<h3 id="list-quote-entitlements-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|quote-id|path|string|true|none|
|limit|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of resources to be returned.<br>|
|offset|query|string|false|Determines your position in the list for pagination. To ensure that the next page is retrieved correctly, always set `offset`<br>to the value of `next_offset`<br>obtained in the previous iteration of the API call.<br>|
|entity_id|query|object|false|Filter quote entitlements by `entity_id`.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>is<br><br>**Example →**<br>*entity_id\[is\] = "price-usd"*<br>|
|start_date|query|object|false|Filter entitlements by ramp start date (unix timestamp). Use with `end_date[on]`.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>on<br><br>**Example →**<br>*start_date\[on\] = "1780252200"*<br>|
|end_date|query|object|false|Filter entitlements by ramp end date (unix timestamp). Use with `start_date[on]`.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>on<br><br>**Example →**<br>*end_date\[on\] = "1782844200"*<br>|

<h1 id="chargebee-api-ramps">ramps</h1>

A `ramp` resource, or subscription ramp, represents a planned change to a [`subscription`](/docs/api/subscriptions) that occurs at a future date.

<a id="opIdretrieve_a_ramp"></a>

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/ramps/string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

Retrieves a specific subscription ramp.

|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|ramp-id|path|string|true|none|

## List subscription ramps

<a id="opIdlist_ramps"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/ramps?subscription_id=8gsnbYfsMLds' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /ramps`

Lists the subscription ramps that match the criteria provided in the filter parameters.  
**Note**
By default, the ramps are returned [sorted](/docs/api/ramps/list-ramps) in descending order (latest first) by [updated_at](/docs/api/ramps/ramp-object#updated_at).


<h3 id="list-subscription-ramps-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|limit|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of resources to be returned.<br>|
|offset|query|string|false|Determines your position in the list for pagination. To ensure that the next page is retrieved correctly, always set `offset`<br>to the value of `next_offset`<br>obtained in the previous iteration of the API call.<br>|
|include_deleted|query|boolean|false|Specifies whether to include deleted resources in the response. Deleted resources are those with the [deleted](/docs/api/ramps/ramp-object#deleted) attribute set to `true`.  <br>**Caution**<br>`status` or `effective_from` filters must not be passed when `include_deleted` is set to `true`.<br><br>.<br>|
|status|query|object|false|optional, enumerated string filter<br><br>Filter subscription ramps based on `status`<br>.  <br>**Caution**<br><br>* The `subscription_id` filter must be passed when filtering by `status`.<br>* `status` filter should not be passed when `include_deleted` is set to `true`.<br><br>Possible values are : scheduled, succeeded, failed.<br><br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, in<br><br>**Example →**<br>*status\[is\] = "SCHEDULED"*<br>|
|subscription_id|query|object|true|optional, string filter<br><br>Filter subscription ramps based on `subscription_id`<br>.  <br>**Caution**<br>This filter is mandatory when filtering by `status` or `effective_from`.<br><br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, in<br><br>**Example →**<br>*subscription_id\[is\] = "8gsnbYfsMLds"*<br>|
|effective_from|query|object|false|optional, timestamp(UTC) in seconds filter<br><br>Filter subscription ramps based on `effective_from`.  <br>**Caution**<br><br>* The `subscription_id` filter must be passed when filtering by `effective_from`.<br>* `effective_from` filter should not be passed when `include_deleted` is set to `true`.<br><br>**Supported operators :**<br>after, before, on, between<br><br>**Example →**<br>*effective_from\[after\] = "1435054328"*<br>|
|updated_at|query|object|false|optional, timestamp(UTC) in seconds filter<br><br>Filter subscription ramps based on `updated_at`<br>.  <br>**Tip**<br>Specify `sort_by` = `updated_at` (whether `asc` oor `desc`) for a faster response when using this filter.<br><br>**Supported operators :**<br>after, before, on, between<br><br>**Example →**<br>*updated_at\[after\] = "1435052328"*<br>|
|sort_by|query|object|false|optional, string filter<br><br>Sorts based on the specified attribute.<br>**Supported attributes :**<br>effective_from, created_at, updated_at<br><br>**Supported sort-orders :**<br>asc, desc<br><br>**Example →**<br>*sort_by\[asc\] = "effective_from"*<br><br>This will sort the result based on the 'effective_from' attribute in ascending(earliest first) order.<br>|

## Update a subscription ramp

<a id="opIdupdate_a_subscription_ramp"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/ramps/string/update' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /ramps/{ramp-id}/update`

Updates an existing subscription ramp by replacing its current attribute values with the new parameters provided. When using this API to modify a ramp, make sure to include all the ramp's attributes as you would do during creation of the ramp with the necessary values updated.
**Example: step-by-step flow**
The following steps explains how to update effective_from value of an existing ramp.

**Step 1: Retrieve current ramp values**

1. Send a request to retrieve the current values of all parameters for the subscription ramp using [Retrieve a subscription ramp](/docs/api/ramps/retrieve-a-ramp) API.
2. Review the response to get the current values of the ramp's attributes. Note down all the parameters and their values.

**Step 2: Update ramp with new values**

1. Prepare the request to update the ramp.
   * Update the effective_from value in the noted down attributes of ramp from the previous step.
   * Ensure all parameters, even those not being changed, are included in the request.
2. Send the prepared request to [Update subscription ramp](/docs/api/ramps/update-a-subscription-ramp) API.
   * Verify the response object to ensure a successful subscription ramp update. If it returns an error, repeat step 1 again.

**Note**

* **Ramp status** : You cannot update a ramp in `succeeded` or `failed` [status](/docs/api/ramps/ramp-object#status).
* **Advance invoice** : You cannot update ramps for subscriptions that have an [advance invoice schedule](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules).


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

## Delete a subscription ramp

<a id="opIddelete_a_ramp"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/ramps/string/delete' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /ramps/{ramp-id}/delete`

Deletes the specified subscription ramp. However, Chargebee only allows deleting a ramp if it does not conflict with future ramps on the subscription. The following checks are performed to ensure compatibility:  

|               Condition                |                                                           Restriction                                                           |
|----------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| The ramp contains `items_to_add[]`     | The ramp cannot be deleted if any of the items in `items_to_add[]` are scheduled to be updated or removed in a subsequent ramp. |
| The ramp contains `coupons_to_add[]`   | The ramp cannot be deleted if any of the coupons in `coupons_to_add[]` are scheduled to be removed in a subsequent ramp.        |
| The ramp contains `discounts_to_add[]` | The ramp cannot be deleted if any of the discounts in `discounts_to_add[]` are scheduled to be removed in a subsequent ramp.    |



<h3 id="delete-a-subscription-ramp-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|
|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|ramp-id|path|string|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|chargebee-event-actions|all-disabled|
|chargebee-event-email|all-disabled|
|chargebee-event-webhook|all-disabled|

## Retrieve a recorded purchase

<a id="opIdretrieve_a_recorded_purchase"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/recorded_purchases/string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /recorded_purchases/{recorded-purchase-id}`

Retrieves a `recorded_purchase` object using the `recorded_purchase.id` returned by the [Record a Purchase API](/docs/api/recorded_purchases/record-a-purchase).

Use this to poll job `status` and, when `completed`, obtain `omnichannel_transaction_id` plus either `linked_omnichannel_subscriptions` (subscription) or `linked_omnichannel_one_time_orders` (one-time order).


<h3 id="retrieve-a-recorded-purchase-parameters">Parameters</h3>

## Record a purchase

<a id="opIdrecord_a_purchase"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/recorded_purchases' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /recorded_purchases`

Records an in-app purchase from Apple App Store or Google Play Store in Chargebee. The API starts an asynchronous verification job and returns a `recorded_purchase` resource. Track progress with `status`: `in_process`, `completed`, `failed`, or `ignored`.

Handle the **synchronous** API response first. The request can fail immediately (for example, an incorrect `app_id`, a malformed URL or request body, or a customer conflict on an already-recorded purchase) before any job is created---treat these as standard API errors (`4xx`). Only after the call is accepted and returns a `recorded_purchase` should you track the **asynchronous** job via `status` (`in_process` → `completed`, `failed`, or `ignored`). Omnichannel subscription or one-time order creation still happens asynchronously after a successful sync acceptance.

### Prerequisites

* Configure the omnichannel app (`app_id`) for Apple or Google in Chargebee.
* Provide exactly one store payload: `apple_app_store[...]` **or** `google_play_store[...]`.
* Associate the purchase with a Chargebee `customer[id]` (created automatically if missing when customer details are supplied).

### Synchronous customer conflicts (existing purchase)

If the store purchase is already recorded in Chargebee under a **different** customer, Record a Purchase returns a synchronous `4xx` (`customer_id_conflict_use_move_api` / `customer_id_mismatch`) and does **not** create a `recorded_purchase` job. To reassign ownership, use [Move an omnichannel subscription](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscriptions/move-an-omnichannel-subscription). Re-recording the same purchase for the **same** customer typically completes asynchronously with `status` `ignored` when the subscription or one-time order already exists.

### Apple App Store input (mutually exclusive paths)

* Prefer `apple_app_store[transaction_id]` for subscriptions and one-time products when you have the StoreKit transaction ID.
* Or pass `apple_app_store[receipt]` **and** `apple_app_store[product_id]`.

### Google Play Store input (mutually exclusive paths)

* Prefer `google_play_store[order_id]` for subscriptions and one-time orders.
* Or pass `google_play_store[purchase_token]` for subscriptions; for one-time orders also pass `google_play_store[product_id]`.

### Impacts (when `status` becomes `completed`)

* **Subscription purchase** : Creates/links `linked_omnichannel_subscriptions`, sets `omnichannel_transaction_id`, and emits [`omnichannel_subscription_created`](/docs/api/events/webhook/omnichannel_subscription_created) (or [`omnichannel_subscription_imported`](/docs/api/events/webhook/omnichannel_subscription_imported) when historical transactions are present). Chargebee may also emit [`omnichannel_transaction_created`](/docs/api/events/webhook/omnichannel_transaction_created).
* **One-time order purchase** : Creates/links `linked_omnichannel_one_time_orders`, sets `omnichannel_transaction_id`, and emits [`omnichannel_one_time_order_created`](/docs/api/events/webhook/omnichannel_one_time_order_created).

### Impacts (when `status` is `failed`)

* Review [`error_detail`](/docs/api/recorded_purchases/recorded_purchase-object#error_detail) and correct the payload. Chargebee emits [`record_purchase_failed`](/docs/api/events/webhook/record_purchase_failed).

### Impacts (when `status` is `ignored`)

* The purchase already has an omnichannel subscription or one-time order in Chargebee. No new linked resource is created for this job---use the existing resource. Linked IDs and `omnichannel_transaction_id` appear when `status` is `completed`, not for `ignored`.

See [omnichannel events](/docs/api/omnichannel_events) for the full recording and notification mapping tables.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|

|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» app_id|body|string|true|App Identifier in Chargebee. This is the handle created by Chargebee for your app. To get the `app_id`:<br><br>* For **Apple** , follow [these steps](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/mobile-subscriptions/omnichannel-app-store#create-an-omnichannel-subscription-for-in-app-purchases).<br>* For **Google** , follow [these steps](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/mobile-subscriptions/omnichannel-play-store#connect-google-app-to-chargebee-to-generate-unique-app-id-and-notifications-url).<br>|
|» customer|body|object|false|Customer parameters for associating (or creating) the Chargebee customer for this purchase.<br>|
|» » id|body|string|true|The `id` of the [customer](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#id)<br>object associated with this purchase. The customer is created if one does not already exist.<br>|
|» » email|body|string(email)|false|Email of the customer. Used only when the customer is being created.<br>|
|» » first_name|body|string|false|First name of the customer. Used only when the customer is being created.<br>|
|» » last_name|body|string|false|Last name of the customer. Used only when the customer is being created.<br>|
|» apple_app_store|body|object|false|Apple App Store--specific payload used to record the purchase. Provide parameters as `apple_app_store[...]`.<br><br>**Google Play Store**: Not applicable. Do not send this object for Google purchases.<br>|
|» » transaction_id|body|string|false|**Apple App Store** : The StoreKit transaction identifier for the purchase to record (new subscription, expired re-purchase, or one-time product). Prefer this over `apple_app_store[receipt]` when you already have a transaction ID. Mutually exclusive with the receipt + product_id pair.<br><br>**Google Play Store**: Not applicable.<br>|
|» » receipt|body|string|false|**Apple App Store** : The Base64-encoded App Store receipt used to locate and record the purchase. Use together with `apple_app_store[product_id]`. Mutually exclusive with `apple_app_store[transaction_id]` --- prefer `transaction_id` when you already have it.<br><br>**Google Play Store**: Not applicable.<br>|
|» » product_id|body|string|false|**Apple App Store** : The App Store Connect `product_id` for the purchase. Required when recording via `apple_app_store[receipt]` (use together with `receipt`). Not required when using `apple_app_store[transaction_id]`.<br><br>**Google Play Store**: Not applicable.<br>|
|» google_play_store|body|object|false|Google Play Store--specific payload used to record the purchase. Provide parameters as `google_play_store[...]`.<br><br>**Apple App Store**: Not applicable. Do not send this object for Apple purchases.<br>|
|» » purchase_token|body|string|false|**Google Play Store** : Purchase token from the Android billing client. For subscriptions, you can record tokens when the subscription state in Google is [`SUBSCRIPTION_STATE_ACTIVE`](https://developers.google.com/android-publisher/api-ref/rest/v3/purchases.subscriptionsv2#subscriptionstate)<br>(or other supported states for your flow). For one-time orders, also pass `google_play_store[product_id]`. Prefer `order_id` when you have it. Mutually exclusive with `google_play_store[order_id]`.<br><br>**Apple App Store**: Not applicable.<br>|
|» » product_id|body|string|false|**Google Play Store** : In-app `product_id` on Google Play for which the purchase must be recorded. Required when recording a one-time order via `google_play_store[purchase_token]`. Not required when using `google_play_store[order_id]`.<br><br>**Apple App Store**: Not applicable.<br>|
|» » order_id|body|string|false|**Google Play Store** : Google Play `orderId`. Recommended for both subscriptions and one-time orders. Prefer this over `purchase_token` when available. Mutually exclusive with `google_play_store[purchase_token]` (+ optional `product_id` for OTO).<br><br>**Apple App Store**: Not applicable.<br>|
|» omnichannel_subscription|body|object|false|Optional parameters for the omnichannel subscription created from this purchase.<br>|
|» » id|body|string|false|Specifies the `id`<br>to assign as the omnichannel subscription identifier for this purchase. If not provided, Chargebee automatically generates an ID. Applicable to subscription purchases.<br>|

|other_site_name|query|object|false|optional, string filter<br><br>Site name to which the record is moved in/out.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, starts_with<br><br>**Example →**<br>*other_site_name\[is\] = "acme-test"*<br>|

Possible values are : customer, subscription, invoice, credit_note, transaction, order.<br><br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, in, not_in<br><br>**Example →**<br>*entity_type\[is\] = "customer"*<br>|
