## Start afresh

<a id="opIdstart_afresh"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/time_machines/string/start_afresh' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /time_machines/{time-machine-name}/start_afresh`

Restart the time machine. This will clear the "customer" data like customer details, subscriptions, invoices, transactions. Also a time travel is initiated to travel back to specified genesis time.

**Note:**
This API call is asynchronous.
You need to check if the "start afresh" operation has completed by checking if the time travel status is **successful**
by retrieving the time machine in a loop with a minimum delay of 3 secs between two retrieve requests. In case you are using any of the client libraries, use the **wait for time travel completion**
function provided as a instance method in the library.
Use method **waitForTimeTravelCompletion()** on the returned **time_machine** resource which will block until the time travel completes. Use method **waitForTimeTravelCompletion()** on the returned **time_machine** resource which will block until the time travel completes. Use method **wait_for_time_travel_completion** on the returned **time_machine** resource which will block until the time travel completes. Use method **wait_for_time_travel_completion** on the returned **time_machine** resource which will block until the time travel completes. Use method **WaitForTimeTravelCompletion** on the returned **time_machine** resource which will block until the time travel completes. Use method **wait_for_time_travel_completion** on the returned **time_machine** resource which will block until the time travel completes. Use method **waitForTimeTravelCompletion** on the returned **time_machine** resource which will block until the time travel completes. Use method **wait_for_time_travel_completion** on the returned **time_machine** resource which will block until the time travel completes.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

<h3 id="start-afresh-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|
|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|time-machine-name|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» genesis_time|body|integer(unix-time)|false|The genesis time to travel back as part of the reset operation. If not provided, then the travel is set to 6 months in the past.<br><br>**Note:**<br>Can only be in the past.<br>|

## Create a card payment method token

<a id="opIdcreate_a_card_payment_method_token"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/tokens/create_for_card' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /tokens/create_for_card`

Generate a token that holds card related information.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

Supported only for Adyen and Chargebee Payments.<br>* mada - A Mada card scheme.<br>* visa - A Visa card scheme.<br>|

|» » additional_information|body|object|false|* `checkout_com`: While adding a new payment method using [permanent token](/docs/api/payment_sources/create-using-permanent-token) or passing raw card details to Checkout.com, `document` ID and `country_of_residence` are required to support payments through [dLocal](https://www.checkout.com/docs/previous/payments/payment-methods/cards/dlocal).<br><br>  * `payer`: User related information.<br>    * `country_of_residence`: This is required since the billing country associated with the user's payment method may not be the same as their country of residence. Hence the user's country of residence needs to be specified. `fraud`: Fraud identification related information.<br>    * `device_session_id`: Session ID associated with the user's device.<br>    * `fraud_merchant_id`: Your [merchant ID](https://developers.braintreepayments.com/guides/premium-fraud-management-tools/device-data-collection/javascript/v3#collecting-device-data) for fraud detection.<br>* `chargebee_payments`: While passing raw card details to Chargebee Payments, if `fraud_session_id` is added, additional validation is performed to avoid fraudulent transactions.<br><br>  * `fraud`: Fraud identification related information.<br>    * `fraud_session_id`: Your Chargebee Payments fraud session ID required to perform anti-fraud validation.<br>* `bank_of_america`: While passing raw card details to Bank of America, your user's `device_session_id` can be added to perform additional validation and avoid fraudulent transactions.<br><br>  * `fraud`: Fraud identification related information.<br>    * `device_session_id`: Session ID associated with the user's device.<br>* `ecentric`: This parameter is used to verify and process payment method details in Ecentric. If the `merchant_id` parameter is included, Chargebee will vault it / perform a lookup and verification against this `merchant_id`, overriding the one configured in Chargebee. If tokens and processing occur in the same Merchant GUID, you can just skip this part.<br><br>  * `merchant_id`: Merchant GUID where the card is vaulted or need to be vaulted.<br>* `ebanx`: While passing raw card details to EBANX, the user's `document` is required for some countries and `device_session_id` can be added to perform [additional validation](https://developer.ebanx.com/docs/payments/guides/features/device-fingerprint#device-fingerprint) and avoid fraudulent transactions.<br><br>  * `payer`: User related information.<br>    * `document`: Document is the user's identification number based on their country.<br>  * `fraud`: Fraud identification related information.<br>    * `device_session_id`: Session ID associated with the user's device<br>|
|» » card_type|body|string|false|Type of the card<br><br>* not_applicable - Used for offline entries in transactions. Not applicable for cards<br>* visa - A Visa card.<br>* electronic_payment_standard - Electronic Payment Standard<br>* jcb - A JCB card.<br>* kbc_payment_button - KBC Payment Button<br>* diners_club - A Diner's Club card.<br>* other - Card belonging to types other than those listed above.<br>* discover - A Discover card.<br>* american_express - An American Express card.<br>* bancontact - A Bancontact card.<br>* pay_by_bank - Pay By Bank<br>* mastercard - A MasterCard.<br>* trustly - Trustly<br>|
|» » email|body|string(email)|false|Email address of the cardholder. Required by some gateways when creating a card token.<br>|

<h1 id="chargebee-api-transactions">transactions</h1>

This resource represents the [transaction](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/transactions.html) event that has happened in your account.

## List transactions

<a id="opIdlist_transactions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/transactions' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /transactions`

Lists all the transactions.  
**Note:**

For better query performance, we recommend using a `date` filter (for example, `date[after]` or `date[between]`) when listing transactions. If you are already filtering by `updated_at`, you do not need to also filter by `date`.


<h3 id="list-transactions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|limit|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of resources to be returned.<br>|
|offset|query|string|false|Determines your position in the list for pagination. To ensure that the next page is retrieved correctly, always set `offset`<br>to the value of `next_offset`<br>obtained in the previous iteration of the API call.<br>|
|include_deleted|query|boolean|false|If set to true, includes the deleted resources in the response. For the deleted resources in the response, the '**deleted**<br>' attribute will be '**true**<br>'.<br>|
|id|query|object|false|optional, string filter<br><br>Uniquely identifies the transaction.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, starts_with, in, not_in<br><br>**Example →**<br>*id\[is\] = "txn_88ybdbsnvf2"*<br>|
|customer_id|query|object|false|optional, string filter<br><br>Identifier of the customer for which this transaction is made.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, starts_with, is_present, in, not_in<br><br>**Example →**<br>*customer_id\[is\] = "5hjdk8nOpd"*<br>|
|subscription_id|query|object|false|optional, string filter<br><br>Identifier of the subscription for which this transaction is made.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, starts_with, is_present, in, not_in<br><br>**Example →**<br>*subscription_id\[is\] = "5hjdk8nOpd"*<br>|
|payment_source_id|query|object|false|optional, string filter<br><br>To filter based on Transaction payment source id.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, starts_with, is_present, in, not_in<br><br>**Example →**<br>*payment_source_id\[is\] = "pm_3Nl8XXUQUXDVFa2"*<br>|
|payment_method|query|object|false|optional, enumerated string filter<br><br>The payment method of this transaction. Possible values are : card, cash, check, chargeback, bank_transfer, amazon_payments, paypal_express_checkout, direct_debit, alipay, alipay_hk, gcash, ovo, momo, mercado_pago, nequi, nupay, picpay, thai_qr, blik, fpx, wero, p24, affirm_pay, rakuten_pay, dana, touch_n_go, tamara, qpay, unionpay, apple_pay, wechat_pay, ach_credit, sepa_credit, ideal, google_pay, sofort, bancontact, giropay, dotpay, other, upi, netbanking_emandates.<br><br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, in, not_in<br><br>**Example →**<br>*payment_method\[is_not\] = "card"*<br>|
|gateway|query|object|false|optional, enumerated string filter<br><br>Gateway through which this transaction was done. Applicable only for 'Card' Payment Method. Possible values are : chargebee, chargebee_payments, stripe, wepay, braintree, authorize_net, paypal_pro, pin, eway, eway_rapid, worldpay, balanced_payments, beanstream, bluepay, elavon, first_data_global, hdfc, migs, nmi, ogone, paymill, paypal_payflow_pro, sage_pay, tco, wirecard, amazon_payments, paypal_express_checkout, gocardless, adyen, orbital, moneris_us, moneris, bluesnap, cybersource, vantiv, checkout_com, paypal, ingenico_direct, exact, mollie, quickbooks, razorpay, payu, not_applicable.<br><br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, in, not_in<br><br>**Example →**<br>*gateway\[is\] = "stripe"*<br>|
|gateway_account_id|query|object|false|optional, string filter<br><br>The gateway account used for this transaction.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, starts_with, in, not_in<br><br>**Example →**<br>*gateway_account_id\[is\] = "gw_3Nl9BNeQ7438Ks1"*<br>|
|id_at_gateway|query|object|false|optional, string filter<br><br>The id with which this transaction is referred in gateway.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, starts_with<br><br>**Example →**<br>*id_at_gateway\[is_not\] = "txn_5678HJS89900"*<br>|
|reference_number|query|object|false|optional, string filter<br><br>The reference number for this transaction. For example, the check number when [payment_method](/docs/api/transactions/transaction-object#payment_method)<br>= `check`<br>.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, starts_with, is_present<br><br>**Example →**<br>*reference_number\[is\] = "cus_u239732"*<br>|
|type|query|object|false|optional, enumerated string filter<br><br>Type of the transaction. Possible values are : authorization, payment, refund, payment_reversal.<br><br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, in, not_in<br><br>**Example →**<br>*type\[is_not\] = "payment"*<br>|
|date|query|object|false|optional, timestamp(UTC) in seconds filter<br><br>Indicates when this transaction occurred.<br>We recommend using this filter when listing transactions for better query performance. It is advisable when using this filter, to pass the `sort_by`<br>input parameter as `date`<br>for a faster response.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>after, before, on, between<br><br>**Example →**<br>*date\[before\] = "1435054328"*<br>|
|amount|query|object|false|optional, in cents filter<br><br>Amount for this transaction.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, lt, lte, gt, gte, between<br><br>**Example →**<br>*amount\[gt\] = "1200"*<br>|
|amount_capturable|query|object|false|optional, in cents filter<br><br>To filter based on transaction's unused authorized/blocked amount.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, lt, lte, gt, gte, between<br><br>**Example →**<br>*amount_capturable\[lt\] = "1200"*<br>|
|status|query|object|false|optional, enumerated string filter<br><br>The status of this transaction. Possible values are : in_progress, success, voided, failure, timeout, needs_attention.<br><br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, in, not_in<br><br>**Example →**<br>*status\[is\] = "success"*<br>|
|updated_at|query|object|false|optional, timestamp(UTC) in seconds filter<br><br>To filter based on `updated_at`.<br>This attribute will be present only if the resource has been updated after 2016-09-28. It is advisable when using this filter, to pass the `sort_by`<br>input parameter as `updated_at`<br>for a faster response.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>after, before, on, between<br><br>**Example →**<br>*updated_at\[after\] = "1243545465"*<br>|
|sort_by|query|object|false|optional, string filter<br><br>Sorts based on the specified attribute.<br>**Supported attributes :**<br>date, updated_at<br><br>**Supported sort-orders :**<br>asc, desc<br><br>**Example →**<br>*sort_by\[asc\] = "date"*<br><br>This will sort the result based on the 'date' attribute in ascending(earliest first) order.<br>|

## Reconcile transaction

<a id="opIdreconcile_transaction"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/transactions/string/reconcile' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /transactions/{transaction-id}/reconcile`

Update selected attributes of the transaction resource: `status`, `id_at_gateway`, and `customer_id`. Use this API for reconciliation purposes where the status of a transaction is in [needs_attention](/docs/api/transactions/transaction-object#status) that can be updated to either [success](/docs/api/transactions/transaction-object#status) or [failure](/docs/api/transactions/transaction-object#status) status.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

<h3 id="reconcile-transaction-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|
|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|transaction-id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» id_at_gateway|body|string|false|The identifier with which this transaction is referred in gateway. The `id_at_gateway`<br>can only be updated when the transaction status is in [needs_attention](/docs/api/transactions/transaction-object#status).  <br>**Note**:<br><br>* It is mandatory to pass this parameter value for updating the transaction status from `needs_attention` to `success`. It is recommended to pass this value if available in the gateway.<br>* An error occurs when the provided `id_at_gateway` value does not match the `id_at_gateway` value stored against the transaction in Chargebee.<br>|
|» customer_id|body|string|false|Unique identifier of the customer for which this transaction is made. This is needed only when the transaction is successful but not associated with any customer.  <br>**Note**:<br><br>An error occurs when the provided `customer_id`<br>value does not match the `customer_id`<br>value stored against the transaction in Chargebee.<br>|
|» status|body|string|false|The status of this transaction. The status can only be updated when the transaction status is in [needs_attention](/docs/api/transactions/transaction-object#status)<br>state.<br><br>* failure -<br>  When the transaction is in failure status.  <br>  **Note**:<br><br>  When the transaction is updated to [failure](/docs/api/transactions/transaction-object#status) status and the invoice is associated with the transaction,<br><br>  * the invoice will be moved to the [payment_due](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status) status if the [dunning](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/payments/2.0/dunning-v2.html) is configured.<br>  * the invoice will be moved to the [not_paid](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status) status if the [dunning](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/payments/2.0/dunning-v2.html) is not configured.<br>* success -<br>  When the transaction is successful.  <br>  **Note**:<br><br>  When the transaction is updated to [success](/docs/api/transactions/transaction-object#status)<br>  status, - and the invoice is associated with the transaction, the transaction [amount](/docs/api/transactions/transaction-object#amount) will be applied to the invoice.<br><br>  * and no invoice is associated but the customer is associated with the transaction, [customer_excess_payments](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#excess_payments) will be updated.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|chargebee-event-actions|all-disabled|
|chargebee-event-email|all-disabled|
|chargebee-event-webhook|all-disabled|
|» status|success|
|» status|failure|

`POST /transactions/{transaction-id}/refund`

* Not supported for ach_credit, sepa_credit, cash, check, bank_transfer, other.
* Contact [Chargebee Support](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/kb/getting-started/how-to-contact-chargebees-support-team?utm_source=docs_api&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=support) to enable this endpoint.

|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|

|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|
|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|transaction-id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» amount|body|integer(int64)|false|The amount to be refunded. Must not exceed [amount_unused](/docs/api/transactions/transaction-object#amount_unused).<br>If not passed then all of [amount_unused](/docs/api/transactions/transaction-object#amount_unused)<br>is refunded.<br>|

## Create an estimate for unbilled charges

<a id="opIdcreate_an_estimate_for_unbilled_charges"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/unbilled_charges/invoice_now_estimate' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /unbilled_charges/invoice_now_estimate`

This is similar to the "Create an invoice for unbilled charges" API but no invoice will be created, only an estimate for this operation is created.

In the estimate response,

* **estimate.invoice_estimates** is an array of **estimate.invoice_estimate**. This has the details of the invoices that will be generated now.

**Note:**

* This API when invoked does not perform the actual operation. It just generates an estimate.
* Both *subscription_id* and *customer_id* parameters should not be given at the same time.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|

## Create an invoice for unbilled charges

<a id="opIdcreate_an_invoice_for_unbilled_charges"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/unbilled_charges/invoice_unbilled_charges' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /unbilled_charges/invoice_unbilled_charges`

Use this API to bill the [unbilled charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/unbilled-charges.html). Available Credits and Excess Payments will automatically be applied while creating the invoice.

If the *Auto Collection* is turned on for the particular customer, the invoice will be created in payment_due state and the payment collection will be scheduled immediately.

During invoice creation, the PO number for the line items will be filled from the subscription's current PO number, if available.

If no recurring item is present in the created invoice, the invoice will be marked as recurring=false.

If consolidated invoicing is enabled and the parameter 'customer_id' is passed, multiple invoices can be created based on the following factors.

* Currency
* PO number if 'Group by PO number' is enabled
* Shipping address
* Auto Collection
* Payment method


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

<h3 id="create-an-invoice-for-unbilled-charges-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|
|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» subscription_id|body|string|false|Identifier of the subscription for which this invoice needs to be created. Should be specified if 'customer_id' is not specified.<br>|
|» customer_id|body|string|false|Identifier of the customer for whom this invoice needs to be created. Should be specified if 'subscription_id' is not specified. Applicable only if the consolidated invoicing is enabled. .<br>|

<h1 id="chargebee-api-usageevents">usage_events</h1>

This resource allows you to record usage events, which are essential for usage-based billing.

## Ingest a usage event

<a id="opIdcreate_a_usage_event"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/usage_events' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /usage_events`

This endpoint ingests a usage event into Chargebee.  
**See also**

* [Limits for Usage-based Billing in Chargebee](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/understanding-usages#usage-based-billing-limits)


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

<h3 id="ingest-a-usage-event-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|
|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» deduplication_id|body|string|true|An identifier used by the Chargebee's customer to distinguish between multiple events generated at the same timestamp for a single `subscription_id`.<br><br>The combination of `usage_timestamp`, `subscription_id`, and `deduplication_id` uniquely identifies each event.<br><br>**Example** :<br>If 3 events are generated for `subscription_id` = `sub-1` at `2025-04-01T00:00:00.000Z`, each event must have a distinct `deduplication_id`.<br>|
|» subscription_id|body|string|true|The unique identifier of a subscription.  <br>**Note:**<br><br>* If an existing `subscription_id` is provided, usage data is recorded against it.<br>* If the subscription does not exist yet in Chargebee, a new `subscription_id` can be used, and the subscription can be imported later, once the usage is successfully recorded.<br>* During invoice generation, recorded usage linked to the `subscription_id` will be applied to the invoice.<br>|
|» usage_timestamp|body|integer(int64)|true|The timestamp indicating when this usage occurred, represented as [Epoch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_time)<br>time in **milliseconds**<br>.<br>Example: `1738732394123`<br>represents the timestamp for February 5, 2025, at 05:13:14.123 UTC.  <br>**Note** :<br>The timestamp must be within the last **12 hours**<br>.<br>|
|» properties|body|object|true|A schema-less field that accepts any JSON-formatted data to define the attributes of the ingested event. It is a requirement to structure the data in a flat format wherever possible for better compatibility with downstream processing.<br>We strongly encourage using unique field names-particularly for fields intended for metering purposes. This approach enhances clarity and maintainability in the future.<br>For example, a field named `status`,<br><br>* Can represent `string` values such as `accepted` or `processing` in one context.<br><br>* In another scenario, it might hold numeric values, such as HTTP response codes like `200`, `300`, or `400`.<br><br>**Note**:<br><br>* Learn more about [field naming guidelines](/docs/api/usage_files).<br>|

## Retrieve usage file upload URL

<a id="opIdget_usages_file_upload_url"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/usage_files/upload_url' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /usage_files/upload_url`

This endpoint returns an upload URL for uploading usage events files, allowing you to upload files in supported formats. The file is processed asynchronously, and its status can be tracked using the [retrieve_file_processing_status](/docs/api/usage_files/get-uploaded-file-processing-status) endpoint.  
Before uploading, review the following guidelines and constraints:

* [Best practices](/docs/api/usage_files)
* [File upload constraints](/docs/api/usage_files#file_upload_constraints)
* [File field constraints](/docs/api/usage_files)
* [Handling errors](/docs/api/usage_files)

```yaml
null
```

<h1 id="chargebee-api-usages">usages</h1>

**Advanced Usage-Based Billing** For high-scale usage ingestion, use [Advanced Usage-Based Billing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/understanding-usages) with the [Usage Events API](/docs/api/usage_events).

## Retrieve usages for an invoice as PDF

<a id="opIdretrieve_usages_for_an_invoice_as_pdf"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/usages/pdf' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /usages/pdf`

**Advanced Usage-Based Billing**

For high-scale usage ingestion, use [Advanced Usage-Based Billing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/understanding-usages) with the [Usage Events API](/docs/api/usage_events). The Usage Events API supports schemaless event ingestion at scale, including [individual events](/docs/api/usage_events/create-a-usage-event), [batch ingestion](/docs/api/usage_events/ingest-usages-in-batch), and [usage file ingestion](/docs/api/usage_files/usage-file-object).

Retrieves usages record for an invoice in PDF file format. This endpoint is part of the [Usages API](/docs/api/usages) for **Automated Metered Billing**.

For Usage-Based Billing invoices, you can optionally group a metered feature's usage by its configured group-by attributes. Automated Metered Billing continues to render the existing ungrouped usage PDF.  
**Availability**

Support for adding `GROUP BY` to metered features and retrieving usage grouped by attributes is an upcoming capability and is not generally available yet. It will be made available in the coming weeks.  

### Use Cases

##### Group usage events in the PDF

This capability applies to Usage-Based Billing. The metered feature's `query` must include a `GROUP BY` clause, such as `SELECT SUM(hours) FROM events GROUP BY gpu_type, region`.

Use `group_by` to show how usage events are distributed across group-by attributes such as GPU type and region.

For example, group the `gpu_cloud` metered feature by `gpu_type` and `region`. Specify the group-by attributes as a JSON array:

```bash
-d "group_by[feature_id][0]"="gpu_cloud" \
-d 'group_by[attributes][0]'='["gpu_type","region"]'
```

Each distinct set of selected group-by attribute values forms a separate usage section in the PDF:

```text
gpu_type = "h100", region = "us-east"  60 hours
gpu_type = "a100", region = "eu-west"  40 hours
```

The order of names in the `group_by[attributes]` array determines their display order. A metered feature that is not included in `group_by[feature_id]` is displayed with a single usage total.

**Null and empty group-by attribute values**

When usage is grouped by `region`, the PDF combines the following usage into one null group:

* Usage recorded before `region` was added to the metered feature's `GROUP BY` clause.
* Events that do not contain `region`.
* Events where `region` is JSON `null`, such as `"region": null`.
* Events where the attribute is the exact string `"null"`, irrespective of capitalization, such as `"region": "null"`, `"region": "NULL"`, or `"region": "nULL"`.

The comparison with `"null"` is case-insensitive, but the entire value must match. Values containing leading or trailing whitespace, such as `"region": " null"` and `"region": "null "`, retain their original values and appear as separate groups.

An event containing `"region": ""` belongs to a separate empty-string group. The PDF displays the null group using an em dash (`---`) and displays the empty-string group as a blank value.  
**Grouped usage and invoice total**

For `SUM` and `COUNT`, all grouped values, including the null and empty-string groups, add up to the overall usage for the same metered feature on the invoice:

```text
region = "us-east"  60 hours
region = "eu-west"  40 hours
Overall usage       100 hours
```

This does not apply to `MIN`, `MAX`, `AVG`, or `COUNT(DISTINCT ...)`. For these functions, each group is calculated separately.

The API response continues to return a `download` object. The grouped usage appears in the PDF, not in the API response.  
**Constraints**

* Provide both `group_by[feature_id]` and `group_by[attributes]` for each entry.
* Each `group_by[feature_id]` value must identify a metered feature billed on the invoice.
* Each `group_by[attributes]` value must be a nonempty JSON array. Exact duplicate names are not allowed.
* Group-by attribute names are case-sensitive and must match the names in that metered feature's `group_by` attribute. For example, `region, region` is invalid, while `region, Region` identifies two different attributes.
* You can specify up to 5 group-by attributes per metered feature.
* The same metered feature cannot be listed more than once.

**Usage line limit**

By default, the PDF can contain up to 1,000 usage lines in total across all metered features.

If the request exceeds the limit, it fails with `invalid_request` and the error code `exceeds_max_allowed_breakdown_rows`.

```yaml
null
```

## List usages

<a id="opIdlist_usages"></a>

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/usages' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /usages`

**Advanced Usage-Based Billing**

For high-scale usage ingestion, use [Advanced Usage-Based Billing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/understanding-usages) with the [Usage Events API](/docs/api/usage_events). The Usage Events API supports schemaless event ingestion at scale, including [individual events](/docs/api/usage_events/create-a-usage-event), [batch ingestion](/docs/api/usage_events/ingest-usages-in-batch), and [usage file ingestion](/docs/api/usage_files/usage-file-object).

Retrieves the list of usages. This endpoint is part of the [Usages API](/docs/api/usages) for **Automated Metered Billing**.


<h3 id="list-usages-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|limit|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of resources to be returned.<br>|
|offset|query|string|false|Determines your position in the list for pagination. To ensure that the next page is retrieved correctly, always set `offset`<br>to the value of `next_offset`<br>obtained in the previous iteration of the API call.<br>|
|id|query|object|false|optional, string filter<br><br>A unique and immutable id for the usage. If not provided, it is autogenerated.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, starts_with<br><br>**Example →**<br>*id\[is\] = "usage_lsfja24411"*<br>|
|subscription_id|query|object|false|optional, string filter<br><br>The id of the [subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions)<br>to which this usage record belongs.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, starts_with<br><br>**Example →**<br>*subscription_id\[is\] = "active2"*<br>|
|usage_date|query|object|false|optional, timestamp(UTC) in seconds filter<br><br>The time at which this usage occurred. Chargebee bills only those usages whose<br>`usage_date`<br>falls within a time when the subscription `status`<br>was `active`<br>or `non_renewing`.<br>However, the remaining usage records are still stored and are<br>[retrievable](/docs/api/usages/retrieve-a-usage).<br><br>**Note:**<br>If `usage_date`<br>corresponds to a time already invoiced, then it is stored but never invoiced unless the [invoice is regenerated](/docs/api/subscriptions/regenerate-an-invoice)<br>.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>after, before, on, between<br><br>**Example →**<br>*usage_date\[after\] = "1601220958"*<br>|

The item price must be a part of the subscription or should have been part of it historically.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, starts_with<br><br>**Example →**<br>*item_price_id\[is\] = "sprout"*<br>|
|invoice_id|query|object|false|optional, string filter<br><br>When the usage has been invoiced, this is the `id`<br>of the [invoice](/docs/api/invoices).<br>This is cleared when the invoice is `voided`<br>or deleted.<br>**Supported operators :**<br>is, is_not, starts_with, is_present<br><br>**Example →**<br>*invoice_id\[is\] = "null"*<br>|

## Create a virtual bank account using permanent token

<a id="opIdcreate_a_virtual_bank_account_using_permanent_token"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/virtual_bank_accounts/create_using_permanent_token' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /virtual_bank_accounts/create_using_permanent_token`

Creates a virtual bank account (VBA) for a [customer](/docs/api/customers) using a [permanent token](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/payments/2.0/payment-gateways-and-configuration/stripe-automated-bank-transfer#supported-token-formats) obtained from a payment gateway.

Use this operation when you have already created a payment source at the gateway and obtained a permanent token (reference ID) for it.  

### Prerequisites \& Constraints

* The customer must not already have an active VBA for the same [`scheme`](/docs/api/virtual_bank_accounts#scheme). For example, if the customer already has a VBA with `scheme` set to `us_automated_bank_transfer`, you cannot create another VBA with the same scheme.  

### Impacts

**Virtual bank account**  
* A new virtual bank account resource is created and associated with the customer. The virtual bank account includes details such as bank account number, routing number (or IBAN), bank name, and other payment instructions retrieved from the gateway using the provided reference ID.
* The [email address](/docs/api/virtual_bank_accounts#email) for the VBA is set at the gateway from the [`customer.email`](/docs/api/customers#email) attribute. Later, if the email address is updated for the customer, the email address for the VBA is also updated.  

### Implementation Notes

* Check if the customer already has a virtual bank account for the same scheme by calling the [List virtual bank accounts API](/docs/api/virtual_bank_accounts/list-virtual-bank-accounts) with the [customer ID](/docs/api/customers/list-customers#list_customers_id) filter. If a virtual bank account exists for the same scheme, the API returns a `payment_method_already_exists` error.

* Validate that the required currency for the scheme is enabled. Use the [List currencies API](/docs/api/currencies/list-currencies) to check if the currency is enabled.



> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

<h3 id="create-a-virtual-bank-account-using-permanent-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|
|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» customer_id|body|string|true|The unique identifier of the [customer](/docs/api/customers) for whom you want to create a virtual bank account.<br>|
|» reference_id|body|string|true|The identifier (permanent token) used to fetch the payment source details from the gateway. For example, in Stripe it may be only the Stripe Customer ID (for example, cus_63MnDn0t6kfDW7), or a combination of Stripe Customer ID and Stripe Source ID separated by a forward slash (for example, cus_63MnDn0t6kfDW7/src_6WjCF20vT9WN1G).  <br>**Constraints**<br><br>* If `gateway_account_id` is provided, the `reference_id` must belong to the gateway account.<br>* If the `gateway_account_id` is not provided, the `reference_id` must belong to the gateway account selected based on the [gateway routing rules](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/payments/2.0/payment-gateways-and-configuration/gateway_settings#smart-routing) for the payment method type and currency combination.<br>|
|» gateway_account_id|body|string|false|Identifier of the payment gateway account to use when creating the virtual bank account.  <br>**Default behavior**<br>When not provided, Chargebee selects an applicable gateway account for the chosen `scheme`. Selection follows your site's [Smart Routing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/payments/2.0/payment-gateways-and-configuration/gateway_settings#smart-routing) rules.<br>|
|» scheme|body|string|false|The type of automated bank transfer scheme for the virtual bank account.  <br>**Prerequisites**<br><br>* If billing address validation is enabled for your site, the customer must have a billing address with a country code.<br><br>* mx_automated_bank_transfer -<br>  Mexico Automated Bank Transfer scheme for Mexico-based customers.  <br>  **Prerequisites**<br><br>  * MXN currency must be [enabled](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/site-configuration/multi-currency-pricing) for the site.<br>  * The customer's [`billing_address.country`](/docs/api/customers#billing_address_country) must be `MX`.<br>* sepa_credit -<br>  **Deprecated**<br><br>  * This scheme is deprecated. Use `eu_automated_bank_transfer` instead.<br><br>  SEPA Credit Transfer scheme for customers in the European Union.<br>* eu_automated_bank_transfer -<br>  EU Automated Bank Transfer scheme for customers in the European Union.  <br>  **Prerequisites**<br><br>  * EUR currency must be [enabled](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/site-configuration/multi-currency-pricing) for the site.<br>  * The customer's [`billing_address.country`](/docs/api/customers#billing_address_country) must be in a SEPA-supported region.<br>* ach_credit -<br>  **Deprecated**<br><br>  * This scheme is deprecated. Use `us_automated_bank_transfer` instead.<br><br>  ACH Credit Transfer scheme for US-based customers.<br>* jp_automated_bank_transfer -<br>  Japan Automated Bank Transfer scheme for Japan-based customers.  <br>  **Prerequisites**<br><br>  * JPY currency must be [enabled](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/site-configuration/multi-currency-pricing) for the site.<br>  * The customer's [`billing_address.country`](/docs/api/customers#billing_address_country) must be `JP`.<br>* us_automated_bank_transfer -<br>  US Automated Bank Transfer scheme for US-based customers.  <br>  **Prerequisites**<br><br>  * USD currency must be [enabled](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/site-configuration/multi-currency-pricing) for the site.<br>  * The customer's [`billing_address.country`](/docs/api/customers#billing_address_country) must be `US`.<br><br>  US Automated Bank Transfer<br>* gb_automated_bank_transfer -<br>  UK Automated Bank Transfer scheme for UK-based customers.  <br>  **Prerequisites**<br><br>  * GBP currency must be [enabled](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/site-configuration/multi-currency-pricing) for the site.<br>  * The customer's [`billing_address.country`](/docs/api/customers#billing_address_country) must be `GB`.<br>|

<h1 id="chargebee-api-webhookendpoints">webhook_endpoints</h1>

A webhook endpoint receives real-time notifications from your Chargebee site when specific events occur, such as invoice generation, payment failures, or subscription updates.

## Delete a webhook endpoint

<a id="opIddelete_a_webhook_endpoint"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/webhook_endpoints/string/delete' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /webhook_endpoints/{webhook-endpoint-id}/delete`

Deletes a webhook endpoint using its unique identifier. Use this API to remove obsolete or inactive webhook endpoints from your Chargebee site. Deleting an endpoint ensures it no longer receives event notifications.


<h3 id="delete-a-webhook-endpoint-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|
|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|webhook-endpoint-id|path|string|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|chargebee-event-actions|all-disabled|
|chargebee-event-email|all-disabled|
|chargebee-event-webhook|all-disabled|

`GET /webhook_endpoints/{webhook-endpoint-id}`

Retrieves the details of a specific webhook endpoint using its unique identifier. Use this API to inspect an endpoint's configuration, such as the target URL, subscribed events, and authentication settings.

|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|

|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|webhook-endpoint-id|path|string|true|none|

## Update webhook endpoint

<a id="opIdupdate_a_webhook_endpoint"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/webhook_endpoints/string' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /webhook_endpoints/{webhook-endpoint-id}`

Updates the configuration of an existing webhook endpoint using its unique identifier. You can use this API to change properties such as the name, URL, subscribed events, authentication credentials, or API version. This is useful when rotating endpoints, updating destination URLs, or modifying which events your system listens to.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

<h3 id="update-webhook-endpoint-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|
|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|webhook-endpoint-id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|A name to identify the webhook endpoint.<br>|
|» api_version|body|string|false|The API version used to format the webhook payload. Ensure this version matches the client library used by your webhook server.<br><br>* v1 - If selected, the payload includes only attributes from API v1 resources.<br>* v2 - If selected, the payload includes only attributes from API v2 resources.<br>|
|» url|body|string|false|The target URL where webhook notifications will be sent.  <br>**Note**<br>Only URL ports `80`, `443`, `8080`, or `8443` are allowed.<br>|
|» primary_url|body|boolean|false|Controls whether card-related resources are included in the webhook payload. Card details are always masked.<br>|
|» send_card_resource|body|boolean|false|Specifies whether card-related resources should be included in the webhook payload.<br>|
|» basic_auth_password|body|string|false|The password used for basic authentication to secure webhook delivery.<br>|
|» basic_auth_username|body|string|false|Username for basic authentication used to secure webhook delivery.<br>|
|» disabled|body|boolean|false|Indicates whether the webhook endpoint is disabled. Set to `true`<br>to disable the endpoint, set to `false`<br>to enable the endpoint.<br>|
|» enabled_events|body|[string]|false|A list of event types that trigger this webhook.  <br>**Note**<br>If this field is left empty, the webhook will enable [all event types](/docs/api/webhook_endpoints) by default.<br>|

## List webhook endpoints

<a id="opIdlist_webhook_endpoints"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/webhook_endpoints' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /webhook_endpoints`

Retrieves all webhook endpoints configured on your Chargebee site. The response includes each endpoint's ID, name, and target URL. Use this API to view, audit, or manage the list of webhook endpoints currently active or configured in your site.


<h3 id="list-webhook-endpoints-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|limit|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of resources to be returned.<br>|
|offset|query|string|false|Determines your position in the list for pagination. To ensure that the next page is retrieved correctly, always set `offset`<br>to the value of `next_offset`<br>obtained in the previous iteration of the API call.<br>|

## Create a webhook endpoint

<a id="opIdcreate_a_webhook_endpoint"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2/webhook_endpoints' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /webhook_endpoints`

Create a new webhook API endpoint on your Chargebee Site.


> Body parameter

```yaml
null
```

<h3 id="create-a-webhook-endpoint-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargebee-request-origin-device|header|string|false|The device from which the customer has made the request|
|chargebee-request-origin-user|header|string(email)|false|The email address of your customer/user. Use this when the email address has only ASCII characters.|
|chargebee-request-origin-user-encoded|header|string(email)|false|The Base64-encoded email address of your customer/user. Use this if the email address has UTF-8 characters. When this header is provided, the header chargebee-request-origin-user is ignored.|
|chargebee-request-origin-ip|header|string|false|The IP address of the customer where the request originated|
|chargebee-event-actions|header|string|false|skip all actions to be done on the events|
|chargebee-event-email|header|string|false|skip only emails|
|chargebee-event-webhook|header|string|false| skip only webhooks|
|chargebee-business-entity-id|header|string|false|If the site has multiple business entities, you can use this custom HTTP header to specify the business entity for which Chargebee should perform the operation.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|A name to identify the webhook endpoint.<br>|
|» api_version|body|string|false|The API version used to format the webhook payload. Ensure this version matches the client library used by your webhook server<br><br>* v1 - If selected, the payload includes only attributes from API v1 resources.<br>* v2 - If selected, the payload includes only attributes from API v2 resources.<br>|
|» url|body|string|true|The target URL where webhook notifications will be sent.  <br>**Note**<br>Only URL ports `80`, `443`, `8080`, or `8443` are allowed.<br>|
|» primary_url|body|boolean|false|Indicates whether this webhook is marked as the primary endpoint. If only one exists, it is primary by default.<br>|
|» disabled|body|boolean|false|Indicates whether the webhook endpoint is disabled. Set to `true`<br>to disable the endpoint, set to `false`<br>to enable the endpoint.<br>|
|» basic_auth_password|body|string|false|The password used for basic authentication to secure webhook delivery.<br>|
|» basic_auth_username|body|string|false|Username for basic authentication used to secure webhook delivery.<br>|
|» send_card_resource|body|boolean|false|Controls whether card-related resources are included in the webhook payload. Card details are always masked.<br>|
|» chargebee_response_schema_type|body|string|false|Indicates the response schema used in the webhook payload, based on the product catalog version configured for the site.  <br>**Note**<br>This field is only applicable if the site is in [`compat`](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/1.0/product-catalog/product-catalog-coexistence-ui-changes) mode.<br><br>* compat - The webhook payload uses a schema compatible with both Product Catalog 1.0 and 2.0. This is applicable only to sites automatically upgraded to Product Catalog 2.0.<br>* plans_addons -<br>  The webhook payload follows the [Product Catalog 1.0](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/1.0/product-catalog/product-catalog)<br>  schema and uses the [Plans](/docs/api/v2/pcv-1/plans)<br>  and [Addons](/docs/api/v2/pcv-1/addons)<br>  model.<br>* items -<br>  The webhook payload follows the [Product Catalog 2.0](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/product-catalog/product-catalog)<br>  schema and uses the [Items API model](/docs/api/items)<br>  .<br>|
|» enabled_events|body|[string]|false|A list of event types that trigger this webhook.  <br>**Note**<br>If this field is left empty, the webhook will enable [all event types](/docs/api/webhook_endpoints) by default.<br>|

|» » advance_invoice_schedule|body|[AdvanceInvoiceSchedule](#schemaadvanceinvoiceschedule)|true|The invoice for a subscription in Chargebee is generated at the time of subscription renewal. Invoices can also be [generated in advance](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/advance-invoices.html) for an upcoming renewal or set of renewals. With Advance Invoicing Schedules, you can set up a plan for when such advance invoices are generated for the lifetime of the subscription. This helps you:<br><br>* Set up a contract with your customers so that they can be notified of their payment schedules in advance.<br>* Allow customers who make offline payments to be alerted about their upcoming dues well ahead of actual subscription renewals.<br>* Prevent post-renewal unpaid usage of your services by customers.<br><br>Advance invoices can be scheduled in two ways:<br><br>#### Specific Dates Schedule<br><br>Advance invoices for a subscription can be scheduled to be generated on specific [dates](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#specific_dates_schedule_date) in the future. You must specify the [number of billing cycles](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#specific_dates_schedule_terms_to_charge) to be invoiced on each date. A maximum of 5 dates can be specified.<br><br>#### Fixed Interval Schedule<br><br>Advance invoices can be scheduled to be generated at fixed intervals of time, where each interval spans the same number of billing cycles of the subscription. The invoice for each interval is generated a specified number of days ([`days_before_interval`](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#fixed_interval_schedule_days_before_renewal)) before the start of the interval. You can configure the schedule to end on a certain date or after a specified number of advance invoices have been generated.<br><br>The start date of the first interval depends on the number of days remaining from current time till the next renewal of the subscription. If this is more than `days_before_interval`, the interval begins at the next renewal. On the other hand, if the number of days remaining before the next renewal is less than `days_before_interval`, the first interval begins at the renewal following the next.<br>|

## Triggered when a gift expires.

<a id="opIdonGift_expiredWebhook"></a>

`POST gift_expired`

Triggered when a gift expires.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-gift-expires-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[GiftExpiredEvent](#schemagiftexpiredevent)|false|Payload for gift_expired event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » gift|body|[Gift](#schemagift)|true|Gift represents a subscription of a customer(**recipient** ) to a 'gift plan' which has been gifted by another customer(**gifter**). It may also have addons and coupons. Gift will be created only on immediate successful payment collection from the gifter's payment method.<br><br>Gift is initially created in '**scheduled** ' state. The gift can be scheduled to be notified on a particular date to the recipient by passing 'scheduled_at'. If not, the recipient is notified immediately. Gift will be moved to '**unclaimed** ' state on the date of notification. If you pass auto_claim as true, gift status will be moved to '**claimed**' immediately, otherwise, the gift will remain 'unclaimed' till the recipient claims the gift.<br><br>If the gift is not claimed before the claim_expiry_date, it will be moved to the '**expired**' state.<br><br>#### GIFT SUBSCRIPTION<br><br>Gift subscriptions will be created in '**future** ' state. Once the gift is claimed, the subscription will be moved to '**non-renewing**' state.<br><br>#### INVOICE<br><br>Gift subscriptions will be invoiced immediately. The invoice created has **is_gifted** as 'true' and **term_finalized** as 'false'. This is because initially the invoice term_start and term_end are set as the subscription's start_date till the end of the plan period. Once the gift is claimed, the invoice's term_finalized will be marked as 'true'. The term_start will be changed to the actual invoice's term, which is the gift-claim date and the term_end will be changed till plan's period.<br>|

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Webhook received successfully|None|

## Triggered when a tax withheld is deleted.

<a id="opIdonTax_withheld_deletedWebhook"></a>

`POST tax_withheld_deleted`

Triggered when a tax withheld is deleted.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-tax-withheld-is-deleted-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TaxWithheldDeletedEvent](#schemataxwithhelddeletedevent)|false|Payload for tax_withheld_deleted event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » tax_withheld|body|[TaxWithheld](#schemataxwithheld)|true|Tax regulations in many countries allow taxes to be deducted by the buyer while making payments for products and services. The buyer then pays this tax to the taxation authority. The `tax_withheld` resource captures the details of such tax deductions.  <br>**Note:**<br><br>* This resource is available as the `linked_taxes_withheld` sub-resource under `invoice`s.<br>* Whenever refunds are provided against this resource, they are available as `linked_tax_withheld_refunds` sub-resource under `credit_note`s.<br>|
|» » invoice|body|[Invoice](#schemainvoice)|true|An invoice is a commercial document representing a sale of products/services offered by you to a customer. It enumerates all the charges, adjustments, payments, discounts and taxes associated with the sale.<br><br>An invoice is said to be a recurring one when it is has at least one charge for [a plan or an addon item price](/docs/api/items). It is a non-recurring one when it has charges for only charge-item prices or [one-time charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/charges.html).<br><br>The item prices for any given billing term of a subscription are billed via an invoice at the beginning of the term (unless the charges are left unbilled). However, item prices that belong to `metered` items are billed at the end of the term via a `pending` invoice that can [close automatically](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing#configuring-metered-billing) or via [an API call](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice). Moreover, when there are no `metered` items in the subscription, the invoices can still be generated as `pending` while [creating](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items) or [updating](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items) a subscription.<br><br>#### Auto-collection<br><br>If [auto-collection](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#auto-collection-status) is enabled, then immediately on invoice generation (or, in case of subscriptions that have `create_pending_invoices` as `true`, on [invoice closure](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice)), the [payment method](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#payment_method) on file is charged:<br><br>* If the payment succeeds, the invoice is marked as `paid`.<br>* On payment failure, the invoice is marked as `payment_due` and [dunning settings](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/dunning-v2.html) are taken into account for payment retries.<br>* If no retry attempts are configured, or when retries are exhausted, the invoice is marked as `not_paid`.<br>* the amount due is zero or negative, the invoice is immediately marked as `paid` and the balance, if any, is added to [excess payments](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#excess-payments) for the customer.<br><br>**Note:** If [consolidated invoicing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html) is enabled, the attribute `subscription_id` is unavailable when the invoice has line items from multiple subscriptions. The individual subscription ids are seen under `line_items.subscription_id`.  <br><br>#### Recurring and non-recurring invoices<br><br>A recurring invoice contains at least one line item that is billed on a recurring basis. Specifically, it has at least one [`line_items[]`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#line_items) with `entity_type` set to `plan_item_price` or `addon_item_price`. A non-recurring invoice contains no recurring line items.  <br><br>#### Refundable amount for an invoice<br><br>The refundable amount for an invoice is the (amount paid on the invoice + refundable credit applied on the invoice + taxes withheld on the invoice) minus (amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice). Each of these amounts is obtained from the invoice resource as follows:<br><br>* Amount paid on the invoice: [`amount_paid`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_amount_paid)<br>* Refundable credit applied on the invoice: [`credits_applied`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_credits_applied)<br>* Taxes withheld on the invoice: Sum of [`linked_taxes_withheld[].amount`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_linked_taxes_withheld)<br>* Amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice: Sum of [`issued_credit_notes[i].cn_total`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_issued_credit_notes) where `issued_credit_notes[i].cn_status` is `refunded` or `refund_due`.<br>|
|» » credit_note|body|[CreditNote](#schemacreditnote)|true|A [Credit Note](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/credit-notes.html) is a document that specifies the money owed by a business to its customer. The seller usually issues a Credit Note for the same or lower amount than the invoice, and then repays the money to the customer or set it off against other 'due' invoices.<br><br>### Credit Note Types<br><br>Credit notes in Chargebee are categorized into three types:<br>1. `adjustment`: Adjustment credit notes are used to adjust the amount of an existing invoice in the `payment_due` or `not_paid` [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status). Use this type of credit note to reduce the invoice amount, typically as a discount to the customer.<br><br>Adjustment credit notes are automatically created in the following cases:<br><br>* When an invoice is written off.<br>* When a subscription is modified with proration enabled, and the invoice for the current term is in the `payment_due` or `not_paid` [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status). 2. `refundable`: Refundable credit notes allow you to return a certain amount to the customer. These credits can be:<br>* Retained for automatic application on future invoices.<br>* Applied to existing unpaid invoices.<br>* Refunded to the customer. Refundable credit notes are automatically created in the following cases:<br>* When an invoice is refunded.<br>* When a subscription is changed or canceled with proration enabled, the invoice for the current term is in the `paid` [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status). Refundable credits are applied to future invoices or can be refunded to the original payment method. 3. `store`: Store credit notes are created for `paid` or `partially_paid` invoice [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status) during subscription changes, such as upgrades, downgrades, or cancellations. Key characteristics of store credits:<br>* No tax component is included at the time of creation.<br>* A credit note document is generated, similar to refundable credits.<br>* Store credits are applied before tax calculations on future invoices.<br><br>**Note:**<br>If you have enabled *consolidated invoicing*<br>, to know the subscriptions attached with a credit note you have to refer [line_item's](/docs/api/credit_notes/credit_note-object#line_items)<br>*subscription_id*<br>. The credit note's *subscription_id*<br>should **not**<br>be used (which will be *null*<br>if the credit note has lines from multiple subscriptions).  <br>Impact on reference invoice  <br>The following updates are made to the reference invoice when a credit note is created/imported:<br><br>* If the credit note `type` is `adjustment`:<br>  * The adjustment credit note details are added to the `adjustment_credit_notes[]` attribute of the invoice.<br>  * The invoice `amount_due` is reduced by the credit note `total`.<br>  * The invoice `status` is updated to `paid` if the invoice `amount_due` equals the credit note `total`.<br>  * The invoice `status` does not change if the invoice `amount_due` is greater than credit note `total`.<br>* If the credit note `type` is `refundable`:<br>  * The refundable credit note details are added to the `issued_credit_notes[]` attribute of the invoice.<br>  * The invoice `status` does not change.<br>* If the credit note `type` is `store`:<br>  * The store credit note details are added to the `issued_credit_notes[]` attribute of the invoice.<br>  * The invoice `status` does not change.<br>|

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Webhook received successfully|None|

This operation does not require authentication

|» » coupon|body|[Coupon](#schemacoupon)|true|Overview<br>--------<br><br>Coupons are deductions applied to invoices or invoice line items. They're designed to be consumed by your customers directly. A coupon deduction can either be for a fixed amount or for a percentage of the amount of the invoice or line item.  <br>**Note:**<br><br>If you wish to provide discounts to your customers via API or the Chargebee app, see [Discounts API](/docs/api/discounts)<br><br>Order of application of coupons and discounts<br>---------------------------------------------<br><br>When both [coupons](/docs/api/coupons) and [discounts](/docs/api/discounts) are applied simultaneously to a [subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions) or [one-time invoice](/docs/api/invoices/create-invoice-for-items-and-one-time-charges), they're applied in the following order:  <br><br>\|---\|---------------------------------------\|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\|<br>\|   \| **Summary**                           \| **Description**                                                                     \|<br>\| 1 \| Line-level, fixed amount coupons      \| `coupon` with `apply_on` = `each_specified_item` and `discount_type` = `flat`       \|<br>\| 2 \| Line-level, fixed amount discounts    \| `discount` with `apply_on` = `specific_item_price` and `type` = `fixed_amount`      \|<br>\| 3 \| Line-level, percentage coupons        \| `coupon` with `apply_on` = `each_specified_item` and `discount_type` = `percentage` \|<br>\| 4 \| Line-level, percentage discounts      \| `discount` with `apply_on` = `specific_item_price` and `type` = `percentage`        \|<br>\| 5 \| Invoice-level, fixed amount coupons   \| `coupon` with `apply_on` = `invoice_amount` and `discount_type` = `flat`            \|<br>\| 6 \| Invoice-level, fixed amount discounts \| `discount` with `apply_on` = `invoice_amount` and `type` = `fixed_amount`           \|<br>\| 7 \| Invoice-level, percentage coupons     \| `coupon` with `apply_on` = `invoice_amount` and `discount_type` = `percentage`      \|<br>\| 8 \| Invoice-level, percentage discounts   \| `discount` with `apply_on` = `invoice_amount` and `type` = `percentage`             \|<br><br>For example, consider the following scenario:<br><br>A subscription is created with:<br><br>* a plan price of $200 per month<br>* an addon price of $20 per month<br>* a flat $5 invoice discount<br>* a 1% off coupon on the addon<br>* a flat $2 coupon on the invoice<br><br>The above coupons and discount are applied in the following order:  <br><br>\|---\|---------------------------------------------\|-----------------------------------------------\|<br>\|   \| **Discount or coupon applied**              \| **Subtotal at each step**                     \|<br>\| 1 \| Initial subtotal (plan price + addon price) \| $200 + $20 = $220                             \|<br>\| 2 \| 1% off coupon on the addon                  \| $200 + $(20 - 0.02) = $200 + $19.98 = $219.98 \|<br>\| 3 \| Flat $2 coupon on the invoice               \| $219.98 - $2 = $217.98                        \|<br>\| 4 \| Flat $5 invoice discount                    \| $217.98 - $5 = **$212.98**                    \|<br><br>|

A dispute is created when a cardholder questions a payment with their card issuer, either as a formal `chargeback` or as a pre-chargeback `inquiry`.<br><br>Chargebee records each dispute against the [transaction](/docs/api/transactions/transaction-object) that was disputed, the [customer](/docs/api/customers/customer-object) who made the payment, and the gateway account that processed it. As the payment gateway moves the dispute toward a resolution, Chargebee updates the dispute [`status`](/docs/api/disputes/dispute-object#status).<br><br>Disputes are read-only through the API. The customer details include their ID, name, contact information, and any [custom attributes](/docs/api/advanced-features) you'd like to associate with them.  <br>**Breaking Change**:<br><br>* [**Sites**](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/sites-intro.html) **created before March 1, 2014** : [updating the card](/docs/api/cards/update-card-for-a-customer) deletes the customer's `billing_address` and `vat_number` and replaces them with values from the request.<br>* **Sites created on or after March 1, 2014** : updating the card doesn't change the `billing_address` and `vat_number`.<br>|
