## Triggered when a price ramp is updated.

<a id="opIdonPrice_ramp_updatedWebhook"></a>

`POST price_ramp_updated`

> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-price-ramp-is-updated-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[PriceRampUpdatedEvent](#schemapricerampupdatedevent)|false|Payload for price_ramp_updated event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » price_ramp|body|[PriceRamp](#schemapriceramp)|true|Price ramp resource lets you define a stepped pricing schedule on an [item price](/docs/api/item_prices) in the Product Catalog. Each ramp is an ordered list of `ramp_intervals` that set the price for contiguous ranges of billing cycles, so new subscriptions inherit introductory or stepped pricing without custom per-subscription logic.<br><br>Here's an example to show how you can use ramp pricing:<br><br>A media streaming company offers a **Basic** monthly plan with a catalog price of $9.99. To grow acquisitions, they configure a price ramp so new subscribers start on an introductory price, then step up to full price.  <br><br>\|----------\|--------------\|---------------\|-------------------\|<br>\| **Plan** \| **Currency** \| **Frequency** \| **Catalog price** \|<br>\| Basic    \| USD          \| Monthly       \| $9.99             \|<br><br>\|--------------------\|-------------------\|-------------------------\|<br>\| **Billing cycles** \| **Price charged** \| **Price type**          \|<br>\| Month 1            \| $0.99             \| Introductory ramp price \|<br>\| Months 2--4        \| $4.99             \| Introductory ramp price \|<br>\| Month 5 onwards    \| $9.99             \| Catalog price           \|<br><br>Every new subscription on this Basic USD Monthly item price inherits the ramp automatically. In this example the final interval uses the catalog price, so the subscriber stays on $9.99 from month 5 onward. The catalog price continues only when that final interval sets `apply_catalog_price` to `true`. A final interval that sets `price` and omits `ending_billing_cycle` keeps that fixed price for the remaining billing cycles.<br><br>An interval that uses the item price's catalog price returns `apply_catalog_price` as `true`. The resolved price for every interval is always available in `price` (in the [minor unit of the currency](/docs/api/currencies)) and, when [multi-decimal pricing](/docs/api/currencies) is enabled, in `price_in_decimal`.  <br>When a price ramp is linked to an item price, the `price_ramp_id` is exposed on the corresponding [item price](/docs/api/item_prices) object.  <br>**See also:**<br>For a more detailed understanding of Price Ramps, including how to configure and manage them, as well as their impact on other features, follow these resources:<br><br>* [Price Ramps](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/product-catalog/price-ramps)<br>* [Configuring a Price Ramp](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/product-catalog/price-ramps-configure)<br>* [How Ramp Pricing works with Create Subscription](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/product-catalog/price-ramps-create-subscription)<br>* [How Ramp Pricing works with Hosted Checkout](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/product-catalog/price-ramps-hosted-checkout)<br>|
|» » ramp_interval|body|[RampInterval](#schemarampinterval)|true|none|

token](/docs/api/payment_sources/create-using-permanent-token) * [Create a card payment source](/docs/api/payment_sources/create-a-card-payment-source) \|<br>\| [Switch gateway](/docs/api/cards/switch-gateway)                             \| [Switch gateway account](/docs/api/payment_sources/switch-gateway-account) |» » invoice|body|[Invoice](#schemainvoice)|true|An invoice is a commercial document representing a sale of products/services offered by you to a customer. It enumerates all the charges, adjustments, payments, discounts and taxes associated with the sale.<br><br>An invoice is said to be a recurring one when it is has at least one charge for [a plan or an addon item price](/docs/api/items). It is a non-recurring one when it has charges for only charge-item prices or [one-time charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/charges.html).<br><br>The item prices for any given billing term of a subscription are billed via an invoice at the beginning of the term (unless the charges are left unbilled). However, item prices that belong to `metered` items are billed at the end of the term via a `pending` invoice that can [close automatically](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing#configuring-metered-billing) or via [an API call](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice). Moreover, when there are no `metered` items in the subscription, the invoices can still be generated as `pending` while [creating](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items) or [updating](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items) a subscription.<br><br>#### Auto-collection<br><br>If [auto-collection](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#auto-collection-status) is enabled, then immediately on invoice generation (or, in case of subscriptions that have `create_pending_invoices` as `true`, on [invoice closure](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice)), the [payment method](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#payment_method) on file is charged:<br><br>* If the payment succeeds, the invoice is marked as `paid`.<br>* On payment failure, the invoice is marked as `payment_due` and [dunning settings](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/dunning-v2.html) are taken into account for payment retries.<br>* If no retry attempts are configured, or when retries are exhausted, the invoice is marked as `not_paid`.<br>* the amount due is zero or negative, the invoice is immediately marked as `paid` and the balance, if any, is added to [excess payments](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#excess-payments) for the customer.<br><br>**Note:** If [consolidated invoicing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html) is enabled, the attribute `subscription_id` is unavailable when the invoice has line items from multiple subscriptions. The individual subscription ids are seen under `line_items.subscription_id`.  <br><br>#### Recurring and non-recurring invoices<br><br>A recurring invoice contains at least one line item that is billed on a recurring basis. Specifically, it has at least one [`line_items[]`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#line_items) with `entity_type` set to `plan_item_price` or `addon_item_price`. A non-recurring invoice contains no recurring line items.  <br><br>#### Refundable amount for an invoice<br><br>The refundable amount for an invoice is the (amount paid on the invoice + refundable credit applied on the invoice + taxes withheld on the invoice) minus (amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice). Each of these amounts is obtained from the invoice resource as follows:<br><br>* Amount paid on the invoice: [`amount_paid`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_amount_paid)<br>* Refundable credit applied on the invoice: [`credits_applied`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_credits_applied)<br>* Taxes withheld on the invoice: Sum of [`linked_taxes_withheld[].amount`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_linked_taxes_withheld)<br>* Amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice: Sum of [`issued_credit_notes[i].cn_total`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_issued_credit_notes) where `issued_credit_notes[i].cn_status` is `refunded` or `refund_due`.<br>|

Unlike subscriptions, one-time order items do not carry a recurring `status` field; cancellation is expressed via item `cancelled_at` / `cancellation_reason`.<br><br>**Apple App Store** : Parent `id_at_source` is the **Transaction ID** . Nested `purchase_transaction.id_at_source` is the same Transaction ID for the purchase row.<br><br>**Google Play Store** : Parent `id_at_source` is the **purchase token** . Nested `purchase_transaction.id_at_source` is the **Order ID** (`GPA....`).<br><br>See [omnichannel events](/docs/api/omnichannel_events) for recording and cancel mappings, and [`omnichannel_transaction`](/docs/api/omnichannel_transactions) for price / `transacted_at` guidance.  <br>**Note:**<br>This resource specifically represents in-app product purchases made via the Apple App Store and Google Play Store.<br>|
|» » omnichannel_one_time_order_item|body|[OmnichannelOneTimeOrderItem](#schemaomnichannelonetimeorderitem)|true|none|
|» » omnichannel_transaction|body|[OmnichannelTransaction](#schemaomnichanneltransaction)|true|A unified representation of a store purchase or renewal transaction across Apple App Store and Google Play Store.<br><br>Use `id_at_source` to correlate with the store-native transaction identifier:<br><br>* **Apple App Store** : App Store **Transaction ID**<br>* **Google Play Store** : Google Play **Order ID** (`GPA....`)<br><br>Parent subscription / one-time-order resources use purchase-token semantics for Google `id_at_source`; do not treat those as interchangeable with this transaction Order ID.<br><br>### Apple App Store<br><br>The [price](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appstoreservernotifications/price) value reflects the price you configured in App Store Connect, which the system records at the time of transaction ([transacted_at](/docs/api/omnichannel_transactions/omnichannel_transaction-object#transacted_at)) after the discount if any offers are applied.  <br>**Important**<br>For financial and accounting purposes, use the App Store Connect reporting tools. For more information, see [Download financial reports](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/getting-paid/download-financial-reports) and [Overview of reporting tools](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/measure-app-performance/overview-of-reporting-tools).<br>[Learn more](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appstoreservernotifications/price) about price in Apple App Store.<br><br>### Google Play Store<br><br>Google Play does not always expose a complete transaction amount or purchase time for every notification path. When Google provides price / time data for a transaction, Chargebee records `price_*` and `transacted_at`; otherwise these attributes may be absent. Some Google one-time-order samples include price and `transacted_at` on `purchase_transaction`.<br><br>Transactions can be linked to subscriptions and/or one-time orders via `linked_omnichannel_subscriptions` and `linked_omnichannel_one_time_orders`. Chargebee may also emit [`omnichannel_transaction_created`](/docs/api/events/webhook/omnichannel_transaction_created) when a new transaction row is recorded.<br>|

(Follow the links to learn more.)<br><br>* The value of the [`subscription.has_scheduled_changes`](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object#has_scheduled_changes) attribute.<br>* [Update subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items#impact-scheduled-changes)<br>* [Create Checkout for updating a subscription](/docs/api/hosted_pages/create-checkout-to-update-a-subscription#impact-scheduled-changes)<br>* [Remove scheduled changes](/docs/api/subscriptions/remove-scheduled-changes)<br>* [Retrieve with scheduled changes](/docs/api/subscriptions/retrieve-with-scheduled-changes)<br>* [Create a quote for updating a subscription](/docs/api/quotes/create-a-quote-for-update-subscription-items)<br>* [Edit a quote for updating a subscription](/docs/api/quotes/edit-update-subscription-quote-for-items)<br>* [Portal sessions](/docs/api/portal_sessions#scheduled-subscription-changes)<br>|
|» » customer|body|[Customer](#schemacustomer)|true|Represents a customer, which can be an individual or organization that subscribes to your products or services. The customer resource associates with [subscriptions](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object), [card information](/docs/api/cards/card-object), and billing addresses. The customer details include their ID, name, contact information, and any [custom attributes](/docs/api/advanced-features) you'd like to associate with them.  <br>**Breaking Change**:<br><br>* [**Sites**](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/sites-intro.html) **created before March 1, 2014** : [updating the card](/docs/api/cards/update-card-for-a-customer) deletes the customer's `billing_address` and `vat_number` and replaces them with values from the request.<br>* **Sites created on or after March 1, 2014** : updating the card doesn't change the `billing_address` and `vat_number`.<br>|

API at Card resource                             \|                                                                                                                                    Use instead \|<br>\|------------------------------------------------------------------------------\|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\|<br>\| [Retrieve card for a customer](/docs/api/cards/retrieve-card-for-a-customer) \| [Retrieve a payment source](/docs/api/payment_sources/retrieve-a-payment-source) customer](/docs/api/cards/update-card-for-a-customer)     \| * [Create using temporary token](/docs/api/payment_sources/create-using-gateway-temporary-token) * [Create using permanent token](/docs/api/payment_sources/create-using-permanent-token) * [Create a card payment source](/docs/api/payment_sources/create-a-card-payment-source) \|<br>\| [Switch gateway](/docs/api/cards/switch-gateway)                             \| [Switch gateway account](/docs/api/payment_sources/switch-gateway-account)                                                                                                                                                                                                         \|<br>\| [Copy card](/docs/api/cards/copy-card)                                       \| [Export payment source](/docs/api/payment_sources/export-payment-source)                                                                                                                                                                                                           \|<br>\| [Delete card for a customer](/docs/api/cards/delete-card-for-a-customer)     \| [Delete a payment source](/docs/api/payment_sources/delete-a-payment-source)                                                                                                                                                                                                       \|<br><br>|
|» » invoice|body|[Invoice](#schemainvoice)|true|An invoice is a commercial document representing a sale of products/services offered by you to a customer. It enumerates all the charges, adjustments, payments, discounts and taxes associated with the sale.<br><br>An invoice is said to be a recurring one when it is has at least one charge for [a plan or an addon item price](/docs/api/items). It is a non-recurring one when it has charges for only charge-item prices or [one-time charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/charges.html).<br><br>The item prices for any given billing term of a subscription are billed via an invoice at the beginning of the term (unless the charges are left unbilled). However, item prices that belong to `metered` items are billed at the end of the term via a `pending` invoice that can [close automatically](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing#configuring-metered-billing) or via [an API call](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice). Moreover, when there are no `metered` items in the subscription, the invoices can still be generated as `pending` while [creating](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items) or [updating](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items) a subscription.<br><br>#### Auto-collection<br><br>If [auto-collection](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#auto-collection-status) is enabled, then immediately on invoice generation (or, in case of subscriptions that have `create_pending_invoices` as `true`, on [invoice closure](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice)), the [payment method](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#payment_method) on file is charged:<br><br>* If the payment succeeds, the invoice is marked as `paid`.<br>* On payment failure, the invoice is marked as `payment_due` and [dunning settings](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/dunning-v2.html) are taken into account for payment retries.<br>* If no retry attempts are configured, or when retries are exhausted, the invoice is marked as `not_paid`.<br>* the amount due is zero or negative, the invoice is immediately marked as `paid` and the balance, if any, is added to [excess payments](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#excess-payments) for the customer.<br><br>**Note:** If [consolidated invoicing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html) is enabled, the attribute `subscription_id` is unavailable when the invoice has line items from multiple subscriptions. The individual subscription ids are seen under `line_items.subscription_id`.  <br><br>#### Recurring and non-recurring invoices<br><br>A recurring invoice contains at least one line item that is billed on a recurring basis. Specifically, it has at least one [`line_items[]`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#line_items) with `entity_type` set to `plan_item_price` or `addon_item_price`. A non-recurring invoice contains no recurring line items.  <br><br>#### Refundable amount for an invoice<br><br>The refundable amount for an invoice is the (amount paid on the invoice + refundable credit applied on the invoice + taxes withheld on the invoice) minus (amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice). Each of these amounts is obtained from the invoice resource as follows:<br><br>* Amount paid on the invoice: [`amount_paid`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_amount_paid)<br>* Refundable credit applied on the invoice: [`credits_applied`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_credits_applied)<br>* Taxes withheld on the invoice: Sum of [`linked_taxes_withheld[].amount`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_linked_taxes_withheld)<br>* Amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice: Sum of [`issued_credit_notes[i].cn_total`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_issued_credit_notes) where `issued_credit_notes[i].cn_status` is `refunded` or `refund_due`.<br>|

## Triggered when a business rule is deleted

<a id="opIdonBusiness_rule_deletedWebhook"></a>

`POST business_rule_deleted`

> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-business-rule-is-deleted-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[BusinessRuleDeletedEvent](#schemabusinessruledeletedevent)|false|Payload for business_rule_deleted event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » business_rule|body|[BusinessRule](#schemabusinessrule)|true|A business rule pairs a condition with the actions to take when that condition is met. You supply the context to evaluate, and Chargebee returns the actions configured in `actions_on_success` when the condition evaluates to `true`.<br><br>Business Rules APIs manage [CPQ Selling Rules](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/cpq/selling-rules).<br><br>The condition is defined in `structured_expression`, a JSON representation of the rule logic that visual editors and dynamic rule builders can both read and write. Chargebee validates and compiles the expression when the rule is created or updated, and evaluates the compiled form when you call [Apply business rules](/docs/api/business_rules/apply-business-rules).<br><br>The `field` of every condition is resolved against the context supplied at evaluation time, so the fields you reference must match the keys of the context the rule is evaluated against. A condition whose `field` is absent from the context never evaluates to `true`, which means the rule never matches.<br><br>Business rules are versioned. Creating a rule releases its first version, so `latest_version` is `1` and `released_at` is set from the outset. Editing a rule leaves that released version untouched: the first edit creates a draft, and every later edit updates the same draft. [Releasing](/docs/api/business_rules/release-a-business-rule) the draft promotes it to the next version number, and that version becomes the latest released version and the one Chargebee evaluates. Until you release it, the previously released version stays in effect, so a rule can keep serving traffic while its next version is being prepared.<br><br>The `active` attribute is an independent switch that controls whether Chargebee evaluates the rule at all. A rule is created inactive, so it has to be [activated](/docs/api/business_rules/activate-a-business-rule) before it takes effect.<br><br>Related rules can be grouped into a [business ruleset](/docs/api/business_rulesets), which evaluates its member rules in priority order using the strategy configured in the ruleset's `execute_mode`.<br><br>For a walkthrough that creates, activates, and applies a rule in three calls, take a look at the [Business Rules quickstart](https://www.chargebee.com/tutorials/business-rules-quickstart/).  <br>**Note:** Business rules are not enabled by default. Contact [Chargebee Support](https://www.chargebee.com/support/) to enable them for your site. Until they are enabled, these endpoints return an error.<br><br>Expressions<br>-----------<br><br>The `structured_expression` of a rule is a tree of nodes that evaluates to a single `true` or `false`. Every node carries a `type`, which determines the rest of the fields the node takes.<br><br>The following expression matches a quote from a customer whose language contains `en` and whose shipping country is India or the United States:<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "type": "GROUP",<br>  "operation": "AND",<br>  "children": [<br>    {<br>      "type": "CONDITION",<br>      "field": "customer.language",<br>      "operator": "CONTAINS",<br>      "value": "en"<br>    },<br>    {<br>      "type": "CONDITION",<br>      "field": "quote.shipping_address_country",<br>      "operator": "ANY_OF",<br>      "values": ["IN", "US"]<br>    }<br>  ]<br>}<br>```<br><br>Every condition is compiled so that it first tests whether the field is present in the context. A condition on a field that the context doesn't carry evaluates to `false` instead of failing, so the rule that holds it never matches and no `error_message` is returned for it.  <br><br>### GROUP node<br><br>Combines the nodes in `children` into a single result. Use a `GROUP` as the root of any expression that has more than one condition, and nest groups to control precedence.<br><br>* `operation`: **Required.** `AND` to match only if every child matches, or `OR` to match if any child matches.<br>* `children`: **Required.** An array holding at least one node. Each entry is itself a `GROUP`, `CONDITION`, or `COLLECTION` node.<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "type": "GROUP",<br>  "operation": "OR",<br>  "children": [<br>    {<br>      "type": "CONDITION",<br>      "field": "quote.payment_terms",<br>      "operator": "GREATER_THAN",<br>      "value": 30<br>    },<br>    {<br>      "type": "CONDITION",<br>      "field": "customer.billing_address_country",<br>      "operator": "EQUALS",<br>      "value": "US"<br>    }<br>  ]<br>}<br>```<br><br>### CONDITION node<br><br>Compares one field of the context against a value.<br><br>* `field`: **Required.** The path of the field through the context, such as `customer.language`. See [Context](/docs/api/business_rules#context) for the paths available.<br>* `operator`: **Required.** How the comparison is made. See [Operators](/docs/api/business_rules#operators) for the operators available and the field types each one compares.<br>* `value`: The single value to compare against. Required for the single-value operators.<br>* `values`: The array of values to compare against. Required for `BETWEEN`, `ANY_OF`, and `NONE_OF`.<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "type": "CONDITION",<br>  "field": "quote.contract_duration",<br>  "operator": "BETWEEN",<br>  "values": [12, 36]<br>}<br>```<br><br>### COLLECTION node<br><br>Tests the entries of an array in the context, such as the line items of a quote. All four fields are required.<br><br>* `field`: **Required.** The array to iterate over, such as `items`.<br>* `variable`: **Required.** The name each entry is bound to while the predicate is evaluated.<br>* `mode`: **Required.** `ANY` to match if at least one entry satisfies the predicate, or `NONE` to match only if no entry does.<br>* `predicate`: **Required.** The expression each entry is tested against, usually a `GROUP` node.<br><br>Inside the predicate, address the fields of an entry through the bound `variable`. The following node matches a quote that has at least one item discounted by more than 20:<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "type": "COLLECTION",<br>  "field": "items",<br>  "variable": "item",<br>  "mode": "ANY",<br>  "predicate": {<br>    "type": "GROUP",<br>    "operation": "AND",<br>    "children": [<br>      {<br>        "type": "CONDITION",<br>        "field": "item.discount",<br>        "operator": "GREATER_THAN",<br>        "value": 20<br>      }<br>    ]<br>  }<br>}<br>```<br><br>### Operators<br><br>The following operators are available. The field type is the type the operator can compare, and the value column shows whether the condition takes `value` or `values`.  <br><br>\|                                   Operator                                   \|       Field type        \|                                        Value                                        \|<br>\|------------------------------------------------------------------------------\|-------------------------\|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\|<br>\| `EQUALS`, `NOT_EQUALS`                                                       \| String, number, boolean \| `value`                                                                             \|<br>\| `GREATER_THAN`, `GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUALS`, `LESS_THAN`, `LESS_THAN_OR_EQUALS` \| Number                  \| `value`                                                                             \|<br>\| `BETWEEN`                                                                    \| Number                  \| `values`, holding exactly two entries, read as the inclusive lower and upper bounds \|<br>\| `CONTAINS`, `NOT_CONTAINS`                                                   \| String                  \| `value`                                                                             \|<br>\| `STARTS_WITH`                                                                \| String                  \| `value`                                                                             \|<br>\| `ANY_OF`, `NONE_OF`                                                          \| String, number, boolean \| `values`, holding at least one entry                                                \|<br><br>An operator used on a field of another type isn't rejected when the rule is saved, so the mismatch surfaces only when the rule is evaluated.<br><br>Context<br>-------<br><br>The `context` you pass to [Apply business rules](/docs/api/business_rules/apply-business-rules) isn't a free-form object. Its `type` selects the schema that the rest of the context is read as, and `CPQ` is the only type available, so a condition can reference only the fields of that schema. A key that falls outside the schema is dropped as the context is read, so a condition on it never evaluates to `true`. A misspelled or unsupported key therefore surfaces as an unmet condition rather than as an error.<br><br>A `CPQ` context carries `items`, `quote`, `customer`, `user`, `site`, and `quote_subscription`, each of them optional. Pass only the parts the rules you're evaluating need:<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "type": "CPQ",<br>  "customer": {<br>    "language": "en",<br>    "billing_address_country": "US"<br>  },<br>  "quote": {<br>    "shipping_address_country": "IN",<br>    "payment_terms": 30,<br>    "custom_fields": { "region": "apac" }<br>  },<br>  "items": [<br>    { "reference_id": "item-1", "amount": 5000, "quantity": 2, "discount": 10 },<br>    { "reference_id": "item-2", "amount": 1200, "quantity": 1, "discount": 0 }<br>  ]<br>}<br>```<br><br>A condition addresses a field by its path through the context, so `customer.language` reads the `language` of the `customer`. A `COLLECTION` node on `items` iterates over the entries of that array.<br><br>Each `custom_fields` object holds your own fields keyed by name, and every value must be a string, a number, or a boolean. A condition reads one through its key, as in `quote.custom_fields.region`.<br><br>The response returns the context back with `rule_ids` filled in on the quote and on each item, so you can see which rules applied where.  <br><br>### quote<br><br>* `type` and `contract_type`: strings.<br>* `contract_duration` and `payment_terms`: numbers.<br>* `billing_address_country` and `shipping_address_country`: strings.<br>* `billing_frequency` and `billing_currency`: strings.<br>* `creator_email` and `creator_role`: strings.<br>* `custom_fields`: object.<br>* `rule_ids`: array of strings. Returned in the response rather than passed, recording the rules that applied to the quote.  <br><br>### customer<br><br>* `billing_address_city`, `billing_address_state`, and `billing_address_country`: strings.<br>* `language`: string.<br>* `payment_terms`: number.<br>* `custom_fields`: object.  <br><br>### items<br><br>An array, with each entry holding the following.<br><br>* `reference_id`: string, identifying the entry within the context.<br>* `type`, `item_name`, and `product_family_name`: strings.<br>* `billing_frequency` and `currency`: strings.<br>* `billing_cycle`, `amount`, `quantity`, and `discount`: numbers.<br>* `start_date` and `end_date`: timestamps.<br>* `rule_ids`: array of strings. Returned in the response rather than passed, recording the rules that applied to that entry.  <br><br>### user<br><br>* `name`, `email`, and `phone`: strings.  <br><br>### site<br><br>* `name`, `domain`, and `currency`: strings.<br>* `sandbox`: boolean.  <br><br>### quote_subscription<br><br>* `custom_fields`: object.<br><br>Actions<br>-------<br><br>Every entry in `actions_on_success` is built from an **action template** , a built-in definition that fixes the kind of change an action makes and the parameters it accepts. An action names its template in `action_template_id` and passes that template's parameters in `input`:<br><br>```json<br>[<br>  {<br>    "action_template_id": "action-apply-discount",<br>    "input": {<br>      "apply_on": "INVOICE_AMOUNT",<br>      "discount": 12.0,<br>      "discount_type": "PERCENTAGE",<br>      "duration_type": "ONE_TIME"<br>    }<br>  }<br>]<br>```<br><br>The `type` of an action is derived from its template, so it's returned with the action but you don't have to pass it. A parameter that the template doesn't define is rejected. The values of enumerated parameters are matched without regard to case, and are returned in the `input` of the action exactly as you passed them.<br><br>An action can also carry a `structured_expression` of its own, written in the same format as the expression of the rule. The rule decides whether the action runs at all, and the action's own expression then narrows it to the items of the context that satisfy that expression. One rule can therefore discount some of the items it matched rather than all of them. Only the apply discount, limit discount, and limit quantity templates accept an action-level expression.  <br><br>### Apply discount<br><br>Applies a discount to the invoice amount or to specific item prices. Built from `action_template_id` `action-apply-discount` and returned with `type` `APPLY_DISCOUNT`.<br><br>* `apply_on`: **Required.** `INVOICE_AMOUNT` to discount the invoice total, or `SPECIFIC_ITEM_PRICE` to discount the item prices the action applies to.<br>* `discount`: **Required.** The discount to apply, such as `12.0`.<br>* `discount_type`: **Required.** `PERCENTAGE`, `FLAT_FEE`, or `OFFER_QUANTITY`, which fixes how `discount` is read.<br>* `duration_type`: **Required.** How long the discount applies, as `ONE_TIME`, `FOREVER`, or `LIMITED_PERIOD`.<br>* `period_unit`: `DAY`, `WEEK`, `MONTH`, or `YEAR`. Required if `duration_type` is `LIMITED_PERIOD`.<br>* `period`: The number of `period_unit`s the discount applies for. Required if `period_unit` is passed.  <br><br>### Apply coupon<br><br>Applies existing [coupons](/docs/api/coupons). Built from `action_template_id` `action-apply-coupon` and returned with `type` `APPLY_COUPON`.<br><br>* `apply_on`: **Required.** `INVOICE_AMOUNT` or `SPECIFIC_ITEM_PRICE`.<br>* `coupon_ids`: **Required.** The coupons to apply, as an array of coupon identifiers. It must hold at least one identifier.  <br><br>### Limit discount<br><br>Caps the discount that can be given. Use this template to enforce a discount ceiling without an approval step.<br><br>Built from `action_template_id` `action-limit-discount` and returned with `type` `LIMIT_DISCOUNT`.<br><br>* `apply_on`: **Required.** `INVOICE_AMOUNT` or `SPECIFIC_ITEM_PRICE`.<br>* `maximum_discount`: **Required.** The largest discount allowed, such as `20.0`.<br>* `discount_type`: **Required.** `PERCENTAGE`, `FLAT_FEE`, or `OFFER_QUANTITY`, which fixes how `maximum_discount` is read.<br>* `disable_price_override`: Pass `true` to disallow overriding the price outright.  <br><br>### Limit quantity<br><br>Constrains the quantities that can be selected. Built from `action_template_id` `action-limit-quantity` and returned with `type` `LIMIT_QUANTITY`. Every parameter is optional, so pass the ones you want to enforce.<br><br>* `minimum_quantity`: The smallest quantity allowed.<br>* `maximum_quantity`: The largest quantity allowed.<br>* `quantity_step_count`: The increment the quantity can be changed in, so `5` allows 5, 10, 15, and so on.  <br><br>### Error<br><br>Returns an error message instead of a change. Use this template to block an operation when the rule matches.<br><br>Built from `action_template_id` `action-error` and returned with `type` `ERROR`.<br><br>* `error_message`: **Required.** The message returned with the action.<br><br>Evaluation results<br>------------------<br><br>[Apply business rules](/docs/api/business_rules/apply-business-rules) returns an `apply_rule` object that echoes back the `context` you passed and carries one entry in `rules` for each rule it evaluated:<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "apply_rule": {<br>    "context": {<br>      "type": "CPQ",<br>      "customer": { "language": "en" },<br>      "quote": { "shipping_address_country": "IN" }<br>    },<br>    "rules": [<br>      {<br>        "id": "quote-discount-en",<br>        "version": 1,<br>        "name": "Apply 12 percent discount at invoice level",<br>        "evaluation_result": true,<br>        "actions": [<br>          {<br>            "action_template_id": "action-apply-discount",<br>            "type": "APPLY_DISCOUNT",<br>            "input": {<br>              "apply_on": "INVOICE_AMOUNT",<br>              "discount": 12.0,<br>              "discount_type": "PERCENTAGE",<br>              "duration_type": "ONE_TIME"<br>            }<br>          }<br>        ],<br>        "object": "applied_rule"<br>      },<br>      {<br>        "id": "quote-discount-uk",<br>        "version": 1,<br>        "name": "Apply 5 percent discount at invoice level for UK quotes",<br>        "evaluation_result": false,<br>        "object": "applied_rule"<br>      }<br>    ],<br>    "object": "apply_rule"<br>  }<br>}<br>```<br><br>Read the result of each rule from `evaluation_result`, and read what the rule produced from `actions`. Two things about the shape are worth knowing before you write code against it.<br><br>* `actions` is absent, rather than empty, for a rule whose `evaluation_result` is `false`. The second entry above shows a rule that didn't match.<br>* An entry for an ad hoc `structured_expression` carries only `evaluation_result`, because there's no stored rule to report an `id`, `name`, or `actions` for.<br><br>A rule that couldn't be evaluated is returned with `error_message` set instead, but only if you passed `skip_failed_rules` as `true`. Otherwise the request fails. For the full list of fields, see the response of [Apply business rules](/docs/api/business_rules/apply-business-rules).<br>|

|» content|body|object|true|none|

|» » metadata|body|[Metadata](#schemametadata)|true|none|
|» » impacted_item|body|[ImpactedItem](#schemaimpacteditem)|true|Item entitlements can change due to certain events in Chargebee. The impacted_items represents the items whose entitlements have changed owing to an event. It is returned as part of the content attribute of the webhook triggered by the event. The following events can contain the impacted_items resource:<br><br>* A feature is created, activated, or deleted.<br>* An item_entitlement is updated or removed.<br>* An entitlement_override is auto-removed.<br><br>**Note**<br><br>impacted_items cannot be retrieved via API; the resource is sent to you only via webhooks.<br>|
|» » impacted_subscription|body|[ImpactedSubscription](#schemaimpactedsubscription)|true|When certain [events](/docs/api/events) in Chargebee cause changes to [subscription entitlements](/docs/api/subscription_entitlements), the `impacted_subscriptions` resource indicates the affected subscriptions. [Contact Support](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/kb/getting-started/how-to-contact-chargebees-support-team?utm_source=docs_api&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=support) to increase this limit for your Chargebee site.<br>* You can't retrieve `impacted_subscriptions` through the API. Only webhooks send you this resource.<br>|

## Triggered when a business entity is created

<a id="opIdonBusiness_entity_createdWebhook"></a>

`POST business_entity_created`

Triggered when a business entity is created


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-business-entity-is-created-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[BusinessEntityCreatedEvent](#schemabusinessentitycreatedevent)|false|Payload for business_entity_created event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » business_entity|body|[BusinessEntity](#schemabusinessentity)|true|The `business_entity` resource represents a business unit or brand under your organization. Key resources in Chargebee Billing (such as [customer](/docs/api/customers), [subscriptions](/docs/api/subscriptions), [invoices](/docs/api/invoices), and [transactions](/docs/api/transactions)) along with the associated site configurations, fall under a [business entity](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/mbe.html). Each Chargebee Billing [site](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/sites-intro.html) has one business entity by default. You may create multiple business entities in the following scenarios:<br><br>* **Multiple Business Units**: You may be running your business under different regional units with different "invoice-from" addresses. This is usually done to manage taxation and bookkeeping. In such a case, you may create a business entity for each business unit.<br>* **Multiple Brands**: You may have multiple brands within your business, such as those acquired via mergers and acquisitions. You may create a business entity for each brand.<br><br>Creating multiple business entities lets you separate configuration and data for your business units or brands so that you can manage their billing and revenue operations independently.  <br>**See also**<br><br>[More information](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/mbe.html) on business entities and the configuration options available.  <br>Specifying business entity in API operations  <br>All API operations in Chargebee have site [context](/docs/api/business_entities). Context restrictions cannot be assigned to [API keys](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/api_keys.html). However, if your site has multiple business entities, you can specify the business entity [context](/docs/api/business_entities) for an API call by passing a [custom HTTP request header](/docs/api/advanced-features).  <br>API behavior based on business entity specified  <br>The table below explains how Chargebee responds to various API calls depending on whether the business entity ID is specified as part of the API call.  <br>**Note**<br><br>Some of the words used here are defined in the [Terminology section](/docs/api/business_entities).  <br><br>\|         **Operation/Type of operation**          \|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                **Behavior**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                \|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    **Examples**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    \|<br>\|--------------------------------------------------\|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\|<br>\| Any operation that creates a `customer` resource \| * If `business_entity_id` **is provided** , the `customer` resource is created and linked to it. * If `business_entity_id` **is not provided** , the `customer` resource is created under the [default business entity](/docs/api/business_entities) of the site.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          \| * [Create a customer](/docs/api/customers/create-a-customer) * When [Create a checkout for charge items and quick charge](/docs/api/hosted_pages/checkout-charge-items-and-one-time-charges)s or [Create checkout for a new subscription](/docs/api/hosted_pages/create-checkout-for-a-new-subscription) is called, providing a value for `customer[id]` that is not already present in the site. This creates a new `customer` resource.                                          \|<br>\| Create a resource other than `customer`          \| * If `business_entity_id` **is provided** , and it is the same as that [linked](/docs/api/business_entities) to the [target resource](/docs/api/business_entities): the resource is created and linked to the business entity provided. * If `business_entity_id` **is provided** , and it is not the same as that linked to the target resource, a `404 Not Found` response is sent because the resource cannot be found in the [context](/docs/api/business_entities) of the business entity specified. * If `business_entity_id` **is not provided**, the resource is created and linked to the business entity of the target resource. \| * [Create a subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items): the target resource is a `customer`. * [Create a comment](/docs/api/comments/create-a-comment): the target resource is specified in the value provided for `entity_type`. * [Create an invoice for items and one-time charges](/docs/api/invoices/create-invoice-for-items-and-one-time-charges): depending on the ID specified, the target resource is either a `customer` or a `subscription`. \|<br>\| Update/delete a resource                         \| * If `business_entity_id` **is provided** , and it is the same as that [linked](/docs/api/business_entities) to the resource, the operation proceeds successfully. * If `business_entity_id` **is provided** , and it is not the same as that [linked](/docs/api/business_entities) to the resource, a `404 Not Found` response is sent because the resource cannot be found in the [context](/docs/api/business_entities) of the business entity specified. * If `business_entity_id` **is not provided**, the operation proceeds successfully.                                                                                           \| * [Update a customer](/docs/api/customers/update-a-customer) * [Update a subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items) * [Update a card payment source](/docs/api/payment_sources/update-a-card-payment-source)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             \|<br>\| List resources                                   \| * If `business_entity_id` **is provided,** then only those resources linked to the business entity are returned since the [context](/docs/api/business_entities) of the operation is now restricted to the business entity specified. * If `business_entity_id` **is not provided**, then all resources in the site are returned.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          \| * [List customers](/docs/api/customers/list-customers) * [List payment sources](/docs/api/payment_sources/list-payment-sources)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    \|<br>\| Retreive a resource                              \| * If `business_entity_id` **is provided** , and it is the same as that [linked](/docs/api/business_entities) to the resource, the resource is retrieved successfully. * If `business_entity_id` **is provided** , and it is not the same as that [linked](/docs/api/business_entities) to the resource, a `404 Not Found` response is sent because the resource cannot be found in the [context](/docs/api/business_entities) of the business entity specified. * If `business_entity_id` **is not provided**, the resource is retrieved successfully.                                                                                     \| * [Retrieve a customer](/docs/api/customers/retrieve-a-customer) * [Retrieve a comment](/docs/api/comments/retrieve-a-comment)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     \|<br><br>Terminology  <br>This section defines some useful terms for describing how business entities work.<br><br>#### Linked business entity {#mbe-terms-content}<br><br>Any resource is always associated with precisely one and only one business entity. We call it the linked business entity of the resource, or simply, the business entity of the resource.<br><br>#### Default business entity<br><br>When `customer` resource is created and no business entity is specified, it is linked to the business entity designated as the default business entity of the site. A site always has a default business entity. Please choose the first business entity details carefully, as it can't be changed later, and this will be your default entity when no business entity is specified.<br><br>#### Context of an operation<br><br>Any site has data in it. This includes all the various resources such as customers, subscriptions, invoices, comments, and so on. The "context" of an API operation is the subset of site data it has access to. An API operation can only read or write data within its context. By default, an API operation has "site context", which means it has access to the entire site's data. However, when a business entity is [specified](/docs/api/business_entities) in an API operation, it has "business entity context", which means that the operation only has access to the data linked to the business entity.  <br>**Example**<br><br>Consider the [List customers API](/docs/api/customers/list-customers). When you call the API without specifying a business entity, its context is that of the site and therefore returns customer resources for the entire site. However, when you specify a business entity, the context is only that of the business entity, and therefore the customer resources of only the selected business entity are returned.<br><br>Let's look at the [Create checkout for a new subscription API](/docs/api/hosted_pages/create-checkout-for-a-new-subscription). Say you're calling this API and providing the `customer[id]` parameter. When no business entity is specified, the operation has *site context* and therefore looks up the ID among all the customer resources in the site. However, when a business entity is provided, the operation has *business entity context* and looks up the ID only among the customers linked to that business entity.<br><br>#### Target resource<br><br>While creating an API resource other than a `customer`, you specify a target resource under which it should be created. For example:<br><br>* While [creating an `invoice` resource for a one-time charge](/docs/api/invoices/create-invoice-for-items-and-one-time-charges), you must specify either the `customer` or the `subscription` resource to which it belongs. The `customer` or `subscription` resource, in this case, is the target resource of the `invoice`.<br>* While [creating a `subscription`](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items), the target resource of a `subscription` resource is always a `customer` resource.<br>* While [creating a `quote` resource of `type` `change_subscription`](/docs/api/quotes/create-a-quote-for-update-subscription-items), the target resource is a `subscription` resource.<br>|

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Webhook received successfully|None|

the Chargebee app, see [Discounts API](/docs/api/discounts)<br><br>Order of application of coupons and discounts<br>---------------------------------------------<br><br>When both [coupons](/docs/api/coupons) and [discounts](/docs/api/discounts) are applied simultaneously to a [subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions) or [one-time invoice](/docs/api/invoices/create-invoice-for-items-and-one-time-charges), they're applied in the following order:  <br><br>\|---\|---------------------------------------\|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\|<br>\|   \| **Summary**                           \| **Description**                                                                     \|<br>\| 1 \| Line-level, fixed amount coupons      \| `coupon` with `apply_on` = `each_specified_item` and `discount_type` = `flat`       \|<br>\| 2 \| Line-level, fixed amount discounts    \| `discount` with `apply_on` = `specific_item_price` and `type` = `fixed_amount`      \|<br>\| 3 \| Line-level, percentage coupons        \| `coupon` with `apply_on` = `each_specified_item` and `discount_type` = `percentage` \|<br>\| 4 \| Line-level, percentage discounts      \| `discount` with `apply_on` = `specific_item_price` and `type` = `percentage`        \|<br>\| 5 \| Invoice-level, fixed amount coupons   \| `coupon` with `apply_on` = `invoice_amount` and `discount_type` = `flat`            \|<br>\| 6 \| Invoice-level, fixed amount discounts \| `discount` with `apply_on` = `invoice_amount` and `type` = `fixed_amount`           \|<br>\| 7 \| Invoice-level, percentage coupons     \| `coupon` with `apply_on` = `invoice_amount` and `discount_type` = `percentage`      \|<br>\| 8 \| Invoice-level, percentage discounts   \| `discount` with `apply_on` = `invoice_amount` and `type` = `percentage`             \|<br><br>For example, consider the following scenario:<br><br>A subscription is created with:<br><br>* a plan price of $200 per month<br>* an addon price of $20 per month<br>* a flat $5 invoice discount<br>* a 1% off coupon on the addon<br>* a flat $2 coupon on the invoice<br><br>The above coupons and discount are applied in the following order:  <br><br>\|---\|---------------------------------------------\|-----------------------------------------------\|<br>\|   \| **Discount or coupon applied**              \| **Subtotal at each step**                     \|<br>\| 1 \| Initial subtotal (plan price + addon price) \| $200 + $20 = $220                             \|<br>\| 2 \| 1% off coupon on the addon                  \| $200 + $(20 - 0.02) = $200 + $19.98 = $219.98 \|<br>\| 3 \| Flat $2 coupon on the invoice               \| $219.98 - $2 = $217.98                        \|<br>\| 4 \| Flat $5 invoice discount                    \| $217.98 - $5 = **$212.98**                    \|<br><br>|

|» » invoice|body|[Invoice](#schemainvoice)|true|An invoice is a commercial document representing a sale of products/services offered by you to a customer. It enumerates all the charges, adjustments, payments, discounts and taxes associated with the sale.<br><br>An invoice is said to be a recurring one when it is has at least one charge for [a plan or an addon item price](/docs/api/items). It is a non-recurring one when it has charges for only charge-item prices or [one-time charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/charges.html).<br><br>The item prices for any given billing term of a subscription are billed via an invoice at the beginning of the term (unless the charges are left unbilled). However, item prices that belong to `metered` items are billed at the end of the term via a `pending` invoice that can [close automatically](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing#configuring-metered-billing) or via [an API call](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice). Moreover, when there are no `metered` items in the subscription, the invoices can still be generated as `pending` while [creating](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items) or [updating](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items) a subscription.<br><br>#### Auto-collection<br><br>If [auto-collection](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#auto-collection-status) is enabled, then immediately on invoice generation (or, in case of subscriptions that have `create_pending_invoices` as `true`, on [invoice closure](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice)), the [payment method](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#payment_method) on file is charged:<br><br>* If the payment succeeds, the invoice is marked as `paid`.<br>* On payment failure, the invoice is marked as `payment_due` and [dunning settings](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/dunning-v2.html) are taken into account for payment retries.<br>* If no retry attempts are configured, or when retries are exhausted, the invoice is marked as `not_paid`.<br>* the amount due is zero or negative, the invoice is immediately marked as `paid` and the balance, if any, is added to [excess payments](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#excess-payments) for the customer.<br><br>**Note:** If [consolidated invoicing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html) is enabled, the attribute `subscription_id` is unavailable when the invoice has line items from multiple subscriptions. The individual subscription ids are seen under `line_items.subscription_id`.  <br><br>#### Recurring and non-recurring invoices<br><br>A recurring invoice contains at least one line item that is billed on a recurring basis. Specifically, it has at least one [`line_items[]`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#line_items) with `entity_type` set to `plan_item_price` or `addon_item_price`. A non-recurring invoice contains no recurring line items.  <br><br>#### Refundable amount for an invoice<br><br>The refundable amount for an invoice is the (amount paid on the invoice + refundable credit applied on the invoice + taxes withheld on the invoice) minus (amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice). Each of these amounts is obtained from the invoice resource as follows:<br><br>* Amount paid on the invoice: [`amount_paid`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_amount_paid)<br>* Refundable credit applied on the invoice: [`credits_applied`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_credits_applied)<br>* Taxes withheld on the invoice: Sum of [`linked_taxes_withheld[].amount`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_linked_taxes_withheld)<br>* Amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice: Sum of [`issued_credit_notes[i].cn_total`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_issued_credit_notes) where `issued_credit_notes[i].cn_status` is `refunded` or `refund_due`.<br>|

|» » advance_invoice_schedule|body|[AdvanceInvoiceSchedule](#schemaadvanceinvoiceschedule)|true|The invoice for a subscription in Chargebee is generated at the time of subscription renewal. Invoices can also be [generated in advance](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/advance-invoices.html) for an upcoming renewal or set of renewals. With Advance Invoicing Schedules, you can set up a plan for when such advance invoices are generated for the lifetime of the subscription. This helps you:<br><br>* Set up a contract with your customers so that they can be notified of their payment schedules in advance.<br>* Allow customers who make offline payments to be alerted about their upcoming dues well ahead of actual subscription renewals.<br>* Prevent post-renewal unpaid usage of your services by customers.<br><br>Advance invoices can be scheduled in two ways:<br><br>#### Specific Dates Schedule<br><br>Advance invoices for a subscription can be scheduled to be generated on specific [dates](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#specific_dates_schedule_date) in the future. You must specify the [number of billing cycles](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#specific_dates_schedule_terms_to_charge) to be invoiced on each date. A maximum of 5 dates can be specified.<br><br>#### Fixed Interval Schedule<br><br>Advance invoices can be scheduled to be generated at fixed intervals of time, where each interval spans the same number of billing cycles of the subscription. The invoice for each interval is generated a specified number of days ([`days_before_interval`](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#fixed_interval_schedule_days_before_renewal)) before the start of the interval. You can configure the schedule to end on a certain date or after a specified number of advance invoices have been generated.<br><br>The start date of the first interval depends on the number of days remaining from current time till the next renewal of the subscription. If this is more than `days_before_interval`, the interval begins at the next renewal. On the other hand, if the number of days remaining before the next renewal is less than `days_before_interval`, the first interval begins at the renewal following the next.<br>|

|» » advance_invoice_schedule|body|[AdvanceInvoiceSchedule](#schemaadvanceinvoiceschedule)|true|The invoice for a subscription in Chargebee is generated at the time of subscription renewal. Invoices can also be [generated in advance](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/advance-invoices.html) for an upcoming renewal or set of renewals. With Advance Invoicing Schedules, you can set up a plan for when such advance invoices are generated for the lifetime of the subscription. This helps you:<br><br>* Set up a contract with your customers so that they can be notified of their payment schedules in advance.<br>* Allow customers who make offline payments to be alerted about their upcoming dues well ahead of actual subscription renewals.<br>* Prevent post-renewal unpaid usage of your services by customers.<br><br>Advance invoices can be scheduled in two ways:<br><br>#### Specific Dates Schedule<br><br>Advance invoices for a subscription can be scheduled to be generated on specific [dates](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#specific_dates_schedule_date) in the future. You must specify the [number of billing cycles](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#specific_dates_schedule_terms_to_charge) to be invoiced on each date. A maximum of 5 dates can be specified.<br><br>#### Fixed Interval Schedule<br><br>Advance invoices can be scheduled to be generated at fixed intervals of time, where each interval spans the same number of billing cycles of the subscription. The invoice for each interval is generated a specified number of days ([`days_before_interval`](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#fixed_interval_schedule_days_before_renewal)) before the start of the interval. You can configure the schedule to end on a certain date or after a specified number of advance invoices have been generated.<br><br>The start date of the first interval depends on the number of days remaining from current time till the next renewal of the subscription. If this is more than `days_before_interval`, the interval begins at the next renewal. On the other hand, if the number of days remaining before the next renewal is less than `days_before_interval`, the first interval begins at the renewal following the next.<br>|

## Triggered when a gift is claimed.

<a id="opIdonGift_claimedWebhook"></a>

`POST gift_claimed`

Triggered when a gift is claimed.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-gift-is-claimed-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[GiftClaimedEvent](#schemagiftclaimedevent)|false|Payload for gift_claimed event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » gift|body|[Gift](#schemagift)|true|Gift represents a subscription of a customer(**recipient** ) to a 'gift plan' which has been gifted by another customer(**gifter**). It may also have addons and coupons. Gift will be created only on immediate successful payment collection from the gifter's payment method.<br><br>Gift is initially created in '**scheduled** ' state. The gift can be scheduled to be notified on a particular date to the recipient by passing 'scheduled_at'. If not, the recipient is notified immediately. Gift will be moved to '**unclaimed** ' state on the date of notification. If you pass auto_claim as true, gift status will be moved to '**claimed**' immediately, otherwise, the gift will remain 'unclaimed' till the recipient claims the gift.<br><br>If the gift is not claimed before the claim_expiry_date, it will be moved to the '**expired**' state.<br><br>#### GIFT SUBSCRIPTION<br><br>Gift subscriptions will be created in '**future** ' state. Once the gift is claimed, the subscription will be moved to '**non-renewing**' state.<br><br>#### INVOICE<br><br>Gift subscriptions will be invoiced immediately. The invoice created has **is_gifted** as 'true' and **term_finalized** as 'false'. This is because initially the invoice term_start and term_end are set as the subscription's start_date till the end of the plan period. Once the gift is claimed, the invoice's term_finalized will be marked as 'true'. The term_start will be changed to the actual invoice's term, which is the gift-claim date and the term_end will be changed till plan's period.<br>|

|200|OK|Webhook received successfully|None|
