## Triggered when a refund is initiated via direct debit.

<a id="opIdonRefund_initiatedWebhook"></a>

`POST refund_initiated`

Triggered when a refund is initiated using the `direct_debit` payment method, or when a transaction enters the `in_progress` status due to asynchronous processing at the payment gateway.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-refund-is-initiated-via-direct-debit-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[RefundInitiatedEvent](#schemarefundinitiatedevent)|false|Payload for refund_initiated event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » transaction|body|[Transaction](#schematransaction)|true|This resource represents the [transaction](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/transactions.html)<br>event that has happened in your account.<br>|
|» » invoice|body|[Invoice](#schemainvoice)|true|An invoice is a commercial document representing a sale of products/services offered by you to a customer. It enumerates all the charges, adjustments, payments, discounts and taxes associated with the sale.<br><br>An invoice is said to be a recurring one when it is has at least one charge for [a plan or an addon item price](/docs/api/items). It is a non-recurring one when it has charges for only charge-item prices or [one-time charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/charges.html).<br><br>The item prices for any given billing term of a subscription are billed via an invoice at the beginning of the term (unless the charges are left unbilled). However, item prices that belong to `metered` items are billed at the end of the term via a `pending` invoice that can [close automatically](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing#configuring-metered-billing) or via [an API call](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice). Moreover, when there are no `metered` items in the subscription, the invoices can still be generated as `pending` while [creating](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items) or [updating](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items) a subscription.<br><br>#### Auto-collection<br><br>If [auto-collection](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#auto-collection-status) is enabled, then immediately on invoice generation (or, in case of subscriptions that have `create_pending_invoices` as `true`, on [invoice closure](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice)), the [payment method](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#payment_method) on file is charged:<br><br>* If the payment succeeds, the invoice is marked as `paid`.<br>* On payment failure, the invoice is marked as `payment_due` and [dunning settings](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/dunning-v2.html) are taken into account for payment retries.<br>* If no retry attempts are configured, or when retries are exhausted, the invoice is marked as `not_paid`.<br>* the amount due is zero or negative, the invoice is immediately marked as `paid` and the balance, if any, is added to [excess payments](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#excess-payments) for the customer.<br><br>**Note:** If [consolidated invoicing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html) is enabled, the attribute `subscription_id` is unavailable when the invoice has line items from multiple subscriptions. The individual subscription ids are seen under `line_items.subscription_id`.  <br><br>#### Recurring and non-recurring invoices<br><br>A recurring invoice contains at least one line item that is billed on a recurring basis. Specifically, it has at least one [`line_items[]`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#line_items) with `entity_type` set to `plan_item_price` or `addon_item_price`. A non-recurring invoice contains no recurring line items.  <br><br>#### Refundable amount for an invoice<br><br>The refundable amount for an invoice is the (amount paid on the invoice + refundable credit applied on the invoice + taxes withheld on the invoice) minus (amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice). Each of these amounts is obtained from the invoice resource as follows:<br><br>* Amount paid on the invoice: [`amount_paid`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_amount_paid)<br>* Refundable credit applied on the invoice: [`credits_applied`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_credits_applied)<br>* Taxes withheld on the invoice: Sum of [`linked_taxes_withheld[].amount`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_linked_taxes_withheld)<br>* Amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice: Sum of [`issued_credit_notes[i].cn_total`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_issued_credit_notes) where `issued_credit_notes[i].cn_status` is `refunded` or `refund_due`.<br>|
|» » credit_note|body|[CreditNote](#schemacreditnote)|true|A [Credit Note](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/credit-notes.html) is a document that specifies the money owed by a business to its customer. The seller usually issues a Credit Note for the same or lower amount than the invoice, and then repays the money to the customer or set it off against other 'due' invoices.<br><br>### Credit Note Types<br><br>Credit notes in Chargebee are categorized into three types:<br>1. `adjustment`: Adjustment credit notes are used to adjust the amount of an existing invoice in the `payment_due` or `not_paid` [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status). Use this type of credit note to reduce the invoice amount, typically as a discount to the customer.<br><br>Adjustment credit notes are automatically created in the following cases:<br><br>* When an invoice is written off.<br>* When a subscription is modified with proration enabled, and the invoice for the current term is in the `payment_due` or `not_paid` [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status). 2. `refundable`: Refundable credit notes allow you to return a certain amount to the customer. These credits can be:<br>* Retained for automatic application on future invoices.<br>* Applied to existing unpaid invoices.<br>* Refunded to the customer. Refundable credit notes are automatically created in the following cases:<br>* When an invoice is refunded.<br>* When a subscription is changed or canceled with proration enabled, the invoice for the current term is in the `paid` [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status). Refundable credits are applied to future invoices or can be refunded to the original payment method. 3. `store`: Store credit notes are created for `paid` or `partially_paid` invoice [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status) during subscription changes, such as upgrades, downgrades, or cancellations. Key characteristics of store credits:<br>* No tax component is included at the time of creation.<br>* A credit note document is generated, similar to refundable credits.<br>* Store credits are applied before tax calculations on future invoices.<br><br>**Note:**<br>If you have enabled *consolidated invoicing*<br>, to know the subscriptions attached with a credit note you have to refer [line_item's](/docs/api/credit_notes/credit_note-object#line_items)<br>*subscription_id*<br>. The credit note's *subscription_id*<br>should **not**<br>be used (which will be *null*<br>if the credit note has lines from multiple subscriptions).  <br>Impact on reference invoice  <br>The following updates are made to the reference invoice when a credit note is created/imported:<br><br>* If the credit note `type` is `adjustment`:<br>  * The adjustment credit note details are added to the `adjustment_credit_notes[]` attribute of the invoice.<br>  * The invoice `amount_due` is reduced by the credit note `total`.<br>  * The invoice `status` is updated to `paid` if the invoice `amount_due` equals the credit note `total`.<br>  * The invoice `status` does not change if the invoice `amount_due` is greater than credit note `total`.<br>* If the credit note `type` is `refundable`:<br>  * The refundable credit note details are added to the `issued_credit_notes[]` attribute of the invoice.<br>  * The invoice `status` does not change.<br>* If the credit note `type` is `store`:<br>  * The store credit note details are added to the `issued_credit_notes[]` attribute of the invoice.<br>  * The invoice `status` does not change.<br>|
|» » customer|body|[Customer](#schemacustomer)|true|Represents a customer, which can be an individual or organization that subscribes to your products or services. The customer resource associates with [subscriptions](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object), [card information](/docs/api/cards/card-object), and billing addresses. The customer details include their ID, name, contact information, and any [custom attributes](/docs/api/advanced-features) you'd like to associate with them.  <br>**Breaking Change**:<br><br>* [**Sites**](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/sites-intro.html) **created before March 1, 2014** : [updating the card](/docs/api/cards/update-card-for-a-customer) deletes the customer's `billing_address` and `vat_number` and replaces them with values from the request.<br>* **Sites created on or after March 1, 2014** : updating the card doesn't change the `billing_address` and `vat_number`.<br>|
|» » subscription|body|[Subscription](#schemasubscription)|true|A Chargebee subscription connects a customer record to products/services. It describes what the customer has signed up for and how often they're charged for it. The essential components of a subscription are:<br><br>* A [plan-item price](/docs/api/item_prices).<br>* Any addon- and charge-item prices applied to the subscription.<br>* Any [coupons](/docs/api/coupons) applied.<br>* Any [discounts](/docs/api/discounts) applied.<br><br>The charges in a subscription are billed via invoices.  <br>**Note:**<br>The maximum number of subscriptions for any given [customer](/docs/api/customers)<br>([active](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object#status)<br>or not) is 900.  <br><br>#### Subscription billing frequencies<br><br>Chargebee offers two billing frequency options for subscriptions:<br><br>* **Plan-based billing** (`default`): Subscriptions are billed based on the billing period defined for the item price of the `item_type` `plan`. [Learn more](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/subscriptions#plan-based-billing).<br><br>* **Multi-frequency billing** : Subscriptions are billed according to the billing period of each recurring item price within the subscription. [Learn more](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/multi-frequency-billing).<br><br>  **Important**<br><br>  [Limitations](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/multi-frequency-billing#limitations) of Multi-frequency billing.<br><br>The selection of the billing frequency preference is configured at the site level.  <br><br>#### Item price compatibility in a subscription<br><br>When creating or updating a subscription, one of the item prices specified under subscription_items must be a plan-item price. The remaining must be compatible addon- or charge-item prices. An item price is compatible with a plan-item price if their currencies are the same. Additionally, an addon-item price is compatible with a plan-item price only if their billing frequencies meet the following conditions:  <br><br>\| `period_unit` for plan-item price \| Compatible `period_unit` for addon-item price \|                                                                                                                                                                                                Compatible period for addon-item price                                                                                                                                                                                                \|<br>\|-----------------------------------\|-----------------------------------------------\|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\|<br>\| `day`                             \| `day`                                         \| The `period` of the plan-item price should be divisible by the `period` of the addon-item price. **Example** If the `period` of the plan-item price is `10`, then the period of the addon-item price can be `10`, `5`, `2`, or `1`.                                                                                                                                                                                                  \|<br>\| `week`                            \| `week` or `day`                               \| The `period` (in days) of the plan-item price should be divisible by the `period` of the addon-item price. **Example** If the `period` of the plan-item price is `2`, then the period of the addon-item price can be as follows depending on the value of `period_unit`: * for `period_unit` as `week`, `period` can be `2` or `1`. * for `period_unit` as `day`, `period` can be `14`, `7`, `2`, or `1`.                            \|<br>\| `month`                           \| `month`                                       \| The `period` of the plan-item price should be divisible by the `period` of the addon-item price. **Example** If the `period` of the plan-item price is `6`, then the `period` of the addon-item price can be `6`, `3`, `2`, or `1`. price is `2`, then the `period` of the addon-item price can be as follows depending on the value of `period_unit`: * for `period_unit` as `year`, `period` can be `2` or `1`. * for `period_unit` as ## Triggered when an invoice has been created with date set to a value in the past. However, if the invoice is created with a pending status and the site setting is to set invoice.date to the date of closing the invoice, this event is never triggered.

<a id="opIdonInvoice_generated_with_backdatingWebhook"></a>

`POST invoice_generated_with_backdating`

Triggered when an invoice has been created with date set to a value in the past. However, if the invoice is created with a pending status and the site setting is to set invoice.date to the date of closing the invoice, this event is never triggered.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-an-invoice-has-been-created-with-date-set-to-a-value-in-the-past-however-if-the-invoice-is-created-with-a-pending-status-and-the-site-setting-is-to-set-invoicedate-to-the-date-of-closing-the-invoice-this-event-is-never-triggered-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[InvoiceGeneratedWithBackdatingEvent](#schemainvoicegeneratedwithbackdatingevent)|false|Payload for invoice_generated_with_backdating event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » invoice|body|[Invoice](#schemainvoice)|true|An invoice is a commercial document representing a sale of products/services offered by you to a customer. It enumerates all the charges, adjustments, payments, discounts and taxes associated with the sale.<br><br>An invoice is said to be a recurring one when it is has at least one charge for [a plan or an addon item price](/docs/api/items). It is a non-recurring one when it has charges for only charge-item prices or [one-time charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/charges.html).<br><br>The item prices for any given billing term of a subscription are billed via an invoice at the beginning of the term (unless the charges are left unbilled). However, item prices that belong to `metered` items are billed at the end of the term via a `pending` invoice that can [close automatically](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing#configuring-metered-billing) or via [an API call](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice). Moreover, when there are no `metered` items in the subscription, the invoices can still be generated as `pending` while [creating](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items) or [updating](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items) a subscription.<br><br>#### Auto-collection<br><br>If [auto-collection](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#auto-collection-status) is enabled, then immediately on invoice generation (or, in case of subscriptions that have `create_pending_invoices` as `true`, on [invoice closure](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice)), the [payment method](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#payment_method) on file is charged:<br><br>* If the payment succeeds, the invoice is marked as `paid`.<br>* On payment failure, the invoice is marked as `payment_due` and [dunning settings](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/dunning-v2.html) are taken into account for payment retries.<br>* If no retry attempts are configured, or when retries are exhausted, the invoice is marked as `not_paid`.<br>* the amount due is zero or negative, the invoice is immediately marked as `paid` and the balance, if any, is added to [excess payments](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#excess-payments) for the customer.<br><br>**Note:** If [consolidated invoicing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html) is enabled, the attribute `subscription_id` is unavailable when the invoice has line items from multiple subscriptions. The individual subscription ids are seen under `line_items.subscription_id`.  <br><br>#### Recurring and non-recurring invoices<br><br>A recurring invoice contains at least one line item that is billed on a recurring basis. Specifically, it has at least one [`line_items[]`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#line_items) with `entity_type` set to `plan_item_price` or `addon_item_price`. A non-recurring invoice contains no recurring line items.  <br><br>#### Refundable amount for an invoice<br><br>The refundable amount for an invoice is the (amount paid on the invoice + refundable credit applied on the invoice + taxes withheld on the invoice) minus (amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice). Each of these amounts is obtained from the invoice resource as follows:<br><br>* Amount paid on the invoice: [`amount_paid`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_amount_paid)<br>* Refundable credit applied on the invoice: [`credits_applied`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_credits_applied)<br>* Taxes withheld on the invoice: Sum of [`linked_taxes_withheld[].amount`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_linked_taxes_withheld)<br>* Amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice: Sum of [`issued_credit_notes[i].cn_total`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_issued_credit_notes) where `issued_credit_notes[i].cn_status` is `refunded` or `refund_due`.<br>|

`POST omnichannel_transaction_created`

Triggered when an omnichannel transaction is created.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-an-omnichannel-transaction-is-created-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[OmnichannelTransactionCreatedEvent](#schemaomnichanneltransactioncreatedevent)|false|Payload for omnichannel_transaction_created event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » omnichannel_transaction|body|[OmnichannelTransaction](#schemaomnichanneltransaction)|true|A unified representation of a store purchase or renewal transaction across Apple App Store and Google Play Store.<br><br>Use `id_at_source` to correlate with the store-native transaction identifier:<br><br>* **Apple App Store** : App Store **Transaction ID**<br>* **Google Play Store** : Google Play **Order ID** (`GPA....`)<br><br>Parent subscription / one-time-order resources use purchase-token semantics for Google `id_at_source`; do not treat those as interchangeable with this transaction Order ID.<br><br>### Apple App Store<br><br>The [price](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appstoreservernotifications/price) value reflects the price you configured in App Store Connect, which the system records at the time of transaction ([transacted_at](/docs/api/omnichannel_transactions/omnichannel_transaction-object#transacted_at)) after the discount if any offers are applied.  <br>**Important**<br>For financial and accounting purposes, use the App Store Connect reporting tools. For more information, see [Download financial reports](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/getting-paid/download-financial-reports) and [Overview of reporting tools](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/measure-app-performance/overview-of-reporting-tools).<br>[Learn more](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appstoreservernotifications/price) about price in Apple App Store.<br><br>### Google Play Store<br><br>Google Play does not always expose a complete transaction amount or purchase time for every notification path. When Google provides price / time data for a transaction, Chargebee records `price_*` and `transacted_at`; otherwise these attributes may be absent. Some Google one-time-order samples include price and `transacted_at` on `purchase_transaction`.<br><br>Transactions can be linked to subscriptions and/or one-time orders via `linked_omnichannel_subscriptions` and `linked_omnichannel_one_time_orders`. Chargebee may also emit [`omnichannel_transaction_created`](/docs/api/events/webhook/omnichannel_transaction_created) when a new transaction row is recorded.<br>|

Additionally, an addon-item price is compatible with a plan-item price only if their billing frequencies meet the following conditions:  <br><br>\| `period_unit` for plan-item price \| Compatible `period_unit` for addon-item price \|                                                                                                                                                                                                Compatible period for addon-item price                                                                                                                                                                                                \|<br>\|-----------------------------------\|-----------------------------------------------\|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\|<br>\| `day`                             \| `day`                                         \| The `period` of the plan-item price should be divisible by the `period` of the addon-item price. **Example** If the `period` of the plan-item price is `10`, then the period of the addon-item price can be `10`, `5`, `2`, or `1`.                                                                                                                                                                                                  \|<br>\| `week`                            \| `week` or `day`                               \| The `period` (in days) of the plan-item price should be divisible by the `period` of the addon-item price. **Example** If the `period` of the plan-item price is `2`, then the period of the addon-item price can be as follows depending on the value of `period_unit`: * for `period_unit` as `week`, `period` can be `2` or `1`. * for `period_unit` as `day`, `period` can be `14`, `7`, `2`, or `1`.                            \|<br>\| `month`                           \| `month`                                       \| The `period` of the plan-item price should be divisible by the `period` of the addon-item price. **Example** If the `period` of the plan-item price is `6`, then the `period` of the addon-item price can be `6`, `3`, `2`, or `1`.                                                                                                                                                                                                  \|<br>\| `year`                            \| `year` or `month`                             \| The `period` (in months) of the plan-item price should be divisible by the `period` of the addon-item price. **Example** If the `period` of the plan-item price is `2`, then the `period` of the addon-item price can be as follows depending on the value of `period_unit`: * for `period_unit` as `year`, `period` can be `2` or `1`. * for `period_unit` as It also defines the entitlements that items and subscriptions can have towards said features.  <br>**Note**<br><br>The maximum number of features a site can have is 400.<br><br>Features of this API<br>--------------------<br><br>The Features API enables you to:<br><br>* Define the set of features provided by your product.<br>* Specify the entitlements that items have towards said features.<br>* For a given subscription, modify the entitlements inherited from items in the subscription.<br>* Offer additional feature entitlements to subscriptions than those inherited from items in the subscription.<br>* Serve as a source of truth to your provisioning systems for subscription entitlements.<br>* Use entitlement information to understand which features drive value and revenue.<br><br>**See also**<br><br>* [Entitlements](/docs/api/entitlements)<br>* [Subscription Entitlements](/docs/api/subscription_entitlements)<br>* [Entitlement Overrides](/docs/api/entitlement_overrides)<br>|

It enumerates all the charges, adjustments, payments, discounts and taxes associated with the sale.<br><br>An invoice is said to be a recurring one when it is has at least one charge for [a plan or an addon item price](/docs/api/items). It is a non-recurring one when it has charges for only charge-item prices or [one-time charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/charges.html).<br><br>The item prices for any given billing term of a subscription are billed via an invoice at the beginning of the term (unless the charges are left unbilled). However, item prices that belong to `metered` items are billed at the end of the term via a `pending` invoice that can [close automatically](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing#configuring-metered-billing) or via [an API call](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice). Moreover, when there are no `metered` items in the subscription, the invoices can still be generated as `pending` while [creating](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items) or [updating](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items) a subscription.<br><br>#### Auto-collection<br><br>If [auto-collection](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#auto-collection-status) is enabled, then immediately on invoice generation (or, in case of subscriptions that have `create_pending_invoices` as `true`, on [invoice closure](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice)), the [payment method](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#payment_method) on file is charged:<br><br>* If the payment succeeds, the invoice is marked as `paid`.<br>* On payment failure, the invoice is marked as `payment_due` and [dunning settings](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/dunning-v2.html) are taken into account for payment retries.<br>* If no retry attempts are configured, or when retries are exhausted, the invoice is marked as `not_paid`.<br>* the amount due is zero or negative, the invoice is immediately marked as `paid` and the balance, if any, is added to [excess payments](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#excess-payments) for the customer.<br><br>**Note:** If [consolidated invoicing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html) is enabled, the attribute `subscription_id` is unavailable when the invoice has line items from multiple subscriptions. The individual subscription ids are seen under `line_items.subscription_id`.  <br><br>#### Recurring and non-recurring invoices<br><br>A recurring invoice contains at least one line item that is billed on a recurring basis. Specifically, it has at least one [`line_items[]`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#line_items) with `entity_type` set to `plan_item_price` or `addon_item_price`. A non-recurring invoice contains no recurring line items.  <br><br>#### Refundable amount for an invoice<br><br>The refundable amount for an invoice is the (amount paid on the invoice + refundable credit applied on the invoice + taxes withheld on the invoice) minus (amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice). Each of these amounts is obtained from the invoice resource as follows:<br><br>* Amount paid on the invoice: [`amount_paid`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_amount_paid)<br>* Refundable credit applied on the invoice: [`credits_applied`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_credits_applied)<br>* Taxes withheld on the invoice: Sum of [`linked_taxes_withheld[].amount`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_linked_taxes_withheld)<br>* Amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice: Sum of [`issued_credit_notes[i].cn_total`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_issued_credit_notes) where `issued_credit_notes[i].cn_status` is `refunded` or `refund_due`.<br>|

## Triggered when a new gift is created.

<a id="opIdonGift_scheduledWebhook"></a>

`POST gift_scheduled`

Triggered when a new gift is created.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-new-gift-is-created-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[GiftScheduledEvent](#schemagiftscheduledevent)|false|Payload for gift_scheduled event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » gift|body|[Gift](#schemagift)|true|Gift represents a subscription of a customer(**recipient** ) to a 'gift plan' which has been gifted by another customer(**gifter**). It may also have addons and coupons. Gift will be created only on immediate successful payment collection from the gifter's payment method.<br><br>Gift is initially created in '**scheduled** ' state. The gift can be scheduled to be notified on a particular date to the recipient by passing 'scheduled_at'. If not, the recipient is notified immediately. Gift will be moved to '**unclaimed** ' state on the date of notification. If you pass auto_claim as true, gift status will be moved to '**claimed**' immediately, otherwise, the gift will remain 'unclaimed' till the recipient claims the gift.<br><br>If the gift is not claimed before the claim_expiry_date, it will be moved to the '**expired**' state.<br><br>#### GIFT SUBSCRIPTION<br><br>Gift subscriptions will be created in '**future** ' state. Once the gift is claimed, the subscription will be moved to '**non-renewing**' state.<br><br>#### INVOICE<br><br>Gift subscriptions will be invoiced immediately. The invoice created has **is_gifted** as 'true' and **term_finalized** as 'false'. This is because initially the invoice term_start and term_end are set as the subscription's start_date till the end of the plan period. Once the gift is claimed, the invoice's term_finalized will be marked as 'true'. The term_start will be changed to the actual invoice's term, which is the gift-claim date and the term_end will be changed till plan's period.<br>|

|» » advance_invoice_schedule|body|[AdvanceInvoiceSchedule](#schemaadvanceinvoiceschedule)|true|The invoice for a subscription in Chargebee is generated at the time of subscription renewal. Invoices can also be [generated in advance](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/advance-invoices.html) for an upcoming renewal or set of renewals. With Advance Invoicing Schedules, you can set up a plan for when such advance invoices are generated for the lifetime of the subscription. This helps you:<br><br>* Set up a contract with your customers so that they can be notified of their payment schedules in advance.<br>* Allow customers who make offline payments to be alerted about their upcoming dues well ahead of actual subscription renewals.<br>* Prevent post-renewal unpaid usage of your services by customers.<br><br>Advance invoices can be scheduled in two ways:<br><br>#### Specific Dates Schedule<br><br>Advance invoices for a subscription can be scheduled to be generated on specific [dates](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#specific_dates_schedule_date) in the future. You must specify the [number of billing cycles](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#specific_dates_schedule_terms_to_charge) to be invoiced on each date. A maximum of 5 dates can be specified.<br><br>#### Fixed Interval Schedule<br><br>Advance invoices can be scheduled to be generated at fixed intervals of time, where each interval spans the same number of billing cycles of the subscription. The invoice for each interval is generated a specified number of days ([`days_before_interval`](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#fixed_interval_schedule_days_before_renewal)) before the start of the interval. You can configure the schedule to end on a certain date or after a specified number of advance invoices have been generated.<br><br>The start date of the first interval depends on the number of days remaining from current time till the next renewal of the subscription. If this is more than `days_before_interval`, the interval begins at the next renewal. On the other hand, if the number of days remaining before the next renewal is less than `days_before_interval`, the first interval begins at the renewal following the next.<br>|

|» » invoice|body|[Invoice](#schemainvoice)|true|An invoice is a commercial document representing a sale of products/services offered by you to a customer. It enumerates all the charges, adjustments, payments, discounts and taxes associated with the sale.<br><br>An invoice is said to be a recurring one when it is has at least one charge for [a plan or an addon item price](/docs/api/items). It is a non-recurring one when it has charges for only charge-item prices or [one-time charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/charges.html).<br><br>The item prices for any given billing term of a subscription are billed via an invoice at the beginning of the term (unless the charges are left unbilled). However, item prices that belong to `metered` items are billed at the end of the term via a `pending` invoice that can [close automatically](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing#configuring-metered-billing) or via [an API call](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice). Moreover, when there are no `metered` items in the subscription, the invoices can still be generated as `pending` while [creating](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items) or [updating](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items) a subscription.<br><br>#### Auto-collection<br><br>If [auto-collection](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#auto-collection-status) is enabled, then immediately on invoice generation (or, in case of subscriptions that have `create_pending_invoices` as `true`, on [invoice closure](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice)), the [payment method](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#payment_method) on file is charged:<br><br>* If the payment succeeds, the invoice is marked as `paid`.<br>* On payment failure, the invoice is marked as `payment_due` and [dunning settings](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/dunning-v2.html) are taken into account for payment retries.<br>* If no retry attempts are configured, or when retries are exhausted, the invoice is marked as `not_paid`.<br>* the amount due is zero or negative, the invoice is immediately marked as `paid` and the balance, if any, is added to [excess payments](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#excess-payments) for the customer.<br><br>**Note:** If [consolidated invoicing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html) is enabled, the attribute `subscription_id` is unavailable when the invoice has line items from multiple subscriptions. The individual subscription ids are seen under `line_items.subscription_id`.  <br><br>#### Recurring and non-recurring invoices<br><br>A recurring invoice contains at least one line item that is billed on a recurring basis. Specifically, it has at least one [`line_items[]`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#line_items) with `entity_type` set to `plan_item_price` or `addon_item_price`. A non-recurring invoice contains no recurring line items.  <br><br>#### Refundable amount for an invoice<br><br>The refundable amount for an invoice is the (amount paid on the invoice + refundable credit applied on the invoice + taxes withheld on the invoice) minus (amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice). Each of these amounts is obtained from the invoice resource as follows:<br><br>* Amount paid on the invoice: [`amount_paid`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_amount_paid)<br>* Refundable credit applied on the invoice: [`credits_applied`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_credits_applied)<br>* Taxes withheld on the invoice: Sum of [`linked_taxes_withheld[].amount`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_linked_taxes_withheld)<br>* Amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice: Sum of [`issued_credit_notes[i].cn_total`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_issued_credit_notes) where `issued_credit_notes[i].cn_status` is `refunded` or `refund_due`.<br>|

Win-back offers and offer codes are not supported.<br><br>When `has_scheduled_changes` is `true`, use [List scheduled changes](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_items/list-scheduled-changes-for-omnichannel-subscription-item) to retrieve deferred product or pause changes.  <br>**Note:**<br>This resource represents in-app subscription items made on Apple App Store and Google Play Store.<br>|

## Triggered when a new gift is unclaimed and is ready to be claimed.

<a id="opIdonGift_unclaimedWebhook"></a>

`POST gift_unclaimed`

Triggered when a new gift is unclaimed and is ready to be claimed.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-new-gift-is-unclaimed-and-is-ready-to-be-claimed-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[GiftUnclaimedEvent](#schemagiftunclaimedevent)|false|Payload for gift_unclaimed event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » gift|body|[Gift](#schemagift)|true|Gift represents a subscription of a customer(**recipient** ) to a 'gift plan' which has been gifted by another customer(**gifter**). It may also have addons and coupons. Gift will be created only on immediate successful payment collection from the gifter's payment method.<br><br>Gift is initially created in '**scheduled** ' state. The gift can be scheduled to be notified on a particular date to the recipient by passing 'scheduled_at'. If not, the recipient is notified immediately. Gift will be moved to '**unclaimed** ' state on the date of notification. If you pass auto_claim as true, gift status will be moved to '**claimed**' immediately, otherwise, the gift will remain 'unclaimed' till the recipient claims the gift.<br><br>If the gift is not claimed before the claim_expiry_date, it will be moved to the '**expired**' state.<br><br>#### GIFT SUBSCRIPTION<br><br>Gift subscriptions will be created in '**future** ' state. Once the gift is claimed, the subscription will be moved to '**non-renewing**' state.<br><br>#### INVOICE<br><br>Gift subscriptions will be invoiced immediately. The invoice created has **is_gifted** as 'true' and **term_finalized** as 'false'. This is because initially the invoice term_start and term_end are set as the subscription's start_date till the end of the plan period. Once the gift is claimed, the invoice's term_finalized will be marked as 'true'. The term_start will be changed to the actual invoice's term, which is the gift-claim date and the term_end will be changed till plan's period.<br>|

|200|OK|Webhook received successfully|None|

This operation does not require authentication

## Triggered when a credit note is created such that generated_at is a value in the past.

<a id="opIdonCredit_note_created_with_backdatingWebhook"></a>

`POST credit_note_created_with_backdating`

Triggered when a credit note is created such that generated_at is a value in the past.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-credit-note-is-created-such-that-generatedat-is-a-value-in-the-past-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreditNoteCreatedWithBackdatingEvent](#schemacreditnotecreatedwithbackdatingevent)|false|Payload for credit_note_created_with_backdating event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » credit_note|body|[CreditNote](#schemacreditnote)|true|A [Credit Note](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/credit-notes.html) is a document that specifies the money owed by a business to its customer. The seller usually issues a Credit Note for the same or lower amount than the invoice, and then repays the money to the customer or set it off against other 'due' invoices.<br><br>### Credit Note Types<br><br>Credit notes in Chargebee are categorized into three types:<br>1. `adjustment`: Adjustment credit notes are used to adjust the amount of an existing invoice in the `payment_due` or `not_paid` [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status). Use this type of credit note to reduce the invoice amount, typically as a discount to the customer.<br><br>Adjustment credit notes are automatically created in the following cases:<br><br>* When an invoice is written off.<br>* When a subscription is modified with proration enabled, and the invoice for the current term is in the `payment_due` or `not_paid` [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status). 2. `refundable`: Refundable credit notes allow you to return a certain amount to the customer. These credits can be:<br>* Retained for automatic application on future invoices.<br>* Applied to existing unpaid invoices.<br>* Refunded to the customer. Refundable credit notes are automatically created in the following cases:<br>* When an invoice is refunded.<br>* When a subscription is changed or canceled with proration enabled, the invoice for the current term is in the `paid` [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status). Refundable credits are applied to future invoices or can be refunded to the original payment method. 3. `store`: Store credit notes are created for `paid` or `partially_paid` invoice [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status) during subscription changes, such as upgrades, downgrades, or cancellations. Key characteristics of store credits:<br>* No tax component is included at the time of creation.<br>* A credit note document is generated, similar to refundable credits.<br>* Store credits are applied before tax calculations on future invoices.<br><br>**Note:**<br>If you have enabled *consolidated invoicing*<br>, to know the subscriptions attached with a credit note you have to refer [line_item's](/docs/api/credit_notes/credit_note-object#line_items)<br>*subscription_id*<br>. The credit note's *subscription_id*<br>should **not**<br>be used (which will be *null*<br>if the credit note has lines from multiple subscriptions).  <br>Impact on reference invoice  <br>The following updates are made to the reference invoice when a credit note is created/imported:<br><br>* If the credit note `type` is `adjustment`:<br>  * The adjustment credit note details are added to the `adjustment_credit_notes[]` attribute of the invoice.<br>  * The invoice `amount_due` is reduced by the credit note `total`.<br>  * The invoice `status` is updated to `paid` if the invoice `amount_due` equals the credit note `total`.<br>  * The invoice `status` does not change if the invoice `amount_due` is greater than credit note `total`.<br>* If the credit note `type` is `refundable`:<br>  * The refundable credit note details are added to the `issued_credit_notes[]` attribute of the invoice.<br>  * The invoice `status` does not change.<br>* If the credit note `type` is `store`:<br>  * The store credit note details are added to the `issued_credit_notes[]` attribute of the invoice.<br>  * The invoice `status` does not change.<br>|

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-credit-note-is-created-such-that-generatedat-is-a-value-in-the-past-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Webhook received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication

## Triggered when contract term is terminated.

<a id="opIdonContract_term_terminatedWebhook"></a>

`POST contract_term_terminated`

Triggered when contract term is terminated.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-contract-term-is-terminated-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ContractTermTerminatedEvent](#schemacontracttermterminatedevent)|false|Payload for contract_term_terminated event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » contract_term|body|[ContractTerm](#schemacontractterm)|true|Subscriptions can run indefinitely or they may run for a fixed number of billing cycles. Subscription can have "contract terms", which define a lock-in period on the subscription for a certain number of billing cycles. This prevents the subscription from being canceled by the customer when it is within the contract term.<br><br>The **contract term** resource described below defines the properties of this lock-in period. This includes the [number of billing cycles](/docs/api/contract_terms/contract_term-object#remaining_billing_cycles), the [total contract value](/docs/api/contract_terms/contract_term-object#total_contract_value), the [action to be taken](/docs/api/contract_terms/contract_term-object#action_at_term_end) at the end of the contract term, and so on. To allow for exceptions, you also have the option of terminating an [`active`](/docs/api/contract_terms/contract_term-object#status) contract term and charging a [termination fee](/docs/api/contract_terms).<br><br>A contract term starts in the `active` state and ends in the `completed` state. If the contract was canceled due to non-payment or other reasons, it can end in the `canceled` or `terminated` state. A given contract term is always associated with one, and only one subscription. A subscription, however, can be associated with only one `active` contract term. Over time, a subscription can be associated with several non-`active` contract terms. The `active` contract term for a subscription is available as an [object](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object#contract_term) within the subscription.<br><br>To enable and configure contract terms, follow these steps in the Chargebee UI:<br><br>1. Click **Settings** on the left navigation.<br>2. Click **Configure Chargebee**.<br>3. Under **Billing** , click **Contract Terms**.<br>4. Enable and configure the feature as needed.<br><br>Once contract terms have been configured, the following actions can be performed using the API:<br><br>* **Define a contract term** for a subscription and **set renewal options** for the contract term. The following endpoints support this:<br><br>* [Create a subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items)<br>* [Update a subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items)<br>* [Reactivate a subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/reactivate-a-subscription)<br>* [Create a subscription ramp](/docs/api/ramps/create-a-ramp)<br>* [Update a subscription ramp](/docs/api/ramps/update-a-subscription-ramp)<br>* **Retrieving** a historical record of all contract terms for a subscription can be done via the following endpoint:<br><br>* [List contract terms for a subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/list-contract-terms-for-a-subscription)<br>* **Canceling a contract term** can be done via the following endpoints:<br><br>* [Update a subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items)<br>* [Cancel a subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/cancel-subscription-for-items)<br>* [Update a subscription ramp](/docs/api/ramps/update-a-subscription-ramp)<br><br>#### Including a termination fee<br><br>When a contract is canceled mid-term, you can set a termination fee to be levied. Here's how:<br><br>1. [Create](/docs/api/item_prices/create-an-item-price) an item price for an item of [type](/docs/api/items/item-object#type) `charge` with [price](/docs/api/item_prices/create-an-item-price#price) set to the termination fee.<br>2. Do one of the following:<br><br>* [Attach the charge-item to a plan](/docs/api/attached_items/create-an-attached-item), setting the `charge_on_event` parameter to `contract_termination`. OR<br>* [Include the charge-item price on a subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items), setting the `subscription_items[charge_on_event][i]` parameter to `contract_termination`.<br><br>Once the above steps are done, the termination fee will be charged automatically if you [terminate the contract in the middle of its term](/docs/api/subscriptions/cancel-subscription-for-items#contract_term_cancel_option).<br>|

<h3 id="triggered-when-contract-term-is-terminated-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Webhook received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication


<h3 id="triggered-when-a-refund-attempt-fails-at-the-gateway-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[RefundFailedEvent](#schemarefundfailedevent)|false|Payload for refund_failed event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » transaction|body|[Transaction](#schematransaction)|true|This resource represents the [transaction](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/transactions.html)<br>event that has happened in your account.<br>|
|» » invoice|body|[Invoice](#schemainvoice)|true|An invoice is a commercial document representing a sale of products/services offered by you to a customer. It enumerates all the charges, adjustments, payments, discounts and taxes associated with the sale.<br><br>An invoice is said to be a recurring one when it is has at least one charge for [a plan or an addon item price](/docs/api/items). It is a non-recurring one when it has charges for only charge-item prices or [one-time charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/charges.html).<br><br>The item prices for any given billing term of a subscription are billed via an invoice at the beginning of the term (unless the charges are left unbilled). However, item prices that belong to `metered` items are billed at the end of the term via a `pending` invoice that can [close automatically](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing#configuring-metered-billing) or via [an API call](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice). Moreover, when there are no `metered` items in the subscription, the invoices can still be generated as `pending` while [creating](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items) or [updating](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items) a subscription.<br><br>#### Auto-collection<br><br>If [auto-collection](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#auto-collection-status) is enabled, then immediately on invoice generation (or, in case of subscriptions that have `create_pending_invoices` as `true`, on [invoice closure](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice)), the [payment method](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#payment_method) on file is charged:<br><br>* If the payment succeeds, the invoice is marked as `paid`.<br>* On payment failure, the invoice is marked as `payment_due` and [dunning settings](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/dunning-v2.html) are taken into account for payment retries.<br>* If no retry attempts are configured, or when retries are exhausted, the invoice is marked as `not_paid`.<br>* the amount due is zero or negative, the invoice is immediately marked as `paid` and the balance, if any, is added to [excess payments](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#excess-payments) for the customer.<br><br>**Note:** If [consolidated invoicing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html) is enabled, the attribute `subscription_id` is unavailable when the invoice has line items from multiple subscriptions. The individual subscription ids are seen under `line_items.subscription_id`.  <br><br>#### Recurring and non-recurring invoices<br><br>A recurring invoice contains at least one line item that is billed on a recurring basis. Specifically, it has at least one [`line_items[]`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#line_items) with `entity_type` set to `plan_item_price` or `addon_item_price`. A non-recurring invoice contains no recurring line items.  <br><br>#### Refundable amount for an invoice<br><br>The refundable amount for an invoice is the (amount paid on the invoice + refundable credit applied on the invoice + taxes withheld on the invoice) minus (amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice). Each of these amounts is obtained from the invoice resource as follows:<br><br>* Amount paid on the invoice: [`amount_paid`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_amount_paid)<br>* Refundable credit applied on the invoice: [`credits_applied`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_credits_applied)<br>* Taxes withheld on the invoice: Sum of [`linked_taxes_withheld[].amount`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_linked_taxes_withheld)<br>* Amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice: Sum of [`issued_credit_notes[i].cn_total`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_issued_credit_notes) where `issued_credit_notes[i].cn_status` is `refunded` or `refund_due`.<br>|
|» » credit_note|body|[CreditNote](#schemacreditnote)|true|A [Credit Note](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/credit-notes.html) is a document that specifies the money owed by a business to its customer. The seller usually issues a Credit Note for the same or lower amount than the invoice, and then repays the money to the customer or set it off against other 'due' invoices.<br><br>### Credit Note Types<br><br>Credit notes in Chargebee are categorized into three types:<br>1. `adjustment`: Adjustment credit notes are used to adjust the amount of an existing invoice in the `payment_due` or `not_paid` [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status). Use this type of credit note to reduce the invoice amount, typically as a discount to the customer.<br><br>Adjustment credit notes are automatically created in the following cases:<br><br>* When an invoice is written off.<br>* When a subscription is modified with proration enabled, and the invoice for the current term is in the `payment_due` or `not_paid` [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status). 2. `refundable`: Refundable credit notes allow you to return a certain amount to the customer. These credits can be:<br>* Retained for automatic application on future invoices.<br>* Applied to existing unpaid invoices.<br>* Refunded to the customer. Refundable credit notes are automatically created in the following cases:<br>* When an invoice is refunded.<br>* When a subscription is changed or canceled with proration enabled, the invoice for the current term is in the `paid` [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status). Refundable credits are applied to future invoices or can be refunded to the original payment method. 3. `store`: Store credit notes are created for `paid` or `partially_paid` invoice [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status) during subscription changes, such as upgrades, downgrades, or cancellations. Key characteristics of store credits:<br>* No tax component is included at the time of creation.<br>* A credit note document is generated, similar to refundable credits.<br>* Store credits are applied before tax calculations on future invoices.<br><br>**Note:**<br>If you have enabled *consolidated invoicing*<br>, to know the subscriptions attached with a credit note you have to refer [line_item's](/docs/api/credit_notes/credit_note-object#line_items)<br>*subscription_id*<br>. The credit note's *subscription_id*<br>should **not**<br>be used (which will be *null*<br>if the credit note has lines from multiple subscriptions).  <br>Impact on reference invoice  <br>The following updates are made to the reference invoice when a credit note is created/imported:<br><br>* If the credit note `type` is `adjustment`:<br>  * The adjustment credit note details are added to the `adjustment_credit_notes[]` attribute of the invoice.<br>  * The invoice `amount_due` is reduced by the credit note `total`.<br>  * The invoice `status` is updated to `paid` if the invoice `amount_due` equals the credit note `total`.<br>  * The invoice `status` does not change if the invoice `amount_due` is greater than credit note `total`.<br>* If the credit note `type` is `refundable`:<br>  * The refundable credit note details are added to the `issued_credit_notes[]` attribute of the invoice.<br>  * The invoice `status` does not change.<br>* If the credit note `type` is `store`:<br>  * The store credit note details are added to the `issued_credit_notes[]` attribute of the invoice.<br>  * The invoice `status` does not change.<br>|
|» » customer|body|[Customer](#schemacustomer)|true|Represents a customer, which can be an individual or organization that subscribes to your products or services. The customer resource associates with [subscriptions](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object), [card information](/docs/api/cards/card-object), and billing addresses. The customer details include their ID, name, contact information, and any [custom attributes](/docs/api/advanced-features) you'd like to associate with them.  <br>**Breaking Change**:<br><br>* [**Sites**](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/sites-intro.html) **created before March 1, 2014** : [updating the card](/docs/api/cards/update-card-for-a-customer) deletes the customer's `billing_address` and `vat_number` and replaces them with values from the request.<br>* **Sites created on or after March 1, 2014** : updating the card doesn't change the `billing_address` and `vat_number`.<br>|
|» » subscription|body|[Subscription](#schemasubscription)|true|A Chargebee subscription connects a customer record to products/services. It describes what the customer has signed up for and how often they're charged for it. The essential components of a subscription are:<br><br>* A [plan-item price](/docs/api/item_prices).<br>* Any addon- and charge-item prices applied to the subscription.<br>* Any [coupons](/docs/api/coupons) applied.<br>* Any [discounts](/docs/api/discounts) applied.<br><br>The charges in a subscription are billed via invoices.  <br>**Note:**<br>The maximum number of subscriptions for any given [customer](/docs/api/customers)<br>([active](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object#status)<br>or not) is 900.  <br><br>#### Subscription billing frequencies<br><br>Chargebee offers two billing frequency options for subscriptions:<br><br>* **Plan-based billing** (`default`): Subscriptions are billed based on the billing period defined for the item price of the `item_type` `plan`. [Learn more](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/subscriptions#plan-based-billing).<br><br>* **Multi-frequency billing** : Subscriptions are billed according to the billing period of each recurring item price within the subscription. [Learn more](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/multi-frequency-billing).<br><br>  **Important**<br><br>  [Limitations](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/multi-frequency-billing#limitations) of Multi-frequency billing.<br><br>The selection of the billing frequency preference is configured at the site level.  <br><br>#### Item price compatibility in a subscription<br><br>When creating or updating a subscription, one of the item prices specified under subscription_items must be a plan-item price. The remaining must be compatible addon- or charge-item prices. An item price is compatible with a plan-item price if their currencies are the same. ## Triggered when the status for an alert changes

<a id="opIdonAlert_status_changedWebhook"></a>

`POST alert_status_changed`

Triggered when an alert's runtime status for a subscription changes between `IN_ALARM` and `WITHIN_LIMIT`.
This indicates a change in the subscription's usage relative to the alert threshold and applies only to usage-based billing.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-the-status-for-an-alert-changes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AlertStatusChangedEvent](#schemaalertstatuschangedevent)|false|Payload for alert_status_changed event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » alert|body|[Alert](#schemaalert)|true|An alert defines a threshold rule for usage, spend, or credit balance. When the configured threshold is crossed, Chargebee triggers a webhook notification so that you can take action such as notifying the customer, upgrading the plan, or pausing further consumption.<br><br>Common examples of alerts include:<br><br>* Notifying a customer when they have consumed 90% of their monthly API call quota.<br>* Alerting your operations team when a customer's spend exceeds a monthly limit.<br>* Warning a customer when their prepaid credit balance drops to or below a replenishment threshold.<br><br>The alert resource represents configuration only. To check the current runtime state of an alert for a subscription (whether it is `within_limit` or `in_alarm`), use the [Alert Status](/docs/api/alert_statuses) endpoints.  <br><br>#### Global vs. subscription-scoped alerts<br><br>Alerts can be created at two levels:<br><br>* **Global alerts** apply across all relevant subscriptions. To restrict a global alert to specific plans, use `filter_conditions` with the `plan_price_id` field. When multiple filter conditions are provided, they are evaluated with OR semantics: the alert applies if any condition matches.<br>* **Subscription-scoped alerts** apply to a single subscription only. Set `subscription_id` when creating the alert. Subscription-scoped alerts cannot have `filter_conditions`.<br><br>**Important**<br><br>A global alert and a subscription-scoped alert are mutually exclusive in their parameters: if `subscription_id` is set, `filter_conditions` must not be provided, and vice versa.  <br><br>#### Alert types<br><br>The `type` attribute determines what an alert measures, which input it requires, and how the threshold is interpreted.  <br>usage_exceeded  <br>Monitors consumption of a [metered feature](/docs/api/usages) for a subscription.<br><br>* **Required input:** `metered_feature_id`.<br>* **Fires when:** measured usage reaches or exceeds the configured threshold.<br>* **Threshold modes:** `percentage` (of the plan or feature quota) or `absolute` (a usage quantity).<br>* **Example:** notify a customer when they reach 90% of their monthly API-call quota.<br><br>Usage alerts are evaluated as [usage data](/docs/api/usage_events) is processed for the subscription.  <br>spend_exceeded  <br>Monitors the total usage-based spend accumulated from metered addons on a subscription. This is the same overage concept surfaced by [usage charges](/docs/api/usage_charges): the monetary overage spend corresponds to the [amount](/docs/api/usage_charges/usage-charge-object#amount) field on the usage charge object (in major units of the currency).<br><br>* **Required input:** `currency_code` --- the ISO [currency code](/docs/api/currencies/currency-object#currency_code) in which overage spend is tracked.<br>* **Fires when:** accumulated overage spend reaches or exceeds the configured threshold.<br>* **Threshold mode:** always `absolute` (an amount in `currency_code`).<br>* **Example:** alert the customer when their spending exceeds a 500 USD limit during the current usage cycle.<br><br>Spend alerts are evaluated as usage and overage charge data is processed for the subscription.  <br>credit_balance_dropped  <br>Monitors the prepaid credit balance of a subscription for a specific credit unit. See [ledger account balances](/docs/api/ledger_account_balances) for how credit balances are tracked.<br><br>* **Required input:** `unit_id` --- the [credit unit](/docs/api/ledger_account_balances/ledger-account-balance-object#unit_id) the alert applies to (for example, `ai_credits`).<br>* **Fires when:** the credit balance drops to or below the configured threshold. This is the opposite direction to the `usage_exceeded` and `spend_exceeded` types, which fire when a value rises.<br>* **Threshold mode:** always `absolute` (a credit-balance floor). `percentage` mode is not supported.<br>* **Example:** warn a customer when their remaining AI credits drop to or below 10.<br><br>Credit-balance alerts are evaluated as [ledger operations](/docs/api/ledger_operations) update the balance.  <br><br>#### Threshold modes<br><br>The `threshold` object defines when the alert should fire. It has two fields:<br><br>* `mode`: Either `percentage` or `absolute`.<br>  * `percentage`: The alert fires when the measured value reaches the specified percentage threshold. The `value` must be between 0 and 100 (inclusive). Supported only for `usage_exceeded` alerts.<br>  * `absolute`: The alert fires when the measured value reaches an absolute quantity. The `value` must be \>= 0.<br>* `value`: The numeric threshold at which the alert triggers.<br><br>The supported modes depend on the alert `type`:<br><br>* `usage_exceeded`: `percentage` or `absolute`.<br>* `spend_exceeded`: `absolute` only.<br>* `credit_balance_dropped`: `absolute` only.  <br>**See also**<br><br>* [Alert Statuses](/docs/api/alert_statuses) --- runtime state of alerts per subscription.<br>* [Usage Events](/docs/api/usage_events) --- usage ingestion for `usage_exceeded` alerts.<br>* [Ledger account balances](/docs/api/ledger_account_balances) --- credit balances for `credit_balance_dropped` alerts.<br>|
|» » alert_status|body|[AlertStatus](#schemaalertstatus)|true|An alert status represents the runtime evaluation of an [alert](/docs/api/alerts) for a specific [subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions). While the [alert](/docs/api/alerts/alert-object) resource defines the threshold rule, the alert status tells you whether a subscription is currently `within_limit` or `in_alarm` for that rule. Statuses are tracked for every alert type --- `usage_exceeded`, `spend_exceeded`, and `credit_balance_dropped`.<br><br>Each alert status tracks:<br><br>* `alarm_status`: The current state --- `within_limit` (the subscription is within the configured threshold) or `in_alarm` (the threshold has been breached).<br>* `alarm_triggered_at`: The timestamp when the alert last entered the `in_alarm` state. This is `null` if the alert has never been triggered for this subscription.<br><br>**Note:** Alert statuses are computed by Chargebee based on billing data and the alert configuration. They are read-only --- you cannot create or update an alert status directly. To change the threshold rule, use the [Alerts](/docs/api/alerts) API.<br>|

The essential components of a subscription are:<br><br>* A [plan-item price](/docs/api/item_prices).<br>* Any addon- and charge-item prices applied to the subscription.<br>* Any [coupons](/docs/api/coupons) applied.<br>* Any [discounts](/docs/api/discounts) applied.<br><br>The charges in a subscription are billed via invoices.  <br>**Note:**<br>The maximum number of subscriptions for any given [customer](/docs/api/customers)<br>([active](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object#status)<br>or not) is 900.  <br><br>#### Subscription billing frequencies<br><br>Chargebee offers two billing frequency options for subscriptions:<br><br>* **Plan-based billing** (`default`): Subscriptions are billed based on the billing period defined for the item price of the `item_type` `plan`. [Learn more](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/multi-frequency-billing).<br><br>  **Important**<br><br>  [Limitations](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/multi-frequency-billing#limitations) of Multi-frequency billing.<br><br>The selection of the billing frequency preference is configured at the site level.  <br><br>#### Item price compatibility in a subscription<br><br>When creating or updating a subscription, one of the item prices specified under subscription_items must be a plan-item price. Once enabled, you can test the Ramps API without impacting your existing integrations.<br><br>The following parts of the Billing API have subtle differences in behavior when the Ramps feature is disabled versus when it is enabled with compatibility mode. (Follow the links to learn more.)<br><br>* The value of the [`subscription.has_scheduled_changes`](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object#has_scheduled_changes) attribute.<br>* [Update subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items#impact-scheduled-changes)<br>* [Create Checkout for updating a subscription](/docs/api/hosted_pages/create-checkout-to-update-a-subscription#impact-scheduled-changes)<br>* [Remove scheduled changes](/docs/api/subscriptions/remove-scheduled-changes)<br>* [Retrieve with scheduled changes](/docs/api/subscriptions/retrieve-with-scheduled-changes)<br>* [Create a quote for updating a subscription](/docs/api/quotes/create-a-quote-for-update-subscription-items)<br>* [Edit a quote for updating a subscription](/docs/api/quotes/edit-update-subscription-quote-for-items)<br>* [Portal sessions](/docs/api/portal_sessions#scheduled-subscription-changes)<br>|

## Triggered when a business ruleset is updated

<a id="opIdonBusiness_ruleset_updatedWebhook"></a>

`POST business_ruleset_updated`

> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-business-ruleset-is-updated-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[BusinessRulesetUpdatedEvent](#schemabusinessrulesetupdatedevent)|false|Payload for business_ruleset_updated event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » business_ruleset|body|[BusinessRuleset](#schemabusinessruleset)|true|A business ruleset groups [business rules](/docs/api/business_rules) so that they can be evaluated together, in the priority order you assign, using the strategy set in `execute_mode`.<br><br>Rulesets let you apply a whole decision at once instead of calling each rule separately. Passing a `ruleset_id` to [Apply business rules](/docs/api/business_rules/apply-business-rules) evaluates the rules the ruleset contains in their priority order and returns a result for each one. The `execute_mode` decides whether evaluation runs through every rule or stops as soon as a rule evaluates to `true` or to `false`, and which of the results are returned.<br><br>Membership is managed separately from the rules themselves. [Add business rules to a ruleset](/docs/api/business_rulesets/add-business-rules-to-a-ruleset) and [Remove business rules from a ruleset](/docs/api/business_rulesets/remove-business-rules-from-a-ruleset) change membership incrementally, while passing `rules` to [Update a business ruleset](/docs/api/business_rulesets/update-a-business-ruleset) replaces it entirely. A rule can belong to more than one ruleset, and removing it from a ruleset does not delete the rule.<br><br>The `active` attribute controls whether Chargebee evaluates the ruleset. A rule is evaluated through a ruleset only when both the ruleset and the rule are `active`.  <br>**Note:** Business rules are not enabled by default. Contact [Chargebee Support](https://www.chargebee.com/support/) to enable them for your site. Until they are enabled, these endpoints return an error.<br>|

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Webhook received successfully|None|

## Triggered when an item is deleted.

<a id="opIdonItem_deletedWebhook"></a>

`POST item_deleted`

Triggered when an item is deleted.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-an-item-is-deleted-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ItemDeletedEvent](#schemaitemdeletedevent)|false|Payload for item_deleted event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » item|body|[Item](#schemaitem)|true|When offering subscriptions of products or services, each entity that is made available for sale is represented by an "item" object. Items therefore represent the various plans, addons or charges that you offer as part of your product catalog. Non-`metered` items are charged upfront in Chargebee, while `metered` items are charged at the end of the billing cycle, based on usage.<br><br>### Types of Items<br><br>There are three types of items and they're listed and explained here. Examples for each type are provided in the table that follows.<br><br>#### Plan-items or Plans<br><br>Plan-items are items that have a recurring charge and are an essential component of any [subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions). Typically, plans represent a principal or key product or service in your catalog. They are charged at recurring intervals and often have other products or services offered along with them as addons and charges.<br><br>#### Addon-items or Addons<br><br>Addon-items are items that are sold along with a plan and are charged for at recurring intervals.<br><br>#### Charge-items or Charges<br><br>Charge-items are items that are sold along with a plan but charged once (or each time) a specified event occurs. A charge can also be [applied to a customer](/docs/api/v2/pcv-1/invoices/create-invoice-for-a-one-time-charge) without attaching to a subscription.<br><br>#### Examples<br><br>To help understand each type of item better, listed below are some examples of items from different business domains:<br><br>##### Non-Metered (SaaS)<br><br>* **Item Family:** A project management solution.<br>* **Plans:**<br>  * A "basic" plan offering a small set of features.<br>  * A "business" plan offering a larger set of features.<br>* **Addons:**<br>  * An analytics plugin that is available only with the "business" plan.<br>  * A reporting plugin, available with both the above plans.<br>* **Charges:**<br>  * Implementation charges.<br>  * Trial charges.<br><br>##### Non-Metered (E-commerce)<br><br>* **Item Family:** A printed news magazine.<br>* **Plans:**<br>  * Periodic issues of the magazine.<br>  * Periodic issues of the magazine, with digital content.<br>* **Addons:**<br>  * Supplementary online content.<br>  * Access to a year's worth of back issues.<br>  * Searchable access to all back issues.<br>* **Charges:**<br>  * Special edition books that are published every so often.<br><br>##### Metered<br><br>* **Item Family:** SMS delivery services.<br>* **Plans:**<br>  * A basic plan of up to 100K messages @ $0.03 per message.<br>  * A volume plan of 2M messages @ $0.01 per message.<br>* **Addons:**<br>  * An addon of 50K MMS messages @ $0.1 per message.<br>  * Instant messaging.<br>* **Charges:**<br>  * Automated Metered Billing is not applicable for charges.<br>|

|200|OK|Webhook received successfully|None|
