## Triggered when a ramp is drafted.

<a id="opIdonSubscription_ramp_draftedWebhook"></a>

`POST subscription_ramp_drafted`

Triggered when a ramp is moved to draft status.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-ramp-is-drafted-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[SubscriptionRampDraftedEvent](#schemasubscriptionrampdraftedevent)|false|Payload for subscription_ramp_drafted event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » ramp|body|[Ramp](#schemaramp)|true|A `ramp` resource, or subscription ramp, represents a planned change to a [`subscription`](/docs/api/subscriptions) that occurs at a future date. Use this resource to define and schedule subscription modifications, such as updating pricing, altering quantity, or transitioning to a different plan, without immediately applying them.  <br>**Note**<br><br>* **Upcoming ramps limit** : A subscription can have a maximum of 12 upcoming ramps at any given time, excluding deleted ramps. Upcoming ramps are ramps with `status` as [`scheduled`](/docs/api/ramps/ramp-object#status).<br>* **Total ramps limit**: A subscription can have a maximum of 100 ramps at any given time, excluding deleted ramps.  <br><br>#### Auto-draft conditions<br><br>When you create or update a ramp, Chargebee automatically moves any existing ramps scheduled after that ramp to `draft` status if either of the following conditions is met:<br><br>* The new or updated ramp changes the subscription [term end date](subscriptions#subscription_current_term_end).<br>* The new or updated ramp changes the subscription billing frequency. That is, either of the following [attributes](subscriptions#subscription_items) is changed:<br>  * `subscription_items[i].billing_period`<br>  * `subscription_items[i].billing_period_unit`<br>  * where `i` is the index where `subscription_items[i].item_type` is `plan`.<br>* The new or updated ramp introduces an [addon](item_prices#item_price_item_type) that is not [applicable](attached_items) to the plan in one or more of the subsequent ramps.<br>|

## Triggered when a business rule is created

<a id="opIdonBusiness_rule_createdWebhook"></a>

`POST business_rule_created`

> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-business-rule-is-created-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[BusinessRuleCreatedEvent](#schemabusinessrulecreatedevent)|false|Payload for business_rule_created event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » business_rule|body|[BusinessRule](#schemabusinessrule)|true|A business rule pairs a condition with the actions to take when that condition is met. You supply the context to evaluate, and Chargebee returns the actions configured in `actions_on_success` when the condition evaluates to `true`.<br><br>Business Rules APIs manage [CPQ Selling Rules](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/cpq/selling-rules).<br><br>The condition is defined in `structured_expression`, a JSON representation of the rule logic that visual editors and dynamic rule builders can both read and write. Chargebee validates and compiles the expression when the rule is created or updated, and evaluates the compiled form when you call [Apply business rules](/docs/api/business_rules/apply-business-rules).<br><br>The `field` of every condition is resolved against the context supplied at evaluation time, so the fields you reference must match the keys of the context the rule is evaluated against. A condition whose `field` is absent from the context never evaluates to `true`, which means the rule never matches.<br><br>Business rules are versioned. Creating a rule releases its first version, so `latest_version` is `1` and `released_at` is set from the outset. Editing a rule leaves that released version untouched: the first edit creates a draft, and every later edit updates the same draft. [Releasing](/docs/api/business_rules/release-a-business-rule) the draft promotes it to the next version number, and that version becomes the latest released version and the one Chargebee evaluates. Until you release it, the previously released version stays in effect, so a rule can keep serving traffic while its next version is being prepared.<br><br>The `active` attribute is an independent switch that controls whether Chargebee evaluates the rule at all. A rule is created inactive, so it has to be [activated](/docs/api/business_rules/activate-a-business-rule) before it takes effect.<br><br>Related rules can be grouped into a [business ruleset](/docs/api/business_rulesets), which evaluates its member rules in priority order using the strategy configured in the ruleset's `execute_mode`.<br><br>For a walkthrough that creates, activates, and applies a rule in three calls, take a look at the [Business Rules quickstart](https://www.chargebee.com/tutorials/business-rules-quickstart/).  <br>**Note:** Business rules are not enabled by default. Contact [Chargebee Support](https://www.chargebee.com/support/) to enable them for your site. Until they are enabled, these endpoints return an error.<br><br>Expressions<br>-----------<br><br>The `structured_expression` of a rule is a tree of nodes that evaluates to a single `true` or `false`. Every node carries a `type`, which determines the rest of the fields the node takes.<br><br>The following expression matches a quote from a customer whose language contains `en` and whose shipping country is India or the United States:<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "type": "GROUP",<br>  "operation": "AND",<br>  "children": [<br>    {<br>      "type": "CONDITION",<br>      "field": "customer.language",<br>      "operator": "CONTAINS",<br>      "value": "en"<br>    },<br>    {<br>      "type": "CONDITION",<br>      "field": "quote.shipping_address_country",<br>      "operator": "ANY_OF",<br>      "values": ["IN", "US"]<br>    }<br>  ]<br>}<br>```<br><br>Every condition is compiled so that it first tests whether the field is present in the context. A condition on a field that the context doesn't carry evaluates to `false` instead of failing, so the rule that holds it never matches and no `error_message` is returned for it.  <br><br>### GROUP node<br><br>Combines the nodes in `children` into a single result. Use a `GROUP` as the root of any expression that has more than one condition, and nest groups to control precedence.<br><br>* `operation`: **Required.** `AND` to match only if every child matches, or `OR` to match if any child matches.<br>* `children`: **Required.** An array holding at least one node. Each entry is itself a `GROUP`, `CONDITION`, or `COLLECTION` node.<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "type": "GROUP",<br>  "operation": "OR",<br>  "children": [<br>    {<br>      "type": "CONDITION",<br>      "field": "quote.payment_terms",<br>      "operator": "GREATER_THAN",<br>      "value": 30<br>    },<br>    {<br>      "type": "CONDITION",<br>      "field": "customer.billing_address_country",<br>      "operator": "EQUALS",<br>      "value": "US"<br>    }<br>  ]<br>}<br>```<br><br>### CONDITION node<br><br>Compares one field of the context against a value.<br><br>* `field`: **Required.** The path of the field through the context, such as `customer.language`. See [Context](/docs/api/business_rules#context) for the paths available.<br>* `operator`: **Required.** How the comparison is made. See [Operators](/docs/api/business_rules#operators) for the operators available and the field types each one compares.<br>* `value`: The single value to compare against. Required for the single-value operators.<br>* `values`: The array of values to compare against. Required for `BETWEEN`, `ANY_OF`, and `NONE_OF`.<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "type": "CONDITION",<br>  "field": "quote.contract_duration",<br>  "operator": "BETWEEN",<br>  "values": [12, 36]<br>}<br>```<br><br>### COLLECTION node<br><br>Tests the entries of an array in the context, such as the line items of a quote. All four fields are required.<br><br>* `field`: **Required.** The array to iterate over, such as `items`.<br>* `variable`: **Required.** The name each entry is bound to while the predicate is evaluated.<br>* `mode`: **Required.** `ANY` to match if at least one entry satisfies the predicate, or `NONE` to match only if no entry does.<br>* `predicate`: **Required.** The expression each entry is tested against, usually a `GROUP` node.<br><br>Inside the predicate, address the fields of an entry through the bound `variable`. The following node matches a quote that has at least one item discounted by more than 20:<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "type": "COLLECTION",<br>  "field": "items",<br>  "variable": "item",<br>  "mode": "ANY",<br>  "predicate": {<br>    "type": "GROUP",<br>    "operation": "AND",<br>    "children": [<br>      {<br>        "type": "CONDITION",<br>        "field": "item.discount",<br>        "operator": "GREATER_THAN",<br>        "value": 20<br>      }<br>    ]<br>  }<br>}<br>```<br><br>### Operators<br><br>The following operators are available. The field type is the type the operator can compare, and the value column shows whether the condition takes `value` or `values`.  <br><br>\|                                   Operator                                   \|       Field type        \|                                        Value                                        \|<br>\|------------------------------------------------------------------------------\|-------------------------\|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\|<br>\| `EQUALS`, `NOT_EQUALS`                                                       \| String, number, boolean \| `value`                                                                             \|<br>\| `GREATER_THAN`, `GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUALS`, `LESS_THAN`, `LESS_THAN_OR_EQUALS` \| Number                  \| `value`                                                                             \|<br>\| `BETWEEN`                                                                    \| Number                  \| `values`, holding exactly two entries, read as the inclusive lower and upper bounds \|<br>\| `CONTAINS`, `NOT_CONTAINS`                                                   \| String                  \| `value`                                                                             \|<br>\| `STARTS_WITH`                                                                \| String                  \| `value`                                                                             \|<br>\| `ANY_OF`, `NONE_OF`                                                          \| String, number, boolean \| `values`, holding at least one entry                                                \|<br><br>An operator used on a field of another type isn't rejected when the rule is saved, so the mismatch surfaces only when the rule is evaluated.<br><br>Context<br>-------<br><br>The `context` you pass to [Apply business rules](/docs/api/business_rules/apply-business-rules) isn't a free-form object. Its `type` selects the schema that the rest of the context is read as, and `CPQ` is the only type available, so a condition can reference only the fields of that schema. A key that falls outside the schema is dropped as the context is read, so a condition on it never evaluates to `true`. A misspelled or unsupported key therefore surfaces as an unmet condition rather than as an error.<br><br>A `CPQ` context carries `items`, `quote`, `customer`, `user`, `site`, and `quote_subscription`, each of them optional. Pass only the parts the rules you're evaluating need:<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "type": "CPQ",<br>  "customer": {<br>    "language": "en",<br>    "billing_address_country": "US"<br>  },<br>  "quote": {<br>    "shipping_address_country": "IN",<br>    "payment_terms": 30,<br>    "custom_fields": { "region": "apac" }<br>  },<br>  "items": [<br>    { "reference_id": "item-1", "amount": 5000, "quantity": 2, "discount": 10 },<br>    { "reference_id": "item-2", "amount": 1200, "quantity": 1, "discount": 0 }<br>  ]<br>}<br>```<br><br>A condition addresses a field by its path through the context, so `customer.language` reads the `language` of the `customer`. A `COLLECTION` node on `items` iterates over the entries of that array.<br><br>Each `custom_fields` object holds your own fields keyed by name, and every value must be a string, a number, or a boolean. A condition reads one through its key, as in `quote.custom_fields.region`.<br><br>The response returns the context back with `rule_ids` filled in on the quote and on each item, so you can see which rules applied where.  <br><br>### quote<br><br>* `type` and `contract_type`: strings.<br>* `contract_duration` and `payment_terms`: numbers.<br>* `billing_address_country` and `shipping_address_country`: strings.<br>* `billing_frequency` and `billing_currency`: strings.<br>* `creator_email` and `creator_role`: strings.<br>* `custom_fields`: object.<br>* `rule_ids`: array of strings. Returned in the response rather than passed, recording the rules that applied to the quote.  <br><br>### customer<br><br>* `billing_address_city`, `billing_address_state`, and `billing_address_country`: strings.<br>* `language`: string.<br>* `payment_terms`: number.<br>* `custom_fields`: object.  <br><br>### items<br><br>An array, with each entry holding the following.<br><br>* `reference_id`: string, identifying the entry within the context.<br>* `type`, `item_name`, and `product_family_name`: strings.<br>* `billing_frequency` and `currency`: strings.<br>* `billing_cycle`, `amount`, `quantity`, and `discount`: numbers.<br>* `start_date` and `end_date`: timestamps.<br>* `rule_ids`: array of strings. Returned in the response rather than passed, recording the rules that applied to that entry.  <br><br>### user<br><br>* `name`, `email`, and `phone`: strings.  <br><br>### site<br><br>* `name`, `domain`, and `currency`: strings.<br>* `sandbox`: boolean.  <br><br>### quote_subscription<br><br>* `custom_fields`: object.<br><br>Actions<br>-------<br><br>Every entry in `actions_on_success` is built from an **action template** , a built-in definition that fixes the kind of change an action makes and the parameters it accepts. An action names its template in `action_template_id` and passes that template's parameters in `input`:<br><br>```json<br>[<br>  {<br>    "action_template_id": "action-apply-discount",<br>    "input": {<br>      "apply_on": "INVOICE_AMOUNT",<br>      "discount": 12.0,<br>      "discount_type": "PERCENTAGE",<br>      "duration_type": "ONE_TIME"<br>    }<br>  }<br>]<br>```<br><br>The `type` of an action is derived from its template, so it's returned with the action but you don't have to pass it. A parameter that the template doesn't define is rejected. The values of enumerated parameters are matched without regard to case, and are returned in the `input` of the action exactly as you passed them.<br><br>An action can also carry a `structured_expression` of its own, written in the same format as the expression of the rule. The rule decides whether the action runs at all, and the action's own expression then narrows it to the items of the context that satisfy that expression. One rule can therefore discount some of the items it matched rather than all of them. Only the apply discount, limit discount, and limit quantity templates accept an action-level expression.  <br><br>### Apply discount<br><br>Applies a discount to the invoice amount or to specific item prices. Built from `action_template_id` `action-apply-discount` and returned with `type` `APPLY_DISCOUNT`.<br><br>* `apply_on`: **Required.** `INVOICE_AMOUNT` to discount the invoice total, or `SPECIFIC_ITEM_PRICE` to discount the item prices the action applies to.<br>* `discount`: **Required.** The discount to apply, such as `12.0`.<br>* `discount_type`: **Required.** `PERCENTAGE`, `FLAT_FEE`, or `OFFER_QUANTITY`, which fixes how `discount` is read.<br>* `duration_type`: **Required.** How long the discount applies, as `ONE_TIME`, `FOREVER`, or `LIMITED_PERIOD`.<br>* `period_unit`: `DAY`, `WEEK`, `MONTH`, or `YEAR`. Required if `duration_type` is `LIMITED_PERIOD`.<br>* `period`: The number of `period_unit`s the discount applies for. Required if `period_unit` is passed.  <br><br>### Apply coupon<br><br>Applies existing [coupons](/docs/api/coupons). Built from `action_template_id` `action-apply-coupon` and returned with `type` `APPLY_COUPON`.<br><br>* `apply_on`: **Required.** `INVOICE_AMOUNT` or `SPECIFIC_ITEM_PRICE`.<br>* `coupon_ids`: **Required.** The coupons to apply, as an array of coupon identifiers. It must hold at least one identifier.  <br><br>### Limit discount<br><br>Caps the discount that can be given. Use this template to enforce a discount ceiling without an approval step.<br><br>Built from `action_template_id` `action-limit-discount` and returned with `type` `LIMIT_DISCOUNT`.<br><br>* `apply_on`: **Required.** `INVOICE_AMOUNT` or `SPECIFIC_ITEM_PRICE`.<br>* `maximum_discount`: **Required.** The largest discount allowed, such as `20.0`.<br>* `discount_type`: **Required.** `PERCENTAGE`, `FLAT_FEE`, or `OFFER_QUANTITY`, which fixes how `maximum_discount` is read.<br>* `disable_price_override`: Pass `true` to disallow overriding the price outright.  <br><br>### Limit quantity<br><br>Constrains the quantities that can be selected. Built from `action_template_id` `action-limit-quantity` and returned with `type` `LIMIT_QUANTITY`. Every parameter is optional, so pass the ones you want to enforce.<br><br>* `minimum_quantity`: The smallest quantity allowed.<br>* `maximum_quantity`: The largest quantity allowed.<br>* `quantity_step_count`: The increment the quantity can be changed in, so `5` allows 5, 10, 15, and so on.  <br><br>### Error<br><br>Returns an error message instead of a change. Use this template to block an operation when the rule matches.<br><br>Built from `action_template_id` `action-error` and returned with `type` `ERROR`.<br><br>* `error_message`: **Required.** The message returned with the action.<br><br>Evaluation results<br>------------------<br><br>[Apply business rules](/docs/api/business_rules/apply-business-rules) returns an `apply_rule` object that echoes back the `context` you passed and carries one entry in `rules` for each rule it evaluated:<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "apply_rule": {<br>    "context": {<br>      "type": "CPQ",<br>      "customer": { "language": "en" },<br>      "quote": { "shipping_address_country": "IN" }<br>    },<br>    "rules": [<br>      {<br>        "id": "quote-discount-en",<br>        "version": 1,<br>        "name": "Apply 12 percent discount at invoice level",<br>        "evaluation_result": true,<br>        "actions": [<br>          {<br>            "action_template_id": "action-apply-discount",<br>            "type": "APPLY_DISCOUNT",<br>            "input": {<br>              "apply_on": "INVOICE_AMOUNT",<br>              "discount": 12.0,<br>              "discount_type": "PERCENTAGE",<br>              "duration_type": "ONE_TIME"<br>            }<br>          }<br>        ],<br>        "object": "applied_rule"<br>      },<br>      {<br>        "id": "quote-discount-uk",<br>        "version": 1,<br>        "name": "Apply 5 percent discount at invoice level for UK quotes",<br>        "evaluation_result": false,<br>        "object": "applied_rule"<br>      }<br>    ],<br>    "object": "apply_rule"<br>  }<br>}<br>```<br><br>Read the result of each rule from `evaluation_result`, and read what the rule produced from `actions`. Two things about the shape are worth knowing before you write code against it.<br><br>* `actions` is absent, rather than empty, for a rule whose `evaluation_result` is `false`. The second entry above shows a rule that didn't match.<br>* An entry for an ad hoc `structured_expression` carries only `evaluation_result`, because there's no stored rule to report an `id`, `name`, or `actions` for.<br><br>A rule that couldn't be evaluated is returned with `error_message` set instead, but only if you passed `skip_failed_rules` as `true`. Otherwise the request fails. For the full list of fields, see the response of [Apply business rules](/docs/api/business_rules/apply-business-rules).<br>|

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Webhook received successfully|None|

## Triggered when dunning is paused for an invoice

<a id="opIdonDunning_updatedWebhook"></a>

`POST dunning_updated`

> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-dunning-is-paused-for-an-invoice-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[DunningUpdatedEvent](#schemadunningupdatedevent)|false|Payload for dunning_updated event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » invoice|body|[Invoice](#schemainvoice)|true|An invoice is a commercial document representing a sale of products/services offered by you to a customer. It enumerates all the charges, adjustments, payments, discounts and taxes associated with the sale.<br><br>An invoice is said to be a recurring one when it is has at least one charge for [a plan or an addon item price](/docs/api/items). It is a non-recurring one when it has charges for only charge-item prices or [one-time charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/charges.html).<br><br>The item prices for any given billing term of a subscription are billed via an invoice at the beginning of the term (unless the charges are left unbilled). However, item prices that belong to `metered` items are billed at the end of the term via a `pending` invoice that can [close automatically](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing#configuring-metered-billing) or via [an API call](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice). Moreover, when there are no `metered` items in the subscription, the invoices can still be generated as `pending` while [creating](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items) or [updating](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items) a subscription.<br><br>#### Auto-collection<br><br>If [auto-collection](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#auto-collection-status) is enabled, then immediately on invoice generation (or, in case of subscriptions that have `create_pending_invoices` as `true`, on [invoice closure](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice)), the [payment method](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#payment_method) on file is charged:<br><br>* If the payment succeeds, the invoice is marked as `paid`.<br>* On payment failure, the invoice is marked as `payment_due` and [dunning settings](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/dunning-v2.html) are taken into account for payment retries.<br>* If no retry attempts are configured, or when retries are exhausted, the invoice is marked as `not_paid`.<br>* the amount due is zero or negative, the invoice is immediately marked as `paid` and the balance, if any, is added to [excess payments](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#excess-payments) for the customer.<br><br>**Note:** If [consolidated invoicing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html) is enabled, the attribute `subscription_id` is unavailable when the invoice has line items from multiple subscriptions. The individual subscription ids are seen under `line_items.subscription_id`.  <br><br>#### Recurring and non-recurring invoices<br><br>A recurring invoice contains at least one line item that is billed on a recurring basis. Specifically, it has at least one [`line_items[]`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#line_items) with `entity_type` set to `plan_item_price` or `addon_item_price`. A non-recurring invoice contains no recurring line items.  <br><br>#### Refundable amount for an invoice<br><br>The refundable amount for an invoice is the (amount paid on the invoice + refundable credit applied on the invoice + taxes withheld on the invoice) minus (amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice). Each of these amounts is obtained from the invoice resource as follows:<br><br>* Amount paid on the invoice: [`amount_paid`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_amount_paid)<br>* Refundable credit applied on the invoice: [`credits_applied`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_credits_applied)<br>* Taxes withheld on the invoice: Sum of [`linked_taxes_withheld[].amount`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_linked_taxes_withheld)<br>* Amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice: Sum of [`issued_credit_notes[i].cn_total`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_issued_credit_notes) where `issued_credit_notes[i].cn_status` is `refunded` or `refund_due`.<br>|

|200|OK|Webhook received successfully|None|

`POST omnichannel_subscription_item_recovered`

Triggered when an omnichannel subscription item recovers from a billing issue and is active again.


|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|

|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » omnichannel_subscription_item|body|[OmnichannelSubscriptionItem](#schemaomnichannelsubscriptionitem)|true|Represents a product entitlement (item) within an [`omnichannel_subscription`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscriptions) purchased on Apple App Store or Google Play Store.<br><br>Status, auto-renew, term dates, and cancel/expire reasons live on this resource. See [omnichannel statuses](/docs/api/omnichannel_statuses) for store mappings.<br><br>Chargebee records introductory and promotional offers on [`omnichannel_subscription_item_offers`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_items/omnichannel_subscription_item-object#omnichannel_subscription_item_offers). Win-back offers and offer codes are not supported.<br><br>When `has_scheduled_changes` is `true`, use [List scheduled changes](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_items/list-scheduled-changes-for-omnichannel-subscription-item) to retrieve deferred product or pause changes.  <br>**Note:**<br>This resource represents in-app subscription items made on Apple App Store and Google Play Store.<br>|

They are store-managed: lifecycle changes come from Apple or Google, not from the Chargebee Subscriptions API.<br><br>Use [omnichannel statuses](/docs/api/omnichannel_statuses) for how store statuses map to `omnichannel_subscription_item.status`, and [omnichannel events](/docs/api/omnichannel_events) for notification-to-webhook mappings.<br><br>Chargebee records introductory and promotional offers on [`omnichannel_subscription_item_offers`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscriptions/omnichannel_subscription-object#omnichannel_subscription_items_omnichannel_subscription_item_offers). Win-back offers and offer codes are not supported.  <br>**Identifier tip:** Parent `id_at_source` is the Apple **Transaction ID** or Google **purchase token** . Nested `initial_purchase_transaction.id_at_source` is the Apple **Transaction ID** or Google **Order ID** (`GPA....`). See attribute descriptions below.  <br>**Note:**<br>This resource represents in-app subscriptions made on Apple App Store and Google Play Store.<br>|
|» » omnichannel_transaction|body|[OmnichannelTransaction](#schemaomnichanneltransaction)|true|A unified representation of a store purchase or renewal transaction across Apple App Store and Google Play Store.<br><br>Use `id_at_source` to correlate with the store-native transaction identifier:<br><br>* **Apple App Store** : App Store **Transaction ID**<br>* **Google Play Store** : Google Play **Order ID** (`GPA....`)<br><br>Parent subscription / one-time-order resources use purchase-token semantics for Google `id_at_source`; do not treat those as interchangeable with this transaction Order ID.<br><br>### Apple App Store<br><br>The [price](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appstoreservernotifications/price) value reflects the price you configured in App Store Connect, which the system records at the time of transaction ([transacted_at](/docs/api/omnichannel_transactions/omnichannel_transaction-object#transacted_at)) after the discount if any offers are applied.  <br>**Important**<br>For financial and accounting purposes, use the App Store Connect reporting tools. For more information, see [Download financial reports](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/getting-paid/download-financial-reports) and [Overview of reporting tools](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/measure-app-performance/overview-of-reporting-tools).<br>[Learn more](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appstoreservernotifications/price) about price in Apple App Store.<br><br>### Google Play Store<br><br>Google Play does not always expose a complete transaction amount or purchase time for every notification path. When Google provides price / time data for a transaction, Chargebee records `price_*` and `transacted_at`; otherwise these attributes may be absent. Some Google one-time-order samples include price and `transacted_at` on `purchase_transaction`.<br><br>Transactions can be linked to subscriptions and/or one-time orders via `linked_omnichannel_subscriptions` and `linked_omnichannel_one_time_orders`. Chargebee may also emit [`omnichannel_transaction_created`](/docs/api/events/webhook/omnichannel_transaction_created) when a new transaction row is recorded.<br>|
|» » customer|body|[Customer](#schemacustomer)|true|Represents a customer, which can be an individual or organization that subscribes to your products or services. The customer resource associates with [subscriptions](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object), [card information](/docs/api/cards/card-object), and billing addresses. The customer details include their ID, name, contact information, and any [custom attributes](/docs/api/advanced-features) you'd like to associate with them.  <br>**Breaking Change**:<br><br>* [**Sites**](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/sites-intro.html) **created before March 1, 2014** : [updating the card](/docs/api/cards/update-card-for-a-customer) deletes the customer's `billing_address` and `vat_number` and replaces them with values from the request.<br>* **Sites created on or after March 1, 2014** : updating the card doesn't change the `billing_address` and `vat_number`.<br>|

```json
null
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » feature|body|[Feature](#schemafeature)|true|Subscriptions are created in Chargebee using items. Items represent the products or services that you offer to your customers. Items often differ in the number of product features that are available to them. The Features API helps you define the various features offered as part of your product line. It also defines the entitlements that items and subscriptions can have towards said features.  <br>**Note**<br><br>The maximum number of features a site can have is 400.<br><br>Features of this API<br>--------------------<br><br>The Features API enables you to:<br><br>* Define the set of features provided by your product.<br>* Specify the entitlements that items have towards said features.<br>* For a given subscription, modify the entitlements inherited from items in the subscription.<br>* Offer additional feature entitlements to subscriptions than those inherited from items in the subscription.<br>* Serve as a source of truth to your provisioning systems for subscription entitlements.<br>* Use entitlement information to understand which features drive value and revenue.<br><br>**See also**<br><br>* [Entitlements](/docs/api/entitlements)<br>* [Subscription Entitlements](/docs/api/subscription_entitlements)<br>* [Entitlement Overrides](/docs/api/entitlement_overrides)<br>|
|» » metadata|body|[Metadata](#schemametadata)|true|none|
|» » impacted_item|body|[ImpactedItem](#schemaimpacteditem)|true|Item entitlements can change due to certain events in Chargebee. The impacted_items represents the items whose entitlements have changed owing to an event. It is returned as part of the content attribute of the webhook triggered by the event. The following events can contain the impacted_items resource:<br><br>* A feature is created, activated, or deleted.<br>* An item_entitlement is updated or removed.<br>* An entitlement_override is auto-removed.<br><br>**Note**<br><br>impacted_items cannot be retrieved via API; the resource is sent to you only via webhooks.<br>|
|» » impacted_subscription|body|[ImpactedSubscription](#schemaimpactedsubscription)|true|When certain [events](/docs/api/events) in Chargebee cause changes to [subscription entitlements](/docs/api/subscription_entitlements), the `impacted_subscriptions` resource indicates the affected subscriptions. This resource is part of the `content` attribute of the triggered [webhook](/docs/api/webhooks) for the following events:<br><br>* When a `feature` is [created](/docs/api/events), [activated](/docs/api/events), or [deleted](/docs/api/events).<br>* When an `item_entitlement` is [updated](/docs/api/events) or [removed](/docs/api/events).<br>* When an `entitlement_override` is [updated](/docs/api/events), [removed](/docs/api/events), or [auto-removed](/docs/api/events).<br><br>**Note**<br><br>* Only a maximum of 100,000 subscription IDs are reported. [Contact Support](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/kb/getting-started/how-to-contact-chargebees-support-team?utm_source=docs_api&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=support) to increase this limit for your Chargebee site.<br>* You can't retrieve `impacted_subscriptions` through the API. Only webhooks send you this resource.<br>|

Invoices can also be [generated in advance](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/advance-invoices.html) for an upcoming renewal or set of renewals. With Advance Invoicing Schedules, you can set up a plan for when such advance invoices are generated for the lifetime of the subscription. This helps you:<br><br>* Set up a contract with your customers so that they can be notified of their payment schedules in advance.<br>* Allow customers who make offline payments to be alerted about their upcoming dues well ahead of actual subscription renewals.<br>* Prevent post-renewal unpaid usage of your services by customers.<br><br>Advance invoices can be scheduled in two ways:<br><br>#### Specific Dates Schedule<br><br>Advance invoices for a subscription can be scheduled to be generated on specific [dates](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#specific_dates_schedule_date) in the future. You must specify the [number of billing cycles](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#specific_dates_schedule_terms_to_charge) to be invoiced on each date. A maximum of 5 dates can be specified.<br><br>#### Fixed Interval Schedule<br><br>Advance invoices can be scheduled to be generated at fixed intervals of time, where each interval spans the same number of billing cycles of the subscription. The invoice for each interval is generated a specified number of days ([`days_before_interval`](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#fixed_interval_schedule_days_before_renewal)) before the start of the interval. You can configure the schedule to end on a certain date or after a specified number of advance invoices have been generated.<br><br>The start date of the first interval depends on the number of days remaining from current time till the next renewal of the subscription. If this is more than `days_before_interval`, the interval begins at the next renewal. On the other hand, if the number of days remaining before the next renewal is less than `days_before_interval`, the first interval begins at the renewal following the next.<br>|

|» » invoice|body|[Invoice](#schemainvoice)|true|An invoice is a commercial document representing a sale of products/services offered by you to a customer. It enumerates all the charges, adjustments, payments, discounts and taxes associated with the sale.<br><br>An invoice is said to be a recurring one when it is has at least one charge for [a plan or an addon item price](/docs/api/items). It is a non-recurring one when it has charges for only charge-item prices or [one-time charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/charges.html).<br><br>The item prices for any given billing term of a subscription are billed via an invoice at the beginning of the term (unless the charges are left unbilled). However, item prices that belong to `metered` items are billed at the end of the term via a `pending` invoice that can [close automatically](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing#configuring-metered-billing) or via [an API call](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice). Moreover, when there are no `metered` items in the subscription, the invoices can still be generated as `pending` while [creating](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items) or [updating](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items) a subscription.<br><br>#### Auto-collection<br><br>If [auto-collection](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#auto-collection-status) is enabled, then immediately on invoice generation (or, in case of subscriptions that have `create_pending_invoices` as `true`, on [invoice closure](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice)), the [payment method](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#payment_method) on file is charged:<br><br>* If the payment succeeds, the invoice is marked as `paid`.<br>* On payment failure, the invoice is marked as `payment_due` and [dunning settings](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/dunning-v2.html) are taken into account for payment retries.<br>* If no retry attempts are configured, or when retries are exhausted, the invoice is marked as `not_paid`.<br>* the amount due is zero or negative, the invoice is immediately marked as `paid` and the balance, if any, is added to [excess payments](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#excess-payments) for the customer.<br><br>**Note:** If [consolidated invoicing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html) is enabled, the attribute `subscription_id` is unavailable when the invoice has line items from multiple subscriptions. The individual subscription ids are seen under `line_items.subscription_id`.  <br><br>#### Recurring and non-recurring invoices<br><br>A recurring invoice contains at least one line item that is billed on a recurring basis. Specifically, it has at least one [`line_items[]`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#line_items) with `entity_type` set to `plan_item_price` or `addon_item_price`. A non-recurring invoice contains no recurring line items.  <br><br>#### Refundable amount for an invoice<br><br>The refundable amount for an invoice is the (amount paid on the invoice + refundable credit applied on the invoice + taxes withheld on the invoice) minus (amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice). Each of these amounts is obtained from the invoice resource as follows:<br><br>* Amount paid on the invoice: [`amount_paid`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_amount_paid)<br>* Refundable credit applied on the invoice: [`credits_applied`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_credits_applied)<br>* Taxes withheld on the invoice: Sum of [`linked_taxes_withheld[].amount`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_linked_taxes_withheld)<br>* Amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice: Sum of [`issued_credit_notes[i].cn_total`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_issued_credit_notes) where `issued_credit_notes[i].cn_status` is `refunded` or `refund_due`.<br>|

The essential components of a subscription are:<br><br>* A [plan-item price](/docs/api/item_prices).<br>* Any addon- and charge-item prices applied to the subscription.<br>* Any [coupons](/docs/api/coupons) applied.<br>* Any [discounts](/docs/api/discounts) applied.<br><br>The charges in a subscription are billed via invoices.  <br>**Note:**<br>The maximum number of subscriptions for any given [customer](/docs/api/customers)<br>([active](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object#status)<br>or not) is 900.  <br><br>#### Subscription billing frequencies<br><br>Chargebee offers two billing frequency options for subscriptions:<br><br>* **Plan-based billing** (`default`): Subscriptions are billed based on the billing period defined for the item price of the `item_type` `plan`. [Learn more](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/subscriptions#plan-based-billing).<br><br>* **Multi-frequency billing** : Subscriptions are billed according to the billing period of each recurring item price within the subscription. [Learn more](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/multi-frequency-billing).<br><br>  **Important**<br><br>  [Limitations](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/multi-frequency-billing#limitations) of Multi-frequency billing.<br><br>The selection of the billing frequency preference is configured at the site level.  <br><br>#### Item price compatibility in a subscription<br><br>When creating or updating a subscription, one of the item prices specified under subscription_items must be a plan-item price. The remaining must be compatible addon- or charge-item prices. An item price is compatible with a plan-item price if their currencies are the same. Additionally, an addon-item price is compatible with a plan-item price only if their billing frequencies meet the following conditions:  <br><br>\| `period_unit` for plan-item price \| Compatible `period_unit` for addon-item price \|                                                                                                                                                                                                Compatible period for addon-item price                                                                                                                                                                                                \|<br>\|-----------------------------------\|-----------------------------------------------\|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\|<br>\| `day`                             \| `day`                                         \| The `period` of the plan-item price should be divisible by the `period` of the addon-item price. **Example** If the `period` of the plan-item price is `10`, then the period of the addon-item price can be `10`, `5`, `2`, or `1`.                                                                                                                                                                                                  \|<br>\| `week`                            \| `week` or `day`                               \| The `period` (in days) of the plan-item price should be divisible by the `period` of the addon-item price. **Example** If the `period` of the plan-item price is `2`, then the period of the addon-item price can be as follows depending on the value of `period_unit`: * for `period_unit` as `week`, `period` can be `2` or `1`. * for `period_unit` as `day`, `period` can be `14`, `7`, `2`, or `1`.                            \|<br>\| `month`                           \| `month`                                       \| The `period` of the plan-item price should be divisible by the `period` of the addon-item price. **Example** If the `period` of the plan-item price is `6`, then the `period` of the addon-item price can be `6`, `3`, `2`, or `1`.                                                                                                                                                                                                  \|<br>\| `year`                            \| `year` or `month`                             \| The `period` (in months) of the plan-item price should be divisible by the `period` of the addon-item price. **Example** If the `period` of the plan-item price is `2`, then the `period` of the addon-item price can be as follows depending on the value of `period_unit`: * for `period_unit` as `year`, `period` can be `2` or `1`. * for `period_unit` as |» » advance_invoice_schedule|body|[AdvanceInvoiceSchedule](#schemaadvanceinvoiceschedule)|true|The invoice for a subscription in Chargebee is generated at the time of subscription renewal. Invoices can also be [generated in advance](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/advance-invoices.html) for an upcoming renewal or set of renewals. With Advance Invoicing Schedules, you can set up a plan for when such advance invoices are generated for the lifetime of the subscription. This helps you:<br><br>* Set up a contract with your customers so that they can be notified of their payment schedules in advance.<br>* Allow customers who make offline payments to be alerted about their upcoming dues well ahead of actual subscription renewals.<br>* Prevent post-renewal unpaid usage of your services by customers.<br><br>Advance invoices can be scheduled in two ways:<br><br>#### Specific Dates Schedule<br><br>Advance invoices for a subscription can be scheduled to be generated on specific [dates](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#specific_dates_schedule_date) in the future. You must specify the [number of billing cycles](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#specific_dates_schedule_terms_to_charge) to be invoiced on each date. A maximum of 5 dates can be specified.<br><br>#### Fixed Interval Schedule<br><br>Advance invoices can be scheduled to be generated at fixed intervals of time, where each interval spans the same number of billing cycles of the subscription. The invoice for each interval is generated a specified number of days ([`days_before_interval`](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#fixed_interval_schedule_days_before_renewal)) before the start of the interval. You can configure the schedule to end on a certain date or after a specified number of advance invoices have been generated.<br><br>The start date of the first interval depends on the number of days remaining from current time till the next renewal of the subscription. If this is more than `days_before_interval`, the interval begins at the next renewal. On the other hand, if the number of days remaining before the next renewal is less than `days_before_interval`, the first interval begins at the renewal following the next.<br>|

|» » coupon|body|[Coupon](#schemacoupon)|true|Overview<br>--------<br><br>Coupons are deductions applied to invoices or invoice line items. They're designed to be consumed by your customers directly. A coupon deduction can either be for a fixed amount or for a percentage of the amount of the invoice or line item.  <br>**Note:**<br><br>If you wish to provide discounts to your customers via API or the Chargebee app, see [Discounts API](/docs/api/discounts)<br><br>Order of application of coupons and discounts<br>---------------------------------------------<br><br>When both [coupons](/docs/api/coupons) and [discounts](/docs/api/discounts) are applied simultaneously to a [subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions) or [one-time invoice](/docs/api/invoices/create-invoice-for-items-and-one-time-charges), they're applied in the following order:  <br><br>\|---\|---------------------------------------\|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\|<br>\|   \| **Summary**                           \| **Description**                                                                     \|<br>\| 1 \| Line-level, fixed amount coupons      \| `coupon` with `apply_on` = `each_specified_item` and `discount_type` = `flat`       \|<br>\| 2 \| Line-level, fixed amount discounts    \| `discount` with `apply_on` = `specific_item_price` and `type` = `fixed_amount`      \|<br>\| 3 \| Line-level, percentage coupons        \| `coupon` with `apply_on` = `each_specified_item` and `discount_type` = `percentage` \|<br>\| 4 \| Line-level, percentage discounts      \| `discount` with `apply_on` = `specific_item_price` and `type` = `percentage`        \|<br>\| 5 \| Invoice-level, fixed amount coupons   \| `coupon` with `apply_on` = `invoice_amount` and `discount_type` = `flat`            \|<br>\| 6 \| Invoice-level, fixed amount discounts \| `discount` with `apply_on` = `invoice_amount` and `type` = `fixed_amount`           \|<br>\| 7 \| Invoice-level, percentage coupons     \| `coupon` with `apply_on` = `invoice_amount` and `discount_type` = `percentage`      \|<br>\| 8 \| Invoice-level, percentage discounts   \| `discount` with `apply_on` = `invoice_amount` and `type` = `percentage`             \|<br><br>For example, consider the following scenario:<br><br>A subscription is created with:<br><br>* a plan price of $200 per month<br>* an addon price of $20 per month<br>* a flat $5 invoice discount<br>* a 1% off coupon on the addon<br>* a flat $2 coupon on the invoice<br><br>The above coupons and discount are applied in the following order:  <br><br>\|---\|---------------------------------------------\|-----------------------------------------------\|<br>\|   \| **Discount or coupon applied**              \| **Subtotal at each step**                     \|<br>\| 1 \| Initial subtotal (plan price + addon price) \| $200 + $20 = $220                             \|<br>\| 2 \| 1% off coupon on the addon                  \| $200 + $(20 - 0.02) = $200 + $19.98 = $219.98 \|<br>\| 3 \| Flat $2 coupon on the invoice               \| $219.98 - $2 = $217.98                        \|<br>\| 4 \| Flat $5 invoice discount                    \| $217.98 - $5 = **$212.98**                    \|<br><br>|

## Triggered when a credit note is updated.

<a id="opIdonCredit_note_updatedWebhook"></a>

`POST credit_note_updated`

Triggered when a credit note is updated.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-credit-note-is-updated-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreditNoteUpdatedEvent](#schemacreditnoteupdatedevent)|false|Payload for credit_note_updated event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » credit_note|body|[CreditNote](#schemacreditnote)|true|A [Credit Note](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/credit-notes.html) is a document that specifies the money owed by a business to its customer. The seller usually issues a Credit Note for the same or lower amount than the invoice, and then repays the money to the customer or set it off against other 'due' invoices.<br><br>### Credit Note Types<br><br>Credit notes in Chargebee are categorized into three types:<br>1. `adjustment`: Adjustment credit notes are used to adjust the amount of an existing invoice in the `payment_due` or `not_paid` [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status). Use this type of credit note to reduce the invoice amount, typically as a discount to the customer.<br><br>Adjustment credit notes are automatically created in the following cases:<br><br>* When an invoice is written off.<br>* When a subscription is modified with proration enabled, and the invoice for the current term is in the `payment_due` or `not_paid` [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status). 2. `refundable`: Refundable credit notes allow you to return a certain amount to the customer. These credits can be:<br>* Retained for automatic application on future invoices.<br>* Applied to existing unpaid invoices.<br>* Refunded to the customer. Refundable credit notes are automatically created in the following cases:<br>* When an invoice is refunded.<br>* When a subscription is changed or canceled with proration enabled, the invoice for the current term is in the `paid` [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status). Refundable credits are applied to future invoices or can be refunded to the original payment method. 3. `store`: Store credit notes are created for `paid` or `partially_paid` invoice [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status) during subscription changes, such as upgrades, downgrades, or cancellations. Key characteristics of store credits:<br>* No tax component is included at the time of creation.<br>* A credit note document is generated, similar to refundable credits.<br>* Store credits are applied before tax calculations on future invoices.<br><br>**Note:**<br>If you have enabled *consolidated invoicing*<br>, to know the subscriptions attached with a credit note you have to refer [line_item's](/docs/api/credit_notes/credit_note-object#line_items)<br>*subscription_id*<br>. The credit note's *subscription_id*<br>should **not**<br>be used (which will be *null*<br>if the credit note has lines from multiple subscriptions).  <br>Impact on reference invoice  <br>The following updates are made to the reference invoice when a credit note is created/imported:<br><br>* If the credit note `type` is `adjustment`:<br>  * The adjustment credit note details are added to the `adjustment_credit_notes[]` attribute of the invoice.<br>  * The invoice `amount_due` is reduced by the credit note `total`.<br>  * The invoice `status` is updated to `paid` if the invoice `amount_due` equals the credit note `total`.<br>  * The invoice `status` does not change if the invoice `amount_due` is greater than credit note `total`.<br>* If the credit note `type` is `refundable`:<br>  * The refundable credit note details are added to the `issued_credit_notes[]` attribute of the invoice.<br>  * The invoice `status` does not change.<br>* If the credit note `type` is `store`:<br>  * The store credit note details are added to the `issued_credit_notes[]` attribute of the invoice.<br>  * The invoice `status` does not change.<br>|

They are store-managed: lifecycle changes come from Apple or Google, not from the Chargebee Subscriptions API.<br><br>Use [omnichannel statuses](/docs/api/omnichannel_statuses) for how store statuses map to `omnichannel_subscription_item.status`, and [omnichannel events](/docs/api/omnichannel_events) for notification-to-webhook mappings.<br><br>Chargebee records introductory and promotional offers on [`omnichannel_subscription_item_offers`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscriptions/omnichannel_subscription-object#omnichannel_subscription_items_omnichannel_subscription_item_offers). See attribute descriptions below.  <br>**Note:**<br>This resource represents in-app subscriptions made on Apple App Store and Google Play Store.<br>|

For more information, see [Download financial reports](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/getting-paid/download-financial-reports) and [Overview of reporting tools](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/measure-app-performance/overview-of-reporting-tools).<br>[Learn more](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appstoreservernotifications/price) about price in Apple App Store.<br><br>### Google Play Store<br><br>Google Play does not always expose a complete transaction amount or purchase time for every notification path. When Google provides price / time data for a transaction, Chargebee records `price_*` and `transacted_at`; otherwise these attributes may be absent. Some Google one-time-order samples include price and `transacted_at` on `purchase_transaction`.<br><br>Transactions can be linked to subscriptions and/or one-time orders via `linked_omnichannel_subscriptions` and `linked_omnichannel_one_time_orders`. Chargebee may also emit [`omnichannel_transaction_created`](/docs/api/events/webhook/omnichannel_transaction_created) when a new transaction row is recorded.<br>|

## Triggered when a business ruleset is deactivated

<a id="opIdonBusiness_ruleset_deactivatedWebhook"></a>

`POST business_ruleset_deactivated`

> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-business-ruleset-is-deactivated-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[BusinessRulesetDeactivatedEvent](#schemabusinessrulesetdeactivatedevent)|false|Payload for business_ruleset_deactivated event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » business_ruleset|body|[BusinessRuleset](#schemabusinessruleset)|true|A business ruleset groups [business rules](/docs/api/business_rules) so that they can be evaluated together, in the priority order you assign, using the strategy set in `execute_mode`.<br><br>Rulesets let you apply a whole decision at once instead of calling each rule separately. Passing a `ruleset_id` to [Apply business rules](/docs/api/business_rules/apply-business-rules) evaluates the rules the ruleset contains in their priority order and returns a result for each one. The `execute_mode` decides whether evaluation runs through every rule or stops as soon as a rule evaluates to `true` or to `false`, and which of the results are returned.<br><br>Membership is managed separately from the rules themselves. [Add business rules to a ruleset](/docs/api/business_rulesets/add-business-rules-to-a-ruleset) and [Remove business rules from a ruleset](/docs/api/business_rulesets/remove-business-rules-from-a-ruleset) change membership incrementally, while passing `rules` to [Update a business ruleset](/docs/api/business_rulesets/update-a-business-ruleset) replaces it entirely. A rule can belong to more than one ruleset, and removing it from a ruleset does not delete the rule.<br><br>The `active` attribute controls whether Chargebee evaluates the ruleset. A rule is evaluated through a ruleset only when both the ruleset and the rule are `active`.  <br>**Note:** Business rules are not enabled by default. Contact [Chargebee Support](https://www.chargebee.com/support/) to enable them for your site. Until they are enabled, these endpoints return an error.<br>|

Passing a `ruleset_id` to [Apply business rules](/docs/api/business_rules/apply-business-rules) evaluates the rules the ruleset contains in their priority order and returns a result for each one. The `execute_mode` decides whether evaluation runs through every rule or stops as soon as a rule evaluates to `true` or to `false`, and which of the results are returned.<br><br>Membership is managed separately from the rules themselves. [Add business rules to a ruleset](/docs/api/business_rulesets/add-business-rules-to-a-ruleset) and [Remove business rules from a ruleset](/docs/api/business_rulesets/remove-business-rules-from-a-ruleset) change membership incrementally, while passing `rules` to [Update a business ruleset](/docs/api/business_rulesets/update-a-business-ruleset) replaces it entirely. A rule can belong to more than one ruleset, and removing it from a ruleset does not delete the rule.<br><br>The `active` attribute controls whether Chargebee evaluates the ruleset. A rule is evaluated through a ruleset only when both the ruleset and the rule are `active`.  <br>**Note:** Business rules are not enabled by default. Contact [Chargebee Support](https://www.chargebee.com/support/) to enable them for your site. Until they are enabled, these endpoints return an error.<br>|

It enumerates all the charges, adjustments, payments, discounts and taxes associated with the sale.<br><br>An invoice is said to be a recurring one when it is has at least one charge for [a plan or an addon item price](/docs/api/items). It is a non-recurring one when it has charges for only charge-item prices or [one-time charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/charges.html).<br><br>The item prices for any given billing term of a subscription are billed via an invoice at the beginning of the term (unless the charges are left unbilled). However, item prices that belong to `metered` items are billed at the end of the term via a `pending` invoice that can [close automatically](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing#configuring-metered-billing) or via [an API call](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice). Moreover, when there are no `metered` items in the subscription, the invoices can still be generated as `pending` while [creating](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items) or [updating](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items) a subscription.<br><br>#### Auto-collection<br><br>If [auto-collection](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#auto-collection-status) is enabled, then immediately on invoice generation (or, in case of subscriptions that have `create_pending_invoices` as `true`, on [invoice closure](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice)), the [payment method](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#payment_method) on file is charged:<br><br>* If the payment succeeds, the invoice is marked as `paid`.<br>* On payment failure, the invoice is marked as `payment_due` and [dunning settings](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/dunning-v2.html) are taken into account for payment retries.<br>* If no retry attempts are configured, or when retries are exhausted, the invoice is marked as `not_paid`.<br>* the amount due is zero or negative, the invoice is immediately marked as `paid` and the balance, if any, is added to [excess payments](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#excess-payments) for the customer.<br><br>**Note:** If [consolidated invoicing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html) is enabled, the attribute `subscription_id` is unavailable when the invoice has line items from multiple subscriptions. The individual subscription ids are seen under `line_items.subscription_id`.  <br><br>#### Recurring and non-recurring invoices<br><br>A recurring invoice contains at least one line item that is billed on a recurring basis. Specifically, it has at least one [`line_items[]`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#line_items) with `entity_type` set to `plan_item_price` or `addon_item_price`. A non-recurring invoice contains no recurring line items.  <br><br>#### Refundable amount for an invoice<br><br>The refundable amount for an invoice is the (amount paid on the invoice + refundable credit applied on the invoice + taxes withheld on the invoice) minus (amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice). Each of these amounts is obtained from the invoice resource as follows:<br><br>* Amount paid on the invoice: [`amount_paid`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_amount_paid)<br>* Refundable credit applied on the invoice: [`credits_applied`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_credits_applied)<br>* Taxes withheld on the invoice: Sum of [`linked_taxes_withheld[].amount`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_linked_taxes_withheld)<br>* Amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice: Sum of [`issued_credit_notes[i].cn_total`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_issued_credit_notes) where `issued_credit_notes[i].cn_status` is `refunded` or `refund_due`.<br>|

[Contact Support](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/kb/getting-started/how-to-contact-chargebees-support-team?utm_source=docs_api&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=support) to increase this limit for your Chargebee site.<br>* You can't retrieve `impacted_subscriptions` through the API. ## Triggered when a credit note is created.

<a id="opIdonCredit_note_createdWebhook"></a>

`POST credit_note_created`

Triggered when a credit note is created.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-credit-note-is-created-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreditNoteCreatedEvent](#schemacreditnotecreatedevent)|false|Payload for credit_note_created event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » credit_note|body|[CreditNote](#schemacreditnote)|true|A [Credit Note](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/credit-notes.html) is a document that specifies the money owed by a business to its customer. The seller usually issues a Credit Note for the same or lower amount than the invoice, and then repays the money to the customer or set it off against other 'due' invoices.<br><br>### Credit Note Types<br><br>Credit notes in Chargebee are categorized into three types:<br>1. `adjustment`: Adjustment credit notes are used to adjust the amount of an existing invoice in the `payment_due` or `not_paid` [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status). Use this type of credit note to reduce the invoice amount, typically as a discount to the customer.<br><br>Adjustment credit notes are automatically created in the following cases:<br><br>* When an invoice is written off.<br>* When a subscription is modified with proration enabled, and the invoice for the current term is in the `payment_due` or `not_paid` [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status). 2. `refundable`: Refundable credit notes allow you to return a certain amount to the customer. These credits can be:<br>* Retained for automatic application on future invoices.<br>* Applied to existing unpaid invoices.<br>* Refunded to the customer. Refundable credit notes are automatically created in the following cases:<br>* When an invoice is refunded.<br>* When a subscription is changed or canceled with proration enabled, the invoice for the current term is in the `paid` [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status). Refundable credits are applied to future invoices or can be refunded to the original payment method. 3. `store`: Store credit notes are created for `paid` or `partially_paid` invoice [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status) during subscription changes, such as upgrades, downgrades, or cancellations. Key characteristics of store credits:<br>* No tax component is included at the time of creation.<br>* A credit note document is generated, similar to refundable credits.<br>* Store credits are applied before tax calculations on future invoices.<br><br>**Note:**<br>If you have enabled *consolidated invoicing*<br>, to know the subscriptions attached with a credit note you have to refer [line_item's](/docs/api/credit_notes/credit_note-object#line_items)<br>*subscription_id*<br>. The credit note's *subscription_id*<br>should **not**<br>be used (which will be *null*<br>if the credit note has lines from multiple subscriptions).  <br>Impact on reference invoice  <br>The following updates are made to the reference invoice when a credit note is created/imported:<br><br>* If the credit note `type` is `adjustment`:<br>  * The adjustment credit note details are added to the `adjustment_credit_notes[]` attribute of the invoice.<br>  * The invoice `amount_due` is reduced by the credit note `total`.<br>  * The invoice `status` is updated to `paid` if the invoice `amount_due` equals the credit note `total`.<br>  * The invoice `status` does not change if the invoice `amount_due` is greater than credit note `total`.<br>* If the credit note `type` is `refundable`:<br>  * The refundable credit note details are added to the `issued_credit_notes[]` attribute of the invoice.<br>  * The invoice `status` does not change.<br>* If the credit note `type` is `store`:<br>  * The store credit note details are added to the `issued_credit_notes[]` attribute of the invoice.<br>  * The invoice `status` does not change.<br>|

|200|OK|Webhook received successfully|None|

<h3 id="triggered-when-an-omnichannel-record-purchase-is-failed-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[RecordPurchaseFailedEvent](#schemarecordpurchasefailedevent)|false|Payload for record_purchase_failed event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » recorded_purchase|body|[RecordedPurchase](#schemarecordedpurchase)|true|**Important**<br><br>* Handle the **synchronous** API response first. Record a Purchase can fail immediately (for example, an incorrect `app_id`, a malformed URL or request, or recording a purchase that already belongs to a different customer) before a job is created---treat these as standard API errors (`4xx`). To reassign an existing omnichannel subscription to another customer, use [Move an omnichannel subscription](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscriptions/move-an-omnichannel-subscription) instead of re-recording the purchase.<br>* After the call is accepted, purchase validation with Apple or Google is **asynchronous** . Track the job with `status` (`in_process` → `completed`, `failed`, or `ignored`). Omnichannel subscription or one-time order creation happens only after successful async completion.<br>* This resource is applicable for Apple App Store and Google Play Store.<br><br>The recorded purchase resource represents a background job that syncs in-app purchases made through Apple App Store and Google Play Store with Chargebee. The [status](/docs/api/recorded_purchases/recorded_purchase-object#status) (`in_process`, `completed`, `failed`, and `ignored`) attribute represents the current status of the background job.<br><br>### Record Apple and Google in-app purchases and retrieve linked omnichannel resources<br><br>You can record subscription and one-time-order purchases made on Apple App Store or Google Play Store, then retrieve the resulting omnichannel resources.<br><br>To record a purchase and retrieve details, follow these steps:<br><br>1. Use the [Record a Purchase API](/docs/api/recorded_purchases/record-a-purchase) with `app_id`, `customer[id]`, and exactly one store payload:<br><br>   * **Apple App Store (preferred)** : `apple_app_store[transaction_id]` for a new subscription, expired re-purchase, or one-time product.<br><br>   * **Apple App Store (receipt path)** : `apple_app_store[receipt]` and `apple_app_store[product_id]`.<br><br>   * **Google Play Store (preferred)** : `google_play_store[order_id]` for a subscription or one-time order.<br><br>   * **Google Play Store (subscription token path)** : `google_play_store[purchase_token]`.<br><br>   * **Google Play Store (one-time order token path)** : `google_play_store[purchase_token]` and `google_play_store[product_id]`.<br><br>2. The API response includes a `recorded_purchase` object with the [status](/docs/api/recorded_purchases/recorded_purchase-object#status) of the job.<br><br>3. When recording completes successfully, `status` updates from `in_process` to `completed` and Chargebee sets `omnichannel_transaction_id` plus either:<br><br>   * **Subscription** : `linked_omnichannel_subscriptions`, with webhook [`omnichannel_subscription_created`](/docs/api/events/webhook/omnichannel_subscription_created) (or [`omnichannel_subscription_imported`](/docs/api/events/webhook/omnichannel_subscription_imported)).<br>   * **One-time order** : `linked_omnichannel_one_time_orders`, with webhook [`omnichannel_one_time_order_created`](/docs/api/events/webhook/omnichannel_one_time_order_created).<br>4. In addition to webhooks, retrieve the job by the `recorded_purchase` [id](/docs/api/recorded_purchases/recorded_purchase-object#id) returned when you record the purchase.<br><br>If `status` is `failed`, review [error_detail](/docs/api/recorded_purchases/recorded_purchase-object#error_detail) and see [`record_purchase_failed`](/docs/api/events/webhook/record_purchase_failed).<br><br>If `status` is `ignored`, the purchase was already recorded in Chargebee as an omnichannel subscription or one-time order. Chargebee does not create a new linked resource for this job---use the existing omnichannel subscription or one-time order. Linked IDs and `omnichannel_transaction_id` are populated when `status` is `completed`, not for `ignored`.<br><br>See also [omnichannel events](/docs/api/omnichannel_events).<br>|
|» » customer|body|[Customer](#schemacustomer)|true|Represents a customer, which can be an individual or organization that subscribes to your products or services. The customer resource associates with [subscriptions](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object), [card information](/docs/api/cards/card-object), and billing addresses. The customer details include their ID, name, contact information, and any [custom attributes](/docs/api/advanced-features) you'd like to associate with them.  <br>**Breaking Change**:<br><br>* [**Sites**](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/sites-intro.html) **created before March 1, 2014** : [updating the card](/docs/api/cards/update-card-for-a-customer) deletes the customer's `billing_address` and `vat_number` and replaces them with values from the request.<br>* **Sites created on or after March 1, 2014** : updating the card doesn't change the `billing_address` and `vat_number`.<br>|

Items therefore represent the various plans, addons or charges that you offer as part of your product catalog. Non-`metered` items are charged upfront in Chargebee, while `metered` items are charged at the end of the billing cycle, based on usage.<br><br>### Types of Items<br><br>There are three types of items and they're listed and explained here. Examples for each type are provided in the table that follows.<br><br>#### Plan-items or Plans<br><br>Plan-items are items that have a recurring charge and are an essential component of any [subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions). Typically, plans represent a principal or key product or service in your catalog. They are charged at recurring intervals and often have other products or services offered along with them as addons and charges.<br><br>#### Addon-items or Addons<br><br>Addon-items are items that are sold along with a plan and are charged for at recurring intervals.<br><br>#### Charge-items or Charges<br><br>Charge-items are items that are sold along with a plan but charged once (or each time) a specified event occurs. A charge can also be [applied to a customer](/docs/api/v2/pcv-1/invoices/create-invoice-for-a-one-time-charge) without attaching to a subscription.<br><br>#### Examples<br><br>To help understand each type of item better, listed below are some examples of items from different business domains:<br><br>##### Non-Metered (SaaS)<br><br>* **Item Family:** A project management solution.<br>* **Plans:**<br>  * A "basic" plan offering a small set of features.<br>  * A "business" plan offering a larger set of features.<br>* **Addons:**<br>  * An analytics plugin that is available only with the "business" plan.<br>  * A reporting plugin, available with both the above plans.<br>* **Charges:**<br>  * Implementation charges.<br>  * Trial charges.<br><br>##### Non-Metered (E-commerce)<br><br>* **Item Family:** A printed news magazine.<br>* **Plans:**<br>  * Periodic issues of the magazine.<br>  * Periodic issues of the magazine, with digital content.<br>* **Addons:**<br>  * Supplementary online content.<br>  * Access to a year's worth of back issues.<br>  * Searchable access to all back issues.<br>* **Charges:**<br>  * Special edition books that are published every so often.<br><br>##### Metered<br><br>* **Item Family:** SMS delivery services.<br>* **Plans:**<br>  * A basic plan of up to 100K messages @ $0.03 per message.<br>  * A volume plan of 2M messages @ $0.01 per message.<br>* **Addons:**<br>  * An addon of 50K MMS messages @ $0.1 per message.<br>  * Instant messaging.<br>* **Charges:**<br>  * Automated Metered Billing is not applicable for charges.<br>|

|» » business_ruleset|body|[BusinessRuleset](#schemabusinessruleset)|true|A business ruleset groups [business rules](/docs/api/business_rules) so that they can be evaluated together, in the priority order you assign, using the strategy set in `execute_mode`.<br><br>Rulesets let you apply a whole decision at once instead of calling each rule separately. Passing a `ruleset_id` to [Apply business rules](/docs/api/business_rules/apply-business-rules) evaluates the rules the ruleset contains in their priority order and returns a result for each one. The `execute_mode` decides whether evaluation runs through every rule or stops as soon as a rule evaluates to `true` or to `false`, and which of the results are returned.<br><br>Membership is managed separately from the rules themselves. [Add business rules to a ruleset](/docs/api/business_rulesets/add-business-rules-to-a-ruleset) and [Remove business rules from a ruleset](/docs/api/business_rulesets/remove-business-rules-from-a-ruleset) change membership incrementally, while passing `rules` to [Update a business ruleset](/docs/api/business_rulesets/update-a-business-ruleset) replaces it entirely. A rule can belong to more than one ruleset, and removing it from a ruleset does not delete the rule.<br><br>The `active` attribute controls whether Chargebee evaluates the ruleset. A rule is evaluated through a ruleset only when both the ruleset and the rule are `active`.  <br>**Note:** Business rules are not enabled by default. Contact [Chargebee Support](https://www.chargebee.com/support/) to enable them for your site. Until they are enabled, these endpoints return an error.<br>|

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Webhook received successfully|None|

This operation does not require authentication
