## Triggered when unbilled charges are invoiced

<a id="opIdonUnbilled_charges_invoicedWebhook"></a>

`POST unbilled_charges_invoiced`

Triggered when unbilled charges are invoiced


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-unbilled-charges-are-invoiced-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[UnbilledChargesInvoicedEvent](#schemaunbilledchargesinvoicedevent)|false|Payload for unbilled_charges_invoiced event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » unbilled_charges|body|[[UnbilledCharge](#schemaunbilledcharge)]|true|none|
|» » invoice|body|[Invoice](#schemainvoice)|true|An invoice is a commercial document representing a sale of products/services offered by you to a customer. It enumerates all the charges, adjustments, payments, discounts and taxes associated with the sale.<br><br>An invoice is said to be a recurring one when it is has at least one charge for [a plan or an addon item price](/docs/api/items). It is a non-recurring one when it has charges for only charge-item prices or [one-time charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/charges.html).<br><br>The item prices for any given billing term of a subscription are billed via an invoice at the beginning of the term (unless the charges are left unbilled). However, item prices that belong to `metered` items are billed at the end of the term via a `pending` invoice that can [close automatically](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing#configuring-metered-billing) or via [an API call](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice). Moreover, when there are no `metered` items in the subscription, the invoices can still be generated as `pending` while [creating](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items) or [updating](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items) a subscription.<br><br>#### Auto-collection<br><br>If [auto-collection](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#auto-collection-status) is enabled, then immediately on invoice generation (or, in case of subscriptions that have `create_pending_invoices` as `true`, on [invoice closure](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice)), the [payment method](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#payment_method) on file is charged:<br><br>* If the payment succeeds, the invoice is marked as `paid`.<br>* On payment failure, the invoice is marked as `payment_due` and [dunning settings](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/dunning-v2.html) are taken into account for payment retries.<br>* If no retry attempts are configured, or when retries are exhausted, the invoice is marked as `not_paid`.<br>* the amount due is zero or negative, the invoice is immediately marked as `paid` and the balance, if any, is added to [excess payments](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#excess-payments) for the customer.<br><br>**Note:** If [consolidated invoicing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html) is enabled, the attribute `subscription_id` is unavailable when the invoice has line items from multiple subscriptions. The individual subscription ids are seen under `line_items.subscription_id`.  <br><br>#### Recurring and non-recurring invoices<br><br>A recurring invoice contains at least one line item that is billed on a recurring basis. Specifically, it has at least one [`line_items[]`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#line_items) with `entity_type` set to `plan_item_price` or `addon_item_price`. A non-recurring invoice contains no recurring line items.  <br><br>#### Refundable amount for an invoice<br><br>The refundable amount for an invoice is the (amount paid on the invoice + refundable credit applied on the invoice + taxes withheld on the invoice) minus (amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice). Each of these amounts is obtained from the invoice resource as follows:<br><br>* Amount paid on the invoice: [`amount_paid`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_amount_paid)<br>* Refundable credit applied on the invoice: [`credits_applied`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_credits_applied)<br>* Taxes withheld on the invoice: Sum of [`linked_taxes_withheld[].amount`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_linked_taxes_withheld)<br>* Amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice: Sum of [`issued_credit_notes[i].cn_total`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_issued_credit_notes) where `issued_credit_notes[i].cn_status` is `refunded` or `refund_due`.<br>|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Webhook received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication

|» » dispute|body|[Dispute](#schemadispute)|true|This resource represents a [dispute](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/payments/2.0/others/chargeback) raised against a payment collected on your site. A dispute is created when a cardholder questions a payment with their card issuer, either as a formal `chargeback` or as a pre-chargeback `inquiry`.<br><br>Chargebee records each dispute against the [transaction](/docs/api/transactions/transaction-object) that was disputed, the [customer](/docs/api/customers/customer-object) who made the payment, and the gateway account that processed it. As the payment gateway moves the dispute toward a resolution, Chargebee updates the dispute [`status`](/docs/api/disputes/dispute-object#status).<br><br>Disputes are read-only through the API. Chargebee creates and updates them from the notifications it receives from the payment gateway, so there are no operations to create, update, or delete a dispute.<br>|
|» » transaction|body|[Transaction](#schematransaction)|true|This resource represents the [transaction](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/transactions.html)<br>event that has happened in your account.<br>|
|» » customer|body|[Customer](#schemacustomer)|true|Represents a customer, which can be an individual or organization that subscribes to your products or services. The customer resource associates with [subscriptions](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object), [card information](/docs/api/cards/card-object), and billing addresses. The customer details include their ID, name, contact information, and any [custom attributes](/docs/api/advanced-features) you'd like to associate with them.  <br>**Breaking Change**:<br><br>* [**Sites**](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/sites-intro.html) **created before March 1, 2014** : [updating the card](/docs/api/cards/update-card-for-a-customer) deletes the customer's `billing_address` and `vat_number` and replaces them with values from the request.<br>* **Sites created on or after March 1, 2014** : updating the card doesn't change the `billing_address` and `vat_number`.<br>|
|» » subscription|body|[Subscription](#schemasubscription)|true|A Chargebee subscription connects a customer record to products/services. It describes what the customer has signed up for and how often they're charged for it. The essential components of a subscription are:<br><br>* A [plan-item price](/docs/api/item_prices).<br>* Any addon- and charge-item prices applied to the subscription.<br>* Any [coupons](/docs/api/coupons) applied.<br>* Any [discounts](/docs/api/discounts) applied.<br><br>The charges in a subscription are billed via invoices.  <br>**Note:**<br>The maximum number of subscriptions for any given [customer](/docs/api/customers)<br>([active](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object#status)<br>or not) is 900.  <br><br>#### Subscription billing frequencies<br><br>Chargebee offers two billing frequency options for subscriptions:<br><br>* **Plan-based billing** (`default`): Subscriptions are billed based on the billing period defined for the item price of the `item_type` `plan`. [Learn more](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/subscriptions#plan-based-billing).<br><br>* **Multi-frequency billing** : Subscriptions are billed according to the billing period of each recurring item price within the subscription. [Learn more](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/multi-frequency-billing).<br><br>  **Important**<br><br>  [Limitations](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/multi-frequency-billing#limitations) of Multi-frequency billing.<br><br>The selection of the billing frequency preference is configured at the site level.  <br><br>#### Item price compatibility in a subscription<br><br>When creating or updating a subscription, one of the item prices specified under subscription_items must be a plan-item price. ## Triggered when an item price is updated.

<a id="opIdonItem_price_updatedWebhook"></a>

`POST item_price_updated`

Triggered when an item price is updated.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-an-item-price-is-updated-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ItemPriceUpdatedEvent](#schemaitempriceupdatedevent)|false|Payload for item_price_updated event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » item_price|body|[ItemPrice](#schemaitemprice)|true|An item price is a price point for an item. It defines the currency, pricing model, price, billing period and other attributes for an [item](/docs/api/items). For example, consider a cloud storage service as an item. Then each of the following defines an item price:<br><br>* The cloud storage sold at USD 10 per month.<br><br>* The same service sold at AUD 100 per year.<br><br>* The service sold at a monthly rate determined by the following [stairstep](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/plans.html#pricing-models) pricing model:<br><br>  * 1-10 users for EUR 10<br>  * 11-25 users for EUR 20<br>  * 26-50 users for EUR 45<br>  * 51 and above for EUR 100<br><br>Types of item prices<br>--------------------<br><br>The type of an item price corresponds to the [type of the item](/docs/api/items) that the item price belongs to. In other words, item prices can be of the following types:<br><br>* Plan-item prices<br>* Addon-item prices<br>* Charge-item prices<br><br>Billing periods for item prices<br>-------------------------------<br><br>The **billing period** of an item price (applicable only to plan-item prices and addon-item prices) is the [`period`](/docs/api/item_prices/item-price-object#period) of the item price in [`period_unit`](/docs/api/item_prices/item-price-object#period_unit)s.<br><br>* When [price variants](/docs/api/price_variants) are **not** enabled, an item can have only one item price for a given currency and billing period.<br>* When price variants **are** enabled, an item can have multiple item prices for the same currency and billing period, as long as each has a distinct [`price_variant_id`](/docs/api/item_prices/item-price-object#price_variant_id). An item price created without a `price_variant_id` is treated as the default ("no variant"), and only one such default item price can exist for a given currency and billing period.<br>|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Webhook received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

```json
null
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CouponCodesUpdatedEvent](#schemacouponcodesupdatedevent)|false|Payload for coupon_codes_updated event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|

|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » coupon|body|[Coupon](#schemacoupon)|true|Overview<br>--------<br><br>Coupons are deductions applied to invoices or invoice line items. They're designed to be consumed by your customers directly. A coupon deduction can either be for a fixed amount or for a percentage of the amount of the invoice or line item.  <br>**Note:**<br><br>If you wish to provide discounts to your customers via API or the Chargebee app, see [Discounts API](/docs/api/discounts)<br><br>Order of application of coupons and discounts<br>---------------------------------------------<br><br>When both [coupons](/docs/api/coupons) and [discounts](/docs/api/discounts) are applied simultaneously to a [subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions) or [one-time invoice](/docs/api/invoices/create-invoice-for-items-and-one-time-charges), they're applied in the following order:  <br><br>\|---\|---------------------------------------\|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\|<br>\|   \| **Summary**                           \| **Description**                                                                     \|<br>\| 1 \| Line-level, fixed amount coupons      \| `coupon` with `apply_on` = `each_specified_item` and `discount_type` = `flat`       \|<br>\| 2 \| Line-level, fixed amount discounts    \| `discount` with `apply_on` = `specific_item_price` and `type` = `fixed_amount`      \|<br>\| 3 \| Line-level, percentage coupons        \| `coupon` with `apply_on` = `each_specified_item` and `discount_type` = `percentage` \|<br>\| 4 \| Line-level, percentage discounts      \| `discount` with `apply_on` = `specific_item_price` and `type` = `percentage`        \|<br>\| 5 \| Invoice-level, fixed amount coupons   \| `coupon` with `apply_on` = `invoice_amount` and `discount_type` = `flat`            \|<br>\| 6 \| Invoice-level, fixed amount discounts \| `discount` with `apply_on` = `invoice_amount` and `type` = `fixed_amount`           \|<br>\| 7 \| Invoice-level, percentage coupons     \| `coupon` with `apply_on` = `invoice_amount` and `discount_type` = `percentage`      \|<br>\| 8 \| Invoice-level, percentage discounts   \| `discount` with `apply_on` = `invoice_amount` and `type` = `percentage`             \|<br><br>For example, consider the following scenario:<br><br>A subscription is created with:<br><br>* a plan price of $200 per month<br>* an addon price of $20 per month<br>* a flat $5 invoice discount<br>* a 1% off coupon on the addon<br>* a flat $2 coupon on the invoice<br><br>The above coupons and discount are applied in the following order:  <br><br>\|---\|---------------------------------------------\|-----------------------------------------------\|<br>\|   \| **Discount or coupon applied**              \| **Subtotal at each step**                     \|<br>\| 1 \| Initial subtotal (plan price + addon price) \| $200 + $20 = $220                             \|<br>\| 2 \| 1% off coupon on the addon                  \| $200 + $(20 - 0.02) = $200 + $19.98 = $219.98 \|<br>\| 3 \| Flat $2 coupon on the invoice               \| $219.98 - $2 = $217.98                        \|<br>\| 4 \| Flat $5 invoice discount                    \| $217.98 - $5 = **$212.98**                    \|<br><br>|
|» » coupon_set|body|[CouponSet](#schemacouponset)|true|A coupon set contains a bunch of coupon codes that can be redeemed by your customers when they are checking out. It belongs to an existing coupon and will usually be combined with other coupons that share similar promotion or discount offers. Using this resource, you can create, update, retrieve, delete coupon sets and add coupon codes to a coupon set.<br>|

|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » contract_term|body|[ContractTerm](#schemacontractterm)|true|Subscriptions can run indefinitely or they may run for a fixed number of billing cycles. Subscription can have "contract terms", which define a lock-in period on the subscription for a certain number of billing cycles. This prevents the subscription from being canceled by the customer when it is within the contract term.<br><br>The **contract term** resource described below defines the properties of this lock-in period. This includes the [number of billing cycles](/docs/api/contract_terms/contract_term-object#remaining_billing_cycles), the [total contract value](/docs/api/contract_terms/contract_term-object#total_contract_value), the [action to be taken](/docs/api/contract_terms/contract_term-object#action_at_term_end) at the end of the contract term, and so on. To allow for exceptions, you also have the option of terminating an [`active`](/docs/api/contract_terms/contract_term-object#status) contract term and charging a [termination fee](/docs/api/contract_terms).<br><br>A contract term starts in the `active` state and ends in the `completed` state. If the contract was canceled due to non-payment or other reasons, it can end in the `canceled` or `terminated` state. A given contract term is always associated with one, and only one subscription. A subscription, however, can be associated with only one `active` contract term. Over time, a subscription can be associated with several non-`active` contract terms. The `active` contract term for a subscription is available as an [object](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object#contract_term) within the subscription.<br><br>To enable and configure contract terms, follow these steps in the Chargebee UI:<br><br>1. Click **Settings** on the left navigation.<br>2. Click **Configure Chargebee**.<br>3. Under **Billing** , click **Contract Terms**.<br>4. Enable and configure the feature as needed.<br><br>Once contract terms have been configured, the following actions can be performed using the API:<br><br>* **Define a contract term** for a subscription and **set renewal options** for the contract term. The following endpoints support this:<br><br>* [Create a subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items)<br>* [Update a subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items)<br>* [Reactivate a subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/reactivate-a-subscription)<br>* [Create a subscription ramp](/docs/api/ramps/create-a-ramp)<br>* [Update a subscription ramp](/docs/api/ramps/update-a-subscription-ramp)<br>* **Retrieving** a historical record of all contract terms for a subscription can be done via the following endpoint:<br><br>* [List contract terms for a subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/list-contract-terms-for-a-subscription)<br>* **Canceling a contract term** can be done via the following endpoints:<br><br>* [Update a subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items)<br>* [Cancel a subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/cancel-subscription-for-items)<br>* [Update a subscription ramp](/docs/api/ramps/update-a-subscription-ramp)<br><br>#### Including a termination fee<br><br>When a contract is canceled mid-term, you can set a termination fee to be levied. Here's how:<br><br>1. [Create](/docs/api/item_prices/create-an-item-price) an item price for an item of [type](/docs/api/items/item-object#type) `charge` with [price](/docs/api/item_prices/create-an-item-price#price) set to the termination fee.<br>2. Do one of the following:<br><br>* [Attach the charge-item to a plan](/docs/api/attached_items/create-an-attached-item), setting the `charge_on_event` parameter to `contract_termination`. OR<br>* [Include the charge-item price on a subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items), setting the `subscription_items[charge_on_event][i]` parameter to `contract_termination`.<br><br>Once the above steps are done, the termination fee will be charged automatically if you [terminate the contract in the middle of its term](/docs/api/subscriptions/cancel-subscription-for-items#contract_term_cancel_option).<br>|

It enumerates all the charges, adjustments, payments, discounts and taxes associated with the sale.<br><br>An invoice is said to be a recurring one when it is has at least one charge for [a plan or an addon item price](/docs/api/items). It is a non-recurring one when it has charges for only charge-item prices or [one-time charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/charges.html).<br><br>The item prices for any given billing term of a subscription are billed via an invoice at the beginning of the term (unless the charges are left unbilled). However, item prices that belong to `metered` items are billed at the end of the term via a `pending` invoice that can [close automatically](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing#configuring-metered-billing) or via [an API call](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice). Moreover, when there are no `metered` items in the subscription, the invoices can still be generated as `pending` while [creating](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items) or [updating](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items) a subscription.<br><br>#### Auto-collection<br><br>If [auto-collection](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#auto-collection-status) is enabled, then immediately on invoice generation (or, in case of subscriptions that have `create_pending_invoices` as `true`, on [invoice closure](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice)), the [payment method](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#payment_method) on file is charged:<br><br>* If the payment succeeds, the invoice is marked as `paid`.<br>* On payment failure, the invoice is marked as `payment_due` and [dunning settings](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/dunning-v2.html) are taken into account for payment retries.<br>* If no retry attempts are configured, or when retries are exhausted, the invoice is marked as `not_paid`.<br>* the amount due is zero or negative, the invoice is immediately marked as `paid` and the balance, if any, is added to [excess payments](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#excess-payments) for the customer.<br><br>**Note:** If [consolidated invoicing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html) is enabled, the attribute `subscription_id` is unavailable when the invoice has line items from multiple subscriptions. The individual subscription ids are seen under `line_items.subscription_id`.  <br><br>#### Recurring and non-recurring invoices<br><br>A recurring invoice contains at least one line item that is billed on a recurring basis. Specifically, it has at least one [`line_items[]`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#line_items) with `entity_type` set to `plan_item_price` or `addon_item_price`. A non-recurring invoice contains no recurring line items.  <br><br>#### Refundable amount for an invoice<br><br>The refundable amount for an invoice is the (amount paid on the invoice + refundable credit applied on the invoice + taxes withheld on the invoice) minus (amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice). Each of these amounts is obtained from the invoice resource as follows:<br><br>* Amount paid on the invoice: [`amount_paid`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_amount_paid)<br>* Refundable credit applied on the invoice: [`credits_applied`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_credits_applied)<br>* Taxes withheld on the invoice: Sum of [`linked_taxes_withheld[].amount`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_linked_taxes_withheld)<br>* Amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice: Sum of [`issued_credit_notes[i].cn_total`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_issued_credit_notes) where `issued_credit_notes[i].cn_status` is `refunded` or `refund_due`.<br>|
|» » credit_notes|body|[[CreditNote](#schemacreditnote)]|true|none|
|» » unbilled_charges|body|[[UnbilledCharge](#schemaunbilledcharge)]|true|none|

It is a non-recurring one when it has charges for only charge-item prices or [one-time charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/charges.html).<br><br>The item prices for any given billing term of a subscription are billed via an invoice at the beginning of the term (unless the charges are left unbilled). However, item prices that belong to `metered` items are billed at the end of the term via a `pending` invoice that can [close automatically](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing#configuring-metered-billing) or via [an API call](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice). Moreover, when there are no `metered` items in the subscription, the invoices can still be generated as `pending` while [creating](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items) or [updating](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items) a subscription.<br><br>#### Auto-collection<br><br>If [auto-collection](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#auto-collection-status) is enabled, then immediately on invoice generation (or, in case of subscriptions that have `create_pending_invoices` as `true`, on [invoice closure](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice)), the [payment method](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#payment_method) on file is charged:<br><br>* If the payment succeeds, the invoice is marked as `paid`.<br>* On payment failure, the invoice is marked as `payment_due` and [dunning settings](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/dunning-v2.html) are taken into account for payment retries.<br>* If no retry attempts are configured, or when retries are exhausted, the invoice is marked as `not_paid`.<br>* the amount due is zero or negative, the invoice is immediately marked as `paid` and the balance, if any, is added to [excess payments](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#excess-payments) for the customer.<br><br>**Note:** If [consolidated invoicing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html) is enabled, the attribute `subscription_id` is unavailable when the invoice has line items from multiple subscriptions. The individual subscription ids are seen under `line_items.subscription_id`.  <br><br>#### Recurring and non-recurring invoices<br><br>A recurring invoice contains at least one line item that is billed on a recurring basis. Specifically, it has at least one [`line_items[]`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#line_items) with `entity_type` set to `plan_item_price` or `addon_item_price`. A non-recurring invoice contains no recurring line items.  <br><br>#### Refundable amount for an invoice<br><br>The refundable amount for an invoice is the (amount paid on the invoice + refundable credit applied on the invoice + taxes withheld on the invoice) minus (amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice). Each of these amounts is obtained from the invoice resource as follows:<br><br>* Amount paid on the invoice: [`amount_paid`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_amount_paid)<br>* Refundable credit applied on the invoice: [`credits_applied`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_credits_applied)<br>* Taxes withheld on the invoice: Sum of [`linked_taxes_withheld[].amount`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_linked_taxes_withheld)<br>* Amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice: Sum of [`issued_credit_notes[i].cn_total`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_issued_credit_notes) where `issued_credit_notes[i].cn_status` is `refunded` or `refund_due`.<br>|
|» » customer|body|[Customer](#schemacustomer)|true|Represents a customer, which can be an individual or organization that subscribes to your products or services. The customer resource associates with [subscriptions](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object), [card information](/docs/api/cards/card-object), and billing addresses. The customer details include their ID, name, contact information, and any [custom attributes](/docs/api/advanced-features) you'd like to associate with them.  <br>**Breaking Change**:<br><br>* [**Sites**](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/sites-intro.html) **created before March 1, 2014** : [updating the card](/docs/api/cards/update-card-for-a-customer) deletes the customer's `billing_address` and `vat_number` and replaces them with values from the request.<br>* **Sites created on or after March 1, 2014** : updating the card doesn't change the `billing_address` and `vat_number`.<br>|
|» » subscription|body|[Subscription](#schemasubscription)|true|A Chargebee subscription connects a customer record to products/services. ## Triggered when a credit note is deleted.

<a id="opIdonCredit_note_deletedWebhook"></a>

`POST credit_note_deleted`

Triggered when a credit note is deleted.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-credit-note-is-deleted-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreditNoteDeletedEvent](#schemacreditnotedeletedevent)|false|Payload for credit_note_deleted event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » credit_note|body|[CreditNote](#schemacreditnote)|true|A [Credit Note](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/credit-notes.html) is a document that specifies the money owed by a business to its customer. The seller usually issues a Credit Note for the same or lower amount than the invoice, and then repays the money to the customer or set it off against other 'due' invoices.<br><br>### Credit Note Types<br><br>Credit notes in Chargebee are categorized into three types:<br>1. `adjustment`: Adjustment credit notes are used to adjust the amount of an existing invoice in the `payment_due` or `not_paid` [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status). Use this type of credit note to reduce the invoice amount, typically as a discount to the customer.<br><br>Adjustment credit notes are automatically created in the following cases:<br><br>* When an invoice is written off.<br>* When a subscription is modified with proration enabled, and the invoice for the current term is in the `payment_due` or `not_paid` [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status). 2. `refundable`: Refundable credit notes allow you to return a certain amount to the customer. These credits can be:<br>* Retained for automatic application on future invoices.<br>* Applied to existing unpaid invoices.<br>* Refunded to the customer. Refundable credit notes are automatically created in the following cases:<br>* When an invoice is refunded.<br>* When a subscription is changed or canceled with proration enabled, the invoice for the current term is in the `paid` [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status). Refundable credits are applied to future invoices or can be refunded to the original payment method. 3. `store`: Store credit notes are created for `paid` or `partially_paid` invoice [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status) during subscription changes, such as upgrades, downgrades, or cancellations. Key characteristics of store credits:<br>* No tax component is included at the time of creation.<br>* A credit note document is generated, similar to refundable credits.<br>* Store credits are applied before tax calculations on future invoices.<br><br>**Note:**<br>If you have enabled *consolidated invoicing*<br>, to know the subscriptions attached with a credit note you have to refer [line_item's](/docs/api/credit_notes/credit_note-object#line_items)<br>*subscription_id*<br>. The credit note's *subscription_id*<br>should **not**<br>be used (which will be *null*<br>if the credit note has lines from multiple subscriptions).  <br>Impact on reference invoice  <br>The following updates are made to the reference invoice when a credit note is created/imported:<br><br>* If the credit note `type` is `adjustment`:<br>  * The adjustment credit note details are added to the `adjustment_credit_notes[]` attribute of the invoice.<br>  * The invoice `amount_due` is reduced by the credit note `total`.<br>  * The invoice `status` is updated to `paid` if the invoice `amount_due` equals the credit note `total`.<br>  * The invoice `status` does not change if the invoice `amount_due` is greater than credit note `total`.<br>* If the credit note `type` is `refundable`:<br>  * The refundable credit note details are added to the `issued_credit_notes[]` attribute of the invoice.<br>  * The invoice `status` does not change.<br>* If the credit note `type` is `store`:<br>  * The store credit note details are added to the `issued_credit_notes[]` attribute of the invoice.<br>  * The invoice `status` does not change.<br>|

|200|OK|Webhook received successfully|None|

This operation does not require authentication

|» » invoice|body|[Invoice](#schemainvoice)|true|An invoice is a commercial document representing a sale of products/services offered by you to a customer. It enumerates all the charges, adjustments, payments, discounts and taxes associated with the sale.<br><br>An invoice is said to be a recurring one when it is has at least one charge for [a plan or an addon item price](/docs/api/items). It is a non-recurring one when it has charges for only charge-item prices or [one-time charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/charges.html).<br><br>The item prices for any given billing term of a subscription are billed via an invoice at the beginning of the term (unless the charges are left unbilled). However, item prices that belong to `metered` items are billed at the end of the term via a `pending` invoice that can [close automatically](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing#configuring-metered-billing) or via [an API call](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice). Moreover, when there are no `metered` items in the subscription, the invoices can still be generated as `pending` while [creating](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items) or [updating](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items) a subscription.<br><br>#### Auto-collection<br><br>If [auto-collection](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#auto-collection-status) is enabled, then immediately on invoice generation (or, in case of subscriptions that have `create_pending_invoices` as `true`, on [invoice closure](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice)), the [payment method](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#payment_method) on file is charged:<br><br>* If the payment succeeds, the invoice is marked as `paid`.<br>* On payment failure, the invoice is marked as `payment_due` and [dunning settings](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/dunning-v2.html) are taken into account for payment retries.<br>* If no retry attempts are configured, or when retries are exhausted, the invoice is marked as `not_paid`.<br>* the amount due is zero or negative, the invoice is immediately marked as `paid` and the balance, if any, is added to [excess payments](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#excess-payments) for the customer.<br><br>**Note:** If [consolidated invoicing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html) is enabled, the attribute `subscription_id` is unavailable when the invoice has line items from multiple subscriptions. The individual subscription ids are seen under `line_items.subscription_id`.  <br><br>#### Recurring and non-recurring invoices<br><br>A recurring invoice contains at least one line item that is billed on a recurring basis. Specifically, it has at least one [`line_items[]`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#line_items) with `entity_type` set to `plan_item_price` or `addon_item_price`. A non-recurring invoice contains no recurring line items.  <br><br>#### Refundable amount for an invoice<br><br>The refundable amount for an invoice is the (amount paid on the invoice + refundable credit applied on the invoice + taxes withheld on the invoice) minus (amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice). Each of these amounts is obtained from the invoice resource as follows:<br><br>* Amount paid on the invoice: [`amount_paid`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_amount_paid)<br>* Refundable credit applied on the invoice: [`credits_applied`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_credits_applied)<br>* Taxes withheld on the invoice: Sum of [`linked_taxes_withheld[].amount`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_linked_taxes_withheld)<br>* Amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice: Sum of [`issued_credit_notes[i].cn_total`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_issued_credit_notes) where `issued_credit_notes[i].cn_status` is `refunded` or `refund_due`.<br>|
|» » credit_note|body|[CreditNote](#schemacreditnote)|true|A [Credit Note](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/credit-notes.html) is a document that specifies the money owed by a business to its customer. The seller usually issues a Credit Note for the same or lower amount than the invoice, and then repays the money to the customer or set it off against other 'due' invoices.<br><br>### Credit Note Types<br><br>Credit notes in Chargebee are categorized into three types:<br>1. `adjustment`: Adjustment credit notes are used to adjust the amount of an existing invoice in the `payment_due` or `not_paid` [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status). Use this type of credit note to reduce the invoice amount, typically as a discount to the customer.<br><br>Adjustment credit notes are automatically created in the following cases:<br><br>* When an invoice is written off.<br>* When a subscription is modified with proration enabled, and the invoice for the current term is in the `payment_due` or `not_paid` [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status). 2. `refundable`: Refundable credit notes allow you to return a certain amount to the customer. These credits can be:<br>* Retained for automatic application on future invoices.<br>* Applied to existing unpaid invoices.<br>* Refunded to the customer. Refundable credit notes are automatically created in the following cases:<br>* When an invoice is refunded.<br>* When a subscription is changed or canceled with proration enabled, the invoice for the current term is in the `paid` [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status). Refundable credits are applied to future invoices or can be refunded to the original payment method. 3. `store`: Store credit notes are created for `paid` or `partially_paid` invoice [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status) during subscription changes, such as upgrades, downgrades, or cancellations. Key characteristics of store credits:<br>* No tax component is included at the time of creation.<br>* A credit note document is generated, similar to refundable credits.<br>* Store credits are applied before tax calculations on future invoices.<br><br>**Note:**<br>If you have enabled *consolidated invoicing*<br>, to know the subscriptions attached with a credit note you have to refer [line_item's](/docs/api/credit_notes/credit_note-object#line_items)<br>*subscription_id*<br>. The credit note's *subscription_id*<br>should **not**<br>be used (which will be *null*<br>if the credit note has lines from multiple subscriptions).  <br>Impact on reference invoice  <br>The following updates are made to the reference invoice when a credit note is created/imported:<br><br>* If the credit note `type` is `adjustment`:<br>  * The adjustment credit note details are added to the `adjustment_credit_notes[]` attribute of the invoice.<br>  * The invoice `amount_due` is reduced by the credit note `total`.<br>  * The invoice `status` is updated to `paid` if the invoice `amount_due` equals the credit note `total`.<br>  * The invoice `status` does not change if the invoice `amount_due` is greater than credit note `total`.<br>* If the credit note `type` is `refundable`:<br>  * The refundable credit note details are added to the `issued_credit_notes[]` attribute of the invoice.<br>  * The invoice `status` does not change.<br>* If the credit note `type` is `store`:<br>  * The store credit note details are added to the `issued_credit_notes[]` attribute of the invoice.<br>  * The invoice `status` does not change.<br>|

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Webhook received successfully|None|

## Triggered when contract term is completed.

<a id="opIdonContract_term_completedWebhook"></a>

`POST contract_term_completed`

Triggered when contract term is completed.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-contract-term-is-completed-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ContractTermCompletedEvent](#schemacontracttermcompletedevent)|false|Payload for contract_term_completed event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » contract_term|body|[ContractTerm](#schemacontractterm)|true|Subscriptions can run indefinitely or they may run for a fixed number of billing cycles. Subscription can have "contract terms", which define a lock-in period on the subscription for a certain number of billing cycles. This prevents the subscription from being canceled by the customer when it is within the contract term.<br><br>The **contract term** resource described below defines the properties of this lock-in period. This includes the [number of billing cycles](/docs/api/contract_terms/contract_term-object#remaining_billing_cycles), the [total contract value](/docs/api/contract_terms/contract_term-object#total_contract_value), the [action to be taken](/docs/api/contract_terms/contract_term-object#action_at_term_end) at the end of the contract term, and so on. To allow for exceptions, you also have the option of terminating an [`active`](/docs/api/contract_terms/contract_term-object#status) contract term and charging a [termination fee](/docs/api/contract_terms).<br><br>A contract term starts in the `active` state and ends in the `completed` state. If the contract was canceled due to non-payment or other reasons, it can end in the `canceled` or `terminated` state. A given contract term is always associated with one, and only one subscription. A subscription, however, can be associated with only one `active` contract term. Over time, a subscription can be associated with several non-`active` contract terms. The `active` contract term for a subscription is available as an [object](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object#contract_term) within the subscription.<br><br>To enable and configure contract terms, follow these steps in the Chargebee UI:<br><br>1. Click **Settings** on the left navigation.<br>2. Click **Configure Chargebee**.<br>3. Under **Billing** , click **Contract Terms**.<br>4. Enable and configure the feature as needed.<br><br>Once contract terms have been configured, the following actions can be performed using the API:<br><br>* **Define a contract term** for a subscription and **set renewal options** for the contract term. The following endpoints support this:<br><br>* [Create a subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items)<br>* [Update a subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items)<br>* [Reactivate a subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/reactivate-a-subscription)<br>* [Create a subscription ramp](/docs/api/ramps/create-a-ramp)<br>* [Update a subscription ramp](/docs/api/ramps/update-a-subscription-ramp)<br>* **Retrieving** a historical record of all contract terms for a subscription can be done via the following endpoint:<br><br>* [List contract terms for a subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/list-contract-terms-for-a-subscription)<br>* **Canceling a contract term** can be done via the following endpoints:<br><br>* [Update a subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items)<br>* [Cancel a subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/cancel-subscription-for-items)<br>* [Update a subscription ramp](/docs/api/ramps/update-a-subscription-ramp)<br><br>#### Including a termination fee<br><br>When a contract is canceled mid-term, you can set a termination fee to be levied. Here's how:<br><br>1. [Create](/docs/api/item_prices/create-an-item-price) an item price for an item of [type](/docs/api/items/item-object#type) `charge` with [price](/docs/api/item_prices/create-an-item-price#price) set to the termination fee.<br>2. Do one of the following:<br><br>* [Attach the charge-item to a plan](/docs/api/attached_items/create-an-attached-item), setting the `charge_on_event` parameter to `contract_termination`. OR<br>* [Include the charge-item price on a subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items), setting the `subscription_items[charge_on_event][i]` parameter to `contract_termination`.<br><br>Once the above steps are done, the termination fee will be charged automatically if you [terminate the contract in the middle of its term](/docs/api/subscriptions/cancel-subscription-for-items#contract_term_cancel_option).<br>|

## Triggered when a price ramp is created.

<a id="opIdonPrice_ramp_createdWebhook"></a>

`POST price_ramp_created`

> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-price-ramp-is-created-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[PriceRampCreatedEvent](#schemapricerampcreatedevent)|false|Payload for price_ramp_created event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » price_ramp|body|[PriceRamp](#schemapriceramp)|true|Price ramp resource lets you define a stepped pricing schedule on an [item price](/docs/api/item_prices) in the Product Catalog. Each ramp is an ordered list of `ramp_intervals` that set the price for contiguous ranges of billing cycles, so new subscriptions inherit introductory or stepped pricing without custom per-subscription logic.<br><br>Here's an example to show how you can use ramp pricing:<br><br>A media streaming company offers a **Basic** monthly plan with a catalog price of $9.99. To grow acquisitions, they configure a price ramp so new subscribers start on an introductory price, then step up to full price.  <br><br>\|----------\|--------------\|---------------\|-------------------\|<br>\| **Plan** \| **Currency** \| **Frequency** \| **Catalog price** \|<br>\| Basic    \| USD          \| Monthly       \| $9.99             \|<br><br>\|--------------------\|-------------------\|-------------------------\|<br>\| **Billing cycles** \| **Price charged** \| **Price type**          \|<br>\| Month 1            \| $0.99             \| Introductory ramp price \|<br>\| Months 2--4        \| $4.99             \| Introductory ramp price \|<br>\| Month 5 onwards    \| $9.99             \| Catalog price           \|<br><br>Every new subscription on this Basic USD Monthly item price inherits the ramp automatically. In this example the final interval uses the catalog price, so the subscriber stays on $9.99 from month 5 onward. The catalog price continues only when that final interval sets `apply_catalog_price` to `true`. A final interval that sets `price` and omits `ending_billing_cycle` keeps that fixed price for the remaining billing cycles.<br><br>An interval that uses the item price's catalog price returns `apply_catalog_price` as `true`. The resolved price for every interval is always available in `price` (in the [minor unit of the currency](/docs/api/currencies)) and, when [multi-decimal pricing](/docs/api/currencies) is enabled, in `price_in_decimal`.  <br>When a price ramp is linked to an item price, the `price_ramp_id` is exposed on the corresponding [item price](/docs/api/item_prices) object.  <br>**See also:**<br>For a more detailed understanding of Price Ramps, including how to configure and manage them, as well as their impact on other features, follow these resources:<br><br>* [Price Ramps](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/product-catalog/price-ramps)<br>* [Configuring a Price Ramp](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/product-catalog/price-ramps-configure)<br>* [How Ramp Pricing works with Create Subscription](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/product-catalog/price-ramps-create-subscription)<br>* [How Ramp Pricing works with Hosted Checkout](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/product-catalog/price-ramps-hosted-checkout)<br>|

Invoices can also be [generated in advance](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/advance-invoices.html) for an upcoming renewal or set of renewals. With Advance Invoicing Schedules, you can set up a plan for when such advance invoices are generated for the lifetime of the subscription. This helps you:<br><br>* Set up a contract with your customers so that they can be notified of their payment schedules in advance.<br>* Allow customers who make offline payments to be alerted about their upcoming dues well ahead of actual subscription renewals.<br>* Prevent post-renewal unpaid usage of your services by customers.<br><br>Advance invoices can be scheduled in two ways:<br><br>#### Specific Dates Schedule<br><br>Advance invoices for a subscription can be scheduled to be generated on specific [dates](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#specific_dates_schedule_date) in the future. You must specify the [number of billing cycles](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#specific_dates_schedule_terms_to_charge) to be invoiced on each date. A maximum of 5 dates can be specified.<br><br>#### Fixed Interval Schedule<br><br>Advance invoices can be scheduled to be generated at fixed intervals of time, where each interval spans the same number of billing cycles of the subscription. The invoice for each interval is generated a specified number of days ([`days_before_interval`](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#fixed_interval_schedule_days_before_renewal)) before the start of the interval. You can configure the schedule to end on a certain date or after a specified number of advance invoices have been generated.<br><br>The start date of the first interval depends on the number of days remaining from current time till the next renewal of the subscription. If this is more than `days_before_interval`, the interval begins at the next renewal. On the other hand, if the number of days remaining before the next renewal is less than `days_before_interval`, the first interval begins at the renewal following the next.<br>|

## Triggered when an omnichannel subscription item mrr is updated

<a id="opIdonOmnichannel_subscription_item_mrr_updatedWebhook"></a>

`POST omnichannel_subscription_item_mrr_updated`

Triggered when the MRR (Monthly Recurring Revenue) computed for an omnichannel subscription item changes, for example due to a renewal, a price or offer change, or a status transition that affects revenue.
Each occurrence delivers a new immutable [`omnichannel_subscription_item_metric`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_item_metrics) snapshot.
The event content includes the related [`omnichannel_subscription`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscriptions), [`omnichannel_subscription_item`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_items), and [`omnichannel_subscription_item_metric`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_item_metrics).


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-an-omnichannel-subscription-item-mrr-is-updated-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[OmnichannelSubscriptionItemMrrUpdatedEvent](#schemaomnichannelsubscriptionitemmrrupdatedevent)|false|Payload for omnichannel_subscription_item_mrr_updated event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » omnichannel_subscription_item|body|[OmnichannelSubscriptionItem](#schemaomnichannelsubscriptionitem)|true|Represents a product entitlement (item) within an [`omnichannel_subscription`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscriptions) purchased on Apple App Store or Google Play Store.<br><br>Status, auto-renew, term dates, and cancel/expire reasons live on this resource. See [omnichannel statuses](/docs/api/omnichannel_statuses) for store mappings.<br><br>Chargebee records introductory and promotional offers on [`omnichannel_subscription_item_offers`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_items/omnichannel_subscription_item-object#omnichannel_subscription_item_offers). Win-back offers and offer codes are not supported.<br><br>When `has_scheduled_changes` is `true`, use [List scheduled changes](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_items/list-scheduled-changes-for-omnichannel-subscription-item) to retrieve deferred product or pause changes.  <br>**Note:**<br>This resource represents in-app subscription items made on Apple App Store and Google Play Store.<br>|
|» » omnichannel_subscription|body|[OmnichannelSubscription](#schemaomnichannelsubscription)|true|Represents a subscription purchased and managed in an external app marketplace (`apple_app_store` or `google_play_store`), normalized into Chargebee's omnichannel model.<br><br>Omnichannel subscriptions are typically created when you [record a purchase](/docs/api/recorded_purchases/record-a-purchase) and are kept in sync via store server notifications. They are store-managed: lifecycle changes come from Apple or Google, not from the Chargebee Subscriptions API.<br><br>Use [omnichannel statuses](/docs/api/omnichannel_statuses) for how store statuses map to `omnichannel_subscription_item.status`, and [omnichannel events](/docs/api/omnichannel_events) for notification-to-webhook mappings.<br><br>Chargebee records introductory and promotional offers on [`omnichannel_subscription_item_offers`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscriptions/omnichannel_subscription-object#omnichannel_subscription_items_omnichannel_subscription_item_offers). Win-back offers and offer codes are not supported.  <br>**Identifier tip:** Parent `id_at_source` is the Apple **Transaction ID** or Google **purchase token** . Nested `initial_purchase_transaction.id_at_source` is the Apple **Transaction ID** or Google **Order ID** (`GPA....`). ## Sent when a invoice's due period is about to end

<a id="opIdonNetd_payment_due_reminderWebhook"></a>

`POST netd_payment_due_reminder`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="sent-when-a-invoices-due-period-is-about-to-end-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[NetdPaymentDueReminderEvent](#schemanetdpaymentduereminderevent)|false|Payload for netd_payment_due_reminder event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » invoice|body|[Invoice](#schemainvoice)|true|An invoice is a commercial document representing a sale of products/services offered by you to a customer. It enumerates all the charges, adjustments, payments, discounts and taxes associated with the sale.<br><br>An invoice is said to be a recurring one when it is has at least one charge for [a plan or an addon item price](/docs/api/items). It is a non-recurring one when it has charges for only charge-item prices or [one-time charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/charges.html).<br><br>The item prices for any given billing term of a subscription are billed via an invoice at the beginning of the term (unless the charges are left unbilled). However, item prices that belong to `metered` items are billed at the end of the term via a `pending` invoice that can [close automatically](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing#configuring-metered-billing) or via [an API call](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice). Moreover, when there are no `metered` items in the subscription, the invoices can still be generated as `pending` while [creating](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items) or [updating](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items) a subscription.<br><br>#### Auto-collection<br><br>If [auto-collection](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#auto-collection-status) is enabled, then immediately on invoice generation (or, in case of subscriptions that have `create_pending_invoices` as `true`, on [invoice closure](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice)), the [payment method](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#payment_method) on file is charged:<br><br>* If the payment succeeds, the invoice is marked as `paid`.<br>* On payment failure, the invoice is marked as `payment_due` and [dunning settings](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/dunning-v2.html) are taken into account for payment retries.<br>* If no retry attempts are configured, or when retries are exhausted, the invoice is marked as `not_paid`.<br>* the amount due is zero or negative, the invoice is immediately marked as `paid` and the balance, if any, is added to [excess payments](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#excess-payments) for the customer.<br><br>**Note:** If [consolidated invoicing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html) is enabled, the attribute `subscription_id` is unavailable when the invoice has line items from multiple subscriptions. The individual subscription ids are seen under `line_items.subscription_id`.  <br><br>#### Recurring and non-recurring invoices<br><br>A recurring invoice contains at least one line item that is billed on a recurring basis. Specifically, it has at least one [`line_items[]`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#line_items) with `entity_type` set to `plan_item_price` or `addon_item_price`. A non-recurring invoice contains no recurring line items.  <br><br>#### Refundable amount for an invoice<br><br>The refundable amount for an invoice is the (amount paid on the invoice + refundable credit applied on the invoice + taxes withheld on the invoice) minus (amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice). Each of these amounts is obtained from the invoice resource as follows:<br><br>* Amount paid on the invoice: [`amount_paid`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_amount_paid)<br>* Refundable credit applied on the invoice: [`credits_applied`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_credits_applied)<br>* Taxes withheld on the invoice: Sum of [`linked_taxes_withheld[].amount`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_linked_taxes_withheld)<br>* Amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice: Sum of [`issued_credit_notes[i].cn_total`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_issued_credit_notes) where `issued_credit_notes[i].cn_status` is `refunded` or `refund_due`.<br>|

<h3 id="sent-when-a-invoices-due-period-is-about-to-end-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Webhook received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Triggered when gift is cancelled.

<a id="opIdonGift_cancelledWebhook"></a>

`POST gift_cancelled`

Triggered when gift is cancelled.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-gift-is-cancelled-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[GiftCancelledEvent](#schemagiftcancelledevent)|false|Payload for gift_cancelled event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » gift|body|[Gift](#schemagift)|true|Gift represents a subscription of a customer(**recipient** ) to a 'gift plan' which has been gifted by another customer(**gifter**). It may also have addons and coupons. Gift will be created only on immediate successful payment collection from the gifter's payment method.<br><br>Gift is initially created in '**scheduled** ' state. The gift can be scheduled to be notified on a particular date to the recipient by passing 'scheduled_at'. If not, the recipient is notified immediately. Gift will be moved to '**unclaimed** ' state on the date of notification. If you pass auto_claim as true, gift status will be moved to '**claimed**' immediately, otherwise, the gift will remain 'unclaimed' till the recipient claims the gift.<br><br>If the gift is not claimed before the claim_expiry_date, it will be moved to the '**expired**' state.<br><br>#### GIFT SUBSCRIPTION<br><br>Gift subscriptions will be created in '**future** ' state. Once the gift is claimed, the subscription will be moved to '**non-renewing**' state.<br><br>#### INVOICE<br><br>Gift subscriptions will be invoiced immediately. The invoice created has **is_gifted** as 'true' and **term_finalized** as 'false'. This is because initially the invoice term_start and term_end are set as the subscription's start_date till the end of the plan period. Once the gift is claimed, the invoice's term_finalized will be marked as 'true'. The term_start will be changed to the actual invoice's term, which is the gift-claim date and the term_end will be changed till plan's period.<br>|

(Follow the links to learn more.)<br><br>* The value of the [`subscription.has_scheduled_changes`](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object#has_scheduled_changes) attribute.<br>* [Update subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items#impact-scheduled-changes)<br>* [Create Checkout for updating a subscription](/docs/api/hosted_pages/create-checkout-to-update-a-subscription#impact-scheduled-changes)<br>* [Remove scheduled changes](/docs/api/subscriptions/remove-scheduled-changes)<br>* [Retrieve with scheduled changes](/docs/api/subscriptions/retrieve-with-scheduled-changes)<br>* [Create a quote for updating a subscription](/docs/api/quotes/create-a-quote-for-update-subscription-items)<br>* [Edit a quote for updating a subscription](/docs/api/quotes/edit-update-subscription-quote-for-items)<br>* [Portal sessions](/docs/api/portal_sessions#scheduled-subscription-changes)<br>|

Invoices can also be [generated in advance](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/advance-invoices.html) for an upcoming renewal or set of renewals. With Advance Invoicing Schedules, you can set up a plan for when such advance invoices are generated for the lifetime of the subscription. This helps you:<br><br>* Set up a contract with your customers so that they can be notified of their payment schedules in advance.<br>* Allow customers who make offline payments to be alerted about their upcoming dues well ahead of actual subscription renewals.<br>* Prevent post-renewal unpaid usage of your services by customers.<br><br>Advance invoices can be scheduled in two ways:<br><br>#### Specific Dates Schedule<br><br>Advance invoices for a subscription can be scheduled to be generated on specific [dates](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#specific_dates_schedule_date) in the future. You must specify the [number of billing cycles](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#specific_dates_schedule_terms_to_charge) to be invoiced on each date. A maximum of 5 dates can be specified.<br><br>#### Fixed Interval Schedule<br><br>Advance invoices can be scheduled to be generated at fixed intervals of time, where each interval spans the same number of billing cycles of the subscription. On the other hand, if the number of days remaining before the next renewal is less than `days_before_interval`, the first interval begins at the renewal following the next.<br>|

## Event triggered (in the case of metered billing) when a &quot;Pending&quot; invoice is created that has usage related charges or line items to be added, before being closed. This is triggered only when the “Notify for Pending Invoices” option is enabled.

<a id="opIdonPending_invoice_createdWebhook"></a>

`POST pending_invoice_created`

Event triggered (in the case of metered billing) when a "Pending" invoice is created that has usage related charges or line items to be added, before being closed. This is triggered only when the "Notify for Pending Invoices" option is enabled.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="event-triggered-in-the-case-of-metered-billing-when-a-pending-invoice-is-created-that-has-usage-related-charges-or-line-items-to-be-added-before-being-closed-this-is-triggered-only-when-the-notify-for-pending-invoices-option-is-enabled-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[PendingInvoiceCreatedEvent](#schemapendinginvoicecreatedevent)|false|Payload for pending_invoice_created event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » invoice|body|[Invoice](#schemainvoice)|true|An invoice is a commercial document representing a sale of products/services offered by you to a customer. It enumerates all the charges, adjustments, payments, discounts and taxes associated with the sale.<br><br>An invoice is said to be a recurring one when it is has at least one charge for [a plan or an addon item price](/docs/api/items). It is a non-recurring one when it has charges for only charge-item prices or [one-time charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/charges.html).<br><br>The item prices for any given billing term of a subscription are billed via an invoice at the beginning of the term (unless the charges are left unbilled). However, item prices that belong to `metered` items are billed at the end of the term via a `pending` invoice that can [close automatically](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing#configuring-metered-billing) or via [an API call](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice). Moreover, when there are no `metered` items in the subscription, the invoices can still be generated as `pending` while [creating](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items) or [updating](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items) a subscription.<br><br>#### Auto-collection<br><br>If [auto-collection](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#auto-collection-status) is enabled, then immediately on invoice generation (or, in case of subscriptions that have `create_pending_invoices` as `true`, on [invoice closure](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice)), the [payment method](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#payment_method) on file is charged:<br><br>* If the payment succeeds, the invoice is marked as `paid`.<br>* On payment failure, the invoice is marked as `payment_due` and [dunning settings](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/dunning-v2.html) are taken into account for payment retries.<br>* If no retry attempts are configured, or when retries are exhausted, the invoice is marked as `not_paid`.<br>* the amount due is zero or negative, the invoice is immediately marked as `paid` and the balance, if any, is added to [excess payments](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#excess-payments) for the customer.<br><br>**Note:** If [consolidated invoicing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html) is enabled, the attribute `subscription_id` is unavailable when the invoice has line items from multiple subscriptions. The individual subscription ids are seen under `line_items.subscription_id`.  <br><br>#### Recurring and non-recurring invoices<br><br>A recurring invoice contains at least one line item that is billed on a recurring basis. Specifically, it has at least one [`line_items[]`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#line_items) with `entity_type` set to `plan_item_price` or `addon_item_price`. A non-recurring invoice contains no recurring line items.  <br><br>#### Refundable amount for an invoice<br><br>The refundable amount for an invoice is the (amount paid on the invoice + refundable credit applied on the invoice + taxes withheld on the invoice) minus (amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice). Each of these amounts is obtained from the invoice resource as follows:<br><br>* Amount paid on the invoice: [`amount_paid`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_amount_paid)<br>* Refundable credit applied on the invoice: [`credits_applied`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_credits_applied)<br>* Taxes withheld on the invoice: Sum of [`linked_taxes_withheld[].amount`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_linked_taxes_withheld)<br>* Amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice: Sum of [`issued_credit_notes[i].cn_total`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_issued_credit_notes) where `issued_credit_notes[i].cn_status` is `refunded` or `refund_due`.<br>|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

## When a limited period `entitlement_override` expires, it is no longer returned. No event is immediately triggered for it. However, after expiry, the `entitlement_override` record gets deleted within 12 hours, triggering the `entitlement_overrides_auto_removed` event. Therefore, this event can be considered a delayed notification for one or more `entitlement_overrides` having expired.

<a id="opIdonEntitlement_overrides_auto_removedWebhook"></a>

Items often differ in the number of product features that are available to them. The Features API helps you define the various features offered as part of your product line. It also defines the entitlements that items and subscriptions can have towards said features.  <br>**Note**<br><br>The maximum number of features a site can have is 400.<br><br>Features of this API<br>--------------------<br><br>The Features API enables you to:<br><br>* Define the set of features provided by your product.<br>* Specify the entitlements that items have towards said features.<br>* For a given subscription, modify the entitlements inherited from items in the subscription.<br>* Offer additional feature entitlements to subscriptions than those inherited from items in the subscription.<br>* Serve as a source of truth to your provisioning systems for subscription entitlements.<br>* Use entitlement information to understand which features drive value and revenue.<br><br>**See also**<br><br>* [Entitlements](/docs/api/entitlements)<br>* [Subscription Entitlements](/docs/api/subscription_entitlements)<br>* [Entitlement Overrides](/docs/api/entitlement_overrides)<br>|

## Triggered when a price ramp is deleted.

<a id="opIdonPrice_ramp_deletedWebhook"></a>

> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-price-ramp-is-deleted-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[PriceRampDeletedEvent](#schemapricerampdeletedevent)|false|Payload for price_ramp_deleted event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » price_ramp|body|[PriceRamp](#schemapriceramp)|true|Price ramp resource lets you define a stepped pricing schedule on an [item price](/docs/api/item_prices) in the Product Catalog. Each ramp is an ordered list of `ramp_intervals` that set the price for contiguous ranges of billing cycles, so new subscriptions inherit introductory or stepped pricing without custom per-subscription logic.<br><br>Here's an example to show how you can use ramp pricing:<br><br>A media streaming company offers a **Basic** monthly plan with a catalog price of $9.99. To grow acquisitions, they configure a price ramp so new subscribers start on an introductory price, then step up to full price.  <br><br>\|----------\|--------------\|---------------\|-------------------\|<br>\| **Plan** \| **Currency** \| **Frequency** \| **Catalog price** \|<br>\| Basic    \| USD          \| Monthly       \| $9.99             \|<br><br>\|--------------------\|-------------------\|-------------------------\|<br>\| **Billing cycles** \| **Price charged** \| **Price type**          \|<br>\| Month 1            \| $0.99             \| Introductory ramp price \|<br>\| Months 2--4        \| $4.99             \| Introductory ramp price \|<br>\| Month 5 onwards    \| $9.99             \| Catalog price           \|<br><br>Every new subscription on this Basic USD Monthly item price inherits the ramp automatically. In this example the final interval uses the catalog price, so the subscriber stays on $9.99 from month 5 onward. The catalog price continues only when that final interval sets `apply_catalog_price` to `true`. A final interval that sets `price` and omits `ending_billing_cycle` keeps that fixed price for the remaining billing cycles.<br><br>An interval that uses the item price's catalog price returns `apply_catalog_price` as `true`. The resolved price for every interval is always available in `price` (in the [minor unit of the currency](/docs/api/currencies)) and, when [multi-decimal pricing](/docs/api/currencies) is enabled, in `price_in_decimal`.  <br>When a price ramp is linked to an item price, the `price_ramp_id` is exposed on the corresponding [item price](/docs/api/item_prices) object.  <br>**See also:**<br>For a more detailed understanding of Price Ramps, including how to configure and manage them, as well as their impact on other features, follow these resources:<br><br>* [Price Ramps](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/product-catalog/price-ramps)<br>* [Configuring a Price Ramp](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/product-catalog/price-ramps-configure)<br>* [How Ramp Pricing works with Create Subscription](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/product-catalog/price-ramps-create-subscription)<br>* [How Ramp Pricing works with Hosted Checkout](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/product-catalog/price-ramps-hosted-checkout)<br>|

## Triggered when a business ruleset is activated

<a id="opIdonBusiness_ruleset_activatedWebhook"></a>

`POST business_ruleset_activated`

> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-business-ruleset-is-activated-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[BusinessRulesetActivatedEvent](#schemabusinessrulesetactivatedevent)|false|Payload for business_ruleset_activated event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » business_ruleset|body|[BusinessRuleset](#schemabusinessruleset)|true|A business ruleset groups [business rules](/docs/api/business_rules) so that they can be evaluated together, in the priority order you assign, using the strategy set in `execute_mode`.<br><br>Rulesets let you apply a whole decision at once instead of calling each rule separately. Passing a `ruleset_id` to [Apply business rules](/docs/api/business_rules/apply-business-rules) evaluates the rules the ruleset contains in their priority order and returns a result for each one. The `execute_mode` decides whether evaluation runs through every rule or stops as soon as a rule evaluates to `true` or to `false`, and which of the results are returned.<br><br>Membership is managed separately from the rules themselves. [Add business rules to a ruleset](/docs/api/business_rulesets/add-business-rules-to-a-ruleset) and [Remove business rules from a ruleset](/docs/api/business_rulesets/remove-business-rules-from-a-ruleset) change membership incrementally, while passing `rules` to [Update a business ruleset](/docs/api/business_rulesets/update-a-business-ruleset) replaces it entirely. A rule can belong to more than one ruleset, and removing it from a ruleset does not delete the rule.<br><br>The `active` attribute controls whether Chargebee evaluates the ruleset. A rule is evaluated through a ruleset only when both the ruleset and the rule are `active`.  <br>**Note:** Business rules are not enabled by default. Contact [Chargebee Support](https://www.chargebee.com/support/) to enable them for your site. Until they are enabled, these endpoints return an error.<br>|
