## Triggered when an omnichannel subscription item is upgraded

<a id="opIdonOmnichannel_subscription_item_upgradedWebhook"></a>

`POST omnichannel_subscription_item_upgraded`

Triggered when an omnichannel subscription item is upgraded.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-an-omnichannel-subscription-item-is-upgraded-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[OmnichannelSubscriptionItemUpgradedEvent](#schemaomnichannelsubscriptionitemupgradedevent)|false|Payload for omnichannel_subscription_item_upgraded event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » omnichannel_subscription_item|body|[OmnichannelSubscriptionItem](#schemaomnichannelsubscriptionitem)|true|Represents a product entitlement (item) within an [`omnichannel_subscription`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscriptions) purchased on Apple App Store or Google Play Store.<br><br>Status, auto-renew, term dates, and cancel/expire reasons live on this resource. See [omnichannel statuses](/docs/api/omnichannel_statuses) for store mappings.<br><br>Chargebee records introductory and promotional offers on [`omnichannel_subscription_item_offers`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_items/omnichannel_subscription_item-object#omnichannel_subscription_item_offers). Win-back offers and offer codes are not supported.<br><br>When `has_scheduled_changes` is `true`, use [List scheduled changes](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_items/list-scheduled-changes-for-omnichannel-subscription-item) to retrieve deferred product or pause changes.  <br>**Note:**<br>This resource represents in-app subscription items made on Apple App Store and Google Play Store.<br>|
|» » omnichannel_subscription|body|[OmnichannelSubscription](#schemaomnichannelsubscription)|true|Represents a subscription purchased and managed in an external app marketplace (`apple_app_store` or `google_play_store`), normalized into Chargebee's omnichannel model.<br><br>Omnichannel subscriptions are typically created when you [record a purchase](/docs/api/recorded_purchases/record-a-purchase) and are kept in sync via store server notifications. They are store-managed: lifecycle changes come from Apple or Google, not from the Chargebee Subscriptions API.<br><br>Use [omnichannel statuses](/docs/api/omnichannel_statuses) for how store statuses map to `omnichannel_subscription_item.status`, and [omnichannel events](/docs/api/omnichannel_events) for notification-to-webhook mappings.<br><br>Chargebee records introductory and promotional offers on [`omnichannel_subscription_item_offers`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscriptions/omnichannel_subscription-object#omnichannel_subscription_items_omnichannel_subscription_item_offers). Win-back offers and offer codes are not supported.  <br>**Identifier tip:** Parent `id_at_source` is the Apple **Transaction ID** or Google **purchase token** . Nested `initial_purchase_transaction.id_at_source` is the Apple **Transaction ID** or Google **Order ID** (`GPA....`). See attribute descriptions below.  <br>**Note:**<br>This resource represents in-app subscriptions made on Apple App Store and Google Play Store.<br>|
|» » omnichannel_transaction|body|[OmnichannelTransaction](#schemaomnichanneltransaction)|true|A unified representation of a store purchase or renewal transaction across Apple App Store and Google Play Store.<br><br>Use `id_at_source` to correlate with the store-native transaction identifier:<br><br>* **Apple App Store** : App Store **Transaction ID**<br>* **Google Play Store** : Google Play **Order ID** (`GPA....`)<br><br>Parent subscription / one-time-order resources use purchase-token semantics for Google `id_at_source`; do not treat those as interchangeable with this transaction Order ID.<br><br>### Apple App Store<br><br>The [price](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appstoreservernotifications/price) value reflects the price you configured in App Store Connect, which the system records at the time of transaction ([transacted_at](/docs/api/omnichannel_transactions/omnichannel_transaction-object#transacted_at)) after the discount if any offers are applied.  <br>**Important**<br>For financial and accounting purposes, use the App Store Connect reporting tools. For more information, see [Download financial reports](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/getting-paid/download-financial-reports) and [Overview of reporting tools](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/measure-app-performance/overview-of-reporting-tools).<br>[Learn more](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appstoreservernotifications/price) about price in Apple App Store.<br><br>### Google Play Store<br><br>Google Play does not always expose a complete transaction amount or purchase time for every notification path. When Google provides price / time data for a transaction, Chargebee records `price_*` and `transacted_at`; otherwise these attributes may be absent. Some Google one-time-order samples include price and `transacted_at` on `purchase_transaction`.<br><br>Transactions can be linked to subscriptions and/or one-time orders via `linked_omnichannel_subscriptions` and `linked_omnichannel_one_time_orders`. Chargebee may also emit [`omnichannel_transaction_created`](/docs/api/events/webhook/omnichannel_transaction_created) when a new transaction row is recorded.<br>|
|» » omnichannel_subscription_item_scheduled_change|body|[OmnichannelSubscriptionItemScheduledChange](#schemaomnichannelsubscriptionitemscheduledchange)|true|Represents a future change to an [`omnichannel_subscription_item`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_items) that the store will apply later (typically at the end of the current term).<br><br>**Apple App Store** : Created when the customer schedules a **downgrade** within the same subscription group (`DID_CHANGE_RENEWAL_PREF` / `DOWNGRADE`). `change_type` is typically `downgrade`. Upgrades apply immediately and do **not** create this resource.<br><br>**Google Play Store** : Created when a product change uses the **`DEFERRED`** replacement mode (applied at term end). Immediate changes use `CHARGE_PRORATED_PRICE` and do **not** create this resource. A `change_type` of `pause` may appear for scheduled pause flows; confirm mapping against [omnichannel events](/docs/api/omnichannel_events).<br><br>Retrieve scheduled changes with [List scheduled changes for an omnichannel subscription item](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_items/list-scheduled-changes-for-omnichannel-subscription-item) when [`has_scheduled_changes`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_items/omnichannel_subscription_item-object#has_scheduled_changes) is `true`.<br>|
|» » customer|body|[Customer](#schemacustomer)|true|Represents a customer, which can be an individual or organization that subscribes to your products or services. The customer resource associates with [subscriptions](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object), [card information](/docs/api/cards/card-object), and billing addresses. The customer details include their ID, name, contact information, and any [custom attributes](/docs/api/advanced-features) you'd like to associate with them.  <br>**Breaking Change**:<br><br>* [**Sites**](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/sites-intro.html) **created before March 1, 2014** : [updating the card](/docs/api/cards/update-card-for-a-customer) deletes the customer's `billing_address` and `vat_number` and replaces them with values from the request.<br>* **Sites created on or after March 1, 2014** : updating the card doesn't change the `billing_address` and `vat_number`.<br>|

For more information, see [Download financial reports](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/getting-paid/download-financial-reports) and [Overview of reporting tools](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/measure-app-performance/overview-of-reporting-tools).<br>[Learn more](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appstoreservernotifications/price) about price in Apple App Store.<br><br>### Google Play Store<br><br>Google Play does not always expose a complete transaction amount or purchase time for every notification path. When Google provides price / time data for a transaction, Chargebee records `price_*` and `transacted_at`; otherwise these attributes may be absent. Some Google one-time-order samples include price and `transacted_at` on `purchase_transaction`.<br><br>Transactions can be linked to subscriptions and/or one-time orders via `linked_omnichannel_subscriptions` and `linked_omnichannel_one_time_orders`. Chargebee may also emit [`omnichannel_transaction_created`](/docs/api/events/webhook/omnichannel_transaction_created) when a new transaction row is recorded.<br>|
|» » customer|body|[Customer](#schemacustomer)|true|Represents a customer, which can be an individual or organization that subscribes to your products or services. The customer resource associates with [subscriptions](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object), [card information](/docs/api/cards/card-object), and billing addresses. The customer details include their ID, name, contact information, and any [custom attributes](/docs/api/advanced-features) you'd like to associate with them.  <br>**Breaking Change**:<br><br>* [**Sites**](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/sites-intro.html) **created before March 1, 2014** : [updating the card](/docs/api/cards/update-card-for-a-customer) deletes the customer's `billing_address` and `vat_number` and replaces them with values from the request.<br>* **Sites created on or after March 1, 2014** : updating the card doesn't change the `billing_address` and `vat_number`.<br>|

## Triggered when you make the following changes to a pending invoice - add a charge, add a non-recurring addon, or delete a line item.

<a id="opIdonInvoice_updatedWebhook"></a>

`POST invoice_updated`

Triggered when changes are made to a finalized invoice, including voiding, deletion, invoice address updates, status changes, and payment changes such as applying or removing a payment, applying or removing a credit, and credit note creation. `pending_invoice_updated` is triggered for changes specific to pending invoices; invoice_updated covers all other invoice changes.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-you-make-the-following-changes-to-a-pending-invoice---add-a-charge-add-a-non-recurring-addon-or-delete-a-line-item-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[InvoiceUpdatedEvent](#schemainvoiceupdatedevent)|false|Payload for invoice_updated event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » invoice|body|[Invoice](#schemainvoice)|true|An invoice is a commercial document representing a sale of products/services offered by you to a customer. It enumerates all the charges, adjustments, payments, discounts and taxes associated with the sale.<br><br>An invoice is said to be a recurring one when it is has at least one charge for [a plan or an addon item price](/docs/api/items). It is a non-recurring one when it has charges for only charge-item prices or [one-time charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/charges.html).<br><br>The item prices for any given billing term of a subscription are billed via an invoice at the beginning of the term (unless the charges are left unbilled). However, item prices that belong to `metered` items are billed at the end of the term via a `pending` invoice that can [close automatically](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing#configuring-metered-billing) or via [an API call](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice). Moreover, when there are no `metered` items in the subscription, the invoices can still be generated as `pending` while [creating](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items) or [updating](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items) a subscription.<br><br>#### Auto-collection<br><br>If [auto-collection](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#auto-collection-status) is enabled, then immediately on invoice generation (or, in case of subscriptions that have `create_pending_invoices` as `true`, on [invoice closure](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice)), the [payment method](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#payment_method) on file is charged:<br><br>* If the payment succeeds, the invoice is marked as `paid`.<br>* On payment failure, the invoice is marked as `payment_due` and [dunning settings](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/dunning-v2.html) are taken into account for payment retries.<br>* If no retry attempts are configured, or when retries are exhausted, the invoice is marked as `not_paid`.<br>* the amount due is zero or negative, the invoice is immediately marked as `paid` and the balance, if any, is added to [excess payments](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#excess-payments) for the customer.<br><br>**Note:** If [consolidated invoicing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html) is enabled, the attribute `subscription_id` is unavailable when the invoice has line items from multiple subscriptions. The individual subscription ids are seen under `line_items.subscription_id`.  <br><br>#### Recurring and non-recurring invoices<br><br>A recurring invoice contains at least one line item that is billed on a recurring basis. Specifically, it has at least one [`line_items[]`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#line_items) with `entity_type` set to `plan_item_price` or `addon_item_price`. A non-recurring invoice contains no recurring line items.  <br><br>#### Refundable amount for an invoice<br><br>The refundable amount for an invoice is the (amount paid on the invoice + refundable credit applied on the invoice + taxes withheld on the invoice) minus (amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice). Each of these amounts is obtained from the invoice resource as follows:<br><br>* Amount paid on the invoice: [`amount_paid`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_amount_paid)<br>* Refundable credit applied on the invoice: [`credits_applied`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_credits_applied)<br>* Taxes withheld on the invoice: Sum of [`linked_taxes_withheld[].amount`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_linked_taxes_withheld)<br>* Amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice: Sum of [`issued_credit_notes[i].cn_total`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_issued_credit_notes) where `issued_credit_notes[i].cn_status` is `refunded` or `refund_due`.<br>|

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Webhook received successfully|None|

[Learn more](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/subscriptions#plan-based-billing).<br><br>* **Multi-frequency billing** : Subscriptions are billed according to the billing period of each recurring item price within the subscription. ## Triggered when a business entity is changed

<a id="opIdonBusiness_entity_updatedWebhook"></a>

`POST business_entity_updated`

Triggered when a business entity is changed


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-business-entity-is-changed-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[BusinessEntityUpdatedEvent](#schemabusinessentityupdatedevent)|false|Payload for business_entity_updated event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » business_entity|body|[BusinessEntity](#schemabusinessentity)|true|The `business_entity` resource represents a business unit or brand under your organization. Key resources in Chargebee Billing (such as [customer](/docs/api/customers), [subscriptions](/docs/api/subscriptions), [invoices](/docs/api/invoices), and [transactions](/docs/api/transactions)) along with the associated site configurations, fall under a [business entity](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/mbe.html). Each Chargebee Billing [site](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/sites-intro.html) has one business entity by default. You may create multiple business entities in the following scenarios:<br><br>* **Multiple Business Units**: You may be running your business under different regional units with different "invoice-from" addresses. This is usually done to manage taxation and bookkeeping. In such a case, you may create a business entity for each business unit.<br>* **Multiple Brands**: You may have multiple brands within your business, such as those acquired via mergers and acquisitions. You may create a business entity for each brand.<br><br>Creating multiple business entities lets you separate configuration and data for your business units or brands so that you can manage their billing and revenue operations independently.  <br>**See also**<br><br>[More information](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/mbe.html) on business entities and the configuration options available.  <br>Specifying business entity in API operations  <br>All API operations in Chargebee have site [context](/docs/api/business_entities). Context restrictions cannot be assigned to [API keys](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/api_keys.html). However, if your site has multiple business entities, you can specify the business entity [context](/docs/api/business_entities) for an API call by passing a [custom HTTP request header](/docs/api/advanced-features).  <br>API behavior based on business entity specified  <br>The table below explains how Chargebee responds to various API calls depending on whether the business entity ID is specified as part of the API call.  <br>**Note**<br><br>Some of the words used here are defined in the [Terminology section](/docs/api/business_entities).  <br><br>\|         **Operation/Type of operation**          \|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                **Behavior**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                \|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    **Examples**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    \|<br>\|--------------------------------------------------\|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\|<br>\| Any operation that creates a `customer` resource \| * If `business_entity_id` **is provided** , the `customer` resource is created and linked to it. * If `business_entity_id` **is not provided** , the `customer` resource is created under the [default business entity](/docs/api/business_entities) of the site.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          \| * [Create a customer](/docs/api/customers/create-a-customer) * When [Create a checkout for charge items and quick charge](/docs/api/hosted_pages/checkout-charge-items-and-one-time-charges)s or [Create checkout for a new subscription](/docs/api/hosted_pages/create-checkout-for-a-new-subscription) is called, providing a value for `customer[id]` that is not already present in the site. This creates a new `customer` resource.                                          \|<br>\| Create a resource other than `customer`          \| * If `business_entity_id` **is provided** , and it is the same as that [linked](/docs/api/business_entities) to the [target resource](/docs/api/business_entities): the resource is created and linked to the business entity provided. * If `business_entity_id` **is provided** , and it is not the same as that linked to the target resource, a `404 Not Found` response is sent because the resource cannot be found in the [context](/docs/api/business_entities) of the business entity specified. * If `business_entity_id` **is not provided**, the resource is created and linked to the business entity of the target resource. \| * [Create a subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items): the target resource is a `customer`. * [Create a comment](/docs/api/comments/create-a-comment): the target resource is specified in the value provided for `entity_type`. * [Create an invoice for items and one-time charges](/docs/api/invoices/create-invoice-for-items-and-one-time-charges): depending on the ID specified, the target resource is either a `customer` or a `subscription`. \|<br>\| Update/delete a resource                         \| * If `business_entity_id` **is provided** , and it is the same as that [linked](/docs/api/business_entities) to the resource, the operation proceeds successfully. * If `business_entity_id` **is provided** , and it is not the same as that [linked](/docs/api/business_entities) to the resource, a `404 Not Found` response is sent because the resource cannot be found in the [context](/docs/api/business_entities) of the business entity specified. * If `business_entity_id` **is not provided**, the operation proceeds successfully.                                                                                           \| * [Update a customer](/docs/api/customers/update-a-customer) * [Update a subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items) * [Update a card payment source](/docs/api/payment_sources/update-a-card-payment-source)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             \|<br>\| List resources                                   \| * If `business_entity_id` **is provided,** then only those resources linked to the business entity are returned since the [context](/docs/api/business_entities) of the operation is now restricted to the business entity specified. * If `business_entity_id` **is not provided**, then all resources in the site are returned.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          \| * [List customers](/docs/api/customers/list-customers) * [List payment sources](/docs/api/payment_sources/list-payment-sources)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    \|<br>\| Retreive a resource                              \| * If `business_entity_id` **is provided** , and it is the same as that [linked](/docs/api/business_entities) to the resource, the resource is retrieved successfully. * If `business_entity_id` **is provided** , and it is not the same as that [linked](/docs/api/business_entities) to the resource, a `404 Not Found` response is sent because the resource cannot be found in the [context](/docs/api/business_entities) of the business entity specified. * If `business_entity_id` **is not provided**, the resource is retrieved successfully.                                                                                     \| * [Retrieve a customer](/docs/api/customers/retrieve-a-customer) * [Retrieve a comment](/docs/api/comments/retrieve-a-comment)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     \|<br><br>Terminology  <br>This section defines some useful terms for describing how business entities work.<br><br>#### Linked business entity {#mbe-terms-content}<br><br>Any resource is always associated with precisely one and only one business entity. We call it the linked business entity of the resource, or simply, the business entity of the resource.<br><br>#### Default business entity<br><br>When `customer` resource is created and no business entity is specified, it is linked to the business entity designated as the default business entity of the site. A site always has a default business entity. Please choose the first business entity details carefully, as it can't be changed later, and this will be your default entity when no business entity is specified.<br><br>#### Context of an operation<br><br>Any site has data in it. This includes all the various resources such as customers, subscriptions, invoices, comments, and so on. The "context" of an API operation is the subset of site data it has access to. An API operation can only read or write data within its context. By default, an API operation has "site context", which means it has access to the entire site's data. However, when a business entity is [specified](/docs/api/business_entities) in an API operation, it has "business entity context", which means that the operation only has access to the data linked to the business entity.  <br>**Example**<br><br>Consider the [List customers API](/docs/api/customers/list-customers). When you call the API without specifying a business entity, its context is that of the site and therefore returns customer resources for the entire site. However, when you specify a business entity, the context is only that of the business entity, and therefore the customer resources of only the selected business entity are returned.<br><br>Let's look at the [Create checkout for a new subscription API](/docs/api/hosted_pages/create-checkout-for-a-new-subscription). Say you're calling this API and providing the `customer[id]` parameter. When no business entity is specified, the operation has *site context* and therefore looks up the ID among all the customer resources in the site. However, when a business entity is provided, the operation has *business entity context* and looks up the ID only among the customers linked to that business entity.<br><br>#### Target resource<br><br>While creating an API resource other than a `customer`, you specify a target resource under which it should be created. For example:<br><br>* While [creating an `invoice` resource for a one-time charge](/docs/api/invoices/create-invoice-for-items-and-one-time-charges), you must specify either the `customer` or the `subscription` resource to which it belongs. The `customer` or `subscription` resource, in this case, is the target resource of the `invoice`.<br>* While [creating a `subscription`](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items), the target resource of a `subscription` resource is always a `customer` resource.<br>* While [creating a `quote` resource of `type` `change_subscription`](/docs/api/quotes/create-a-quote-for-update-subscription-items), the target resource is a `subscription` resource.<br>|

It describes what the customer has signed up for and how often they're charged for it. The essential components of a subscription are:<br><br>* A [plan-item price](/docs/api/item_prices).<br>* Any addon- and charge-item prices applied to the subscription.<br>* Any [coupons](/docs/api/coupons) applied.<br>* Any [discounts](/docs/api/discounts) applied.<br><br>The charges in a subscription are billed via invoices.  <br>**Note:**<br>The maximum number of subscriptions for any given [customer](/docs/api/customers)<br>([active](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object#status)<br>or not) is 900.  <br><br>#### Subscription billing frequencies<br><br>Chargebee offers two billing frequency options for subscriptions:<br><br>* **Plan-based billing** (`default`): Subscriptions are billed based on the billing period defined for the item price of the `item_type` `plan`. [Learn more](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/subscriptions#plan-based-billing).<br><br>* **Multi-frequency billing** : Subscriptions are billed according to the billing period of each recurring item price within the subscription. |» » advance_invoice_schedule|body|[AdvanceInvoiceSchedule](#schemaadvanceinvoiceschedule)|true|The invoice for a subscription in Chargebee is generated at the time of subscription renewal. Invoices can also be [generated in advance](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/advance-invoices.html) for an upcoming renewal or set of renewals. With Advance Invoicing Schedules, you can set up a plan for when such advance invoices are generated for the lifetime of the subscription. This helps you:<br><br>* Set up a contract with your customers so that they can be notified of their payment schedules in advance.<br>* Allow customers who make offline payments to be alerted about their upcoming dues well ahead of actual subscription renewals.<br>* Prevent post-renewal unpaid usage of your services by customers.<br><br>Advance invoices can be scheduled in two ways:<br><br>#### Specific Dates Schedule<br><br>Advance invoices for a subscription can be scheduled to be generated on specific [dates](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#specific_dates_schedule_date) in the future. You must specify the [number of billing cycles](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#specific_dates_schedule_terms_to_charge) to be invoiced on each date. A maximum of 5 dates can be specified.<br><br>#### Fixed Interval Schedule<br><br>Advance invoices can be scheduled to be generated at fixed intervals of time, where each interval spans the same number of billing cycles of the subscription. The invoice for each interval is generated a specified number of days ([`days_before_interval`](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#fixed_interval_schedule_days_before_renewal)) before the start of the interval. You can configure the schedule to end on a certain date or after a specified number of advance invoices have been generated.<br><br>The start date of the first interval depends on the number of days remaining from current time till the next renewal of the subscription. If this is more than `days_before_interval`, the interval begins at the next renewal. On the other hand, if the number of days remaining before the next renewal is less than `days_before_interval`, the first interval begins at the renewal following the next.<br>|

## Triggered when a payment is initiated via direct debit.

<a id="opIdonPayment_initiatedWebhook"></a>

`POST payment_initiated`

Triggered when a payment is initiated using the `direct_debit` payment method, or when a transaction enters the `in_progress` status due to asynchronous processing at the payment gateway.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-payment-is-initiated-via-direct-debit-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[PaymentInitiatedEvent](#schemapaymentinitiatedevent)|false|Payload for payment_initiated event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » transaction|body|[Transaction](#schematransaction)|true|This resource represents the [transaction](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/transactions.html)<br>event that has happened in your account.<br>|
|» » invoice|body|[Invoice](#schemainvoice)|true|An invoice is a commercial document representing a sale of products/services offered by you to a customer. It enumerates all the charges, adjustments, payments, discounts and taxes associated with the sale.<br><br>An invoice is said to be a recurring one when it is has at least one charge for [a plan or an addon item price](/docs/api/items). It is a non-recurring one when it has charges for only charge-item prices or [one-time charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/charges.html).<br><br>The item prices for any given billing term of a subscription are billed via an invoice at the beginning of the term (unless the charges are left unbilled). However, item prices that belong to `metered` items are billed at the end of the term via a `pending` invoice that can [close automatically](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing#configuring-metered-billing) or via [an API call](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice). Moreover, when there are no `metered` items in the subscription, the invoices can still be generated as `pending` while [creating](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items) or [updating](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items) a subscription.<br><br>#### Auto-collection<br><br>If [auto-collection](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#auto-collection-status) is enabled, then immediately on invoice generation (or, in case of subscriptions that have `create_pending_invoices` as `true`, on [invoice closure](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice)), the [payment method](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#payment_method) on file is charged:<br><br>* If the payment succeeds, the invoice is marked as `paid`.<br>* On payment failure, the invoice is marked as `payment_due` and [dunning settings](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/dunning-v2.html) are taken into account for payment retries.<br>* If no retry attempts are configured, or when retries are exhausted, the invoice is marked as `not_paid`.<br>* the amount due is zero or negative, the invoice is immediately marked as `paid` and the balance, if any, is added to [excess payments](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#excess-payments) for the customer.<br><br>**Note:** If [consolidated invoicing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html) is enabled, the attribute `subscription_id` is unavailable when the invoice has line items from multiple subscriptions. The individual subscription ids are seen under `line_items.subscription_id`.  <br><br>#### Recurring and non-recurring invoices<br><br>A recurring invoice contains at least one line item that is billed on a recurring basis. Specifically, it has at least one [`line_items[]`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#line_items) with `entity_type` set to `plan_item_price` or `addon_item_price`. A non-recurring invoice contains no recurring line items.  <br><br>#### Refundable amount for an invoice<br><br>The refundable amount for an invoice is the (amount paid on the invoice + refundable credit applied on the invoice + taxes withheld on the invoice) minus (amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice). Each of these amounts is obtained from the invoice resource as follows:<br><br>* Amount paid on the invoice: [`amount_paid`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_amount_paid)<br>* Refundable credit applied on the invoice: [`credits_applied`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_credits_applied)<br>* Taxes withheld on the invoice: Sum of [`linked_taxes_withheld[].amount`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_linked_taxes_withheld)<br>* Amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice: Sum of [`issued_credit_notes[i].cn_total`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_issued_credit_notes) where `issued_credit_notes[i].cn_status` is `refunded` or `refund_due`.<br>|
|» » customer|body|[Customer](#schemacustomer)|true|Represents a customer, which can be an individual or organization that subscribes to your products or services. The customer resource associates with [subscriptions](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object), [card information](/docs/api/cards/card-object), and billing addresses. |» » subscription|body|[Subscription](#schemasubscription)|true|A Chargebee subscription connects a customer record to products/services. It describes what the customer has signed up for and how often they're charged for it. The essential components of a subscription are:<br><br>* A [plan-item price](/docs/api/item_prices).<br>* Any addon- and charge-item prices applied to the subscription.<br>* Any [coupons](/docs/api/coupons) applied.<br>* Any [discounts](/docs/api/discounts) applied.<br><br>The charges in a subscription are billed via invoices.  <br>**Note:**<br>The maximum number of subscriptions for any given [customer](/docs/api/customers)<br>([active](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object#status)<br>or not) is 900.  <br><br>#### Subscription billing frequencies<br><br>Chargebee offers two billing frequency options for subscriptions:<br><br>* **Plan-based billing** (`default`): Subscriptions are billed based on the billing period defined for the item price of the `item_type` `plan`. [Learn more](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/subscriptions#plan-based-billing).<br><br>* **Multi-frequency billing** : Subscriptions are billed according to the billing period of each recurring item price within the subscription. [Learn more](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/multi-frequency-billing).<br><br>  **Important**<br><br>  [Limitations](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/multi-frequency-billing#limitations) of Multi-frequency billing.<br><br>The selection of the billing frequency preference is configured at the site level.  <br><br>#### Item price compatibility in a subscription<br><br>When creating or updating a subscription, one of the item prices specified under subscription_items must be a plan-item price. ## Triggered when a `feature` status transitions to `archived`.

<a id="opIdonFeature_archivedWebhook"></a>

`POST feature_archived`

Triggered when a `feature` status transitions to `archived`.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|

|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » feature|body|[Feature](#schemafeature)|true|Subscriptions are created in Chargebee using items. Items represent the products or services that you offer to your customers. Items often differ in the number of product features that are available to them. The Features API helps you define the various features offered as part of your product line. It also defines the entitlements that items and subscriptions can have towards said features.  <br>**Note**<br><br>The maximum number of features a site can have is 400.<br><br>Features of this API<br>--------------------<br><br>The Features API enables you to:<br><br>* Define the set of features provided by your product.<br>* Specify the entitlements that items have towards said features.<br>* For a given subscription, modify the entitlements inherited from items in the subscription.<br>* Offer additional feature entitlements to subscriptions than those inherited from items in the subscription.<br>* Serve as a source of truth to your provisioning systems for subscription entitlements.<br>* Use entitlement information to understand which features drive value and revenue.<br><br>**See also**<br><br>* [Entitlements](/docs/api/entitlements)<br>* [Subscription Entitlements](/docs/api/subscription_entitlements)<br>* [Entitlement Overrides](/docs/api/entitlement_overrides)<br>|

|» » invoice|body|[Invoice](#schemainvoice)|true|An invoice is a commercial document representing a sale of products/services offered by you to a customer. It enumerates all the charges, adjustments, payments, discounts and taxes associated with the sale.<br><br>An invoice is said to be a recurring one when it is has at least one charge for [a plan or an addon item price](/docs/api/items). It is a non-recurring one when it has charges for only charge-item prices or [one-time charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/charges.html).<br><br>The item prices for any given billing term of a subscription are billed via an invoice at the beginning of the term (unless the charges are left unbilled). However, item prices that belong to `metered` items are billed at the end of the term via a `pending` invoice that can [close automatically](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing#configuring-metered-billing) or via [an API call](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice). Moreover, when there are no `metered` items in the subscription, the invoices can still be generated as `pending` while [creating](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items) or [updating](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items) a subscription.<br><br>#### Auto-collection<br><br>If [auto-collection](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#auto-collection-status) is enabled, then immediately on invoice generation (or, in case of subscriptions that have `create_pending_invoices` as `true`, on [invoice closure](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice)), the [payment method](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#payment_method) on file is charged:<br><br>* If the payment succeeds, the invoice is marked as `paid`.<br>* On payment failure, the invoice is marked as `payment_due` and [dunning settings](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/dunning-v2.html) are taken into account for payment retries.<br>* If no retry attempts are configured, or when retries are exhausted, the invoice is marked as `not_paid`.<br>* the amount due is zero or negative, the invoice is immediately marked as `paid` and the balance, if any, is added to [excess payments](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#excess-payments) for the customer.<br><br>**Note:** If [consolidated invoicing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html) is enabled, the attribute `subscription_id` is unavailable when the invoice has line items from multiple subscriptions. The individual subscription ids are seen under `line_items.subscription_id`.  <br><br>#### Recurring and non-recurring invoices<br><br>A recurring invoice contains at least one line item that is billed on a recurring basis. Specifically, it has at least one [`line_items[]`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#line_items) with `entity_type` set to `plan_item_price` or `addon_item_price`. A non-recurring invoice contains no recurring line items.  <br><br>#### Refundable amount for an invoice<br><br>The refundable amount for an invoice is the (amount paid on the invoice + refundable credit applied on the invoice + taxes withheld on the invoice) minus (amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice). Each of these amounts is obtained from the invoice resource as follows:<br><br>* Amount paid on the invoice: [`amount_paid`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_amount_paid)<br>* Refundable credit applied on the invoice: [`credits_applied`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_credits_applied)<br>* Taxes withheld on the invoice: Sum of [`linked_taxes_withheld[].amount`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_linked_taxes_withheld)<br>* Amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice: Sum of [`issued_credit_notes[i].cn_total`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_issued_credit_notes) where `issued_credit_notes[i].cn_status` is `refunded` or `refund_due`.<br>|

|» » omnichannel_subscription_item|body|[OmnichannelSubscriptionItem](#schemaomnichannelsubscriptionitem)|true|Represents a product entitlement (item) within an [`omnichannel_subscription`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscriptions) purchased on Apple App Store or Google Play Store.<br><br>Status, auto-renew, term dates, and cancel/expire reasons live on this resource. See [omnichannel statuses](/docs/api/omnichannel_statuses) for store mappings.<br><br>Chargebee records introductory and promotional offers on [`omnichannel_subscription_item_offers`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_items/omnichannel_subscription_item-object#omnichannel_subscription_item_offers). Win-back offers and offer codes are not supported.<br><br>When `has_scheduled_changes` is `true`, use [List scheduled changes](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_items/list-scheduled-changes-for-omnichannel-subscription-item) to retrieve deferred product or pause changes.  <br>**Note:**<br>This resource represents in-app subscription items made on Apple App Store and Google Play Store.<br>|
|» » omnichannel_subscription|body|[OmnichannelSubscription](#schemaomnichannelsubscription)|true|Represents a subscription purchased and managed in an external app marketplace (`apple_app_store` or `google_play_store`), normalized into Chargebee's omnichannel model.<br><br>Omnichannel subscriptions are typically created when you [record a purchase](/docs/api/recorded_purchases/record-a-purchase) and are kept in sync via store server notifications. They are store-managed: lifecycle changes come from Apple or Google, not from the Chargebee Subscriptions API.<br><br>Use [omnichannel statuses](/docs/api/omnichannel_statuses) for how store statuses map to `omnichannel_subscription_item.status`, and [omnichannel events](/docs/api/omnichannel_events) for notification-to-webhook mappings.<br><br>Chargebee records introductory and promotional offers on [`omnichannel_subscription_item_offers`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscriptions/omnichannel_subscription-object#omnichannel_subscription_items_omnichannel_subscription_item_offers). Win-back offers and offer codes are not supported.  <br>**Identifier tip:** Parent `id_at_source` is the Apple **Transaction ID** or Google **purchase token** . Nested `initial_purchase_transaction.id_at_source` is the Apple **Transaction ID** or Google **Order ID** (`GPA....`). See attribute descriptions below.  <br>**Note:**<br>This resource represents in-app subscriptions made on Apple App Store and Google Play Store.<br>|
|» » omnichannel_transaction|body|[OmnichannelTransaction](#schemaomnichanneltransaction)|true|A unified representation of a store purchase or renewal transaction across Apple App Store and Google Play Store.<br><br>Use `id_at_source` to correlate with the store-native transaction identifier:<br><br>* **Apple App Store** : App Store **Transaction ID**<br>* **Google Play Store** : Google Play **Order ID** (`GPA....`)<br><br>Parent subscription / one-time-order resources use purchase-token semantics for Google `id_at_source`; do not treat those as interchangeable with this transaction Order ID.<br><br>### Apple App Store<br><br>The [price](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appstoreservernotifications/price) value reflects the price you configured in App Store Connect, which the system records at the time of transaction ([transacted_at](/docs/api/omnichannel_transactions/omnichannel_transaction-object#transacted_at)) after the discount if any offers are applied.  <br>**Important**<br>For financial and accounting purposes, use the App Store Connect reporting tools. For more information, see [Download financial reports](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/getting-paid/download-financial-reports) and [Overview of reporting tools](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/measure-app-performance/overview-of-reporting-tools).<br>[Learn more](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appstoreservernotifications/price) about price in Apple App Store.<br><br>### Google Play Store<br><br>Google Play does not always expose a complete transaction amount or purchase time for every notification path. When Google provides price / time data for a transaction, Chargebee records `price_*` and `transacted_at`; otherwise these attributes may be absent. Some Google one-time-order samples include price and `transacted_at` on `purchase_transaction`.<br><br>Transactions can be linked to subscriptions and/or one-time orders via `linked_omnichannel_subscriptions` and `linked_omnichannel_one_time_orders`. Chargebee may also emit [`omnichannel_transaction_created`](/docs/api/events/webhook/omnichannel_transaction_created) when a new transaction row is recorded.<br>|
|» » omnichannel_subscription_item_scheduled_change|body|[OmnichannelSubscriptionItemScheduledChange](#schemaomnichannelsubscriptionitemscheduledchange)|true|Represents a future change to an [`omnichannel_subscription_item`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_items) that the store will apply later (typically at the end of the current term).<br><br>**Apple App Store** : Created when the customer schedules a **downgrade** within the same subscription group (`DID_CHANGE_RENEWAL_PREF` / `DOWNGRADE`). `change_type` is typically `downgrade`. Upgrades apply immediately and do **not** create this resource.<br><br>**Google Play Store** : Created when a product change uses the **`DEFERRED`** replacement mode (applied at term end). Immediate changes use `CHARGE_PRORATED_PRICE` and do **not** create this resource. A `change_type` of `pause` may appear for scheduled pause flows; confirm mapping against [omnichannel events](/docs/api/omnichannel_events).<br><br>Retrieve scheduled changes with [List scheduled changes for an omnichannel subscription item](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_items/list-scheduled-changes-for-omnichannel-subscription-item) when [`has_scheduled_changes`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_items/omnichannel_subscription_item-object#has_scheduled_changes) is `true`.<br>|
|» » customer|body|[Customer](#schemacustomer)|true|Represents a customer, which can be an individual or organization that subscribes to your products or services. The customer resource associates with [subscriptions](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object), [card information](/docs/api/cards/card-object), and billing addresses. The customer details include their ID, name, contact information, and any [custom attributes](/docs/api/advanced-features) you'd like to associate with them.  <br>**Breaking Change**:<br><br>* [**Sites**](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/sites-intro.html) **created before March 1, 2014** : [updating the card](/docs/api/cards/update-card-for-a-customer) deletes the customer's `billing_address` and `vat_number` and replaces them with values from the request.<br>* **Sites created on or after March 1, 2014** : updating the card doesn't change the `billing_address` and `vat_number`.<br>|

## Triggered when a coupon is created.

<a id="opIdonCoupon_createdWebhook"></a>

`POST coupon_created`

Triggered when a coupon is created.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-coupon-is-created-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CouponCreatedEvent](#schemacouponcreatedevent)|false|Payload for coupon_created event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » coupon|body|[Coupon](#schemacoupon)|true|Overview<br>--------<br><br>Coupons are deductions applied to invoices or invoice line items. They're designed to be consumed by your customers directly. A coupon deduction can either be for a fixed amount or for a percentage of the amount of the invoice or line item.  <br>**Note:**<br><br>If you wish to provide discounts to your customers via API or the Chargebee app, see [Discounts API](/docs/api/discounts)<br><br>Order of application of coupons and discounts<br>---------------------------------------------<br><br>When both [coupons](/docs/api/coupons) and [discounts](/docs/api/discounts) are applied simultaneously to a [subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions) or [one-time invoice](/docs/api/invoices/create-invoice-for-items-and-one-time-charges), they're applied in the following order:  <br><br>\|---\|---------------------------------------\|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\|<br>\|   \| **Summary**                           \| **Description**                                                                     \|<br>\| 1 \| Line-level, fixed amount coupons      \| `coupon` with `apply_on` = `each_specified_item` and `discount_type` = `flat`       \|<br>\| 2 \| Line-level, fixed amount discounts    \| `discount` with `apply_on` = `specific_item_price` and `type` = `fixed_amount`      \|<br>\| 3 \| Line-level, percentage coupons        \| `coupon` with `apply_on` = `each_specified_item` and `discount_type` = `percentage` \|<br>\| 4 \| Line-level, percentage discounts      \| `discount` with `apply_on` = `specific_item_price` and `type` = `percentage`        \|<br>\| 5 \| Invoice-level, fixed amount coupons   \| `coupon` with `apply_on` = `invoice_amount` and `discount_type` = `flat`            \|<br>\| 6 \| Invoice-level, fixed amount discounts \| `discount` with `apply_on` = `invoice_amount` and `type` = `fixed_amount`           \|<br>\| 7 \| Invoice-level, percentage coupons     \| `coupon` with `apply_on` = `invoice_amount` and `discount_type` = `percentage`      \|<br>\| 8 \| Invoice-level, percentage discounts   \| `discount` with `apply_on` = `invoice_amount` and `type` = `percentage`             \|<br><br>For example, consider the following scenario:<br><br>A subscription is created with:<br><br>* a plan price of $200 per month<br>* an addon price of $20 per month<br>* a flat $5 invoice discount<br>* a 1% off coupon on the addon<br>* a flat $2 coupon on the invoice<br><br>The above coupons and discount are applied in the following order:  <br><br>\|---\|---------------------------------------------\|-----------------------------------------------\|<br>\|   \| **Discount or coupon applied**              \| **Subtotal at each step**                     \|<br>\| 1 \| Initial subtotal (plan price + addon price) \| $200 + $20 = $220                             \|<br>\| 2 \| 1% off coupon on the addon                  \| $200 + $(20 - 0.02) = $200 + $19.98 = $219.98 \|<br>\| 3 \| Flat $2 coupon on the invoice               \| $219.98 - $2 = $217.98                        \|<br>\| 4 \| Flat $5 invoice discount                    \| $217.98 - $5 = **$212.98**                    \|<br><br>|

## Triggered when an item price is deleted.

<a id="opIdonItem_price_deletedWebhook"></a>

> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-an-item-price-is-deleted-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ItemPriceDeletedEvent](#schemaitempricedeletedevent)|false|Payload for item_price_deleted event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|

|» » item_price|body|[ItemPrice](#schemaitemprice)|true|An item price is a price point for an item. It defines the currency, pricing model, price, billing period and other attributes for an [item](/docs/api/items). For example, consider a cloud storage service as an item. Then each of the following defines an item price:<br><br>* The cloud storage sold at USD 10 per month.<br><br>* The same service sold at AUD 100 per year.<br><br>* The service sold at a monthly rate determined by the following [stairstep](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/plans.html#pricing-models) pricing model:<br><br>  * 1-10 users for EUR 10<br>  * 11-25 users for EUR 20<br>  * 26-50 users for EUR 45<br>  * 51 and above for EUR 100<br><br>Types of item prices<br>--------------------<br><br>The type of an item price corresponds to the [type of the item](/docs/api/items) that the item price belongs to. In other words, item prices can be of the following types:<br><br>* Plan-item prices<br>* Addon-item prices<br>* Charge-item prices<br><br>Billing periods for item prices<br>-------------------------------<br><br>The **billing period** of an item price (applicable only to plan-item prices and addon-item prices) is the [`period`](/docs/api/item_prices/item-price-object#period) of the item price in [`period_unit`](/docs/api/item_prices/item-price-object#period_unit)s.<br><br>* When [price variants](/docs/api/price_variants) are **not** enabled, an item can have only one item price for a given currency and billing period.<br>* When price variants **are** enabled, an item can have multiple item prices for the same currency and billing period, as long as each has a distinct [`price_variant_id`](/docs/api/item_prices/item-price-object#price_variant_id). An item price created without a `price_variant_id` is treated as the default ("no variant"), and only one such default item price can exist for a given currency and billing period.<br>|

It enumerates all the charges, adjustments, payments, discounts and taxes associated with the sale.<br><br>An invoice is said to be a recurring one when it is has at least one charge for [a plan or an addon item price](/docs/api/items). It is a non-recurring one when it has charges for only charge-item prices or [one-time charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/charges.html).<br><br>The item prices for any given billing term of a subscription are billed via an invoice at the beginning of the term (unless the charges are left unbilled). However, item prices that belong to `metered` items are billed at the end of the term via a `pending` invoice that can [close automatically](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing#configuring-metered-billing) or via [an API call](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice). Moreover, when there are no `metered` items in the subscription, the invoices can still be generated as `pending` while [creating](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items) or [updating](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items) a subscription.<br><br>#### Auto-collection<br><br>If [auto-collection](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#auto-collection-status) is enabled, then immediately on invoice generation (or, in case of subscriptions that have `create_pending_invoices` as `true`, on [invoice closure](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice)), the [payment method](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#payment_method) on file is charged:<br><br>* If the payment succeeds, the invoice is marked as `paid`.<br>* On payment failure, the invoice is marked as `payment_due` and [dunning settings](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/dunning-v2.html) are taken into account for payment retries.<br>* If no retry attempts are configured, or when retries are exhausted, the invoice is marked as `not_paid`.<br>* the amount due is zero or negative, the invoice is immediately marked as `paid` and the balance, if any, is added to [excess payments](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#excess-payments) for the customer.<br><br>**Note:** If [consolidated invoicing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html) is enabled, the attribute `subscription_id` is unavailable when the invoice has line items from multiple subscriptions. The individual subscription ids are seen under `line_items.subscription_id`.  <br><br>#### Recurring and non-recurring invoices<br><br>A recurring invoice contains at least one line item that is billed on a recurring basis. Specifically, it has at least one [`line_items[]`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#line_items) with `entity_type` set to `plan_item_price` or `addon_item_price`. A non-recurring invoice contains no recurring line items.  <br><br>#### Refundable amount for an invoice<br><br>The refundable amount for an invoice is the (amount paid on the invoice + refundable credit applied on the invoice + taxes withheld on the invoice) minus (amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice). Each of these amounts is obtained from the invoice resource as follows:<br><br>* Amount paid on the invoice: [`amount_paid`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_amount_paid)<br>* Refundable credit applied on the invoice: [`credits_applied`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_credits_applied)<br>* Taxes withheld on the invoice: Sum of [`linked_taxes_withheld[].amount`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_linked_taxes_withheld)<br>* Amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice: Sum of [`issued_credit_notes[i].cn_total`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_issued_credit_notes) where `issued_credit_notes[i].cn_status` is `refunded` or `refund_due`.<br>|

API at Card resource                             \|                                                                                                                                    Use instead |» » advance_invoice_schedule|body|[AdvanceInvoiceSchedule](#schemaadvanceinvoiceschedule)|true|The invoice for a subscription in Chargebee is generated at the time of subscription renewal. Invoices can also be [generated in advance](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/advance-invoices.html) for an upcoming renewal or set of renewals. With Advance Invoicing Schedules, you can set up a plan for when such advance invoices are generated for the lifetime of the subscription. This helps you:<br><br>* Set up a contract with your customers so that they can be notified of their payment schedules in advance.<br>* Allow customers who make offline payments to be alerted about their upcoming dues well ahead of actual subscription renewals.<br>* Prevent post-renewal unpaid usage of your services by customers.<br><br>Advance invoices can be scheduled in two ways:<br><br>#### Specific Dates Schedule<br><br>Advance invoices for a subscription can be scheduled to be generated on specific [dates](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#specific_dates_schedule_date) in the future. You must specify the [number of billing cycles](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#specific_dates_schedule_terms_to_charge) to be invoiced on each date. A maximum of 5 dates can be specified.<br><br>#### Fixed Interval Schedule<br><br>Advance invoices can be scheduled to be generated at fixed intervals of time, where each interval spans the same number of billing cycles of the subscription. The invoice for each interval is generated a specified number of days ([`days_before_interval`](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#fixed_interval_schedule_days_before_renewal)) before the start of the interval. You can configure the schedule to end on a certain date or after a specified number of advance invoices have been generated.<br><br>The start date of the first interval depends on the number of days remaining from current time till the next renewal of the subscription. If this is more than `days_before_interval`, the interval begins at the next renewal. On the other hand, if the number of days remaining before the next renewal is less than `days_before_interval`, the first interval begins at the renewal following the next.<br>|

[Learn more](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/multi-frequency-billing).<br><br>  **Important**<br><br>  [Limitations](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/multi-frequency-billing#limitations) of Multi-frequency billing.<br><br>The selection of the billing frequency preference is configured at the site level.  <br><br>#### Item price compatibility in a subscription<br><br>When creating or updating a subscription, one of the item prices specified under subscription_items must be a plan-item price. The remaining must be compatible addon- or charge-item prices. An item price is compatible with a plan-item price if their currencies are the same. Additionally, an addon-item price is compatible with a plan-item price only if their billing frequencies meet the following conditions:  <br><br>\| `period_unit` for plan-item price \| Compatible `period_unit` for addon-item price \|                                                                                                                                                                                                Compatible period for addon-item price                                                                                                                                                                                                \|<br>\|-----------------------------------\|-----------------------------------------------\|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\|<br>\| `day`                             \| `day`                                         \| The `period` of the plan-item price should be divisible by the `period` of the addon-item price. **Example** If the `period` of the plan-item price is `10`, then the period of the addon-item price can be `10`, `5`, `2`, or `1`.                                                                                                                                                                                                  \|<br>\| `week`                            \| `week` or `day`                               \| The `period` (in days) of the plan-item price should be divisible by the `period` of the addon-item price. **Example** If the `period` of the plan-item price is `2`, then the period of the addon-item price can be as follows depending on the value of `period_unit`: * for `period_unit` as `week`, `period` can be `2` or `1`. * for `period_unit` as `day`, `period` can be `14`, `7`, `2`, or `1`.                            \|<br>\| `month`                           \| `month`                                       \| The `period` of the plan-item price should be divisible by the `period` of the addon-item price. **Example** If the `period` of the plan-item price is `6`, then the `period` of the addon-item price can be `6`, `3`, `2`, or `1`. or `month`                             \| The `period` (in months) of the plan-item price should be divisible by the `period` of the addon-item price. **Example** If the `period` of the plan-item price is `2`, then the `period` of the addon-item price can be as follows depending on the value of `period_unit`: * for `period_unit` as `year`, `period` can be `2` or `1`. * for `period_unit` as ## Triggered when a batch of ledger operations is persisted for a subscription unit.

<a id="opIdonLedger_updatedWebhook"></a>

`POST ledger_updated`

Triggered when a batch of [ledger operations](/docs/api/ledger_operations) is persisted for a subscription unit.
The event content includes the related `ledger_operations`, `ledger_account_balance`, `grant_blocks`, and `ledger_entries`.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-batch-of-ledger-operations-is-persisted-for-a-subscription-unit-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[LedgerUpdatedEvent](#schemaledgerupdatedevent)|false|Payload for ledger_updated event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » ledger_operations|body|[[LedgerOperation](#schemaledgeroperation)]|true|none|
|» » ledger_account_balance|body|[LedgerAccountBalance](#schemaledgeraccountbalance)|true|Credit Grants<br>-------------<br><br>A credit grant is a quantified allocation of credits given to a subscription through a configured [item price](/docs/api/item_prices) or via the [allocate](/docs/api/ledger_operations/allocate) operation, consumed over time through ledger operations.  <br>**Example**<br><br>A subscription receives a credit grant of 100 AI credits as a balance. As the customer uses AI features<br>(e.g., Image Generation), the provisioned balance is consumed first. Once exhausted, further consumption is deducted from the overdraft balance until its limit is reached.<br><br>The Ledger Account Balance object<br>---------------------------------<br><br>The `ledger_account_balance` object is a real-time snapshot of credit grants for a single combination of subscription_id, unit_id and unit_type.<br><br>The ledger tracks two balances:<br><br>* [**provisioned_balance**](#provisioned_balance): Reflects the credit grants given through the configured item price or allocate operations. These are prepaid credit grants for which the customer has already paid. Any ledger operation will prioritize consuming this balance first.<br>* [**overdraft_balance**](#overdraft_balance): Reflects the extra limit provided to a subscription in case it exhausts all credit grants before they are renewed or refreshed. Any ledger operation will consume this balance only when the provisioned balance has been exhausted.<br><br>**Note**<br><br>These two balances are always tracked together for a subscription with credit grants.  <br>**Example**<br><br>A subscription has a credit grant of 100 AI credits, added to its provisioned balance. Once the provisioned balance is exhausted, further consumption is drawn from the overdraft balance up to its configured limit.<br>screenshot\\|/images/account_balance.png<br><br>**Returned by**<br><br>* [List ledger account balances](/docs/api/ledger_account_balances/list-ledger-account-balances) API.<br>* Ledger [operations](/docs/api/ledger_operations) such as [allocate](/docs/api/ledger_operations/allocate), [capture](/docs/api/ledger_operations/capture), and [authorize](/docs/api/ledger_operations/authorize).<br>|
|» » grant_blocks|body|[[GrantBlock](#schemagrantblock)]|true|none|
|» » ledger_entries|body|[[LedgerEntry](#schemaledgerentry)]|true|none|

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-batch-of-ledger-operations-is-persisted-for-a-subscription-unit-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Webhook received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Triggered when an item price is created.

<a id="opIdonItem_price_createdWebhook"></a>

`POST item_price_created`

Triggered when an item price is created.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-an-item-price-is-created-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ItemPriceCreatedEvent](#schemaitempricecreatedevent)|false|Payload for item_price_created event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » item_price|body|[ItemPrice](#schemaitemprice)|true|An item price is a price point for an item. It defines the currency, pricing model, price, billing period and other attributes for an [item](/docs/api/items). For example, consider a cloud storage service as an item. Then each of the following defines an item price:<br><br>* The cloud storage sold at USD 10 per month.<br><br>* The same service sold at AUD 100 per year.<br><br>* The service sold at a monthly rate determined by the following [stairstep](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/plans.html#pricing-models) pricing model:<br><br>  * 1-10 users for EUR 10<br>  * 11-25 users for EUR 20<br>  * 26-50 users for EUR 45<br>  * 51 and above for EUR 100<br><br>Types of item prices<br>--------------------<br><br>The type of an item price corresponds to the [type of the item](/docs/api/items) that the item price belongs to. In other words, item prices can be of the following types:<br><br>* Plan-item prices<br>* Addon-item prices<br>* Charge-item prices<br><br>Billing periods for item prices<br>-------------------------------<br><br>The **billing period** of an item price (applicable only to plan-item prices and addon-item prices) is the [`period`](/docs/api/item_prices/item-price-object#period) of the item price in [`period_unit`](/docs/api/item_prices/item-price-object#period_unit)s.<br><br>* When [price variants](/docs/api/price_variants) are **not** enabled, an item can have only one item price for a given currency and billing period.<br>* When price variants **are** enabled, an item can have multiple item prices for the same currency and billing period, as long as each has a distinct [`price_variant_id`](/docs/api/item_prices/item-price-object#price_variant_id). An item price created without a `price_variant_id` is treated as the default ("no variant"), and only one such default item price can exist for a given currency and billing period.<br>|

|200|OK|Webhook received successfully|None|

|» » advance_invoice_schedule|body|[AdvanceInvoiceSchedule](#schemaadvanceinvoiceschedule)|true|The invoice for a subscription in Chargebee is generated at the time of subscription renewal. Invoices can also be [generated in advance](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/advance-invoices.html) for an upcoming renewal or set of renewals. With Advance Invoicing Schedules, you can set up a plan for when such advance invoices are generated for the lifetime of the subscription. This helps you:<br><br>* Set up a contract with your customers so that they can be notified of their payment schedules in advance.<br>* Allow customers who make offline payments to be alerted about their upcoming dues well ahead of actual subscription renewals.<br>* Prevent post-renewal unpaid usage of your services by customers.<br><br>Advance invoices can be scheduled in two ways:<br><br>#### Specific Dates Schedule<br><br>Advance invoices for a subscription can be scheduled to be generated on specific [dates](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#specific_dates_schedule_date) in the future. You must specify the [number of billing cycles](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#specific_dates_schedule_terms_to_charge) to be invoiced on each date. A maximum of 5 dates can be specified.<br><br>#### Fixed Interval Schedule<br><br>Advance invoices can be scheduled to be generated at fixed intervals of time, where each interval spans the same number of billing cycles of the subscription. The invoice for each interval is generated a specified number of days ([`days_before_interval`](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#fixed_interval_schedule_days_before_renewal)) before the start of the interval. You can configure the schedule to end on a certain date or after a specified number of advance invoices have been generated.<br><br>The start date of the first interval depends on the number of days remaining from current time till the next renewal of the subscription. If this is more than `days_before_interval`, the interval begins at the next renewal. On the other hand, if the number of days remaining before the next renewal is less than `days_before_interval`, the first interval begins at the renewal following the next.<br>|
