## Triggered when a payment refund is made.

<a id="opIdonPayment_refundedWebhook"></a>

`POST payment_refunded`

Triggered when a payment refund is made.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-payment-refund-is-made-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[PaymentRefundedEvent](#schemapaymentrefundedevent)|false|Payload for payment_refunded event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » transaction|body|[Transaction](#schematransaction)|true|This resource represents the [transaction](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/transactions.html)<br>event that has happened in your account.<br>|
|» » invoice|body|[Invoice](#schemainvoice)|true|An invoice is a commercial document representing a sale of products/services offered by you to a customer. It enumerates all the charges, adjustments, payments, discounts and taxes associated with the sale.<br><br>An invoice is said to be a recurring one when it is has at least one charge for [a plan or an addon item price](/docs/api/items). It is a non-recurring one when it has charges for only charge-item prices or [one-time charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/charges.html).<br><br>The item prices for any given billing term of a subscription are billed via an invoice at the beginning of the term (unless the charges are left unbilled). However, item prices that belong to `metered` items are billed at the end of the term via a `pending` invoice that can [close automatically](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing#configuring-metered-billing) or via [an API call](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice). Moreover, when there are no `metered` items in the subscription, the invoices can still be generated as `pending` while [creating](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items) or [updating](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items) a subscription.<br><br>#### Auto-collection<br><br>If [auto-collection](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#auto-collection-status) is enabled, then immediately on invoice generation (or, in case of subscriptions that have `create_pending_invoices` as `true`, on [invoice closure](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice)), the [payment method](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#payment_method) on file is charged:<br><br>* If the payment succeeds, the invoice is marked as `paid`.<br>* On payment failure, the invoice is marked as `payment_due` and [dunning settings](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/dunning-v2.html) are taken into account for payment retries.<br>* If no retry attempts are configured, or when retries are exhausted, the invoice is marked as `not_paid`.<br>* the amount due is zero or negative, the invoice is immediately marked as `paid` and the balance, if any, is added to [excess payments](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#excess-payments) for the customer.<br><br>**Note:** If [consolidated invoicing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html) is enabled, the attribute `subscription_id` is unavailable when the invoice has line items from multiple subscriptions. The individual subscription ids are seen under `line_items.subscription_id`.  <br><br>#### Recurring and non-recurring invoices<br><br>A recurring invoice contains at least one line item that is billed on a recurring basis. Specifically, it has at least one [`line_items[]`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#line_items) with `entity_type` set to `plan_item_price` or `addon_item_price`. A non-recurring invoice contains no recurring line items.  <br><br>#### Refundable amount for an invoice<br><br>The refundable amount for an invoice is the (amount paid on the invoice + refundable credit applied on the invoice + taxes withheld on the invoice) minus (amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice). Each of these amounts is obtained from the invoice resource as follows:<br><br>* Amount paid on the invoice: [`amount_paid`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_amount_paid)<br>* Refundable credit applied on the invoice: [`credits_applied`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_credits_applied)<br>* Taxes withheld on the invoice: Sum of [`linked_taxes_withheld[].amount`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_linked_taxes_withheld)<br>* Amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice: Sum of [`issued_credit_notes[i].cn_total`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_issued_credit_notes) where `issued_credit_notes[i].cn_status` is `refunded` or `refund_due`.<br>|
|» » credit_note|body|[CreditNote](#schemacreditnote)|true|A [Credit Note](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/credit-notes.html) is a document that specifies the money owed by a business to its customer. The seller usually issues a Credit Note for the same or lower amount than the invoice, and then repays the money to the customer or set it off against other 'due' invoices.<br><br>### Credit Note Types<br><br>Credit notes in Chargebee are categorized into three types:<br>1. `adjustment`: Adjustment credit notes are used to adjust the amount of an existing invoice in the `payment_due` or `not_paid` [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status). Use this type of credit note to reduce the invoice amount, typically as a discount to the customer.<br><br>Adjustment credit notes are automatically created in the following cases:<br><br>* When an invoice is written off.<br>* When a subscription is modified with proration enabled, and the invoice for the current term is in the `payment_due` or `not_paid` [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status). 2. `refundable`: Refundable credit notes allow you to return a certain amount to the customer. These credits can be:<br>* Retained for automatic application on future invoices.<br>* Applied to existing unpaid invoices.<br>* Refunded to the customer. Refundable credit notes are automatically created in the following cases:<br>* When an invoice is refunded.<br>* When a subscription is changed or canceled with proration enabled, the invoice for the current term is in the `paid` [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status). Refundable credits are applied to future invoices or can be refunded to the original payment method. 3. `store`: Store credit notes are created for `paid` or `partially_paid` invoice [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status) during subscription changes, such as upgrades, downgrades, or cancellations. Key characteristics of store credits:<br>* No tax component is included at the time of creation.<br>* A credit note document is generated, similar to refundable credits.<br>* Store credits are applied before tax calculations on future invoices.<br><br>**Note:**<br>If you have enabled *consolidated invoicing*<br>, to know the subscriptions attached with a credit note you have to refer [line_item's](/docs/api/credit_notes/credit_note-object#line_items)<br>*subscription_id*<br>. The credit note's *subscription_id*<br>should **not**<br>be used (which will be *null*<br>if the credit note has lines from multiple subscriptions).  <br>Impact on reference invoice  <br>The following updates are made to the reference invoice when a credit note is created/imported:<br><br>* If the credit note `type` is `adjustment`:<br>  * The adjustment credit note details are added to the `adjustment_credit_notes[]` attribute of the invoice.<br>  * The invoice `amount_due` is reduced by the credit note `total`.<br>  * The invoice `status` is updated to `paid` if the invoice `amount_due` equals the credit note `total`.<br>  * The invoice `status` does not change if the invoice `amount_due` is greater than credit note `total`.<br>* If the credit note `type` is `refundable`:<br>  * The refundable credit note details are added to the `issued_credit_notes[]` attribute of the invoice.<br>  * The invoice `status` does not change.<br>* If the credit note `type` is `store`:<br>  * The store credit note details are added to the `issued_credit_notes[]` attribute of the invoice.<br>  * The invoice `status` does not change.<br>|

|» » subscription|body|[Subscription](#schemasubscription)|true|A Chargebee subscription connects a customer record to products/services. It describes what the customer has signed up for and how often they're charged for it. [Learn more](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/subscriptions#plan-based-billing).<br><br>* **Multi-frequency billing** : Subscriptions are billed according to the billing period of each recurring item price within the subscription. [Learn more](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/multi-frequency-billing).<br><br>  **Important**<br><br>  [Limitations](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/multi-frequency-billing#limitations) of Multi-frequency billing.<br><br>The selection of the billing frequency preference is configured at the site level.  <br><br>#### Item price compatibility in a subscription<br><br>When creating or updating a subscription, one of the item prices specified under subscription_items must be a plan-item price. ## Triggered when a usage file is ingested

<a id="opIdonUsage_file_ingestedWebhook"></a>

`POST usage_file_ingested`

> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-usage-file-is-ingested-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[UsageFileIngestedEvent](#schemausagefileingestedevent)|false|Payload for usage_file_ingested event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » usage_file|body|[UsageFile](#schemausagefile)|true|Represents a file containing usage events that has been uploaded for processing.<br><br>Upload usage events using files {#steps_to_upload_usages_file}<br>--------------------------------------------------------------<br><br><br>Follow these steps to upload usage event files:<br><br>**Step 1:** Request an [usage_file](/docs/api/usage_files/usage-file-object) object using the upload endpoint. This returns an [url](/docs/api/usage_files/usage_file-object#upload_details).<br><br>**Step 2:** Create a CSV file containing the usage event records. Ensure that the file meets the expected format and complies with the [file upload constraints](/docs/api/usage_files#file_upload_constraints). Only `text/csv` files are supported.<br><br>**Step 3:** Upload the CSV file using the returned [url](/docs/api/usage_files/usage_file-object#upload_details).<br><br>Make an HTTP `PUT` request to the upload URL. Include the file in the request body as binary data (raw file content).<br><br>**Step 4:** Check the uploaded [usage_file_status](/docs/api/usage_files/usage_file-object#status) using the [retrieve_file_processing_status](/docs/api/usage_files/get-uploaded-file-processing-status) endpoint.  <br>**Important**<br>:<br>[Learn more](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/ingesting-usage-from-amazon-s3) about ingesting usage events from Amazon S3.<br><br>### Best practices {#best_practices}<br><br>* We recommend not to create empty files which contain only header rows.<br>* We recommend uploading files in batches of **100,000** events per file or lesser to ensure optimal performance.<br>* We recommend ensuring that no row contains extra columns without corresponding headers.<br><br>### File upload constraints {#file_upload_constraints}<br><br>* File names should not contain any special characters except for underscores `_` and hyphens `-`.<br>* File names must be under **150** characters and include the appropriate extensions, such as `.csv`.<br>* The supported delimiter for CSV file format is **comma(,)**.<br><br>**See also**<br><br>* [Limits for Usage-based Billing in Chargebee](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/understanding-usages#usage-based-billing-limits)<br><br>### File field constraints {#file_field_constraints}<br><br>* Make sure your file follows the sample file format:<br><br>\|----------------------\|---------------------\|---------------------\|------------------\|-------------------\|<br>\| **deduplication_id** \| **subscription_id** \| **usage_timestamp** \| **input_tokens** \| **output_tokens** \|<br>\| 123e4567-e89b-12d3   \| Sub-01              \| 1741156511000       \| 100              \| 100               \|<br>\| 987f6543-b21c-34a5   \| Sub-02              \| 1741156511001       \| 859              \| 194               \|<br><br>* Learn more about [deduplication_id](/docs/api/usage_events/create-a-usage-event#deduplication_id), [subscription_id](/docs/api/usage_events/create-a-usage-event#subscription_id), and [usage_timestamp](/docs/api/usage_events/create-a-usage-event#usage_timestamp).<br><br>* Each row must include [deduplication_id](/docs/api/usage_events/create-a-usage-event#deduplication_id), [subscription_id](/docs/api/usage_events/create-a-usage-event#subscription_id), and [usage_timestamp](/docs/api/usage_events/create-a-usage-event#usage_timestamp). Rows missing any of these fields are flagged as failed events.<br><br>* Any top-level fields in the event row that are not a recognized field ([deduplication_id](/docs/api/usage_events/create-a-usage-event#deduplication_id), [subscription_id](/docs/api/usage_events/create-a-usage-event#subscription_id), and [usage_timestamp](/docs/api/usage_events/create-a-usage-event#usage_timestamp)) will automatically be added to the [properties](/docs/api/usage_events/create-a-usage-event#properties).<br><br>  **Field Naming Guidelines**: Ensure that your file's column headers follow the required naming rules to avoid processing issues:<br>  * **Start with:** a lowercase letter (`a-z`)<br>* **May include:**<br><br>  * Lowercase letters (`a-z`)<br>  * Numbers (`0-9`)<br>  * Underscores (`_`)<br><br>\|--------------------\|----------------------\|<br>\| **Valid Examples** \| **Invalid Examples** \|<br>\| `input_tokens`     \| `InputTokens`        \|<br>\| `output_tokens`    \| `Output Tokens`      \|<br>\| `feature_usage_1`  \| `123output`          \|<br>\| `output_value`     \| `output@value`       \|<br>\| `input_value`      \| `input-value`        \|<br><br>### Validating and handling errors {#validating_and_handling_errors}<br><br>When uploading a usage events file using the API, certain validation checks are performed. If issues are detected, the upload or processing may fail. The following sections explain the possible error scenarios and how they are handled.  <br><br>\|       Error Code        \|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        \|<br>\|-------------------------\|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\|<br>\| `INVALID_FILE`          \| This error occurs in the following scenarios: * The file is not in a supported [MIME type](/docs/api/usage_files/get-usages-file-upload-url#mime_type), so the upload [URL](/docs/api/usage_files/usage_file-object#upload_details) is not generated. * The file contains invalid or corrupt content that prevents successful parsing. **Error Message:** "The file format, size, or content is invalid. Please ensure the file is in the correct format and adheres to the size limits." \|<br>\| `DUPLICATE_COLUMNS`     \| This error occurs when the file contains duplicate column headers, which must be unique. **Error Message:** "Duplicate columns found: \[list of duplicates\]. Please remove duplicates from your file before uploading again."                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            \|<br>\| `RECORD_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` \| This error occurs when the number of records in the uploaded file exceeds the system-defined limit. The `[limit]` placeholder specifies the maximum allowed records. **Error Message:** "The number of records exceeds the allowed limit of \[limit\]. Please reduce the number of records in the file and try uploading again."                                                                                                                                                          \|<br>\| `PARTIAL_FAILURE`       \| This error indicates that some records in the file failed to process, while others were processed successfully. Review the failed records in the UI or failed queue for more details. **Error Message:** "Some records in the file could not be processed successfully. Please check the failed records in the \[UI/Failed Queue\] for more details."                                                                                                                                     \|<br>\| `COMPLETE_FAILURE`      \| This error indicates that all records in the uploaded file failed to process. Review the file, fix the issues, and try uploading it again. **Error Message:** "All records in the file failed to process. Please check the failed records in the \[UI/Failed Queue\] for more details."                                                                                                                                                                                                   \|<br>\| `INVALID_COLUMNS`       \| This error indicates that the file contains invalid column headers. **Error Message:** "Invalid columns found: \[list of invalid headers\]. Please correct column names in your file before uploading again."                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             \|<br><br>**Note** :<br>Usage events flagged as failed appear in the **Usages** \> [**Failed Events**](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/ingesting-usage-events-into-chargebee#failed_events)<br>section of the **Admin UI Dashboard**.<br>|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Webhook received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication

|» » omnichannel_subscription|body|[OmnichannelSubscription](#schemaomnichannelsubscription)|true|Represents a subscription purchased and managed in an external app marketplace (`apple_app_store` or `google_play_store`), normalized into Chargebee's omnichannel model.<br><br>Omnichannel subscriptions are typically created when you [record a purchase](/docs/api/recorded_purchases/record-a-purchase) and are kept in sync via store server notifications. They are store-managed: lifecycle changes come from Apple or Google, not from the Chargebee Subscriptions API.<br><br>Use [omnichannel statuses](/docs/api/omnichannel_statuses) for how store statuses map to `omnichannel_subscription_item.status`, and [omnichannel events](/docs/api/omnichannel_events) for notification-to-webhook mappings.<br><br>Chargebee records introductory and promotional offers on [`omnichannel_subscription_item_offers`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscriptions/omnichannel_subscription-object#omnichannel_subscription_items_omnichannel_subscription_item_offers). Win-back offers and offer codes are not supported.  <br>**Identifier tip:** Parent `id_at_source` is the Apple **Transaction ID** or Google **purchase token** . Nested `initial_purchase_transaction.id_at_source` is the Apple **Transaction ID** or Google **Order ID** (`GPA....`). See attribute descriptions below.  <br>**Note:**<br>This resource represents in-app subscriptions made on Apple App Store and Google Play Store.<br>|

The customer resource associates with [subscriptions](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object), [card information](/docs/api/cards/card-object), and billing addresses. The customer details include their ID, name, contact information, and any [custom attributes](/docs/api/advanced-features) you'd like to associate with them.  <br>**Breaking Change**:<br><br>* [**Sites**](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/sites-intro.html) **created before March 1, 2014** : [updating the card](/docs/api/cards/update-card-for-a-customer) deletes the customer's `billing_address` and `vat_number` and replaces them with values from the request.<br>* **Sites created on or after March 1, 2014** : updating the card doesn't change the `billing_address` and `vat_number`.<br>|

|» » differential_price|body|[DifferentialPrice](#schemadifferentialprice)|true|Differential pricing helps implement a pricing strategy for addons and charges based on the plans they're purchased with. A differential price a specific price for an addon- or charge-[item price](/docs/api/item_prices) when purchased along with a particular plan.<br><br>Differential pricing for addons<br>-------------------------------<br><br>Consider an addon called 24x7 Customer Support provided with a cloud storage service. You can configure differential prices for each of the addon-item prices based on the plan they are purchased with, as follows:  <br><br>\|---\|-----------------------------------------------------\|-----------------------------------------------\|-----------------------------------------------------\|<br>\|   \| **Addon item price**                                \| **Price when applied to *Standard*** **Plan** \| **Price when applied to** ***Enterprise*** **Plan** \|<br>\| 1 \| 24x7 Customer Support, USD, Monthly, Flat fee, $100 \| $90                                           \| $150                                                \|<br>\| 2 \| 24x7 Customer Support, USD, Yearly, Flat fee, $1000 \| $900                                          \| $1500                                               \|<br><br>Differential pricing for charges<br>--------------------------------<br><br>Consider a charge, called Setup fee, for installing and configuring a cloud-based project management platform. There are two modes in which you can set up differential pricing for a charge:<br><br>#### Mode A: One charge differential price per plan-item<br><br>This mode is used to specify one differential price for the charge-item price per [plan-item](/docs/api/items) it is applied to.  <br><br>\|-------------------------------\|---------------------------------------------------\|-----------------------------------------------------\|<br>\| **Charge-item price**         \| **Price when applied to** ***Standard*** **plan** \| **Price when applied to** ***Enterprise*** **plan** \|<br>\| Setup fee, USD, Flat fee $500 \| $400                                              \| $700                                                \|<br><br>#### Mode B: Multiple charge differential prices per plan item<br><br>This mode is used to specify multiple differential prices for the charge per plan-item, based on the plan period.  <br><br>\|-------------------------------\|-------------------------------------------------------------\|-----------------------------------------------------------\|<br>\| **Charge-item price**         \| **Price when applied to** ***Standard*** **plan, 6 months** \| **Price when applied to** ***Standard*** **plan, yearly** \|<br>\| Setup fee, USD, Flat fee $500 \| $400                                                        \| $300                                                      \|<br><br>In the above example, even if the "6 month" or "yearly" plan-item prices do not exist, the differential prices for the charge can still be created. They take effect whenever the plan-item prices are eventually created and used in subscriptions.<br>|

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Webhook received successfully|None|

|» » transaction|body|[Transaction](#schematransaction)|true|This resource represents the [transaction](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/transactions.html)<br>event that has happened in your account.<br>|
|» » invoice|body|[Invoice](#schemainvoice)|true|An invoice is a commercial document representing a sale of products/services offered by you to a customer. It enumerates all the charges, adjustments, payments, discounts and taxes associated with the sale.<br><br>An invoice is said to be a recurring one when it is has at least one charge for [a plan or an addon item price](/docs/api/items). It is a non-recurring one when it has charges for only charge-item prices or [one-time charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/charges.html).<br><br>The item prices for any given billing term of a subscription are billed via an invoice at the beginning of the term (unless the charges are left unbilled). However, item prices that belong to `metered` items are billed at the end of the term via a `pending` invoice that can [close automatically](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing#configuring-metered-billing) or via [an API call](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice). Moreover, when there are no `metered` items in the subscription, the invoices can still be generated as `pending` while [creating](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items) or [updating](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items) a subscription.<br><br>#### Auto-collection<br><br>If [auto-collection](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#auto-collection-status) is enabled, then immediately on invoice generation (or, in case of subscriptions that have `create_pending_invoices` as `true`, on [invoice closure](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice)), the [payment method](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#payment_method) on file is charged:<br><br>* If the payment succeeds, the invoice is marked as `paid`.<br>* On payment failure, the invoice is marked as `payment_due` and [dunning settings](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/dunning-v2.html) are taken into account for payment retries.<br>* If no retry attempts are configured, or when retries are exhausted, the invoice is marked as `not_paid`.<br>* the amount due is zero or negative, the invoice is immediately marked as `paid` and the balance, if any, is added to [excess payments](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#excess-payments) for the customer.<br><br>**Note:** If [consolidated invoicing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html) is enabled, the attribute `subscription_id` is unavailable when the invoice has line items from multiple subscriptions. The individual subscription ids are seen under `line_items.subscription_id`.  <br><br>#### Recurring and non-recurring invoices<br><br>A recurring invoice contains at least one line item that is billed on a recurring basis. Specifically, it has at least one [`line_items[]`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#line_items) with `entity_type` set to `plan_item_price` or `addon_item_price`. A non-recurring invoice contains no recurring line items.  <br><br>#### Refundable amount for an invoice<br><br>The refundable amount for an invoice is the (amount paid on the invoice + refundable credit applied on the invoice + taxes withheld on the invoice) minus (amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice). Each of these amounts is obtained from the invoice resource as follows:<br><br>* Amount paid on the invoice: [`amount_paid`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_amount_paid)<br>* Refundable credit applied on the invoice: [`credits_applied`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_credits_applied)<br>* Taxes withheld on the invoice: Sum of [`linked_taxes_withheld[].amount`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_linked_taxes_withheld)<br>* Amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice: Sum of [`issued_credit_notes[i].cn_total`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_issued_credit_notes) where `issued_credit_notes[i].cn_status` is `refunded` or `refund_due`.<br>|
|» » customer|body|[Customer](#schemacustomer)|true|Represents a customer, which can be an individual or organization that subscribes to your products or services. The customer resource associates with [subscriptions](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object), [card information](/docs/api/cards/card-object), and billing addresses. The customer details include their ID, name, contact information, and any [custom attributes](/docs/api/advanced-features) you'd like to associate with them.  <br>**Breaking Change**:<br><br>* [**Sites**](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/sites-intro.html) **created before March 1, 2014** : [updating the card](/docs/api/cards/update-card-for-a-customer) deletes the customer's `billing_address` and `vat_number` and replaces them with values from the request.<br>* **Sites created on or after March 1, 2014** : updating the card doesn't change the `billing_address` and `vat_number`.<br>|
|» » subscription|body|[Subscription](#schemasubscription)|true|A Chargebee subscription connects a customer record to products/services. It describes what the customer has signed up for and how often they're charged for it. The essential components of a subscription are:<br><br>* A [plan-item price](/docs/api/item_prices).<br>* Any addon- and charge-item prices applied to the subscription.<br>* Any [coupons](/docs/api/coupons) applied.<br>* Any [discounts](/docs/api/discounts) applied.<br><br>The charges in a subscription are billed via invoices.  <br>**Note:**<br>The maximum number of subscriptions for any given [customer](/docs/api/customers)<br>([active](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object#status)<br>or not) is 900.  <br><br>#### Subscription billing frequencies<br><br>Chargebee offers two billing frequency options for subscriptions:<br><br>* **Plan-based billing** (`default`): Subscriptions are billed based on the billing period defined for the item price of the `item_type` `plan`. [Learn more](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/subscriptions#plan-based-billing).<br><br>* **Multi-frequency billing** : Subscriptions are billed according to the billing period of each recurring item price within the subscription. [Learn more](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/multi-frequency-billing).<br><br>  **Important**<br><br>  [Limitations](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/multi-frequency-billing#limitations) of Multi-frequency billing.<br><br>The selection of the billing frequency preference is configured at the site level.  <br><br>#### Item price compatibility in a subscription<br><br>When creating or updating a subscription, one of the item prices specified under subscription_items must be a plan-item price. |» » invoice|body|[Invoice](#schemainvoice)|true|An invoice is a commercial document representing a sale of products/services offered by you to a customer. It enumerates all the charges, adjustments, payments, discounts and taxes associated with the sale.<br><br>An invoice is said to be a recurring one when it is has at least one charge for [a plan or an addon item price](/docs/api/items). It is a non-recurring one when it has charges for only charge-item prices or [one-time charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/charges.html).<br><br>The item prices for any given billing term of a subscription are billed via an invoice at the beginning of the term (unless the charges are left unbilled). However, item prices that belong to `metered` items are billed at the end of the term via a `pending` invoice that can [close automatically](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing#configuring-metered-billing) or via [an API call](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice). Moreover, when there are no `metered` items in the subscription, the invoices can still be generated as `pending` while [creating](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items) or [updating](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items) a subscription.<br><br>#### Auto-collection<br><br>If [auto-collection](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#auto-collection-status) is enabled, then immediately on invoice generation (or, in case of subscriptions that have `create_pending_invoices` as `true`, on [invoice closure](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice)), the [payment method](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#payment_method) on file is charged:<br><br>* If the payment succeeds, the invoice is marked as `paid`.<br>* On payment failure, the invoice is marked as `payment_due` and [dunning settings](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/dunning-v2.html) are taken into account for payment retries.<br>* If no retry attempts are configured, or when retries are exhausted, the invoice is marked as `not_paid`.<br>* the amount due is zero or negative, the invoice is immediately marked as `paid` and the balance, if any, is added to [excess payments](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#excess-payments) for the customer.<br><br>**Note:** If [consolidated invoicing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html) is enabled, the attribute `subscription_id` is unavailable when the invoice has line items from multiple subscriptions. The individual subscription ids are seen under `line_items.subscription_id`.  <br><br>#### Recurring and non-recurring invoices<br><br>A recurring invoice contains at least one line item that is billed on a recurring basis. Specifically, it has at least one [`line_items[]`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#line_items) with `entity_type` set to `plan_item_price` or `addon_item_price`. A non-recurring invoice contains no recurring line items.  <br><br>#### Refundable amount for an invoice<br><br>The refundable amount for an invoice is the (amount paid on the invoice + refundable credit applied on the invoice + taxes withheld on the invoice) minus (amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice). Each of these amounts is obtained from the invoice resource as follows:<br><br>* Amount paid on the invoice: [`amount_paid`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_amount_paid)<br>* Refundable credit applied on the invoice: [`credits_applied`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_credits_applied)<br>* Taxes withheld on the invoice: Sum of [`linked_taxes_withheld[].amount`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_linked_taxes_withheld)<br>* Amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice: Sum of [`issued_credit_notes[i].cn_total`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_issued_credit_notes) where `issued_credit_notes[i].cn_status` is `refunded` or `refund_due`.<br>|

## Triggered when an attached item is created.

<a id="opIdonAttached_item_createdWebhook"></a>

`POST attached_item_created`

Triggered when an attached item is created.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-an-attached-item-is-created-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AttachedItemCreatedEvent](#schemaattacheditemcreatedevent)|false|Payload for attached_item_created event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » attached_item|body|[AttachedItem](#schemaattacheditem)|true|Addon-item and charge-item prices are purchased with plan-item prices in subscriptions. You can automate this process by configuring certain addons and charges as "attached" to certain plans. This is done at the "item" level. In other words, addon- and charge-items can be attached to plan-items.<br><br>Once the attachment is defined, while creating or updating a subscription, the addon- or charge-item prices are selected automatically based on the plan-item price selected . Let's look at the details:<br><br>### Addons<br><br>Addons can be attached to plans as `recommended`, `mandatory` or `optional`.<br><br>* When an addon is attached as `recommended` for a plan, the addon is suggested to be applied to subscriptions for the plan in [Checkout](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/configure-inapp.html#fundamental-settings_recommending-addons-in-checkout) and [Self-Serve Portal](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/inapp-self-serve-portal.html#allow-change-subscription). Alternatively, if you build your own payment pages or have a sales team, you can suggest recommended addons to your customers or salespeople on your website or CRM respectively<br>* When an addon is attached as `mandatory` for a plan, the addon gets applied to subscriptions for the plan compulsorily, unless [removed explicitly](/docs/api/subscriptions). If you do not pass an item price for a mandatory addon when including the plan in a subscription, an addon-item price is automatically applied as explained below.<br>* Attaching an addon as `optional` neither marks it as recommended or mandatory but allows you a way to set a `quantity` and `billing_cycles` for the addon, for when it is applied to subscriptions with the plan.<br><br>How auto-selection of the addon-item price works<br>------------------------------------------------<br><br>Once an addon has been attached as mandatory, the addon-item price to be applied to the plan-item price is selected based on the following rule: The addon-item price with the same currency as that of the plan-item price and the longest compatible period is selected.<br><br>Here's an example:<br><br>Consider a plan **Standard Cloud Storage** has an addon **Extra Storage** attached to it. Note that each of the two are items. Now consider that they have item prices with the following periods and currencies:<br><br>**Item price for "Standard Cloud Storage" plan-item:**<br><br>* Standard Cloud Storage, 3 years, AUD.<br><br>**Item prices for "Extra Storage" addon-item:**<br><br>* Extra Storage, 1 year, EUR.<br>* Extra Storage, 1 year, USD.<br>* Extra Storage, 1 year, AUD.<br>* Extra Storage, 18 months, AUD.<br>* Extra Storage, 2 years, AUD.<br>* Extra Storage, 30 months, AUD.<br><br>For the plan-item price (Standard Cloud Storage, 3 years, AUD), the addon-item prices with matching currencies are the last 4 from the above list:<br><br>* Extra Storage, 1 year, AUD.<br>* Extra Storage, 18 months, AUD.<br>* Extra Storage, 2 years, AUD.<br>* Extra Storage, 30 months, AUD.<br><br>From among them, the last two have periods that are incompatible with the plan-item price period of 3 years. From the remaining 2 addon-item prices, the one with the longest period is of 18 months. So, "Extra Storage, 18 months, AUD" is selected for mandatory application to the plan item price.<br><br>### Charges<br><br>Charges can also be attached to plans. When doing so, you specify [the event](/docs/api/attached_items/attached_item-object#charge_on_event) at which the charge is to be applied to the subscription. For some events that can occur multiple times in a subscription lifetime, you can also set whether to apply the charge each time the event occurs or just once.<br><br>There may be multiple item prices for a given attached charge. The item price that matches the currency of the plan-item price is automatically selected for application.<br><br>Here's an example:<br><br>Consider a plan **Standard Cloud Storage** has a charge named **Implementation Fee** attached to it. Now consider their item prices below, with the following periods and currencies:<br><br>**Item price for "Standard Cloud Storage" plan-item:**<br><br>* Standard Cloud Storage, 3 years, AUD.<br><br>**Item prices for "Implementation Fee" charge-item:**<br><br>* Implementation Fee, USD.<br>* Implementation Fee, AUD.<br>* Implementation Fee, EUR.<br><br>From among the charge-item prices above, the one compatible with the plan-item price is "Implementation Fee, AUD" since it has the same currency as the plan-item price.<br>|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Webhook received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

|» » invoice|body|[Invoice](#schemainvoice)|true|An invoice is a commercial document representing a sale of products/services offered by you to a customer. It enumerates all the charges, adjustments, payments, discounts and taxes associated with the sale.<br><br>An invoice is said to be a recurring one when it is has at least one charge for [a plan or an addon item price](/docs/api/items). It is a non-recurring one when it has charges for only charge-item prices or [one-time charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/charges.html).<br><br>The item prices for any given billing term of a subscription are billed via an invoice at the beginning of the term (unless the charges are left unbilled). However, item prices that belong to `metered` items are billed at the end of the term via a `pending` invoice that can [close automatically](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing#configuring-metered-billing) or via [an API call](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice). Moreover, when there are no `metered` items in the subscription, the invoices can still be generated as `pending` while [creating](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items) or [updating](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items) a subscription.<br><br>#### Auto-collection<br><br>If [auto-collection](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#auto-collection-status) is enabled, then immediately on invoice generation (or, in case of subscriptions that have `create_pending_invoices` as `true`, on [invoice closure](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice)), the [payment method](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#payment_method) on file is charged:<br><br>* If the payment succeeds, the invoice is marked as `paid`.<br>* On payment failure, the invoice is marked as `payment_due` and [dunning settings](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/dunning-v2.html) are taken into account for payment retries.<br>* If no retry attempts are configured, or when retries are exhausted, the invoice is marked as `not_paid`.<br>* the amount due is zero or negative, the invoice is immediately marked as `paid` and the balance, if any, is added to [excess payments](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#excess-payments) for the customer.<br><br>**Note:** If [consolidated invoicing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html) is enabled, the attribute `subscription_id` is unavailable when the invoice has line items from multiple subscriptions. The individual subscription ids are seen under `line_items.subscription_id`.  <br><br>#### Recurring and non-recurring invoices<br><br>A recurring invoice contains at least one line item that is billed on a recurring basis. Specifically, it has at least one [`line_items[]`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#line_items) with `entity_type` set to `plan_item_price` or `addon_item_price`. A non-recurring invoice contains no recurring line items.  <br><br>#### Refundable amount for an invoice<br><br>The refundable amount for an invoice is the (amount paid on the invoice + refundable credit applied on the invoice + taxes withheld on the invoice) minus (amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice). Each of these amounts is obtained from the invoice resource as follows:<br><br>* Amount paid on the invoice: [`amount_paid`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_amount_paid)<br>* Refundable credit applied on the invoice: [`credits_applied`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_credits_applied)<br>* Taxes withheld on the invoice: Sum of [`linked_taxes_withheld[].amount`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_linked_taxes_withheld)<br>* Amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice: Sum of [`issued_credit_notes[i].cn_total`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_issued_credit_notes) where `issued_credit_notes[i].cn_status` is `refunded` or `refund_due`.<br>|

## Triggered after the subscription has been moved from &quot;Trial&quot; to &quot;Active&quot; state.

<a id="opIdonSubscription_activatedWebhook"></a>

`POST subscription_activated`

Triggered after the subscription has been moved from "Trial" to "Active" state.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

gateway](/docs/api/cards/switch-gateway)                             \| [Switch gateway account](/docs/api/payment_sources/switch-gateway-account)                                                                                                                                                                                                         \|<br>\| [Copy card](/docs/api/cards/copy-card)                                       \| [Export payment source](/docs/api/payment_sources/export-payment-source)                                                                                                                                                                                                           \|<br>\| [Delete card for a customer](/docs/api/cards/delete-card-for-a-customer)     \| [Delete a payment source](/docs/api/payment_sources/delete-a-payment-source)                                                                                                                                                                                                       \|<br><br>|
|» » invoice|body|[Invoice](#schemainvoice)|true|An invoice is a commercial document representing a sale of products/services offered by you to a customer. It enumerates all the charges, adjustments, payments, discounts and taxes associated with the sale.<br><br>An invoice is said to be a recurring one when it is has at least one charge for [a plan or an addon item price](/docs/api/items). It is a non-recurring one when it has charges for only charge-item prices or [one-time charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/charges.html).<br><br>The item prices for any given billing term of a subscription are billed via an invoice at the beginning of the term (unless the charges are left unbilled). However, item prices that belong to `metered` items are billed at the end of the term via a `pending` invoice that can [close automatically](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing#configuring-metered-billing) or via [an API call](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice). Moreover, when there are no `metered` items in the subscription, the invoices can still be generated as `pending` while [creating](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items) or [updating](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items) a subscription.<br><br>#### Auto-collection<br><br>If [auto-collection](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#auto-collection-status) is enabled, then immediately on invoice generation (or, in case of subscriptions that have `create_pending_invoices` as `true`, on [invoice closure](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice)), the [payment method](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#payment_method) on file is charged:<br><br>* If the payment succeeds, the invoice is marked as `paid`.<br>* On payment failure, the invoice is marked as `payment_due` and [dunning settings](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/dunning-v2.html) are taken into account for payment retries.<br>* If no retry attempts are configured, or when retries are exhausted, the invoice is marked as `not_paid`.<br>* the amount due is zero or negative, the invoice is immediately marked as `paid` and the balance, if any, is added to [excess payments](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#excess-payments) for the customer.<br><br>**Note:** If [consolidated invoicing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html) is enabled, the attribute `subscription_id` is unavailable when the invoice has line items from multiple subscriptions. The individual subscription ids are seen under `line_items.subscription_id`.  <br><br>#### Recurring and non-recurring invoices<br><br>A recurring invoice contains at least one line item that is billed on a recurring basis. Specifically, it has at least one [`line_items[]`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#line_items) with `entity_type` set to `plan_item_price` or `addon_item_price`. A non-recurring invoice contains no recurring line items.  <br><br>#### Refundable amount for an invoice<br><br>The refundable amount for an invoice is the (amount paid on the invoice + refundable credit applied on the invoice + taxes withheld on the invoice) minus (amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice). Each of these amounts is obtained from the invoice resource as follows:<br><br>* Amount paid on the invoice: [`amount_paid`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_amount_paid)<br>* Refundable credit applied on the invoice: [`credits_applied`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_credits_applied)<br>* Taxes withheld on the invoice: Sum of [`linked_taxes_withheld[].amount`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_linked_taxes_withheld)<br>* Amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice: Sum of [`issued_credit_notes[i].cn_total`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_issued_credit_notes) where `issued_credit_notes[i].cn_status` is `refunded` or `refund_due`.<br>|

It is a non-recurring one when it has charges for only charge-item prices or [one-time charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/charges.html).<br><br>The item prices for any given billing term of a subscription are billed via an invoice at the beginning of the term (unless the charges are left unbilled). However, item prices that belong to `metered` items are billed at the end of the term via a `pending` invoice that can [close automatically](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing#configuring-metered-billing) or via [an API call](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice). Moreover, when there are no `metered` items in the subscription, the invoices can still be generated as `pending` while [creating](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items) or [updating](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items) a subscription.<br><br>#### Auto-collection<br><br>If [auto-collection](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#auto-collection-status) is enabled, then immediately on invoice generation (or, in case of subscriptions that have `create_pending_invoices` as `true`, on [invoice closure](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice)), the [payment method](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#payment_method) on file is charged:<br><br>* If the payment succeeds, the invoice is marked as `paid`.<br>* On payment failure, the invoice is marked as `payment_due` and [dunning settings](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/dunning-v2.html) are taken into account for payment retries.<br>* If no retry attempts are configured, or when retries are exhausted, the invoice is marked as `not_paid`.<br>* the amount due is zero or negative, the invoice is immediately marked as `paid` and the balance, if any, is added to [excess payments](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#excess-payments) for the customer.<br><br>**Note:** If [consolidated invoicing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html) is enabled, the attribute `subscription_id` is unavailable when the invoice has line items from multiple subscriptions. The individual subscription ids are seen under `line_items.subscription_id`.  <br><br>#### Recurring and non-recurring invoices<br><br>A recurring invoice contains at least one line item that is billed on a recurring basis. Specifically, it has at least one [`line_items[]`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#line_items) with `entity_type` set to `plan_item_price` or `addon_item_price`. A non-recurring invoice contains no recurring line items.  <br><br>#### Refundable amount for an invoice<br><br>The refundable amount for an invoice is the (amount paid on the invoice + refundable credit applied on the invoice + taxes withheld on the invoice) minus (amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice). Each of these amounts is obtained from the invoice resource as follows:<br><br>* Amount paid on the invoice: [`amount_paid`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_amount_paid)<br>* Refundable credit applied on the invoice: [`credits_applied`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_credits_applied)<br>* Taxes withheld on the invoice: Sum of [`linked_taxes_withheld[].amount`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_linked_taxes_withheld)<br>* Amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice: Sum of [`issued_credit_notes[i].cn_total`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_issued_credit_notes) where `issued_credit_notes[i].cn_status` is `refunded` or `refund_due`.<br>|
|» » unbilled_charges|body|[[UnbilledCharge](#schemaunbilledcharge)]|true|none|

|» » advance_invoice_schedule|body|[AdvanceInvoiceSchedule](#schemaadvanceinvoiceschedule)|true|The invoice for a subscription in Chargebee is generated at the time of subscription renewal. Invoices can also be [generated in advance](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/advance-invoices.html) for an upcoming renewal or set of renewals. With Advance Invoicing Schedules, you can set up a plan for when such advance invoices are generated for the lifetime of the subscription. This helps you:<br><br>* Set up a contract with your customers so that they can be notified of their payment schedules in advance.<br>* Allow customers who make offline payments to be alerted about their upcoming dues well ahead of actual subscription renewals.<br>* Prevent post-renewal unpaid usage of your services by customers.<br><br>Advance invoices can be scheduled in two ways:<br><br>#### Specific Dates Schedule<br><br>Advance invoices for a subscription can be scheduled to be generated on specific [dates](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#specific_dates_schedule_date) in the future. You must specify the [number of billing cycles](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#specific_dates_schedule_terms_to_charge) to be invoiced on each date. A maximum of 5 dates can be specified.<br><br>#### Fixed Interval Schedule<br><br>Advance invoices can be scheduled to be generated at fixed intervals of time, where each interval spans the same number of billing cycles of the subscription. The invoice for each interval is generated a specified number of days ([`days_before_interval`](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#fixed_interval_schedule_days_before_renewal)) before the start of the interval. You can configure the schedule to end on a certain date or after a specified number of advance invoices have been generated.<br><br>The start date of the first interval depends on the number of days remaining from current time till the next renewal of the subscription. If this is more than `days_before_interval`, the interval begins at the next renewal. On the other hand, if the number of days remaining before the next renewal is less than `days_before_interval`, the first interval begins at the renewal following the next.<br>|

The customer details include their ID, name, contact information, and any [custom attributes](/docs/api/advanced-features) you'd like to associate with them.  <br>**Breaking Change**:<br><br>* [**Sites**](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/sites-intro.html) **created before March 1, 2014** : [updating the card](/docs/api/cards/update-card-for-a-customer) deletes the customer's `billing_address` and `vat_number` and replaces them with values from the request.<br>* **Sites created on or after March 1, 2014** : updating the card doesn't change the `billing_address` and `vat_number`.<br>|

|» » advance_invoice_schedule|body|[AdvanceInvoiceSchedule](#schemaadvanceinvoiceschedule)|true|The invoice for a subscription in Chargebee is generated at the time of subscription renewal. Invoices can also be [generated in advance](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/advance-invoices.html) for an upcoming renewal or set of renewals. With Advance Invoicing Schedules, you can set up a plan for when such advance invoices are generated for the lifetime of the subscription. This helps you:<br><br>* Set up a contract with your customers so that they can be notified of their payment schedules in advance.<br>* Allow customers who make offline payments to be alerted about their upcoming dues well ahead of actual subscription renewals.<br>* Prevent post-renewal unpaid usage of your services by customers.<br><br>Advance invoices can be scheduled in two ways:<br><br>#### Specific Dates Schedule<br><br>Advance invoices for a subscription can be scheduled to be generated on specific [dates](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#specific_dates_schedule_date) in the future. You must specify the [number of billing cycles](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#specific_dates_schedule_terms_to_charge) to be invoiced on each date. A maximum of 5 dates can be specified.<br><br>#### Fixed Interval Schedule<br><br>Advance invoices can be scheduled to be generated at fixed intervals of time, where each interval spans the same number of billing cycles of the subscription. The invoice for each interval is generated a specified number of days ([`days_before_interval`](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#fixed_interval_schedule_days_before_renewal)) before the start of the interval. You can configure the schedule to end on a certain date or after a specified number of advance invoices have been generated.<br><br>The start date of the first interval depends on the number of days remaining from current time till the next renewal of the subscription. If this is more than `days_before_interval`, the interval begins at the next renewal. On the other hand, if the number of days remaining before the next renewal is less than `days_before_interval`, the first interval begins at the renewal following the next.<br>|

<h3 id="triggered-6-days-prior-to-the-scheduled-cancellation-date-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Webhook received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

|» » invoice|body|[Invoice](#schemainvoice)|true|An invoice is a commercial document representing a sale of products/services offered by you to a customer. It enumerates all the charges, adjustments, payments, discounts and taxes associated with the sale.<br><br>An invoice is said to be a recurring one when it is has at least one charge for [a plan or an addon item price](/docs/api/items). It is a non-recurring one when it has charges for only charge-item prices or [one-time charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/charges.html).<br><br>The item prices for any given billing term of a subscription are billed via an invoice at the beginning of the term (unless the charges are left unbilled). However, item prices that belong to `metered` items are billed at the end of the term via a `pending` invoice that can [close automatically](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing#configuring-metered-billing) or via [an API call](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice). Moreover, when there are no `metered` items in the subscription, the invoices can still be generated as `pending` while [creating](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items) or [updating](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items) a subscription.<br><br>#### Auto-collection<br><br>If [auto-collection](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#auto-collection-status) is enabled, then immediately on invoice generation (or, in case of subscriptions that have `create_pending_invoices` as `true`, on [invoice closure](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice)), the [payment method](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#payment_method) on file is charged:<br><br>* If the payment succeeds, the invoice is marked as `paid`.<br>* On payment failure, the invoice is marked as `payment_due` and [dunning settings](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/dunning-v2.html) are taken into account for payment retries.<br>* If no retry attempts are configured, or when retries are exhausted, the invoice is marked as `not_paid`.<br>* the amount due is zero or negative, the invoice is immediately marked as `paid` and the balance, if any, is added to [excess payments](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#excess-payments) for the customer.<br><br>**Note:** If [consolidated invoicing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html) is enabled, the attribute `subscription_id` is unavailable when the invoice has line items from multiple subscriptions. The individual subscription ids are seen under `line_items.subscription_id`.  <br><br>#### Recurring and non-recurring invoices<br><br>A recurring invoice contains at least one line item that is billed on a recurring basis. Specifically, it has at least one [`line_items[]`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#line_items) with `entity_type` set to `plan_item_price` or `addon_item_price`. A non-recurring invoice contains no recurring line items.  <br><br>#### Refundable amount for an invoice<br><br>The refundable amount for an invoice is the (amount paid on the invoice + refundable credit applied on the invoice + taxes withheld on the invoice) minus (amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice). Each of these amounts is obtained from the invoice resource as follows:<br><br>* Amount paid on the invoice: [`amount_paid`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_amount_paid)<br>* Refundable credit applied on the invoice: [`credits_applied`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_credits_applied)<br>* Taxes withheld on the invoice: Sum of [`linked_taxes_withheld[].amount`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_linked_taxes_withheld)<br>* Amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice: Sum of [`issued_credit_notes[i].cn_total`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_issued_credit_notes) where `issued_credit_notes[i].cn_status` is `refunded` or `refund_due`.<br>|

Triggered when a ramp is created.

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-ramp-is-created-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[SubscriptionRampCreatedEvent](#schemasubscriptionrampcreatedevent)|false|Payload for subscription_ramp_created event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|

|» » ramp|body|[Ramp](#schemaramp)|true|A `ramp` resource, or subscription ramp, represents a planned change to a [`subscription`](/docs/api/subscriptions) that occurs at a future date. Use this resource to define and schedule subscription modifications, such as updating pricing, altering quantity, or transitioning to a different plan, without immediately applying them.  <br>**Note**<br><br>* **Upcoming ramps limit** : A subscription can have a maximum of 12 upcoming ramps at any given time, excluding deleted ramps. Upcoming ramps are ramps with `status` as [`scheduled`](/docs/api/ramps/ramp-object#status).<br>* **Total ramps limit**: A subscription can have a maximum of 100 ramps at any given time, excluding deleted ramps.  <br><br>#### Auto-draft conditions<br><br>When you create or update a ramp, Chargebee automatically moves any existing ramps scheduled after that ramp to `draft` status if either of the following conditions is met:<br><br>* The new or updated ramp changes the subscription [term end date](subscriptions#subscription_current_term_end).<br>* The new or updated ramp changes the subscription billing frequency. That is, either of the following [attributes](subscriptions#subscription_items) is changed:<br>  * `subscription_items[i].billing_period`<br>  * `subscription_items[i].billing_period_unit`<br>  * where `i` is the index where `subscription_items[i].item_type` is `plan`.<br>* The new or updated ramp introduces an [addon](item_prices#item_price_item_type) that is not [applicable](attached_items) to the plan in one or more of the subsequent ramps.<br>|

## Triggered when a gift is updated.

<a id="opIdonGift_updatedWebhook"></a>

`POST gift_updated`

Triggered when a gift is updated.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-gift-is-updated-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[GiftUpdatedEvent](#schemagiftupdatedevent)|false|Payload for gift_updated event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|

|» » gift|body|[Gift](#schemagift)|true|Gift represents a subscription of a customer(**recipient** ) to a 'gift plan' which has been gifted by another customer(**gifter**). It may also have addons and coupons. Gift will be created only on immediate successful payment collection from the gifter's payment method.<br><br>Gift is initially created in '**scheduled** ' state. The gift can be scheduled to be notified on a particular date to the recipient by passing 'scheduled_at'. If not, the recipient is notified immediately. Gift will be moved to '**unclaimed** ' state on the date of notification. If you pass auto_claim as true, gift status will be moved to '**claimed**' immediately, otherwise, the gift will remain 'unclaimed' till the recipient claims the gift.<br><br>If the gift is not claimed before the claim_expiry_date, it will be moved to the '**expired**' state.<br><br>#### GIFT SUBSCRIPTION<br><br>Gift subscriptions will be created in '**future** ' state. Once the gift is claimed, the subscription will be moved to '**non-renewing**' state.<br><br>#### INVOICE<br><br>Gift subscriptions will be invoiced immediately. The invoice created has **is_gifted** as 'true' and **term_finalized** as 'false'. This is because initially the invoice term_start and term_end are set as the subscription's start_date till the end of the plan period. Once the gift is claimed, the invoice's term_finalized will be marked as 'true'. The term_start will be changed to the actual invoice's term, which is the gift-claim date and the term_end will be changed till plan's period.<br>|

## Trial Extension

<a id="opIdonSubscription_trial_extendedWebhook"></a>

> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="trial-extension-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|body|body|[SubscriptionTrialExtendedEvent](#schemasubscriptiontrialextendedevent)|false|Payload for subscription_trial_extended event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|

|» » subscription|body|[Subscription](#schemasubscription)|true|A Chargebee subscription connects a customer record to products/services. It describes what the customer has signed up for and how often they're charged for it. The essential components of a subscription are:<br><br>* A [plan-item price](/docs/api/item_prices).<br>* Any addon- and charge-item prices applied to the subscription.<br>* Any [coupons](/docs/api/coupons) applied.<br>* Any [discounts](/docs/api/discounts) applied.<br><br>The charges in a subscription are billed via invoices.  <br>**Note:**<br>The maximum number of subscriptions for any given [customer](/docs/api/customers)<br>([active](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object#status)<br>or not) is 900.  <br><br>#### Subscription billing frequencies<br><br>Chargebee offers two billing frequency options for subscriptions:<br><br>* **Plan-based billing** (`default`): Subscriptions are billed based on the billing period defined for the item price of the `item_type` `plan`. [Learn more](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/subscriptions#plan-based-billing).<br><br>* **Multi-frequency billing** : Subscriptions are billed according to the billing period of each recurring item price within the subscription. [Learn more](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/multi-frequency-billing).<br><br>  **Important**<br><br>  [Limitations](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/multi-frequency-billing#limitations) of Multi-frequency billing.<br><br>The selection of the billing frequency preference is configured at the site level.  <br><br>#### Item price compatibility in a subscription<br><br>When creating or updating a subscription, one of the item prices specified under subscription_items must be a plan-item price. The remaining must be compatible addon- or charge-item prices. An item price is compatible with a plan-item price if their currencies are the same. Additionally, an addon-item price is compatible with a plan-item price only if their billing frequencies meet the following conditions:  <br><br>\| `period_unit` for plan-item price \| Compatible `period_unit` for addon-item price \|                                                                                                                                                                                                Compatible period for addon-item price                                                                                                                                                                                                \|<br>\|-----------------------------------\|-----------------------------------------------\|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\|<br>\| `day`                             \| `day`                                         \| The `period` of the plan-item price should be divisible by the `period` of the addon-item price. **Example** If the `period` of the plan-item price is `10`, then the period of the addon-item price can be `10`, `5`, `2`, or `1`.                                                                                                                                                                                                  \|<br>\| `week`                            \| `week` or `day`                               \| The `period` (in days) of the plan-item price should be divisible by the `period` of the addon-item price. **Example** If the `period` of the plan-item price is `2`, then the period of the addon-item price can be as follows depending on the value of `period_unit`: * for `period_unit` as `week`, `period` can be `2` or `1`. * for `period_unit` as `day`, `period` can be `14`, `7`, `2`, or `1`.                            \|<br>\| `month`                           \| `month`                                       \| The `period` of the plan-item price should be divisible by the `period` of the addon-item price. **Example** If the `period` of the plan-item price is `6`, then the `period` of the addon-item price can be `6`, `3`, `2`, or `1`.                                                                                                                                                                                                  \|<br>\| `year`                            \| `year` or `month`                             \| The `period` (in months) of the plan-item price should be divisible by the `period` of the addon-item price. **Example** If the `period` of the plan-item price is `2`, then the `period` of the addon-item price can be as follows depending on the value of `period_unit`: * for `period_unit` as `year`, `period` can be `2` or `1`. * for `period_unit` as `month`, `period` can be `24`, `12`, `8`, `6`, `4`, `3`, `2`, or `1`. \|<br><br>#### Tax provider fields<br><br>**Avalara** : Merchants using **Avalara Sales Tax** can optionally associate each item |» » advance_invoice_schedule|body|[AdvanceInvoiceSchedule](#schemaadvanceinvoiceschedule)|true|The invoice for a subscription in Chargebee is generated at the time of subscription renewal. Invoices can also be [generated in advance](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/advance-invoices.html) for an upcoming renewal or set of renewals. With Advance Invoicing Schedules, you can set up a plan for when such advance invoices are generated for the lifetime of the subscription. This helps you:<br><br>* Set up a contract with your customers so that they can be notified of their payment schedules in advance.<br>* Allow customers who make offline payments to be alerted about their upcoming dues well ahead of actual subscription renewals.<br>* Prevent post-renewal unpaid usage of your services by customers.<br><br>Advance invoices can be scheduled in two ways:<br><br>#### Specific Dates Schedule<br><br>Advance invoices for a subscription can be scheduled to be generated on specific [dates](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#specific_dates_schedule_date) in the future. You must specify the [number of billing cycles](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#specific_dates_schedule_terms_to_charge) to be invoiced on each date. A maximum of 5 dates can be specified.<br><br>#### Fixed Interval Schedule<br><br>Advance invoices can be scheduled to be generated at fixed intervals of time, where each interval spans the same number of billing cycles of the subscription. The invoice for each interval is generated a specified number of days ([`days_before_interval`](/docs/api/advance_invoice_schedules/advance_invoice_schedule-object#fixed_interval_schedule_days_before_renewal)) before the start of the interval. You can configure the schedule to end on a certain date or after a specified number of advance invoices have been generated.<br><br>The start date of the first interval depends on the number of days remaining from current time till the next renewal of the subscription. If this is more than `days_before_interval`, the interval begins at the next renewal. On the other hand, if the number of days remaining before the next renewal is less than `days_before_interval`, the first interval begins at the renewal following the next.<br>|

|» » omnichannel_subscription|body|[OmnichannelSubscription](#schemaomnichannelsubscription)|true|Represents a subscription purchased and managed in an external app marketplace (`apple_app_store` or `google_play_store`), normalized into Chargebee's omnichannel model.<br><br>Omnichannel subscriptions are typically created when you [record a purchase](/docs/api/recorded_purchases/record-a-purchase) and are kept in sync via store server notifications. They are store-managed: lifecycle changes come from Apple or Google, not from the Chargebee Subscriptions API.<br><br>Use [omnichannel statuses](/docs/api/omnichannel_statuses) for how store statuses map to `omnichannel_subscription_item.status`, and [omnichannel events](/docs/api/omnichannel_events) for notification-to-webhook mappings.<br><br>Chargebee records introductory and promotional offers on [`omnichannel_subscription_item_offers`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscriptions/omnichannel_subscription-object#omnichannel_subscription_items_omnichannel_subscription_item_offers). Win-back offers and offer codes are not supported.  <br>**Identifier tip:** Parent `id_at_source` is the Apple **Transaction ID** or Google **purchase token** . Nested `initial_purchase_transaction.id_at_source` is the Apple **Transaction ID** or Google **Order ID** (`GPA....`). See attribute descriptions below.  <br>**Note:**<br>This resource represents in-app subscriptions made on Apple App Store and Google Play Store.<br>|

See [omnichannel statuses](/docs/api/omnichannel_statuses) for store mappings.<br><br>Chargebee records introductory and promotional offers on [`omnichannel_subscription_item_offers`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_items/omnichannel_subscription_item-object#omnichannel_subscription_item_offers). Win-back offers and offer codes are not supported.<br><br>When `has_scheduled_changes` is `true`, use [List scheduled changes](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_items/list-scheduled-changes-for-omnichannel-subscription-item) to retrieve deferred product or pause changes.  <br>**Note:**<br>This resource represents in-app subscription items made on Apple App Store and Google Play Store.<br>|

The customer details include their ID, name, contact information, and any [custom attributes](/docs/api/advanced-features) you'd like to associate with them.  <br>**Breaking Change**:<br><br>* [**Sites**](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/sites-intro.html) **created before March 1, 2014** : [updating the card](/docs/api/cards/update-card-for-a-customer) deletes the customer's `billing_address` and `vat_number` and replaces them with values from the request.<br>* **Sites created on or after March 1, 2014** : updating the card doesn't change the `billing_address` and `vat_number`.<br>|
