## Triggered when a business rule is deactivated

<a id="opIdonBusiness_rule_deactivatedWebhook"></a>

`POST business_rule_deactivated`

> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-business-rule-is-deactivated-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[BusinessRuleDeactivatedEvent](#schemabusinessruledeactivatedevent)|false|Payload for business_rule_deactivated event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » business_rule|body|[BusinessRule](#schemabusinessrule)|true|A business rule pairs a condition with the actions to take when that condition is met. You supply the context to evaluate, and Chargebee returns the actions configured in `actions_on_success` when the condition evaluates to `true`.<br><br>Business Rules APIs manage [CPQ Selling Rules](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/cpq/selling-rules).<br><br>The condition is defined in `structured_expression`, a JSON representation of the rule logic that visual editors and dynamic rule builders can both read and write. Chargebee validates and compiles the expression when the rule is created or updated, and evaluates the compiled form when you call [Apply business rules](/docs/api/business_rules/apply-business-rules).<br><br>The `field` of every condition is resolved against the context supplied at evaluation time, so the fields you reference must match the keys of the context the rule is evaluated against. A condition whose `field` is absent from the context never evaluates to `true`, which means the rule never matches.<br><br>Business rules are versioned. Creating a rule releases its first version, so `latest_version` is `1` and `released_at` is set from the outset. Editing a rule leaves that released version untouched: the first edit creates a draft, and every later edit updates the same draft. [Releasing](/docs/api/business_rules/release-a-business-rule) the draft promotes it to the next version number, and that version becomes the latest released version and the one Chargebee evaluates. Until you release it, the previously released version stays in effect, so a rule can keep serving traffic while its next version is being prepared.<br><br>The `active` attribute is an independent switch that controls whether Chargebee evaluates the rule at all. A rule is created inactive, so it has to be [activated](/docs/api/business_rules/activate-a-business-rule) before it takes effect.<br><br>Related rules can be grouped into a [business ruleset](/docs/api/business_rulesets), which evaluates its member rules in priority order using the strategy configured in the ruleset's `execute_mode`.<br><br>For a walkthrough that creates, activates, and applies a rule in three calls, take a look at the [Business Rules quickstart](https://www.chargebee.com/tutorials/business-rules-quickstart/).  <br>**Note:** Business rules are not enabled by default. Contact [Chargebee Support](https://www.chargebee.com/support/) to enable them for your site. Until they are enabled, these endpoints return an error.<br><br>Expressions<br>-----------<br><br>The `structured_expression` of a rule is a tree of nodes that evaluates to a single `true` or `false`. Every node carries a `type`, which determines the rest of the fields the node takes.<br><br>The following expression matches a quote from a customer whose language contains `en` and whose shipping country is India or the United States:<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "type": "GROUP",<br>  "operation": "AND",<br>  "children": [<br>    {<br>      "type": "CONDITION",<br>      "field": "customer.language",<br>      "operator": "CONTAINS",<br>      "value": "en"<br>    },<br>    {<br>      "type": "CONDITION",<br>      "field": "quote.shipping_address_country",<br>      "operator": "ANY_OF",<br>      "values": ["IN", "US"]<br>    }<br>  ]<br>}<br>```<br><br>Every condition is compiled so that it first tests whether the field is present in the context. A condition on a field that the context doesn't carry evaluates to `false` instead of failing, so the rule that holds it never matches and no `error_message` is returned for it.  <br><br>### GROUP node<br><br>Combines the nodes in `children` into a single result. Use a `GROUP` as the root of any expression that has more than one condition, and nest groups to control precedence.<br><br>* `operation`: **Required.** `AND` to match only if every child matches, or `OR` to match if any child matches.<br>* `children`: **Required.** An array holding at least one node. Each entry is itself a `GROUP`, `CONDITION`, or `COLLECTION` node.<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "type": "GROUP",<br>  "operation": "OR",<br>  "children": [<br>    {<br>      "type": "CONDITION",<br>      "field": "quote.payment_terms",<br>      "operator": "GREATER_THAN",<br>      "value": 30<br>    },<br>    {<br>      "type": "CONDITION",<br>      "field": "customer.billing_address_country",<br>      "operator": "EQUALS",<br>      "value": "US"<br>    }<br>  ]<br>}<br>```<br><br>### CONDITION node<br><br>Compares one field of the context against a value.<br><br>* `field`: **Required.** The path of the field through the context, such as `customer.language`. See [Context](/docs/api/business_rules#context) for the paths available.<br>* `operator`: **Required.** How the comparison is made. See [Operators](/docs/api/business_rules#operators) for the operators available and the field types each one compares.<br>* `value`: The single value to compare against. Required for the single-value operators.<br>* `values`: The array of values to compare against. Required for `BETWEEN`, `ANY_OF`, and `NONE_OF`.<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "type": "CONDITION",<br>  "field": "quote.contract_duration",<br>  "operator": "BETWEEN",<br>  "values": [12, 36]<br>}<br>```<br><br>### COLLECTION node<br><br>Tests the entries of an array in the context, such as the line items of a quote. All four fields are required.<br><br>* `field`: **Required.** The array to iterate over, such as `items`.<br>* `variable`: **Required.** The name each entry is bound to while the predicate is evaluated.<br>* `mode`: **Required.** `ANY` to match if at least one entry satisfies the predicate, or `NONE` to match only if no entry does.<br>* `predicate`: **Required.** The expression each entry is tested against, usually a `GROUP` node.<br><br>Inside the predicate, address the fields of an entry through the bound `variable`. The following node matches a quote that has at least one item discounted by more than 20:<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "type": "COLLECTION",<br>  "field": "items",<br>  "variable": "item",<br>  "mode": "ANY",<br>  "predicate": {<br>    "type": "GROUP",<br>    "operation": "AND",<br>    "children": [<br>      {<br>        "type": "CONDITION",<br>        "field": "item.discount",<br>        "operator": "GREATER_THAN",<br>        "value": 20<br>      }<br>    ]<br>  }<br>}<br>```<br><br>### Operators<br><br>The following operators are available. The field type is the type the operator can compare, and the value column shows whether the condition takes `value` or `values`.  <br><br>\|                                   Operator                                   \|       Field type        \|                                        Value                                        \|<br>\|------------------------------------------------------------------------------\|-------------------------\|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\|<br>\| `EQUALS`, `NOT_EQUALS`                                                       \| String, number, boolean \| `value`                                                                             \|<br>\| `GREATER_THAN`, `GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUALS`, `LESS_THAN`, `LESS_THAN_OR_EQUALS` \| Number                  \| `value`                                                                             \|<br>\| `BETWEEN`                                                                    \| Number                  \| `values`, holding exactly two entries, read as the inclusive lower and upper bounds \|<br>\| `CONTAINS`, `NOT_CONTAINS`                                                   \| String                  \| `value`                                                                             \|<br>\| `STARTS_WITH`                                                                \| String                  \| `value`                                                                             \|<br>\| `ANY_OF`, `NONE_OF`                                                          \| String, number, boolean \| `values`, holding at least one entry                                                \|<br><br>An operator used on a field of another type isn't rejected when the rule is saved, so the mismatch surfaces only when the rule is evaluated.<br><br>Context<br>-------<br><br>The `context` you pass to [Apply business rules](/docs/api/business_rules/apply-business-rules) isn't a free-form object. Its `type` selects the schema that the rest of the context is read as, and `CPQ` is the only type available, so a condition can reference only the fields of that schema. A key that falls outside the schema is dropped as the context is read, so a condition on it never evaluates to `true`. A misspelled or unsupported key therefore surfaces as an unmet condition rather than as an error.<br><br>A `CPQ` context carries `items`, `quote`, `customer`, `user`, `site`, and `quote_subscription`, each of them optional. Pass only the parts the rules you're evaluating need:<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "type": "CPQ",<br>  "customer": {<br>    "language": "en",<br>    "billing_address_country": "US"<br>  },<br>  "quote": {<br>    "shipping_address_country": "IN",<br>    "payment_terms": 30,<br>    "custom_fields": { "region": "apac" }<br>  },<br>  "items": [<br>    { "reference_id": "item-1", "amount": 5000, "quantity": 2, "discount": 10 },<br>    { "reference_id": "item-2", "amount": 1200, "quantity": 1, "discount": 0 }<br>  ]<br>}<br>```<br><br>A condition addresses a field by its path through the context, so `customer.language` reads the `language` of the `customer`. A `COLLECTION` node on `items` iterates over the entries of that array.<br><br>Each `custom_fields` object holds your own fields keyed by name, and every value must be a string, a number, or a boolean. A condition reads one through its key, as in `quote.custom_fields.region`.<br><br>The response returns the context back with `rule_ids` filled in on the quote and on each item, so you can see which rules applied where.  <br><br>### quote<br><br>* `type` and `contract_type`: strings.<br>* `contract_duration` and `payment_terms`: numbers.<br>* `billing_address_country` and `shipping_address_country`: strings.<br>* `billing_frequency` and `billing_currency`: strings.<br>* `creator_email` and `creator_role`: strings.<br>* `custom_fields`: object.<br>* `rule_ids`: array of strings. Returned in the response rather than passed, recording the rules that applied to the quote.  <br><br>### customer<br><br>* `billing_address_city`, `billing_address_state`, and `billing_address_country`: strings.<br>* `language`: string.<br>* `payment_terms`: number.<br>* `custom_fields`: object.  <br><br>### items<br><br>An array, with each entry holding the following.<br><br>* `reference_id`: string, identifying the entry within the context.<br>* `type`, `item_name`, and `product_family_name`: strings.<br>* `billing_frequency` and `currency`: strings.<br>* `billing_cycle`, `amount`, `quantity`, and `discount`: numbers.<br>* `start_date` and `end_date`: timestamps.<br>* `rule_ids`: array of strings. Returned in the response rather than passed, recording the rules that applied to that entry.  <br><br>### user<br><br>* `name`, `email`, and `phone`: strings.  <br><br>### site<br><br>* `name`, `domain`, and `currency`: strings.<br>* `sandbox`: boolean.  <br><br>### quote_subscription<br><br>* `custom_fields`: object.<br><br>Actions<br>-------<br><br>Every entry in `actions_on_success` is built from an **action template** , a built-in definition that fixes the kind of change an action makes and the parameters it accepts. An action names its template in `action_template_id` and passes that template's parameters in `input`:<br><br>```json<br>[<br>  {<br>    "action_template_id": "action-apply-discount",<br>    "input": {<br>      "apply_on": "INVOICE_AMOUNT",<br>      "discount": 12.0,<br>      "discount_type": "PERCENTAGE",<br>      "duration_type": "ONE_TIME"<br>    }<br>  }<br>]<br>```<br><br>The `type` of an action is derived from its template, so it's returned with the action but you don't have to pass it. A parameter that the template doesn't define is rejected. The values of enumerated parameters are matched without regard to case, and are returned in the `input` of the action exactly as you passed them.<br><br>An action can also carry a `structured_expression` of its own, written in the same format as the expression of the rule. The rule decides whether the action runs at all, and the action's own expression then narrows it to the items of the context that satisfy that expression. One rule can therefore discount some of the items it matched rather than all of them. Only the apply discount, limit discount, and limit quantity templates accept an action-level expression.  <br><br>### Apply discount<br><br>Applies a discount to the invoice amount or to specific item prices. Built from `action_template_id` `action-apply-discount` and returned with `type` `APPLY_DISCOUNT`.<br><br>* `apply_on`: **Required.** `INVOICE_AMOUNT` to discount the invoice total, or `SPECIFIC_ITEM_PRICE` to discount the item prices the action applies to.<br>* `discount`: **Required.** The discount to apply, such as `12.0`.<br>* `discount_type`: **Required.** `PERCENTAGE`, `FLAT_FEE`, or `OFFER_QUANTITY`, which fixes how `discount` is read.<br>* `duration_type`: **Required.** How long the discount applies, as `ONE_TIME`, `FOREVER`, or `LIMITED_PERIOD`.<br>* `period_unit`: `DAY`, `WEEK`, `MONTH`, or `YEAR`. Required if `duration_type` is `LIMITED_PERIOD`.<br>* `period`: The number of `period_unit`s the discount applies for. Required if `period_unit` is passed.  <br><br>### Apply coupon<br><br>Applies existing [coupons](/docs/api/coupons). Built from `action_template_id` `action-apply-coupon` and returned with `type` `APPLY_COUPON`.<br><br>* `apply_on`: **Required.** `INVOICE_AMOUNT` or `SPECIFIC_ITEM_PRICE`.<br>* `coupon_ids`: **Required.** The coupons to apply, as an array of coupon identifiers. It must hold at least one identifier.  <br><br>### Limit discount<br><br>Caps the discount that can be given. Use this template to enforce a discount ceiling without an approval step.<br><br>Built from `action_template_id` `action-limit-discount` and returned with `type` `LIMIT_DISCOUNT`.<br><br>* `apply_on`: **Required.** `INVOICE_AMOUNT` or `SPECIFIC_ITEM_PRICE`.<br>* `maximum_discount`: **Required.** The largest discount allowed, such as `20.0`.<br>* `discount_type`: **Required.** `PERCENTAGE`, `FLAT_FEE`, or `OFFER_QUANTITY`, which fixes how `maximum_discount` is read.<br>* `disable_price_override`: Pass `true` to disallow overriding the price outright.  <br><br>### Limit quantity<br><br>Constrains the quantities that can be selected. Built from `action_template_id` `action-limit-quantity` and returned with `type` `LIMIT_QUANTITY`. Every parameter is optional, so pass the ones you want to enforce.<br><br>* `minimum_quantity`: The smallest quantity allowed.<br>* `maximum_quantity`: The largest quantity allowed.<br>* `quantity_step_count`: The increment the quantity can be changed in, so `5` allows 5, 10, 15, and so on.  <br><br>### Error<br><br>Returns an error message instead of a change. Use this template to block an operation when the rule matches.<br><br>Built from `action_template_id` `action-error` and returned with `type` `ERROR`.<br><br>* `error_message`: **Required.** The message returned with the action.<br><br>Evaluation results<br>------------------<br><br>[Apply business rules](/docs/api/business_rules/apply-business-rules) returns an `apply_rule` object that echoes back the `context` you passed and carries one entry in `rules` for each rule it evaluated:<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "apply_rule": {<br>    "context": {<br>      "type": "CPQ",<br>      "customer": { "language": "en" },<br>      "quote": { "shipping_address_country": "IN" }<br>    },<br>    "rules": [<br>      {<br>        "id": "quote-discount-en",<br>        "version": 1,<br>        "name": "Apply 12 percent discount at invoice level",<br>        "evaluation_result": true,<br>        "actions": [<br>          {<br>            "action_template_id": "action-apply-discount",<br>            "type": "APPLY_DISCOUNT",<br>            "input": {<br>              "apply_on": "INVOICE_AMOUNT",<br>              "discount": 12.0,<br>              "discount_type": "PERCENTAGE",<br>              "duration_type": "ONE_TIME"<br>            }<br>          }<br>        ],<br>        "object": "applied_rule"<br>      },<br>      {<br>        "id": "quote-discount-uk",<br>        "version": 1,<br>        "name": "Apply 5 percent discount at invoice level for UK quotes",<br>        "evaluation_result": false,<br>        "object": "applied_rule"<br>      }<br>    ],<br>    "object": "apply_rule"<br>  }<br>}<br>```<br><br>Read the result of each rule from `evaluation_result`, and read what the rule produced from `actions`. Two things about the shape are worth knowing before you write code against it.<br><br>* `actions` is absent, rather than empty, for a rule whose `evaluation_result` is `false`. The second entry above shows a rule that didn't match.<br>* An entry for an ad hoc `structured_expression` carries only `evaluation_result`, because there's no stored rule to report an `id`, `name`, or `actions` for.<br><br>A rule that couldn't be evaluated is returned with `error_message` set instead, but only if you passed `skip_failed_rules` as `true`. Otherwise the request fails. For the full list of fields, see the response of [Apply business rules](/docs/api/business_rules/apply-business-rules).<br>|

|200|OK|Webhook received successfully|None|

|» » ledger_account_balance|body|[LedgerAccountBalance](#schemaledgeraccountbalance)|true|Credit Grants<br>-------------<br><br>A credit grant is a quantified allocation of credits given to a subscription through a configured [item price](/docs/api/item_prices) or via the [allocate](/docs/api/ledger_operations/allocate) operation, consumed over time through ledger operations.  <br>**Example**<br><br>A subscription receives a credit grant of 100 AI credits as a balance. As the customer uses AI features<br>(e.g., Image Generation), the provisioned balance is consumed first. Once exhausted, further consumption is deducted from the overdraft balance until its limit is reached.<br><br>The Ledger Account Balance object<br>---------------------------------<br><br>The `ledger_account_balance` object is a real-time snapshot of credit grants for a single combination of subscription_id, unit_id and unit_type.<br><br>The ledger tracks two balances:<br><br>* [**provisioned_balance**](#provisioned_balance): Reflects the credit grants given through the configured item price or allocate operations. These are prepaid credit grants for which the customer has already paid. Any ledger operation will prioritize consuming this balance first.<br>* [**overdraft_balance**](#overdraft_balance): Reflects the extra limit provided to a subscription in case it exhausts all credit grants before they are renewed or refreshed. Any ledger operation will consume this balance only when the provisioned balance has been exhausted.<br><br>**Note**<br><br>These two balances are always tracked together for a subscription with credit grants.  <br>**Example**<br><br>A subscription has a credit grant of 100 AI credits, added to its provisioned balance. Once the provisioned balance is exhausted, further consumption is drawn from the overdraft balance up to its configured limit.<br>screenshot\\|/images/account_balance.png<br><br>**Returned by**<br><br>* [List ledger account balances](/docs/api/ledger_account_balances/list-ledger-account-balances) API.<br>* Ledger [operations](/docs/api/ledger_operations) such as [allocate](/docs/api/ledger_operations/allocate), [capture](/docs/api/ledger_operations/capture), and [authorize](/docs/api/ledger_operations/authorize).<br>|

## Triggered when a business rule is released

<a id="opIdonBusiness_rule_releasedWebhook"></a>

`POST business_rule_released`

> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-business-rule-is-released-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[BusinessRuleReleasedEvent](#schemabusinessrulereleasedevent)|false|Payload for business_rule_released event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » business_rule|body|[BusinessRule](#schemabusinessrule)|true|A business rule pairs a condition with the actions to take when that condition is met. You supply the context to evaluate, and Chargebee returns the actions configured in `actions_on_success` when the condition evaluates to `true`.<br><br>Business Rules APIs manage [CPQ Selling Rules](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/cpq/selling-rules).<br><br>The condition is defined in `structured_expression`, a JSON representation of the rule logic that visual editors and dynamic rule builders can both read and write. Chargebee validates and compiles the expression when the rule is created or updated, and evaluates the compiled form when you call [Apply business rules](/docs/api/business_rules/apply-business-rules).<br><br>The `field` of every condition is resolved against the context supplied at evaluation time, so the fields you reference must match the keys of the context the rule is evaluated against. A condition whose `field` is absent from the context never evaluates to `true`, which means the rule never matches.<br><br>Business rules are versioned. Creating a rule releases its first version, so `latest_version` is `1` and `released_at` is set from the outset. Editing a rule leaves that released version untouched: the first edit creates a draft, and every later edit updates the same draft. [Releasing](/docs/api/business_rules/release-a-business-rule) the draft promotes it to the next version number, and that version becomes the latest released version and the one Chargebee evaluates. Until you release it, the previously released version stays in effect, so a rule can keep serving traffic while its next version is being prepared.<br><br>The `active` attribute is an independent switch that controls whether Chargebee evaluates the rule at all. A rule is created inactive, so it has to be [activated](/docs/api/business_rules/activate-a-business-rule) before it takes effect.<br><br>Related rules can be grouped into a [business ruleset](/docs/api/business_rulesets), which evaluates its member rules in priority order using the strategy configured in the ruleset's `execute_mode`.<br><br>For a walkthrough that creates, activates, and applies a rule in three calls, take a look at the [Business Rules quickstart](https://www.chargebee.com/tutorials/business-rules-quickstart/).  <br>**Note:** Business rules are not enabled by default. Contact [Chargebee Support](https://www.chargebee.com/support/) to enable them for your site. Until they are enabled, these endpoints return an error.<br><br>Expressions<br>-----------<br><br>The `structured_expression` of a rule is a tree of nodes that evaluates to a single `true` or `false`. Every node carries a `type`, which determines the rest of the fields the node takes.<br><br>The following expression matches a quote from a customer whose language contains `en` and whose shipping country is India or the United States:<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "type": "GROUP",<br>  "operation": "AND",<br>  "children": [<br>    {<br>      "type": "CONDITION",<br>      "field": "customer.language",<br>      "operator": "CONTAINS",<br>      "value": "en"<br>    },<br>    {<br>      "type": "CONDITION",<br>      "field": "quote.shipping_address_country",<br>      "operator": "ANY_OF",<br>      "values": ["IN", "US"]<br>    }<br>  ]<br>}<br>```<br><br>Every condition is compiled so that it first tests whether the field is present in the context. A condition on a field that the context doesn't carry evaluates to `false` instead of failing, so the rule that holds it never matches and no `error_message` is returned for it.  <br><br>### GROUP node<br><br>Combines the nodes in `children` into a single result. Use a `GROUP` as the root of any expression that has more than one condition, and nest groups to control precedence.<br><br>* `operation`: **Required.** `AND` to match only if every child matches, or `OR` to match if any child matches.<br>* `children`: **Required.** An array holding at least one node. Each entry is itself a `GROUP`, `CONDITION`, or `COLLECTION` node.<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "type": "GROUP",<br>  "operation": "OR",<br>  "children": [<br>    {<br>      "type": "CONDITION",<br>      "field": "quote.payment_terms",<br>      "operator": "GREATER_THAN",<br>      "value": 30<br>    },<br>    {<br>      "type": "CONDITION",<br>      "field": "customer.billing_address_country",<br>      "operator": "EQUALS",<br>      "value": "US"<br>    }<br>  ]<br>}<br>```<br><br>### CONDITION node<br><br>Compares one field of the context against a value.<br><br>* `field`: **Required.** The path of the field through the context, such as `customer.language`. See [Context](/docs/api/business_rules#context) for the paths available.<br>* `operator`: **Required.** How the comparison is made. See [Operators](/docs/api/business_rules#operators) for the operators available and the field types each one compares.<br>* `value`: The single value to compare against. Required for the single-value operators.<br>* `values`: The array of values to compare against. Required for `BETWEEN`, `ANY_OF`, and `NONE_OF`.<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "type": "CONDITION",<br>  "field": "quote.contract_duration",<br>  "operator": "BETWEEN",<br>  "values": [12, 36]<br>}<br>```<br><br>### COLLECTION node<br><br>Tests the entries of an array in the context, such as the line items of a quote. All four fields are required.<br><br>* `field`: **Required.** The array to iterate over, such as `items`.<br>* `variable`: **Required.** The name each entry is bound to while the predicate is evaluated.<br>* `mode`: **Required.** `ANY` to match if at least one entry satisfies the predicate, or `NONE` to match only if no entry does.<br>* `predicate`: **Required.** The expression each entry is tested against, usually a `GROUP` node.<br><br>Inside the predicate, address the fields of an entry through the bound `variable`. The following node matches a quote that has at least one item discounted by more than 20:<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "type": "COLLECTION",<br>  "field": "items",<br>  "variable": "item",<br>  "mode": "ANY",<br>  "predicate": {<br>    "type": "GROUP",<br>    "operation": "AND",<br>    "children": [<br>      {<br>        "type": "CONDITION",<br>        "field": "item.discount",<br>        "operator": "GREATER_THAN",<br>        "value": 20<br>      }<br>    ]<br>  }<br>}<br>```<br><br>### Operators<br><br>The following operators are available. The field type is the type the operator can compare, and the value column shows whether the condition takes `value` or `values`.  <br><br>\|                                   Operator                                   \|       Field type        \|                                        Value                                        \|<br>\|------------------------------------------------------------------------------\|-------------------------\|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\|<br>\| `EQUALS`, `NOT_EQUALS`                                                       \| String, number, boolean \| `value`                                                                             \|<br>\| `GREATER_THAN`, `GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUALS`, `LESS_THAN`, `LESS_THAN_OR_EQUALS` \| Number                  \| `value`                                                                             \|<br>\| `BETWEEN`                                                                    \| Number                  \| `values`, holding exactly two entries, read as the inclusive lower and upper bounds \|<br>\| `CONTAINS`, `NOT_CONTAINS`                                                   \| String                  \| `value`                                                                             \|<br>\| `STARTS_WITH`                                                                \| String                  \| `value`                                                                             \|<br>\| `ANY_OF`, `NONE_OF`                                                          \| String, number, boolean \| `values`, holding at least one entry                                                \|<br><br>An operator used on a field of another type isn't rejected when the rule is saved, so the mismatch surfaces only when the rule is evaluated.<br><br>Context<br>-------<br><br>The `context` you pass to [Apply business rules](/docs/api/business_rules/apply-business-rules) isn't a free-form object. Its `type` selects the schema that the rest of the context is read as, and `CPQ` is the only type available, so a condition can reference only the fields of that schema. A key that falls outside the schema is dropped as the context is read, so a condition on it never evaluates to `true`. A misspelled or unsupported key therefore surfaces as an unmet condition rather than as an error.<br><br>A `CPQ` context carries `items`, `quote`, `customer`, `user`, `site`, and `quote_subscription`, each of them optional. Pass only the parts the rules you're evaluating need:<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "type": "CPQ",<br>  "customer": {<br>    "language": "en",<br>    "billing_address_country": "US"<br>  },<br>  "quote": {<br>    "shipping_address_country": "IN",<br>    "payment_terms": 30,<br>    "custom_fields": { "region": "apac" }<br>  },<br>  "items": [<br>    { "reference_id": "item-1", "amount": 5000, "quantity": 2, "discount": 10 },<br>    { "reference_id": "item-2", "amount": 1200, "quantity": 1, "discount": 0 }<br>  ]<br>}<br>```<br><br>A condition addresses a field by its path through the context, so `customer.language` reads the `language` of the `customer`. A `COLLECTION` node on `items` iterates over the entries of that array.<br><br>Each `custom_fields` object holds your own fields keyed by name, and every value must be a string, a number, or a boolean. A condition reads one through its key, as in `quote.custom_fields.region`.<br><br>The response returns the context back with `rule_ids` filled in on the quote and on each item, so you can see which rules applied where.  <br><br>### quote<br><br>* `type` and `contract_type`: strings.<br>* `contract_duration` and `payment_terms`: numbers.<br>* `billing_address_country` and `shipping_address_country`: strings.<br>* `billing_frequency` and `billing_currency`: strings.<br>* `creator_email` and `creator_role`: strings.<br>* `custom_fields`: object.<br>* `rule_ids`: array of strings. Returned in the response rather than passed, recording the rules that applied to the quote.  <br><br>### customer<br><br>* `billing_address_city`, `billing_address_state`, and `billing_address_country`: strings.<br>* `language`: string.<br>* `payment_terms`: number.<br>* `custom_fields`: object.  <br><br>### items<br><br>An array, with each entry holding the following.<br><br>* `reference_id`: string, identifying the entry within the context.<br>* `type`, `item_name`, and `product_family_name`: strings.<br>* `billing_frequency` and `currency`: strings.<br>* `billing_cycle`, `amount`, `quantity`, and `discount`: numbers.<br>* `start_date` and `end_date`: timestamps.<br>* `rule_ids`: array of strings. Returned in the response rather than passed, recording the rules that applied to that entry.  <br><br>### user<br><br>* `name`, `email`, and `phone`: strings.  <br><br>### site<br><br>* `name`, `domain`, and `currency`: strings.<br>* `sandbox`: boolean.  <br><br>### quote_subscription<br><br>* `custom_fields`: object.<br><br>Actions<br>-------<br><br>Every entry in `actions_on_success` is built from an **action template** , a built-in definition that fixes the kind of change an action makes and the parameters it accepts. An action names its template in `action_template_id` and passes that template's parameters in `input`:<br><br>```json<br>[<br>  {<br>    "action_template_id": "action-apply-discount",<br>    "input": {<br>      "apply_on": "INVOICE_AMOUNT",<br>      "discount": 12.0,<br>      "discount_type": "PERCENTAGE",<br>      "duration_type": "ONE_TIME"<br>    }<br>  }<br>]<br>```<br><br>The `type` of an action is derived from its template, so it's returned with the action but you don't have to pass it. A parameter that the template doesn't define is rejected. The values of enumerated parameters are matched without regard to case, and are returned in the `input` of the action exactly as you passed them.<br><br>An action can also carry a `structured_expression` of its own, written in the same format as the expression of the rule. The rule decides whether the action runs at all, and the action's own expression then narrows it to the items of the context that satisfy that expression. One rule can therefore discount some of the items it matched rather than all of them. Only the apply discount, limit discount, and limit quantity templates accept an action-level expression.  <br><br>### Apply discount<br><br>Applies a discount to the invoice amount or to specific item prices. Built from `action_template_id` `action-apply-discount` and returned with `type` `APPLY_DISCOUNT`.<br><br>* `apply_on`: **Required.** `INVOICE_AMOUNT` to discount the invoice total, or `SPECIFIC_ITEM_PRICE` to discount the item prices the action applies to.<br>* `discount`: **Required.** The discount to apply, such as `12.0`.<br>* `discount_type`: **Required.** `PERCENTAGE`, `FLAT_FEE`, or `OFFER_QUANTITY`, which fixes how `discount` is read.<br>* `duration_type`: **Required.** How long the discount applies, as `ONE_TIME`, `FOREVER`, or `LIMITED_PERIOD`.<br>* `period_unit`: `DAY`, `WEEK`, `MONTH`, or `YEAR`. Required if `duration_type` is `LIMITED_PERIOD`.<br>* `period`: The number of `period_unit`s the discount applies for. Required if `period_unit` is passed.  <br><br>### Apply coupon<br><br>Applies existing [coupons](/docs/api/coupons). Built from `action_template_id` `action-apply-coupon` and returned with `type` `APPLY_COUPON`.<br><br>* `apply_on`: **Required.** `INVOICE_AMOUNT` or `SPECIFIC_ITEM_PRICE`.<br>* `coupon_ids`: **Required.** The coupons to apply, as an array of coupon identifiers. It must hold at least one identifier.  <br><br>### Limit discount<br><br>Caps the discount that can be given. Use this template to enforce a discount ceiling without an approval step.<br><br>Built from `action_template_id` `action-limit-discount` and returned with `type` `LIMIT_DISCOUNT`.<br><br>* `apply_on`: **Required.** `INVOICE_AMOUNT` or `SPECIFIC_ITEM_PRICE`.<br>* `maximum_discount`: **Required.** The largest discount allowed, such as `20.0`.<br>* `discount_type`: **Required.** `PERCENTAGE`, `FLAT_FEE`, or `OFFER_QUANTITY`, which fixes how `maximum_discount` is read.<br>* `disable_price_override`: Pass `true` to disallow overriding the price outright.  <br><br>### Limit quantity<br><br>Constrains the quantities that can be selected. Built from `action_template_id` `action-limit-quantity` and returned with `type` `LIMIT_QUANTITY`. Every parameter is optional, so pass the ones you want to enforce.<br><br>* `minimum_quantity`: The smallest quantity allowed.<br>* `maximum_quantity`: The largest quantity allowed.<br>* `quantity_step_count`: The increment the quantity can be changed in, so `5` allows 5, 10, 15, and so on.  <br><br>### Error<br><br>Returns an error message instead of a change. Use this template to block an operation when the rule matches.<br><br>Built from `action_template_id` `action-error` and returned with `type` `ERROR`.<br><br>* `error_message`: **Required.** The message returned with the action.<br><br>Evaluation results<br>------------------<br><br>[Apply business rules](/docs/api/business_rules/apply-business-rules) returns an `apply_rule` object that echoes back the `context` you passed and carries one entry in `rules` for each rule it evaluated:<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "apply_rule": {<br>    "context": {<br>      "type": "CPQ",<br>      "customer": { "language": "en" },<br>      "quote": { "shipping_address_country": "IN" }<br>    },<br>    "rules": [<br>      {<br>        "id": "quote-discount-en",<br>        "version": 1,<br>        "name": "Apply 12 percent discount at invoice level",<br>        "evaluation_result": true,<br>        "actions": [<br>          {<br>            "action_template_id": "action-apply-discount",<br>            "type": "APPLY_DISCOUNT",<br>            "input": {<br>              "apply_on": "INVOICE_AMOUNT",<br>              "discount": 12.0,<br>              "discount_type": "PERCENTAGE",<br>              "duration_type": "ONE_TIME"<br>            }<br>          }<br>        ],<br>        "object": "applied_rule"<br>      },<br>      {<br>        "id": "quote-discount-uk",<br>        "version": 1,<br>        "name": "Apply 5 percent discount at invoice level for UK quotes",<br>        "evaluation_result": false,<br>        "object": "applied_rule"<br>      }<br>    ],<br>    "object": "apply_rule"<br>  }<br>}<br>```<br><br>Read the result of each rule from `evaluation_result`, and read what the rule produced from `actions`. Two things about the shape are worth knowing before you write code against it.<br><br>* `actions` is absent, rather than empty, for a rule whose `evaluation_result` is `false`. The second entry above shows a rule that didn't match.<br>* An entry for an ad hoc `structured_expression` carries only `evaluation_result`, because there's no stored rule to report an `id`, `name`, or `actions` for.<br><br>A rule that couldn't be evaluated is returned with `error_message` set instead, but only if you passed `skip_failed_rules` as `true`. Otherwise the request fails. For the full list of fields, see the response of [Apply business rules](/docs/api/business_rules/apply-business-rules).<br>|

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-business-rule-is-released-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Webhook received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication

## Triggered on subscription update, alongside the subscription_updated event whenever the subscription has subscription_entitlements updated. The event payload contains the first 100 subscription_entitlements. The has_next attribute is set to true if more than 100 subscription entitlements are available. You can retrieve the next page by calling the “List subscription entitlements” endpoint, passing the offset parameter as 1.

<a id="opIdonSubscription_entitlements_updatedWebhook"></a>

null

`POST omnichannel_subscription_item_dunning_expired`

Triggered when an omnichannel subscription item's dunning period has expired.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-an-omnichannel-subscription-items-dunning-has-expired-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[OmnichannelSubscriptionItemDunningExpiredEvent](#schemaomnichannelsubscriptionitemdunningexpiredevent)|false|Payload for omnichannel_subscription_item_dunning_expired event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » omnichannel_subscription|body|[OmnichannelSubscription](#schemaomnichannelsubscription)|true|Represents a subscription purchased and managed in an external app marketplace (`apple_app_store` or `google_play_store`), normalized into Chargebee's omnichannel model.<br><br>Omnichannel subscriptions are typically created when you [record a purchase](/docs/api/recorded_purchases/record-a-purchase) and are kept in sync via store server notifications. They are store-managed: lifecycle changes come from Apple or Google, not from the Chargebee Subscriptions API.<br><br>Use [omnichannel statuses](/docs/api/omnichannel_statuses) for how store statuses map to `omnichannel_subscription_item.status`, and [omnichannel events](/docs/api/omnichannel_events) for notification-to-webhook mappings.<br><br>Chargebee records introductory and promotional offers on [`omnichannel_subscription_item_offers`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscriptions/omnichannel_subscription-object#omnichannel_subscription_items_omnichannel_subscription_item_offers). Win-back offers and offer codes are not supported.  <br>**Identifier tip:** Parent `id_at_source` is the Apple **Transaction ID** or Google **purchase token** . Nested `initial_purchase_transaction.id_at_source` is the Apple **Transaction ID** or Google **Order ID** (`GPA....`). See attribute descriptions below.  <br>**Note:**<br>This resource represents in-app subscriptions made on Apple App Store and Google Play Store.<br>|
|» » omnichannel_subscription_item|body|[OmnichannelSubscriptionItem](#schemaomnichannelsubscriptionitem)|true|Represents a product entitlement (item) within an [`omnichannel_subscription`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscriptions) purchased on Apple App Store or Google Play Store.<br><br>Status, auto-renew, term dates, and cancel/expire reasons live on this resource. See [omnichannel statuses](/docs/api/omnichannel_statuses) for store mappings.<br><br>Chargebee records introductory and promotional offers on [`omnichannel_subscription_item_offers`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_items/omnichannel_subscription_item-object#omnichannel_subscription_item_offers). Win-back offers and offer codes are not supported.<br><br>When `has_scheduled_changes` is `true`, use [List scheduled changes](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_items/list-scheduled-changes-for-omnichannel-subscription-item) to retrieve deferred product or pause changes.  <br>**Note:**<br>This resource represents in-app subscription items made on Apple App Store and Google Play Store.<br>|
|» » customer|body|[Customer](#schemacustomer)|true|Represents a customer, which can be an individual or organization that subscribes to your products or services. The customer resource associates with [subscriptions](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object), [card information](/docs/api/cards/card-object), and billing addresses. The customer details include their ID, name, contact information, and any [custom attributes](/docs/api/advanced-features) you'd like to associate with them.  <br>**Breaking Change**:<br><br>* [**Sites**](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/sites-intro.html) **created before March 1, 2014** : [updating the card](/docs/api/cards/update-card-for-a-customer) deletes the customer's `billing_address` and `vat_number` and replaces them with values from the request.<br>* **Sites created on or after March 1, 2014** : updating the card doesn't change the `billing_address` and `vat_number`.<br>|

## Triggered when an attached item is deleted.

<a id="opIdonAttached_item_deletedWebhook"></a>

`POST attached_item_deleted`

Triggered when an attached item is deleted.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-an-attached-item-is-deleted-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AttachedItemDeletedEvent](#schemaattacheditemdeletedevent)|false|Payload for attached_item_deleted event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » attached_item|body|[AttachedItem](#schemaattacheditem)|true|Addon-item and charge-item prices are purchased with plan-item prices in subscriptions. You can automate this process by configuring certain addons and charges as "attached" to certain plans. This is done at the "item" level. In other words, addon- and charge-items can be attached to plan-items.<br><br>Once the attachment is defined, while creating or updating a subscription, the addon- or charge-item prices are selected automatically based on the plan-item price selected . Let's look at the details:<br><br>### Addons<br><br>Addons can be attached to plans as `recommended`, `mandatory` or `optional`.<br><br>* When an addon is attached as `recommended` for a plan, the addon is suggested to be applied to subscriptions for the plan in [Checkout](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/configure-inapp.html#fundamental-settings_recommending-addons-in-checkout) and [Self-Serve Portal](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/inapp-self-serve-portal.html#allow-change-subscription). Alternatively, if you build your own payment pages or have a sales team, you can suggest recommended addons to your customers or salespeople on your website or CRM respectively<br>* When an addon is attached as `mandatory` for a plan, the addon gets applied to subscriptions for the plan compulsorily, unless [removed explicitly](/docs/api/subscriptions). If you do not pass an item price for a mandatory addon when including the plan in a subscription, an addon-item price is automatically applied as explained below.<br>* Attaching an addon as `optional` neither marks it as recommended or mandatory but allows you a way to set a `quantity` and `billing_cycles` for the addon, for when it is applied to subscriptions with the plan.<br><br>How auto-selection of the addon-item price works<br>------------------------------------------------<br><br>Once an addon has been attached as mandatory, the addon-item price to be applied to the plan-item price is selected based on the following rule: The addon-item price with the same currency as that of the plan-item price and the longest compatible period is selected.<br><br>Here's an example:<br><br>Consider a plan **Standard Cloud Storage** has an addon **Extra Storage** attached to it. Note that each of the two are items. Now consider that they have item prices with the following periods and currencies:<br><br>**Item price for "Standard Cloud Storage" plan-item:**<br><br>* Standard Cloud Storage, 3 years, AUD.<br><br>**Item prices for "Extra Storage" addon-item:**<br><br>* Extra Storage, 1 year, EUR.<br>* Extra Storage, 1 year, USD.<br>* Extra Storage, 1 year, AUD.<br>* Extra Storage, 18 months, AUD.<br>* Extra Storage, 2 years, AUD.<br>* Extra Storage, 30 months, AUD.<br><br>For the plan-item price (Standard Cloud Storage, 3 years, AUD), the addon-item prices with matching currencies are the last 4 from the above list:<br><br>* Extra Storage, 1 year, AUD.<br>* Extra Storage, 18 months, AUD.<br>* Extra Storage, 2 years, AUD.<br>* Extra Storage, 30 months, AUD.<br><br>From among them, the last two have periods that are incompatible with the plan-item price period of 3 years. From the remaining 2 addon-item prices, the one with the longest period is of 18 months. So, "Extra Storage, 18 months, AUD" is selected for mandatory application to the plan item price.<br><br>### Charges<br><br>Charges can also be attached to plans. When doing so, you specify [the event](/docs/api/attached_items/attached_item-object#charge_on_event) at which the charge is to be applied to the subscription. For some events that can occur multiple times in a subscription lifetime, you can also set whether to apply the charge each time the event occurs or just once.<br><br>There may be multiple item prices for a given attached charge. The item price that matches the currency of the plan-item price is automatically selected for application.<br><br>Here's an example:<br><br>Consider a plan **Standard Cloud Storage** has a charge named **Implementation Fee** attached to it. Now consider their item prices below, with the following periods and currencies:<br><br>**Item price for "Standard Cloud Storage" plan-item:**<br><br>* Standard Cloud Storage, 3 years, AUD.<br><br>**Item prices for "Implementation Fee" charge-item:**<br><br>* Implementation Fee, USD.<br>* Implementation Fee, AUD.<br>* Implementation Fee, EUR.<br><br>From among the charge-item prices above, the one compatible with the plan-item price is "Implementation Fee, AUD" since it has the same currency as the plan-item price.<br>|

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Webhook received successfully|None|

This operation does not require authentication

## Triggered when an item is updated.

<a id="opIdonItem_updatedWebhook"></a>

`POST item_updated`

Triggered when an item is updated.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-an-item-is-updated-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ItemUpdatedEvent](#schemaitemupdatedevent)|false|Payload for item_updated event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » item|body|[Item](#schemaitem)|true|When offering subscriptions of products or services, each entity that is made available for sale is represented by an "item" object. Items therefore represent the various plans, addons or charges that you offer as part of your product catalog. Non-`metered` items are charged upfront in Chargebee, while `metered` items are charged at the end of the billing cycle, based on usage.<br><br>### Types of Items<br><br>There are three types of items and they're listed and explained here. Examples for each type are provided in the table that follows.<br><br>#### Plan-items or Plans<br><br>Plan-items are items that have a recurring charge and are an essential component of any [subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions). Typically, plans represent a principal or key product or service in your catalog. They are charged at recurring intervals and often have other products or services offered along with them as addons and charges.<br><br>#### Addon-items or Addons<br><br>Addon-items are items that are sold along with a plan and are charged for at recurring intervals.<br><br>#### Charge-items or Charges<br><br>Charge-items are items that are sold along with a plan but charged once (or each time) a specified event occurs. A charge can also be [applied to a customer](/docs/api/v2/pcv-1/invoices/create-invoice-for-a-one-time-charge) without attaching to a subscription.<br><br>#### Examples<br><br>To help understand each type of item better, listed below are some examples of items from different business domains:<br><br>##### Non-Metered (SaaS)<br><br>* **Item Family:** A project management solution.<br>* **Plans:**<br>  * A "basic" plan offering a small set of features.<br>  * A "business" plan offering a larger set of features.<br>* **Addons:**<br>  * An analytics plugin that is available only with the "business" plan.<br>  * A reporting plugin, available with both the above plans.<br>* **Charges:**<br>  * Implementation charges.<br>  * Trial charges.<br><br>##### Non-Metered (E-commerce)<br><br>* **Item Family:** A printed news magazine.<br>* **Plans:**<br>  * Periodic issues of the magazine.<br>  * Periodic issues of the magazine, with digital content.<br>* **Addons:**<br>  * Supplementary online content.<br>  * Access to a year's worth of back issues.<br>  * Searchable access to all back issues.<br>* **Charges:**<br>  * Special edition books that are published every so often.<br><br>##### Metered<br><br>* **Item Family:** SMS delivery services.<br>* **Plans:**<br>  * A basic plan of up to 100K messages @ $0.03 per message.<br>  * A volume plan of 2M messages @ $0.01 per message.<br>* **Addons:**<br>  * An addon of 50K MMS messages @ $0.1 per message.<br>  * Instant messaging.<br>* **Charges:**<br>  * Automated Metered Billing is not applicable for charges.<br>|

|» » coupon|body|[Coupon](#schemacoupon)|true|Overview<br>--------<br><br>Coupons are deductions applied to invoices or invoice line items. They're designed to be consumed by your customers directly. A coupon deduction can either be for a fixed amount or for a percentage of the amount of the invoice or line item.  <br>**Note:**<br><br>If you wish to provide discounts to your customers via API or the Chargebee app, see [Discounts API](/docs/api/discounts)<br><br>Order of application of coupons and discounts<br>---------------------------------------------<br><br>When both [coupons](/docs/api/coupons) and [discounts](/docs/api/discounts) are applied simultaneously to a [subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions) or [one-time invoice](/docs/api/invoices/create-invoice-for-items-and-one-time-charges), they're applied in the following order:  <br><br>\|---\|---------------------------------------\|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\|<br>\|   \| **Summary**                           \| **Description**                                                                     \|<br>\| 1 \| Line-level, fixed amount coupons      \| `coupon` with `apply_on` = `each_specified_item` and `discount_type` = `flat`       \|<br>\| 2 \| Line-level, fixed amount discounts    \| `discount` with `apply_on` = `specific_item_price` and `type` = `fixed_amount`      \|<br>\| 3 \| Line-level, percentage coupons        \| `coupon` with `apply_on` = `each_specified_item` and `discount_type` = `percentage` \|<br>\| 4 \| Line-level, percentage discounts      \| `discount` with `apply_on` = `specific_item_price` and `type` = `percentage`        \|<br>\| 5 \| Invoice-level, fixed amount coupons   \| `coupon` with `apply_on` = `invoice_amount` and `discount_type` = `flat`            \|<br>\| 6 \| Invoice-level, fixed amount discounts \| `discount` with `apply_on` = `invoice_amount` and `type` = `fixed_amount`           \|<br>\| 7 \| Invoice-level, percentage coupons     \| `coupon` with `apply_on` = `invoice_amount` and `discount_type` = `percentage`      \|<br>\| 8 \| Invoice-level, percentage discounts   \| `discount` with `apply_on` = `invoice_amount` and `type` = `percentage`             \|<br><br>For example, consider the following scenario:<br><br>A subscription is created with:<br><br>* a plan price of $200 per month<br>* an addon price of $20 per month<br>* a flat $5 invoice discount<br>* a 1% off coupon on the addon<br>* a flat $2 coupon on the invoice<br><br>The above coupons and discount are applied in the following order:  <br><br>\|---\|---------------------------------------------\|-----------------------------------------------\|<br>\|   \| **Discount or coupon applied**              \| **Subtotal at each step**                     \|<br>\| 1 \| Initial subtotal (plan price + addon price) \| $200 + $20 = $220                             \|<br>\| 2 \| 1% off coupon on the addon                  \| $200 + $(20 - 0.02) = $200 + $19.98 = $219.98 \|<br>\| 3 \| Flat $2 coupon on the invoice               \| $219.98 - $2 = $217.98                        \|<br>\| 4 \| Flat $5 invoice discount                    \| $217.98 - $5 = **$212.98**                    \|<br><br>|

## Triggered when a tax withheld is recorded for an invoice.

<a id="opIdonTax_withheld_recordedWebhook"></a>

`POST tax_withheld_recorded`

Triggered when a tax withheld is recorded for an invoice.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="triggered-when-a-tax-withheld-is-recorded-for-an-invoice-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TaxWithheldRecordedEvent](#schemataxwithheldrecordedevent)|false|Payload for tax_withheld_recorded event|
|» id|body|string|true|The ID of the event|
|» occurred_at|body|integer(int64)|true|Timestamp of the event|
|» source|body|string|true|Source of the event|
|» object|body|string|true|The object of the event|
|» api_version|body|string|true|API version|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Type of the event|
|» webhook_status|body|string|true|Status of webhook|
|» content|body|object|true|none|
|» » tax_withheld|body|[TaxWithheld](#schemataxwithheld)|true|Tax regulations in many countries allow taxes to be deducted by the buyer while making payments for products and services. The buyer then pays this tax to the taxation authority. The `tax_withheld` resource captures the details of such tax deductions.  <br>**Note:**<br><br>* This resource is available as the `linked_taxes_withheld` sub-resource under `invoice`s.<br>* Whenever refunds are provided against this resource, they are available as `linked_tax_withheld_refunds` sub-resource under `credit_note`s.<br>|
|» » invoice|body|[Invoice](#schemainvoice)|true|An invoice is a commercial document representing a sale of products/services offered by you to a customer. It enumerates all the charges, adjustments, payments, discounts and taxes associated with the sale.<br><br>An invoice is said to be a recurring one when it is has at least one charge for [a plan or an addon item price](/docs/api/items). It is a non-recurring one when it has charges for only charge-item prices or [one-time charges](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/charges.html).<br><br>The item prices for any given billing term of a subscription are billed via an invoice at the beginning of the term (unless the charges are left unbilled). However, item prices that belong to `metered` items are billed at the end of the term via a `pending` invoice that can [close automatically](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing#configuring-metered-billing) or via [an API call](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice). Moreover, when there are no `metered` items in the subscription, the invoices can still be generated as `pending` while [creating](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items) or [updating](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items) a subscription.<br><br>#### Auto-collection<br><br>If [auto-collection](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#auto-collection-status) is enabled, then immediately on invoice generation (or, in case of subscriptions that have `create_pending_invoices` as `true`, on [invoice closure](/docs/api/invoices/close-a-pending-invoice)), the [payment method](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#payment_method) on file is charged:<br><br>* If the payment succeeds, the invoice is marked as `paid`.<br>* On payment failure, the invoice is marked as `payment_due` and [dunning settings](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/dunning-v2.html) are taken into account for payment retries.<br>* If no retry attempts are configured, or when retries are exhausted, the invoice is marked as `not_paid`.<br>* the amount due is zero or negative, the invoice is immediately marked as `paid` and the balance, if any, is added to [excess payments](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/customers.html#excess-payments) for the customer.<br><br>**Note:** If [consolidated invoicing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html) is enabled, the attribute `subscription_id` is unavailable when the invoice has line items from multiple subscriptions. The individual subscription ids are seen under `line_items.subscription_id`.  <br><br>#### Recurring and non-recurring invoices<br><br>A recurring invoice contains at least one line item that is billed on a recurring basis. Specifically, it has at least one [`line_items[]`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#line_items) with `entity_type` set to `plan_item_price` or `addon_item_price`. A non-recurring invoice contains no recurring line items.  <br><br>#### Refundable amount for an invoice<br><br>The refundable amount for an invoice is the (amount paid on the invoice + refundable credit applied on the invoice + taxes withheld on the invoice) minus (amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice). Each of these amounts is obtained from the invoice resource as follows:<br><br>* Amount paid on the invoice: [`amount_paid`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_amount_paid)<br>* Refundable credit applied on the invoice: [`credits_applied`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_credits_applied)<br>* Taxes withheld on the invoice: Sum of [`linked_taxes_withheld[].amount`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_linked_taxes_withheld)<br>* Amount issued as refundable credit notes from the invoice: Sum of [`issued_credit_notes[i].cn_total`](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#invoice_issued_credit_notes) where `issued_credit_notes[i].cn_status` is `refunded` or `refund_due`.<br>|
|» » credit_note|body|[CreditNote](#schemacreditnote)|true|A [Credit Note](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/credit-notes.html) is a document that specifies the money owed by a business to its customer. The seller usually issues a Credit Note for the same or lower amount than the invoice, and then repays the money to the customer or set it off against other 'due' invoices.<br><br>### Credit Note Types<br><br>Credit notes in Chargebee are categorized into three types:<br>1. `adjustment`: Adjustment credit notes are used to adjust the amount of an existing invoice in the `payment_due` or `not_paid` [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status). Use this type of credit note to reduce the invoice amount, typically as a discount to the customer.<br><br>Adjustment credit notes are automatically created in the following cases:<br><br>* When an invoice is written off.<br>* When a subscription is modified with proration enabled, and the invoice for the current term is in the `payment_due` or `not_paid` [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status). 2. `refundable`: Refundable credit notes allow you to return a certain amount to the customer. These credits can be:<br>* Retained for automatic application on future invoices.<br>* Applied to existing unpaid invoices.<br>* Refunded to the customer. Refundable credit notes are automatically created in the following cases:<br>* When an invoice is refunded.<br>* When a subscription is changed or canceled with proration enabled, the invoice for the current term is in the `paid` [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status). Refundable credits are applied to future invoices or can be refunded to the original payment method. 3. `store`: Store credit notes are created for `paid` or `partially_paid` invoice [status](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#status) during subscription changes, such as upgrades, downgrades, or cancellations. Key characteristics of store credits:<br>* No tax component is included at the time of creation.<br>* A credit note document is generated, similar to refundable credits.<br>* Store credits are applied before tax calculations on future invoices.<br><br>**Note:**<br>If you have enabled *consolidated invoicing*<br>, to know the subscriptions attached with a credit note you have to refer [line_item's](/docs/api/credit_notes/credit_note-object#line_items)<br>*subscription_id*<br>. The credit note's *subscription_id*<br>should **not**<br>be used (which will be *null*<br>if the credit note has lines from multiple subscriptions).  <br>Impact on reference invoice  <br>The following updates are made to the reference invoice when a credit note is created/imported:<br><br>* If the credit note `type` is `adjustment`:<br>  * The adjustment credit note details are added to the `adjustment_credit_notes[]` attribute of the invoice.<br>  * The invoice `amount_due` is reduced by the credit note `total`.<br>  * The invoice `status` is updated to `paid` if the invoice `amount_due` equals the credit note `total`.<br>  * The invoice `status` does not change if the invoice `amount_due` is greater than credit note `total`.<br>* If the credit note `type` is `refundable`:<br>  * The refundable credit note details are added to the `issued_credit_notes[]` attribute of the invoice.<br>  * The invoice `status` does not change.<br>* If the credit note `type` is `store`:<br>  * The store credit note details are added to the `issued_credit_notes[]` attribute of the invoice.<br>  * The invoice `status` does not change.<br>|
