<h2 id="tocS_LedgerAccountBalance">LedgerAccountBalance</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaledgeraccountbalance"></a>
<a id="schema_LedgerAccountBalance"></a>
<a id="tocSledgeraccountbalance"></a>
<a id="tocsledgeraccountbalance"></a>

```json
null
```

Credit Grants
-------------

A credit grant is a quantified allocation of credits given to a subscription through a configured [item price](/docs/api/item_prices) or via the [allocate](/docs/api/ledger_operations/allocate) operation, consumed over time through ledger operations.  
**Example**

A subscription receives a credit grant of 100 AI credits as a balance. As the customer uses AI features
(e.g., Image Generation), the provisioned balance is consumed first. Once exhausted, further consumption is deducted from the overdraft balance until its limit is reached.

The Ledger Account Balance object
---------------------------------

The `ledger_account_balance` object is a real-time snapshot of credit grants for a single combination of subscription_id, unit_id and unit_type.

The ledger tracks two balances:

* [**provisioned_balance**](#provisioned_balance): Reflects the credit grants given through the configured item price or allocate operations. These are prepaid credit grants for which the customer has already paid. Any ledger operation will prioritize consuming this balance first.
* [**overdraft_balance**](#overdraft_balance): Reflects the extra limit provided to a subscription in case it exhausts all credit grants before they are renewed or refreshed. Any ledger operation will consume this balance only when the provisioned balance has been exhausted.

**Note**

These two balances are always tracked together for a subscription with credit grants.  
**Example**

A subscription has a credit grant of 100 AI credits, added to its provisioned balance. Once the provisioned balance is exhausted, further consumption is drawn from the overdraft balance up to its configured limit.
screenshot\|/images/account_balance.png

**Returned by**

* [List ledger account balances](/docs/api/ledger_account_balances/list-ledger-account-balances) API.
* Ledger [operations](/docs/api/ledger_operations) such as [allocate](/docs/api/ledger_operations/allocate), [capture](/docs/api/ledger_operations/capture), and [authorize](/docs/api/ledger_operations/authorize).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subscription_id|string|true|none|A unique, immutable identifier for the [subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object#id) this account belongs to.<br>|
|unit_id|string|true|none|Identifier of the credit unit this account tracks. For example, a credit unit id such as `ai_credits`.<br>|
|unit_type|string|true|none|Type of unit used for this balance.<br><br>* credit_unit - The unit represents a credit unit, the type used by credit grants.<br>|
|created_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Unix timestamp (in seconds) indicating when this ledger account balance was first recorded.<br>|
|modified_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Unix timestamp (seconds) when the balance was last updated. For example, after [allocate](/docs/api/ledger_operations/allocate), [capture](/docs/api/ledger_operations/capture), or [authorize](/docs/api/ledger_operations/authorize).<br>|
|resource_version|integer(int64)|false|none|Version number of this resource. The `resource_version` is updated with a new timestamp for every change made to the resource.<br>|
|provisioned_balance|object|false|none|Stores credit grants given through the configured item price. Used first before overdraft.<br>|
|overdraft_balance|object|false|none|Extra credit available after provisioned balance is exhausted.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_LedgerEntry">LedgerEntry</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaledgerentry"></a>
<a id="schema_LedgerEntry"></a>
<a id="tocSledgerentry"></a>
<a id="tocsledgerentry"></a>

```json
null
```

A ledger entry is the lowest-level, immutable record of a single movement of credit grants against one [grant block](/docs/api/grant_blocks). While a [ledger operation](/docs/api/ledger_operations) represents the business action (for example, a `capture` or `authorize`), each operation is expanded internally into one or more ledger entries that describe exactly how individual grant blocks were affected.  
**Behavior**

* Ledger entries are immutable once recorded.
* A single ledger operation can generate multiple entries. When a capture (or other consumption) spans several grant blocks, a ledger entry is created corresponding to each grant block, reflecting the amount captured from that grant block.
* The [`type`](#type) field conveys the direction of each movement; [`amount`](#amount) is always positive.  
**Usage**

Ledger entries provide the granular, per-grant-block audit trail.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|A unique identifier for this ledger entry.  <br>**Behavior**<br><br>* Automatically assigned by the ledger at creation time.<br>* Immutable and cannot be modified once written.<br>|
|subscription_id|string|true|none|A unique, immutable identifier for the [subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object#id) against which this ledger entry was recorded. Always returned.<br>|
|unit_id|string|true|none|Identifier of the credit unit this entry affects. For example, a credit unit id such as `ai_credits`. Always returned.<br>|
|unit_type|string|true|none|Type of unit used for this entry. Always returned.<br><br>* credit_unit - The unit represents a credit unit, the type used by credit grants.<br>|
|account_type|string|true|none|The account this entry belongs to: **provisioned** (credit grants issued per the plan, consumed first) or<br>**overdraft** (consumption beyond the configured credit grants, after the provisioned account is exhausted). Always returned.<br><br>* overdraft -<br>  Allows consumption beyond the configured credit grants. Used once the credit grants in the provisioned account<br>  are exhausted.<br>* provisioned -<br>  Stores the credit grants given as per the plan configuration. Consumption of credit grants is first done<br>  through this account.<br>|
|amount|string|true|none|The number of credit grants moved by this entry against a single grant block.<br>Returned as a decimal string.  <br>**Constraints**<br><br>Maximum supported value: `9999999999999999999999999.9999999999` (up to 25 digits before the decimal and up to 10 digits after).  <br>**Behavior**<br><br>* Always a positive value; the direction of the movement is conveyed by [`type`](#type).<br>|
|grant_block_start_balance|string|true|none|The grant block balance immediately before this ledger entry was applied.<br>Returned as a decimal string.  <br>**Constraints**<br><br>Maximum supported value: `9999999999999999999999999.9999999999` (up to 25 digits before the decimal and up to 10 digits after).<br>|
|grant_block_end_balance|string|true|none|The grant block balance immediately after this ledger entry was applied.<br>Returned as a decimal string.  <br>**Constraints**<br><br>Maximum supported value: `9999999999999999999999999.9999999999` (up to 25 digits before the decimal and up to 10 digits after).<br>|
|account_start_balance|string|true|none|The account balance (provisioned or overdraft, matching [`account_type`](#account_type)) immediately before this ledger entry was applied.<br>Returned as a decimal string.  <br>**Constraints**<br><br>Maximum supported value: `9999999999999999999999999.9999999999` (up to 25 digits before the decimal and up to 10 digits after).<br>|
|account_end_balance|string|true|none|The account balance (provisioned or overdraft, matching [`account_type`](#account_type)) immediately after this ledger entry was applied.<br>Returned as a decimal string.  <br>**Constraints**<br><br>Maximum supported value: `9999999999999999999999999.9999999999` (up to 25 digits before the decimal and up to 10 digits after).<br>|
|type|string|true|none|Specifies the direction of the movement of credit grants recorded by this entry.<br><br>* debit - Credit grants consumed from a grant block.<br>* credit - Credit grants added when a grant block is allocated.<br>* unhold -<br>  Credit grants released allowing the amount to go from hold amount back to the usable amount via<br>  release_authorization or the auto-release job.<br>* hold - Credit grants reserved on a grant block by an authorize operation, moved from usable balance to hold amount.<br>|
|ledger_operation_id|string|true|none|Identifier of the [ledger operation](/docs/api/ledger_operations) that produced this entry. Multiple<br>entries can share the same `ledger_operation_id` when a single operation spans more than one grant block<br>or produces more than one movement.<br>|
|grant_block_id|string|true|none|Identifier of the [grant block](/docs/api/grant_blocks) this entry acts upon.<br>|
|created_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Unix timestamp (in seconds) indicating when this ledger entry was recorded in the ledger.  <br>**Behavior**<br><br>* Automatically set by the ledger at creation time.<br>* Immutable and cannot be modified once written.<br>|
|modified_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Unix timestamp (in seconds) indicating when this ledger entry record was last updated in the ledger.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|unit_type|credit_unit|
|account_type|provisioned|
|account_type|overdraft|
|type|credit|
|type|debit|
|type|hold|
|type|unhold|

<h2 id="tocS_LedgerOperation">LedgerOperation</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaledgeroperation"></a>
<a id="schema_LedgerOperation"></a>
<a id="tocSledgeroperation"></a>
<a id="tocsledgeroperation"></a>

```json
null
```

A ledger operation represents a single action recorded in the ledger that results in a state change. Each ledger operation corresponds to one atomic event, whether initiated externally or internally.  
**Behavior**

* Ledger Operations are immutable once recorded.
* They provide traceability, idempotency, and a complete audit trail of all state transitions.  
**Usage**

Serves as the fundamental unit for representing, tracking, and reconciling all changes within the system.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|A unique identifier for this ledger operation.  <br>**Behavior**<br><br>* In case of external ledger operations, the id can be optionally provided by the upstream system.<br>* In case of internal ledger operations, the id is generated by the ledger.<br>* Immutable and cannot be modified once written.<br>|
|subscription_id|string|true|none|A unique, immutable identifier for the [subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object#id) against which this ledger operation was recorded. Always returned.<br>|
|unit_id|string|true|none|Identifier of the credit unit this ledger operation affects. For example, a credit unit id such as `ai_credits`. Always returned.<br>|
|unit_type|string|true|none|Type of unit used for this ledger operation. Always returned.<br><br>* credit_unit - The unit represents a credit unit, the type used by credit grants.<br>|
|type|string|true|none|Specifies the type of ledger operation, indicating the kind of business event this record represents.  <br>**Types**<br><br>**External Ledger Operations**: Triggered via API calls<br><br>* `allocation` (via the allocate API)<br>* `authorize`<br>* `capture`<br>* `capture_authorization`<br>* `release_authorization`<br><br>**Internal Ledger Operations**: Triggered via system processes<br><br>* `allocation` (plan-driven / configured credit grants)<br>* `expiry`<br>* `rollover`<br>* `void`<br>* `adjustment`<br>* `overdraft_settlement`<br><br>* authorize - Reserves credit grants (moves from `usable_balance` to `hold_amount`) for later capture or release.<br>* release_authorization - Returns a hold to the usable balance, or finalizes an auto-release of the hold.<br>* allocation - Credit grants allocated into an account, such as allocations created from configured credit grants or the allocate operation.<br>* overdraft_settlement - Finalizes overdraft usage once it has been invoiced, marking the used credits as billed.<br>* void - Credit grants removed from a grant block through administrative updates.<br>* rollover - Carry-forward of balance into a new grant block or related rollover run.<br>* capture - Immediate one-step debit of credit grants from the usable balance.<br>* expiry - Credit grants expired from a grant block (and related account movements).<br>* capture_authorization -<br>  Finalizes a hold, converting all or part of the held amount into a final debit; any remainder can be<br>  auto-released.<br>* adjustment - When overdraft is in adjustment mode, new credit grants can adjust an existing overdraft balance.<br>|
|amount|string|true|none|Represents the quantity of credit grants affected by this ledger operation.<br>Returned as a decimal string.  <br>**Constraints**<br><br>Maximum supported value: `9999999999999999999999999.9999999999` (up to 25 digits before the decimal and up to 10 digits after).  <br>**Behavior by Ledger Operation Type**<br><br>* `capture`: Credit grants debited from the account immediately.<br>* `authorize`: Credit grants reserved, moving from usable balance to hold amount.<br>* `capture_authorization`: Credit grants finalized as consumption (converted from hold amount to debited); any remaining hold amount is automatically released.<br>* `release_authorization`: Credit grants released from hold amount back to the usable balance.<br>* `expiry`: Credit grants that have lapsed after the validity and grace period.<br>* `rollover`: Credit grants carried forward into a new grant block.<br>* `void`: Credit grants removed through administrative updates.<br>|
|provisioned_start_balance|string|true|none|The provisioned account balance immediately before this ledger operation was applied.<br>Returned as a decimal string.  <br>**Constraints**<br><br>Maximum supported value: `9999999999999999999999999.9999999999` (up to 25 digits before the decimal and up to 10 digits after).  <br>**Usage**<br><br>Use alongside `provisioned_end_balance` to trace exactly how each ledger operation moved the provisioned account balance over time.<br>|
|provisioned_end_balance|string|true|none|The provisioned account balance immediately after this ledger operation was applied.<br>Returned as a decimal string.  <br>**Constraints**<br><br>Maximum supported value: `9999999999999999999999999.9999999999` (up to 25 digits before the decimal and up to 10 digits after).  <br>**Usage**<br><br>Use alongside `provisioned_start_balance` to trace exactly how each ledger operation moved the provisioned account balance over time.<br>|
|overdraft_start_balance|string|true|none|The overdraft account balance immediately before this ledger operation was applied.<br>Returned as a decimal string.  <br>**Constraints**<br><br>Maximum supported value: `9999999999999999999999999.9999999999` (up to 25 digits before the decimal and up to 10 digits after).  <br>**Usage**<br><br>Use alongside `overdraft_end_balance` to trace exactly how each ledger operation moved the overdraft account balance over time.<br>|
|overdraft_end_balance|string|true|none|The overdraft account balance immediately after this ledger operation was applied.<br>Returned as a decimal string.  <br>**Constraints**<br><br>Maximum supported value: `9999999999999999999999999.9999999999` (up to 25 digits before the decimal and up to 10 digits after).  <br>**Usage**<br><br>Use alongside `overdraft_start_balance` to trace exactly how each ledger operation moved the overdraft account balance over time.<br>|
|parent_ledger_operation_id|string|false|none|The `ledger_operation_id` of the parent `authorize` ledger operation associated with this ledger operation.  <br>**Usage**<br><br>* Present on `capture_authorization` and `release_authorization` ledger operations to identify the hold being finalized or released.<br>* Also present on internally generated release ledger operations (for example, partial-capture remainders) to correlate them back to the original authorization.  <br>**Constraints**<br><br>* Must match the `ledger_operation_id` used in the original `authorize` call.<br>* The same value should be reused across retries.<br>|
|ledger_operation_timestamp|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Unix timestamp (in seconds) representing when the business event occurred in the upstream system. Used for period attribution, grace-period eligibility, and reporting accuracy.  <br>**Note**<br><br>Late or out-of-order submissions appear in arrival order, while attribution and eligibility logic rely on `ledger_operation_timestamp`.  <br>**Constraints**<br><br>* For `authorize`, the `ledger_operation_timestamp` must be within the last 10 minutes from the time of the request.<br>* Grant blocks in the grace period are not eligible for authorization and are excluded from authorization balance checks.<br>* For `capture`, older timestamps are allowed if they fall within the grant block's original validity window (`effective_from` inclusive, `expires_at` exclusive) and the block is still active or in the grace period.<br>* Grant blocks outside their active window (including those in the grace period) are not eligible for authorization and are excluded from balance checks for this ledger operation.<br>|
|auto_release_timestamp|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Unix timestamp (in seconds) indicating when an unfinalized hold amount from an authorize request will be automatically released back to the usable balance.  <br>**Behavior**<br><br>* Applies only to authorize ledger operations.<br>* If not explicitly provided, the system assigns a default expiry.<br>* Defaults to approximately 10 minutes after the authorize request is processed.  <br>**Usage**<br><br>Ensures held credit grants are not locked indefinitely by abandoned or unfinalized authorizations.  <br>**Note**<br><br>* By default, the value reflects what is provided in the request.<br>* If the specified timestamp exceeds the end of the block's grace period, it is adjusted (clamped) to the grace period end and returned in the response.<br>|
|created_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Unix timestamp (in seconds) indicating when this ledger operation was recorded in the system.  <br>**Behavior**<br><br>* Automatically set by the system at the time of persistence.<br>* Immutable and cannot be modified once written.  <br>**Note**<br><br>Serves as the source of truth for ordering ledger operations and tracking how they affected the balance over time.<br>|
|modified_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Unix timestamp (in seconds) indicating when this ledger operation record was last updated in the system.  <br>**Behavior**<br><br>Automatically updated by the system whenever the record is modified.<br>|
|metadata|object|false|none|Optional opaque JSON object carrying additional business context  <br>**Behavior**<br><br>* Stored as-is and returned verbatim by the system.<br>* Not interpreted, validated, or indexed by the system.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|unit_type|credit_unit|
|type|allocation|
|type|capture|
|type|authorize|
|type|release_authorization|
|type|capture_authorization|
|type|expiry|
|type|void|
|type|rollover|
|type|adjustment|
|type|overdraft_settlement|

This resource returns the entitlement level attributes.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|false|none|A case-sensitive display name for the entitlement level. Provide a name that helps you clearly identify the entitlement level. For example: a feature such as `Email Support`<br>can have entitlement levels named as `All weekdays`<br>, `All days`<br>, `40 hours per week`<br>and so on.<br><br>When not provided for `feature.type`<br>`quantity`<br>or `range`<br>, this name is auto-generated as the space-separated concatenation of `levels[].value`<br>and the pluralized version of `unit`.<br>For example, if `levels[].value`<br>is `20`<br>and `unit`<br>is `user`<br>, then `levels[].name`<br>becomes `20 users`<br>.<br>|
|value|string|true|none|The value denoting the entitlement level granted.<br><br>* **When `type` is `quantity`:** this attribute denotes the quantity of units of the feature for this entitlement level. For example, a feature such as `number of users` can have `levels[].value` as `5`, `20`, `50`, and `100`. `levels[].is_unlimited` is used to set the entitlement level to "unlimited".<br>* **When `type` is `range`:** there can be be only two elements in the `levels[]` array; one corresponding to the minimum value (`levels[0]`) and the other to the maximum value (`levels[1]`) of the range of possible entitlement levels. For example, a feature such as `number of users` may have `levels[0].value` = `5` and `levels[1].value` = `50000`. When the upper limit is "unlimited", then `levels[1].value` is not set and `levels[1].is_unlimited` is `true`.<br>* **When `type` is `custom`:** this attribute denotes the value of this custom entitlement level. For example, a feature `Email Support` can have `levels[].value` as one of say, `24×7` and `24×5`.<br>|
|level|integer(int32)|true|none|This attribute represents the order of the entitlement levels from lowest to highest.<br><br>* When `type` is `quantity` or `custom`: The lowest entitlement level has the value `0`, the next higher level has the value `1`, followed by `2`, and so on.<br>* When `type` is `range`: This attribute is `0` for the minimum value and `1` for the maximum value in the range.<br><br>When not defined, it is assumed as the index of the `levels[]`<br>array.<br>|
|is_unlimited|boolean|true|none|When `type`<br>is `quantity`<br>or `range`<br>, this attribute indicates whether the entitlement level corresponds to unlimited units of the feature. Possible values:<br><br>* `true`: The entitlement level corresponds to unlimited units of the feature. `levels[].value` is ignored for this level. This can only be set for the level that has the highest value for `levels[].level.`<br>* `false`: The entitlement level does not correspond to unlimited units of the feature.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_Meter">Meter</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemameter"></a>
<a id="schema_Meter"></a>
<a id="tocSmeter"></a>
<a id="tocsmeter"></a>

```json
null
```

A **meter** captures the usage measurement configuration of a [metered feature](/docs/api/metered_features).

### Meter configuration examples

The following response excerpts show how `query`, `column_definitions`, and `group_by` represent the metering configuration.  
**Availability**

Support for adding `GROUP BY` to metered features and retrieving usage grouped by attributes is an upcoming capability and is not generally available yet. It will be made available in the coming weeks.

When `query` includes a `GROUP BY` clause, the response includes `group_by` as an ordered list of the group-by attributes. Their order matches the order in the `GROUP BY` clause. The `group_by` attribute is not returned when the query does not include a `GROUP BY` clause.

#### Without group-by attributes

```json
{
  "query": "SELECT SUM(request_count) FROM events WHERE status = 'completed'",
  "column_definitions": [
    {
      "column_name": "request_count",
      "data_type": "number"
    },
    {
      "column_name": "status",
      "data_type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

#### With group-by attributes

```json
{
  "query": "SELECT SUM(hours) FROM events WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY gpu_type, region",
  "column_definitions": [
    {
      "column_name": "hours",
      "data_type": "number"
    },
    {
      "column_name": "status",
      "data_type": "string"
    }
  ],
  "group_by": [
    "gpu_type",
    "region"
  ]
}
```

Group-by attributes used only in the `GROUP BY` clause are returned in `group_by` and do not require `column_definitions` entries.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|A unique identifier for the meter. This is the same as `feature.id`.<br>|
|name|string|true|none|A case-sensitive name for the meter. For example: `API Calls`, `Input Tokens`.<br>|
|description|string|false|none|A brief description of the meter.<br>|
|type|string|true|none|The type of meter that determines how usage is measured for the meter.<br><br>* compound - Usage is computed from a mathematical formula combining other meters.<br>* simple - Usage is computed from the SQL `query` over [`usage_event`](/docs/api/usage_events) properties.<br>|
|status|string|false|none|The current status of the meter.<br><br>* active - The meter is active and **new** entitlements can be created towards it.<br>* deleted - The meter has been permanently deleted.<br>* archived - No **new** entitlements can be created towards the meter. However, any pre-existing entitlements from the time that the meter was `active` remain effective.<br>|
|query|string|true|none|The SQL query used to calculate usage from [`usage_event`](/docs/api/usage_events) properties. For example: `SELECT SUM(api_calls) FROM events WHERE status = 'completed'`.<br><br>To group usage by attribute values, include a `GROUP BY` clause. Each distinct set of group-by attribute values forms a separate usage group. For example: `SELECT SUM(hours) FROM events WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY gpu_type, region`. The response returns the group-by attribute names in `group_by`, in the same order.  <br>**Availability**<br><br>Support for adding `GROUP BY` to metered features and retrieving usage grouped by attributes is an upcoming capability and is not generally available yet. It will be made available in the coming weeks.  <br>**Constraints**<br><br>* Properties used in the aggregate expression or `WHERE` clause must be listed in `column_definitions.column_name`.<br>* A group-by attribute used only in the `GROUP BY` clause does not require a `column_definitions` entry. Its value is treated as a string.<br>* The `GROUP BY` clause can contain up to 5 group-by attributes.<br>* Exact duplicate group-by attribute names are not allowed. Names are case-sensitive, so `region, region` is invalid, while `region, Region` identifies two different attributes.<br>|
|created_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|When the meter was created.<br>|
|updated_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|When the meter was last updated.<br>|
|group_by|[string]|false|none|An ordered list of the group-by attributes in the `GROUP BY` clause of `query`. This attribute is returned only when `query` includes a `GROUP BY` clause.  <br>**Availability**<br><br>Support for adding `GROUP BY` to metered features and retrieving usage grouped by attributes is an upcoming capability and is not generally available yet. It will be made available in the coming weeks.<br><br>For example, when `query` is `SELECT SUM(hours) FROM events WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY gpu_type, region`, `group_by` is `["gpu_type", "region"]`.<br>|
|column_definitions|[object]|false|none|Definitions of the columns or properties referenced by the meter's `query`. Each entry describes one column used to measure usage.<br>|
|features|[object]|false|none|The [feature](/docs/api/features) associated with this meter. This array has only one element since any given meter is associated with only one feature.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|simple|
|type|compound|
|status|active|
|status|archived|
|status|deleted|

<h2 id="tocS_MeteredFeature">MeteredFeature</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemameteredfeature"></a>
<a id="schema_MeteredFeature"></a>
<a id="tocSmeteredfeature"></a>
<a id="tocsmeteredfeature"></a>

```json
null
```

A metered feature object represents two things:

* the [feature](/docs/api/features) whose entitlement is consumed based on measured usage.
* the configuration that measures that usage.

### Meter configuration examples

The following response excerpts show how `query`, `column_definitions`, and `group_by` represent the metering configuration.  
**Availability**

Support for adding `GROUP BY` to metered features and retrieving usage grouped by attributes is an upcoming capability and is not generally available yet. It will be made available in the coming weeks.

When `query` includes a `GROUP BY` clause, the response includes `group_by` as an ordered list of the group-by attributes. Their order matches the order in the `GROUP BY` clause. The `group_by` attribute is not returned when the query does not include a `GROUP BY` clause.

#### Without group-by attributes

```json
{
  "query": "SELECT SUM(request_count) FROM events WHERE status = 'completed'",
  "column_definitions": [
    {
      "column_name": "request_count",
      "data_type": "number"
    },
    {
      "column_name": "status",
      "data_type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

#### With group-by attributes

```json
{
  "query": "SELECT SUM(hours) FROM events WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY gpu_type, region",
  "column_definitions": [
    {
      "column_name": "hours",
      "data_type": "number"
    },
    {
      "column_name": "status",
      "data_type": "string"
    }
  ],
  "group_by": [
    "gpu_type",
    "region"
  ]
}
```

Group-by attributes used only in the `GROUP BY` clause are returned in `group_by` and do not require `column_definitions` entries.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|A unique identifier for the metered feature. This is the same as `feature.id`.<br>|
|name|string|false|none|A case-sensitive name for the metered feature. For example: `API Calls`, `Input Tokens`.<br>|
|description|string|false|none|A brief description of the metered feature.<br>|
|type|string|false|none|The type of meter. Determines how usage is measured for the metered feature.<br><br>* compound - Usage is computed from a mathematical formula combining other meters.<br>* simple - Usage is computed from a SQL `query` over [`usage_event`](/docs/api/usage_events) properties.<br>|
|status|string|false|none|The current status of the metered feature.<br><br>* active - The metered feature is active and **new** [entitlements](/docs/api/entitlements) and [subscription entitlements](/docs/api/subscription_entitlements) can be created for it.<br>* deleted - The metered feature has been permanently deleted.<br>* archived - No **new** [entitlements](/docs/api/entitlements) and [subscription entitlements](/docs/api/subscription_entitlements) can be created for the metered feature. However, any pre-existing entitlements and subscription entitlements remain effective.<br>|
|query|string|false|none|The SQL query used to calculate usage from [`usage_event`](/docs/api/usage_events) properties. For example: `SELECT SUM(api_calls) FROM events WHERE status = 'completed'`.<br><br>To group usage by attribute values, include a `GROUP BY` clause. Each distinct set of group-by attribute values forms a separate usage group. For example: `SELECT SUM(hours) FROM events WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY gpu_type, region`. The response returns the group-by attribute names in `group_by`, in the same order.  <br>**Availability**<br><br>Support for adding `GROUP BY` to metered features and retrieving usage grouped by attributes is an upcoming capability and is not generally available yet. It will be made available in the coming weeks.  <br>**Constraints**<br><br>* Properties used in the aggregate expression or `WHERE` clause must be listed in `column_definitions.column_name`.<br>* A group-by attribute used only in the `GROUP BY` clause does not require a `column_definitions` entry. Its value is treated as a string.<br>* The `GROUP BY` clause can contain up to 5 group-by attributes.<br>* Exact duplicate group-by attribute names are not allowed. Names are case-sensitive, so `region, region` is invalid, while `region, Region` identifies two different attributes.  <br>**Usage reporting and subscription billing**<br><br>For a metered feature whose `query` includes a `GROUP BY` clause, grouped usage is available in [Retrieve usage summary for a subscription](/docs/api/usage_summary/retrieve-usage-summary-for-a-subscription) and [Retrieve usages for an invoice as PDF](/docs/api/usages/retrieve-usages-for-an-invoice-as-pdf). These groups are for reporting only. Subscription billing uses the overall aggregate for the metered feature and does not bill each group separately.<br><br>For example, a `SUM` query can return 60 hours for `region=us-east` and 40 hours for `region=eu-west`. The reporting operations can display both groups. Subscription billing uses the overall aggregate of 100 hours.<br>|
|group_by|[string]|false|none|An ordered list of the group-by attributes in the `GROUP BY` clause of `query`. This attribute is returned only when `query` includes a `GROUP BY` clause.  <br>**Availability**<br><br>Support for adding `GROUP BY` to metered features and retrieving usage grouped by attributes is an upcoming capability and is not generally available yet. It will be made available in the coming weeks.<br><br>For example, when `query` is `SELECT SUM(hours) FROM events WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY gpu_type, region`, `group_by` is `["gpu_type", "region"]`.<br>|
|column_definitions|[object]|false|none|Definitions of the columns or properties referenced by the metered feature's `query`.<br>|
|features|[object]|false|none|The [feature](/docs/api/features) associated with this metered feature. This array has only one element since any given metered feature is associated with only one feature.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|simple|
|type|compound|
|status|active|
|status|archived|
|status|deleted|

<h2 id="tocS_OfferFulfillment">OfferFulfillment</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaofferfulfillment"></a>
<a id="schema_OfferFulfillment"></a>
<a id="tocSofferfulfillment"></a>
<a id="tocsofferfulfillment"></a>

```json
null
```

Offer fulfillment allows you to initiate, update, and retrieve the lifecycle of an offer fulfillment, after a personalized offer has been accepted. Whether the personalized offer triggers a direct billing change, a hosted checkout flow, or a redirect-based workflow, these APIs track acceptance, execution status, and completion, providing a consistent interface for fulfillment tracking and notifications.

**Features of this object:**

* Records fulfillment IDs for tracking and reference.
* Captures status (`in_progress`, `completed`, `failed`).
* Stores redirect/checkout URLs as needed.
* Contains timestamps for creation, completion, or failure.
* Includes error codes and messages for failure analysis.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|ID of the fulfillment that was created.<br>|
|personalized_offer_id|string|true|none|ID of the personalized offer that was accepted.<br>|
|option_id|string|true|none|ID of the offer option that was selected by the user.<br>|
|processing_type|string|true|none|The processing mode of the option. This indicates how the offer option is fulfilled: e.g., a direct billing change, a checkout flow, or a redirect to a URL.<br><br>* webhook - Chargebee triggers webhook and fulfillment is processed by your system<br>* email - Chargebee sends an email as configured in the Growth application and the fulfillment is processed by your system<br>* checkout - The offer fulfillment is processed using Chargebee hosted checkout<br>* url_redirect - The offer fulfillment is processed by your system<br>* billing_update - The offer fulfillment is processed by Chargebee<br>|
|status|string|true|none|Current status of the offer fulfillment process.<br><br>* in_progress - The offer fulfillment is underway (not yet completed).<br>* completed - The offer was successfully applied . For URL redirects, this might be returned immediately if the action is completed, potentially along with a redirect_url if the user should be navigated to a specific page.<br>* failed -<br>  The offer fulfillment failed. The `error object`<br>  field will be present to provide more details in this case.<br>|
|redirect_url|string|false|none|A URL to which the user should be redirected. Returned only if the offer's processing type is billing_update or url_redirect<br>|
|failed_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Timestamp when the fulfillment failed (present only when status = failed).<br>|
|created_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Timestamp when the fulfillment record was created.<br>|
|completed_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Timestamp when the fulfillment succeeded (present only when status = completed).<br>|
|error|object|false|none|Error details describing the reason for failure (present only if status is failed).<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|processing_type|billing_update|
|processing_type|checkout|
|processing_type|url_redirect|
|processing_type|webhook|
|processing_type|email|
|status|in_progress|
|status|completed|
|status|failed|

<h2 id="tocS_OmnichannelOneTimeOrder">OmnichannelOneTimeOrder</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaomnichannelonetimeorder"></a>
<a id="schema_OmnichannelOneTimeOrder"></a>
<a id="tocSomnichannelonetimeorder"></a>
<a id="tocsomnichannelonetimeorder"></a>

```json
null
```

Represents a one-time in-app product purchase from Apple App Store or Google Play Store, normalized into Chargebee's omnichannel model.

Omnichannel one-time orders are typically created when you [record a purchase](/docs/api/recorded_purchases/record-a-purchase) and may be updated via store notifications (for example, refunds). Unlike subscriptions, one-time order items do not carry a recurring `status` field; cancellation is expressed via item `cancelled_at` / `cancellation_reason`.

**Apple App Store** : Parent `id_at_source` is the **Transaction ID** . Nested `purchase_transaction.id_at_source` is the same Transaction ID for the purchase row.

**Google Play Store** : Parent `id_at_source` is the **purchase token** . Nested `purchase_transaction.id_at_source` is the **Order ID** (`GPA....`).

See [omnichannel events](/docs/api/omnichannel_events) for recording and cancel mappings, and [`omnichannel_transaction`](/docs/api/omnichannel_transactions) for price / `transacted_at` guidance.  
**Note:**
This resource specifically represents in-app product purchases made via the Apple App Store and Google Play Store.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|The ID generated by Chargebee for the recorded one-time order.<br>|
|app_id|string|true|none|App Identifier in Chargebee. This is the handle created by Chargebee for your app. To get the `app_id`:<br><br>* For **Apple** , follow [these steps](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/mobile-subscriptions/omnichannel-app-store#create-an-omnichannel-subscription-for-in-app-purchases).<br>* For **Google** , follow [these steps](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/mobile-subscriptions/omnichannel-play-store#connect-google-app-to-chargebee-to-generate-unique-app-id-and-notifications-url).<br>|
|customer_id|string|false|none|The `id`<br>of the [customer](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#id)<br>object that is associated with this one-time order.<br>|
|id_at_source|string|true|none|The store-native identifier for this one-time order.<br><br>**Apple App Store** : The App Store **Transaction ID** for the purchase (same value as `purchase_transaction.id_at_source` for the initial purchase row).<br><br>**Google Play Store** : The Google Play **purchase token** for the one-time product purchase --- not the **Order ID** . The Order ID (`GPA....`) is on `purchase_transaction.id_at_source`.<br>|
|origin|string|false|none|Country code indicating where the one-time order originated, such as `US`<br>for the United States.<br>|
|source|string|true|none|The storefront where the one-time order was originally made and managed (`apple_app_store` or `google_play_store`).<br><br>* google_play_store - The source of the app is `google_play_store`.<br>* apple_app_store - The source of the app is `apple_app_store`.<br>|
|created_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Timestamp when the `omnichannel_one_time_order` was created in Chargebee.<br>|
|resource_version|integer(int64)|false|none|Version number of this resource. The `resource_version`<br>is updated with a new timestamp in milliseconds for every change made to the resource. This attribute will be present only if the resource has been updated after 2016-09-28.<br>|
|omnichannel_one_time_order_items|[object]|true|none|List of `omnichannel_one_time_order_item` objects in the one-time order.<br>|
|purchase_transaction|object|false|none|Details of the purchase transaction associated with the one-time order.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|source|apple_app_store|
|source|google_play_store|
|source|roku|
|source|amazon_app_store|

<h2 id="tocS_OmnichannelSubscription">OmnichannelSubscription</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaomnichannelsubscription"></a>
<a id="schema_OmnichannelSubscription"></a>
<a id="tocSomnichannelsubscription"></a>
<a id="tocsomnichannelsubscription"></a>

```json
null
```

Represents a subscription purchased and managed in an external app marketplace (`apple_app_store` or `google_play_store`), normalized into Chargebee's omnichannel model.

Omnichannel subscriptions are typically created when you [record a purchase](/docs/api/recorded_purchases/record-a-purchase) and are kept in sync via store server notifications. They are store-managed: lifecycle changes come from Apple or Google, not from the Chargebee Subscriptions API.

Use [omnichannel statuses](/docs/api/omnichannel_statuses) for how store statuses map to `omnichannel_subscription_item.status`, and [omnichannel events](/docs/api/omnichannel_events) for notification-to-webhook mappings.

Chargebee records introductory and promotional offers on [`omnichannel_subscription_item_offers`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscriptions/omnichannel_subscription-object#omnichannel_subscription_items_omnichannel_subscription_item_offers). Win-back offers and offer codes are not supported.  
**Identifier tip:** Parent `id_at_source` is the Apple **Transaction ID** or Google **purchase token** . Nested `initial_purchase_transaction.id_at_source` is the Apple **Transaction ID** or Google **Order ID** (`GPA....`). See attribute descriptions below.  
**Note:**
This resource represents in-app subscriptions made on Apple App Store and Google Play Store.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|The ID generated by Chargebee for the omnichannel subscription.<br>|
|id_at_source|string|true|none|The identifier of the subscription in the `source`.<br><br>**Apple App Store** : The original purchase **Transaction ID** (stable for the subscription lifecycle).<br><br>**Google Play Store** : The subscription **purchase token** . This value can change when Google issues a new token after certain subscription changes; Chargebee updates `id_at_source` to the latest token.<br>> **Note:** Do not confuse this with `initial_purchase_transaction.id_at_source`. For Google, the nested transaction uses the **Order ID** (`GPA....`), not the purchase token.<br>|
|app_id|string|true|none|App Identifier in Chargebee. This is the handle created by Chargebee for your app. To get the `app_id`:<br><br>* For **Apple** , follow [these steps](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/mobile-subscriptions/omnichannel-app-store#create-an-omnichannel-subscription-for-in-app-purchases).<br>* For **Google** , follow [these steps](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/mobile-subscriptions/omnichannel-play-store#connect-google-app-to-chargebee-to-generate-unique-app-id-and-notifications-url).<br>|
|source|string|true|none|The storefront where the purchase is originally made and managed (`apple_app_store` or `google_play_store`).<br><br>* google_play_store - The purchase originated from the Google Play Store.<br>* apple_app_store - The purchase originated from the Apple App Store.<br>|
|customer_id|string|false|none|The `id`<br>of the [customer](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#id)<br>object that is associated with this purchase.<br>|
|origin|string|false|none|The two-letter [ISO 3166 alpha-2](https://www.iso.org/iso-3166-country-codes.html) country code of the store where the subscription was purchased, such as `US` for the United States. For Apple App Store, this is the storefront country. For Google Play, this is the subscription region code. The attribute may be absent when the store does not provide a country.<br>|
|created_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Timestamp when the `omnichannel_subscription` was created in Chargebee.<br>|
|purchased_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Timestamp (UTC) when the subscription was originally purchased in the app marketplace (initial purchase). This corresponds to the time of the initial purchase transaction in the [`source`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscriptions/omnichannel_subscription-object#source).<br>|
|updated_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Indicates timestamp when the `omnichannel_subscription` was last updated<br>.<br>|
|resource_version|integer(int64)|false|none|Version number of this resource. The `resource_version`<br>is updated with a new timestamp in milliseconds for every change made to the resource.<br>|
|omnichannel_subscription_items|[object]|true|none|Items associated with the omnichannel_subscription.<br>|
|initial_purchase_transaction|object|false|none|Refers to the record created when a customer makes their first purchase.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|source|apple_app_store|
|source|google_play_store|
|source|roku|
|source|amazon_app_store|

<h2 id="tocS_OmnichannelSubscriptionItem">OmnichannelSubscriptionItem</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaomnichannelsubscriptionitem"></a>
<a id="schema_OmnichannelSubscriptionItem"></a>
<a id="tocSomnichannelsubscriptionitem"></a>
<a id="tocsomnichannelsubscriptionitem"></a>

```json
null
```

Represents a product entitlement (item) within an [`omnichannel_subscription`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscriptions) purchased on Apple App Store or Google Play Store.

Status, auto-renew, term dates, and cancel/expire reasons live on this resource. See [omnichannel statuses](/docs/api/omnichannel_statuses) for store mappings.

Chargebee records introductory and promotional offers on [`omnichannel_subscription_item_offers`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_items/omnichannel_subscription_item-object#omnichannel_subscription_item_offers). Win-back offers and offer codes are not supported.

When `has_scheduled_changes` is `true`, use [List scheduled changes](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_items/list-scheduled-changes-for-omnichannel-subscription-item) to retrieve deferred product or pause changes.  
**Note:**
This resource represents in-app subscription items made on Apple App Store and Google Play Store.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|Uniquely identifies an `omnichannel_subscription_item`.<br>|
|item_id_at_source|string|true|none|Product identifier of this subscription item in the source store.<br><br>**Apple App Store**: The App Store Connect product identifier.<br><br>**Google Play Store** : The Google Play product / base-plan identifier associated with the active entitlement. See also `item_parent_id_at_source` when a parent/child hierarchy applies.<br>|
|item_parent_id_at_source|string|false|none|Parent product identifier in the source store, when the store exposes a parent/child product hierarchy.<br><br>**Apple App Store**: Typically the subscription group / parent product context when applicable.<br><br>**Google Play Store**: Typically the parent product ID associated with the base plan / offer hierarchy when applicable.<br>|
|status|string|true|none|Status of the `omnichannel_subscription_item`. Status lives on the item, not on the parent subscription.<br>[Learn more](/docs/api/omnichannel_statuses) about status and store mappings.<br><br>* in_grace_period - Billing is retrying during a grace period; service should typically continue.<br>* in_dunning - Billing is retrying after a payment failure and access may be restricted (Apple billing retry / Google account hold).<br>* expired - The subscription item expired for a non-cancellation reason. See `expiration_reason`.<br>* active -<br>  The subscription item is active and entitled for the current term.<br><br>  **Google Play Store** : Also used when Google has canceled auto-renew but the term has not ended (`auto_renew_status` = `off`).<br>* cancelled - The subscription item is cancelled (entitlement ended due to cancellation / revoke / refund contexts). See `cancellation_reason`.<br>* paused - The subscription item is paused. See `resumes_at` when available.<br>|
|auto_renew_status|string|false|none|Whether the subscription item is set to auto-renew at the end of the current term (`on` or `off`).<br><br>**Google Play Store** : When the customer cancels but remains in-term, `status` stays `active` and `auto_renew_status` is `off`.<br><br>* on - Auto-renewal is enabled for the `omnichannel_subscription_item`.<br>* off - Auto-renewal is disabled for the `omnichannel_subscription_item`.<br>|
|current_term_start|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Start of the current billing period of the subscription item. Applicable when `status` is `active`.<br>|
|current_term_end|integer(unix-time)|false|none|End of the current billing period of the subscription item. Applicable when [`status`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_items/omnichannel_subscription_item-object#status) is `active`.<br><br>**Apple App Store** : Closest analogue to [`next_billing_at`](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object#next_billing_at) because Apple does not expose a separate next-renewal timestamp. Apple may renew up to 24 hours before expiry and, in billing retry, may retry for up to 60 days. [Learn more](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/storekit/in-app_purchase/original_api_for_in-app_purchase/subscriptions_and_offers/handling_subscriptions_billing#3221910).<br><br>**Google Play Store** : Corresponds to the subscription expiry / next billing boundary from Play. When the customer has canceled but the term has not ended, `status` remains `active` with `auto_renew_status` = `off` (see [omnichannel statuses](/docs/api/omnichannel_statuses)).<br>|
|expired_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Timestamp when the subscription associated with the `omnichannel_subscription_item` expired in the `source`.<br>|
|expiration_reason|string|false|none|Specifies the reason for the subscription expiration. Present when `status` is `expired`.<br><br>**Apple App Store** : Commonly maps from Apple expiration intents such as `BILLING_ERROR`, `PRODUCT_NOT_AVAILABLE`, and `OTHER`.<br><br>**Google Play Store** : User-initiated and merchant-revoked expirations typically map to `cancelled` with a `cancellation_reason` instead of `expired`.<br><br>* subscription_not_found_in_source - Indicates that the subscription expired because it was not found in the [`source`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscriptions/omnichannel_subscription-object#source).<br>* other -<br>  The subscription associated with the item expired for an unspecified reason.<br><br>  **Apple App Store** : Maps from expiration intent `OTHER`.<br>* product_not_available -<br>  The product was unavailable for purchase at the time of renewal.<br><br>  **Apple App Store** : Maps from expiration intent `PRODUCT_NOT_AVAILABLE`.<br>* billing_error -<br>  Billing error, such as invalid customer payment information.<br><br>  **Apple App Store** : Maps from expiration intent `BILLING_ERROR`.<br>|
|expiration_reason_at_source|string|false|none|none|
|cancelled_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Timestamp when the subscription associated with the `omnichannel_subscription_item` was cancelled in the `source`.<br>|
|cancellation_reason|string|false|none|The reason the subscription item was cancelled. Present when `status` is `cancelled`. Store applicability varies by enum value.<br><br>* refunded_for_other_reason -<br>  The subscription was cancelled and refunded for another reason.<br><br>  **Apple App Store**: Commonly set for refund notifications with a non-app-issue refund reason.<br><br>  **Google Play Store**: Not typically used for this reason code.<br>* refunded_due_to_app_issue -<br>  The subscription was cancelled and refunded due to an app issue.<br><br>  **Apple App Store**: Commonly set for refund notifications with an app-issue refund reason.<br><br>  **Google Play Store**: Not typically used for this reason code.<br>* customer_did_not_consent_to_price_increase -<br>  The customer did not consent to a price increase for the subscription item.<br><br>  **Apple App Store** : Maps from expiration intent `CUSTOMER_DID_NOT_CONSENT_TO_PRICE_INCREASE`.<br><br>  **Google Play Store**: Not typically used for this reason code.<br>* customer_cancelled -<br>  The customer voluntarily cancelled the subscription.<br><br>  **Apple App Store** : Commonly maps from expiration intent `CUSTOMER_CANCELLED`.<br><br>  **Google Play Store**: Commonly maps from user-initiated cancellation / cancel-at-term-end flows.<br>* merchant_revoked -<br>  The merchant revoked access to the subscription.<br><br>  **Apple App Store** : Can apply when access is revoked (for example, `REVOKED` / related refund revoke flows).<br><br>  **Google Play Store** : Commonly maps from revoke / chargeback-style contexts (for example, `SUBSCRIPTION_REVOKED`).<br>|
|cancellation_reason_at_source|string|false|none|none|
|grace_period_expires_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Timestamp when the grace period for the `omnichannel_subscription_item` expires in the `source`.<br><br>**Apple App Store** : Present when the item is in `in_grace_period` (Apple billing grace period).<br><br>**Google Play Store** : Present when the item is in `in_grace_period` (`SUBSCRIPTION_STATE_IN_GRACE_PERIOD`).<br>|
|resumes_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Timestamp when the subscription automatically resumes after being set to `paused`.<br><br>**Google Play Store**: Typically present for paused subscriptions.<br><br>**Apple App Store**: Pause is not generally applicable in the same way; this attribute is usually absent.<br>|
|has_scheduled_changes|boolean|true|none|Indicates whether the `omnichannel_subscription_item` has any scheduled changes. When `true`, use [List scheduled changes for an omnichannel subscription item](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_items/list-scheduled-changes-for-omnichannel-subscription-item) to retrieve them.<br>|
|updated_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Timestamp when the `omnichannel_subscription_item` was last updated in Chargebee.<br>|
|resource_version|integer(int64)|false|none|Version number of this resource. The `resource_version`<br>is updated with a new timestamp in milliseconds for every change made to the resource.<br>|
|omnichannel_subscription_item_offers|[object]|false|none|Represents the `omnichannel_subscription_item_offers`<br>associated with the `omnichannel_subscription_item`.<br>Chargebee supports introductory and promotional offers.<br>Win-back offers and offer codes are not supported.<br>|
|upcoming_renewal|object|false|none|Information about the upcoming renewal price.<br><br>**Google Play Store** : Present when Google provides renewal price information and [`auto_renew_status`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_items/omnichannel_subscription_item-object#auto_renew_status) is `on`.<br><br>**Apple App Store**: Not applicable; this field is absent.<br>|
|linked_item|object|false|none|Represents an active product catalog mapping between an `omnichannel_subscription_item`<br>and a Chargebee `item`.<br>Use this attribute to retrieve entitlements for the `omnichannel_subscription_item`<br>that are associated with the linked Chargebee `item`.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_OmnichannelSubscriptionItemMetric">OmnichannelSubscriptionItemMetric</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaomnichannelsubscriptionitemmetric"></a>

```json
null
```

This resource represents the revenue metrics, such as MRR, computed for an [Omnichannel subscription item](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_items).

This resource is available only with [Product Catalog 2.0](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/product-catalog.html) and the Omnichannel Subscriptions feature. It is not available through any standalone API operation; it is returned only in the [`omnichannel_subscription_item_mrr_updated`](/docs/api/events/webhook/omnichannel_subscription_item_mrr_updated) webhook event payload.

The event `content` includes the related [`omnichannel_subscription`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscriptions), [`omnichannel_subscription_item`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_items), and `omnichannel_subscription_item_metric`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|customer_id|string|false|none|The `id` of the [customer](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#id) object<br>associated with this metric.<br>|
|omnichannel_subscription_id|string|false|none|The `id`<br>of the [omnichannel_subscription](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscriptions/omnichannel_subscription-object)<br>associated with this metric.<br>|
|omnichannel_subscription_item_id|string|false|none|The `id`<br>of the [omnichannel_subscription_item](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_items/omnichannel_subscription_item-object)<br>associated with this metric.<br>|
|item_id_at_source|string|true|none|Product identifier of the subscription item in the [`source`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscriptions/omnichannel_subscription-object#source) store.<br><br>**Apple App Store**: The App Store Connect product identifier.<br><br>**Google Play Store**: The Google Play product / base-plan identifier associated with the active entitlement.<br>|
|mrr_currency|string|false|none|The three-letter [ISO 4217](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/supported-currencies.html) currency code in which the MRR is calculated. May be absent when the MRR is unavailable.<br>|
|mrr_units|integer(int64)|false|none|The whole-unit portion of the calculated MRR amount. Defaults to **0** when the MRR is zero or unavailable.<br>For example:<br>if `mrr_currency` is **USD** (i.e. two decimal currency), then the unit value for **USD** **1.23** will be **1**<br>if `mrr_currency` is **JPY** (i.e. zero decimal currency), then the unit value for **JPY** **123** will be **123**<br>|
|mrr_nanos|integer(int64)|false|none|The fractional portion of the calculated MRR amount, in nanos (billionths of the currency unit). Defaults to **0** when the MRR is zero or unavailable.<br>The value must be between **0** and **+999,999,999** inclusive.<br>For example:<br>if `mrr_currency` is **USD** (i.e. two decimal currency), then the nanos value for **USD** **1.23** will be **230,000,000**<br>if `mrr_currency` is **JPY** (i.e. zero decimal currency), then the nanos value for **JPY** **123** will be **0**<br>|
|effective_from|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Timestamp from which this metric value is effective.<br>|
|calculated_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|The time at which Chargebee computed this metric value.<br>|
|created_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Indicates timestamp when the `omnichannel_subscription_item_metric`<br>was created in Chargebee.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_OmnichannelSubscriptionItemScheduledChange">OmnichannelSubscriptionItemScheduledChange</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaomnichannelsubscriptionitemscheduledchange"></a>
<a id="schema_OmnichannelSubscriptionItemScheduledChange"></a>
<a id="tocSomnichannelsubscriptionitemscheduledchange"></a>
<a id="tocsomnichannelsubscriptionitemscheduledchange"></a>

```json
null
```

Represents a future change to an [`omnichannel_subscription_item`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_items) that the store will apply later (typically at the end of the current term).

**Apple App Store** : Created when the customer schedules a **downgrade** within the same subscription group (`DID_CHANGE_RENEWAL_PREF` / `DOWNGRADE`). `change_type` is typically `downgrade`. Upgrades apply immediately and do **not** create this resource.

**Google Play Store** : Created when a product change uses the **`DEFERRED`** replacement mode (applied at term end). Immediate changes use `CHARGE_PRORATED_PRICE` and do **not** create this resource. A `change_type` of `pause` may appear for scheduled pause flows; confirm mapping against [omnichannel events](/docs/api/omnichannel_events).

Retrieve scheduled changes with [List scheduled changes for an omnichannel subscription item](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_items/list-scheduled-changes-for-omnichannel-subscription-item) when [`has_scheduled_changes`](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_items/omnichannel_subscription_item-object#has_scheduled_changes) is `true`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|Uniquely identifies an `omnichannel_subscription_item_scheduled_change`.<br>|
|omnichannel_subscription_item_id|string|false|none|The `id`<br>of the [omnichannel subscription item](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscription_items/omnichannel_subscription_item-object#id)<br>associated with this scheduled change.<br>|
|scheduled_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Timestamp when the scheduled change is expected to take effect (typically at the end of the current term).<br>|
|change_type|string|true|none|Indicates the type of scheduled change.<br><br>**Apple App Store** : Scheduled product downgrades typically use `downgrade`.<br><br>**Google Play Store** : Deferred product replacements (`DEFERRED` replacement mode) are represented here. Immediate prorated replacements do not create this resource.<br><br>See also [omnichannel events](/docs/api/omnichannel_events) for store notification mappings.<br><br>* pause -<br>  A scheduled pause of the subscription item, applied later (usually at term end).<br><br>  **Google Play Store**: May correspond to a pause that is scheduled rather than applied immediately (for example, pause-schedule notifications). Confirm store mapping with your Chargebee omnichannel configuration.<br><br>  **Apple App Store**: Pause scheduling is generally not applicable in the same way.<br>* downgrade -<br>  A scheduled product change to a different (typically lower) product / plan, applied later (usually at term end).<br><br>  **Apple App Store** : Created for scheduled downgrades (`DID_CHANGE_RENEWAL_PREF` / `DOWNGRADE`).<br><br>  **Google Play Store** : Used for deferred product changes (`DEFERRED` replacement mode). Confirm with your integration whether all deferred replacements use this enum or only true downgrades.<br>|
|created_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Timestamp when the `omnichannel_subscription_item_scheduled_change` was created in Chargebee.<br>|
|modified_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Timestamp when the `omnichannel_subscription_item_scheduled_change` was last modified in Chargebee.<br>|
|resource_version|integer(int64)|false|none|Version number of this resource. The `resource_version`<br>is updated with a new timestamp in milliseconds for every change made to the resource.<br>|
|current_state|object|false|none|Snapshot of relevant item attributes before the scheduled change takes effect.<br>|
|scheduled_state|object|false|none|Snapshot of the attributes that will apply after the scheduled change takes effect.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|change_type|downgrade|
|change_type|pause|

<h2 id="tocS_OmnichannelTransaction">OmnichannelTransaction</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaomnichanneltransaction"></a>
<a id="schema_OmnichannelTransaction"></a>
<a id="tocSomnichanneltransaction"></a>
<a id="tocsomnichanneltransaction"></a>

```json
null
```

A unified representation of a store purchase or renewal transaction across Apple App Store and Google Play Store.

Use `id_at_source` to correlate with the store-native transaction identifier:

* **Apple App Store** : App Store **Transaction ID**
* **Google Play Store** : Google Play **Order ID** (`GPA....`)

Parent subscription / one-time-order resources use purchase-token semantics for Google `id_at_source`; do not treat those as interchangeable with this transaction Order ID.

### Apple App Store

The [price](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appstoreservernotifications/price) value reflects the price you configured in App Store Connect, which the system records at the time of transaction ([transacted_at](/docs/api/omnichannel_transactions/omnichannel_transaction-object#transacted_at)) after the discount if any offers are applied.  
**Important**
For financial and accounting purposes, use the App Store Connect reporting tools. For more information, see [Download financial reports](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/getting-paid/download-financial-reports) and [Overview of reporting tools](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/measure-app-performance/overview-of-reporting-tools).
[Learn more](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appstoreservernotifications/price) about price in Apple App Store.

### Google Play Store

Google Play does not always expose a complete transaction amount or purchase time for every notification path. When Google provides price / time data for a transaction, Chargebee records `price_*` and `transacted_at`; otherwise these attributes may be absent. Some Google one-time-order samples include price and `transacted_at` on `purchase_transaction`.

Transactions can be linked to subscriptions and/or one-time orders via `linked_omnichannel_subscriptions` and `linked_omnichannel_one_time_orders`. Chargebee may also emit [`omnichannel_transaction_created`](/docs/api/events/webhook/omnichannel_transaction_created) when a new transaction row is recorded.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|The ID generated by Chargebee for the omnichannel transaction.<br>|
|id_at_source|string|true|none|The store-native identifier for this transaction.<br><br>**Apple App Store** : The App Store **Transaction ID** for this purchase or renewal.<br><br>**Google Play Store** : The Google Play **Order ID** (typically `GPA....`) --- not the subscription or one-time-order **purchase token** (those live on `omnichannel_subscription.id_at_source` / `omnichannel_one_time_order.id_at_source`).<br>|
|app_id|string|true|none|App Identifier in Chargebee. This is the handle created by Chargebee for your app. To get the `app_id`:<br><br>* For **Apple** , follow [these steps](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/mobile-subscriptions/omnichannel-app-store#create-an-omnichannel-subscription-for-in-app-purchases).<br>* For **Google** , follow [these steps](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/mobile-subscriptions/omnichannel-play-store#connect-google-app-to-chargebee-to-generate-unique-app-id-and-notifications-url).<br>|
|price_currency|string|false|none|The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code associated with the transaction (`price_currency`), when price data is available.<br>|
|price_units|integer(int64)|false|none|The whole units of the amount, when price data is available.<br>For example:<br>if `price_currency` is **USD** (two-decimal currency), then the unit value for **USD** **1.23** will be **1**<br>if `price_currency` is **JPY** (zero-decimal currency), then the unit value for **JPY** **123** will be **123**<br>if `price_currency` is **BHD** (three-decimal currency), then the unit value for **BHD** **1.234** will be **1**<br>|
|price_nanos|integer(int64)|false|none|The fraction part of the amount, when price data is available.<br>The value must be between **0** and **+999,999,999** inclusive.<br>For example:<br>If `price_currency` is **USD** (two-decimal currency), then nanos value for **USD** **1.23** will be **230,000,000**<br>If `price_currency` is **JPY** (zero-decimal currency), then nanos value for **JPY** **123** will be **0**<br>If `price_currency` is **BHD** (three-decimal currency), then nanos value for **BHD** **1.234** will be **234,000,000**<br>|
|type|string|true|none|Type of omnichannel transaction. Applies to both subscription and one-time-order purchase flows.<br><br>* renewal - Indicates a renewal transaction for a previously completed subscription purchase. Not used for one-time orders.<br>* purchase - Indicates an initial purchase transaction (subscription or one-time order).<br>|
|transacted_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Timestamp when the transaction occurred in the store, when available.<br>|
|created_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Timestamp when the omnichannel transaction was created in Chargebee.<br>|
|resource_version|integer(int64)|false|none|Version number of this resource. The `resource_version`<br>is updated with a new timestamp in milliseconds for every change made to the resource.<br>|
|linked_omnichannel_subscriptions|[object]|false|none|A list of `omnichannel_subscription` objects linked to this transaction.<br>|
|linked_omnichannel_one_time_orders|[object]|false|none|A list of `omnichannel_one_time_order` objects linked to this transaction.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|purchase|
|type|renewal|

<h2 id="tocS_Order">Order</h2>

**Note:**
This doc is for the latest version of Chargebee Orders. If you enabled Chargebee Orders before *September-30-2018*
, you may be using the legacy version of the feature and its API. For help in migrating to the current system or using the legacy API for Chargebee Orders, please [contact support](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/kb/getting-started/how-to-contact-chargebees-support-team?utm_source=docs_api&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=support)

Orders are automatically generated for an invoice when it gets paid, based on the shipping preference chosen for the invoice's product and the shipping date configuration. They can be updated either via api or merchant web console (a.k.a admin console).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|Uniquely identifies the order. It is the api identifier for the order<br>|
|document_number|string|false|none|The order's serial number<br>|
|invoice_id|string|false|none|The invoice number which acts as an identifier for invoice and is generated sequentially.<br>|
|subscription_id|string|false|none|The subscription for which the order is created<br>|
|customer_id|string|false|none|The customer for which the order is created<br>|
|status|string|false|none|The status of this order.<br><br>* complete - Order has been processed successfully. Applicable only if you are using Chargebee's legacy order management system<br>* partially_delivered - The order has been partially delivered to the customer.<br>* voided - Order has been voided. Applicable only if you are using Chargebee's legacy order management system<br>* on_hold - The order is paused from being processed.<br>* awaiting_shipment - The order has been picked up by an integration system, and synced to a shipping management platform<br>* shipped - The order has moved from order management system to a shipping system.<br>* queued - Order is yet to be processed by any system, these are scheduled orders created by Chargebee<br>* new - Order has been created. Applicable only if you are using Chargebee's legacy order management system.<br>* returned - The order has been returned after delivery.<br>* delivered - The order has been delivered to the customer.<br>* cancelled - Order has been cancelled. Applicable only if you are using Chargebee's legacy order management system<br>* processing - Order is being processed. Applicable only if you are using Chargebee's legacy order management system<br>|
|cancellation_reason|string|false|none|Cancellation reason<br><br>* payment_declined - Payment declined.<br>* shipping_cut_off_passed - The invoice has been paid late and Chargebee cancel's the first order for the invoice.<br>* product_not_available - Product not available.<br>* alternative_found - Alternative found.<br>* others - Other reason<br>* order_resent - Order resent<br>* product_unsatisfactory - Product unsatisfactory.<br>* delivery_date_missed - Delivery date missed.<br>* fraudulent_transaction - Fraudulent transaction.<br>* invoice_voided - The invoice for which the order was createed has been voided.<br>* subscription_cancelled - The subsctiption for which the order was created has been cancelled.<br>* invoice_written_off - The invoice has been completely written off. Orders are generated by Chargebee in cancelled state.<br>* product_not_required - Product not required.<br>* third_party_cancellation - Third party cancellation.<br>|
|payment_status|string|false|none|The payment status of the order<br><br>* paid - PAID<br>* not_paid - NOT_PAID<br>|
|order_type|string|false|none|Order type<br><br>* manual - The order has been created by the user using Chargebee's legacy order management system.<br>* system_generated - The order has been created by Chargebee automatically based on the preferences set by the user.<br>|
|price_type|string|true|none|The price type of the order<br><br>* tax_inclusive - All amounts in the document are inclusive of tax.<br>* tax_exclusive - All amounts in the document are exclusive of tax.<br>|
|reference_id|string|false|none|Reference id can be used to map the orders in the shipping/order management application to the orders in ChargeBee. The reference_id generally is same as the order id in the third party application.<br>|
|fulfillment_status|string|false|none|The fulfillment status of an order as reflected in the shipping/order management application. Typical statuses include Shipped,Awaiting Shipment,Not fulfilled etc;<br>|
|order_date|integer(unix-time)|false|none|The date on which the order will start getting processed.<br>|
|shipping_date|integer(unix-time)|false|none|This is the date on which the order will be delivered to the customer.<br>|
|note|string|false|none|The custom note for the order.<br>|
|tracking_id|string|false|none|The tracking id of the order.<br>|
|tracking_url|string|false|none|The tracking url of the order.<br>|
|batch_id|string|false|none|Unique id to identify a group of orders.<br>|
|created_by|string|false|none|The source (or the user) from where the order has been created.<br>|
|shipment_carrier|string|false|none|Shipment carrier<br>|
|invoice_round_off_amount|integer(int64)|false|none|The total round off taken from the invoice level<br>|
|tax|integer(int64)|false|none|The total tax for the order.<br>|
|amount_paid|integer(int64)|false|none|Total amount paid for the order.<br>|
|amount_adjusted|integer(int64)|false|none|Total amount adjusted for the order.<br>|
|refundable_credits_issued|integer(int64)|false|none|The total amount issued as credits on behalf of this order.<br>|
|refundable_credits|integer(int64)|false|none|The total amount that can be issued as credits for this order.<br>|
|rounding_adjustement|integer(int64)|false|none|Rounding adjustment<br>|
|paid_on|integer(unix-time)|false|none|The timestamp indicating the date \& time the order's invoice got paid.<br>|
|shipping_cut_off_date|integer(unix-time)|false|none|The time after which an order becomes unservicable<br>|
|created_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|The time at which the order was created<br>|
|status_update_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|The time at which the order status was last updated.<br>|
|delivered_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|The time at which the order was delivered<br>|
|shipped_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|The time at which the order was shipped.<br>|
|resource_version|integer(int64)|false|none|Version number of this resource. The `resource_version`<br>is updated with a new timestamp in milliseconds for every change made to the resource. This attribute will be present only if the resource has been updated after 2016-09-28.<br>|
|updated_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|The order's last modified time.<br>|
|cancelled_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|The time at which the order was cancelled.<br>|
|resent_status|string|false|none|Resent status of the order.<br><br>* fully_resent - Order is Fully resent<br>* partially_resent - Order is Partially resent<br>|
|is_resent|boolean|true|none|Show if the order is resent order or not.<br>|
|original_order_id|string|false|none|Refers to the original order id of the resent order.<br>|
|discount|integer(int64)|false|none|Total discount given for the order.<br>|
|sub_total|integer(int64)|false|none|The order's sub-total<br>|
|total|integer(int64)|false|none|Total amount charged for the order.<br>|
|deleted|boolean|true|none|Indicates that this resource has been deleted.<br>|
|currency_code|string|false|none|The currency code (ISO 4217 format) for the invoice<br>|
|is_gifted|boolean|false|none|Boolean indicating whether this order is gifted or not.<br>|
|gift_note|string|false|none|The gift message added by the gifter during purchase<br>|
|gift_id|string|false|none|The gift_id if the order is a gift order<br>|
|resend_reason|string|false|none|Reason code for resending the order. Must be one from a list of reason codes set in the Chargebee app in **Settings \> Configure Chargebee \> Reason Codes \> Orders \> Order Resend**.<br>Must be passed if set as mandatory in the app. The codes are case-sensitive<br>|
|business_entity_id|string|false|none|The unique ID of the<br>[business entity](/docs/api/advanced-features)<br>of this subscription. This is always the same as the<br>[business entity](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object#customer_id)<br>of the customer.<br>|
|order_line_items|[object]|false|none|The list of line items for this order.<br>|
|shipping_address|object|false|none|Shipping address for the order.<br>|
|billing_address|object|false|none|Billing address for the order.<br>|
|line_item_taxes|[object]|false|none|The list of taxes applied on the order line items.<br>|
|line_item_discounts|[object]|false|none|The list of discounts applied for the order<br>|
|linked_credit_notes|[object]|false|none|The credit notes linked to the order<br>|
|resent_orders|[object]|false|none|The list of resent orders applied on the order.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_PaymentIntent">PaymentIntent</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapaymentintent"></a>
