<a id="tocSpaymentintent"></a>
<a id="tocspaymentintent"></a>

```json
null
```

A `payment_intent` is created to help you navigate the 3DS flow of collecting payment from your customer. It is necessary only for implementing 3DS flow using Chargebee.js.

#### Auto-expiry

All `payment_intent`s with `status` as `inited`, `in_progress` or `authorized` become `expired` after an **hour** automatically.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|Identifier for PaymentIntent.<br>|
|status|string|true|none|Current status of PaymentIntent.<br><br>* in_progress - Status will be in_progress if the Active Payment Attempt state is in requires_identification, requires_challenge or requires_redirection.<br>* inited - Intent is initialized.<br>* authorized - 3DS verification successfully completed.<br>* consumed - If any Chargebee operation such as create subscription etc. is completed using the intent, it will be in consumed state. Intent cannot be used if it's already in consumed state.<br>* expired - Intent has expired, since it was not consumed before the predefined time-out.<br>|
|currency_code|string|false|none|The currency code (ISO 4217 format) of the amount used in transaction.<br>|
|amount|integer(int64)|true|none|Amount(in cents) to be authorized for 3DS flow.<br>|
|gateway_account_id|string|false|none|The gateway account used for performing the 3DS flow.<br>|
|expires_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Timestamp indicating when the PaymentIntent will expire if left unconsumed.<br>|
|reference_id|string|false|none|Reference for payment method at gateway. Only applicable when the PaymentIntent is created for cards stored in the gateway.<br>|
|payment_method_type|string|false|none|The payment method of this intent<br><br>* tamara - Payments made via Tamara.<br>* alipay_hk - Payments made via Alipay HK.<br>* apple_pay - apple_pay<br>* netbanking_emandates - netbanking_emandates<br>* venmo - Venmo<br>* after_pay - Payments made via Afterpay<br>* giropay - giropay<br>* momo - Payments made via MoMo.<br>* blik - Payments made via BLIK.<br>* dana - Payments made via Dana.<br>* paypal_express_checkout - paypal_express_checkout<br>* touch_n_go - Payments made via Touch 'n Go.<br>* pix - Pix<br>* amazon_payments - amazon_payments<br>* grab_pay - Payments made via GrabPay<br>* card - card<br>* affirm_pay - Payments made via Affirm Pay.<br>* go_pay - Payments made via GoPay<br>* google_pay - google_pay<br>* cash_app_pay - Payments made via Cash App Pay.<br>* ideal - ideal<br>* nequi - Payments made via Nequi.<br>* dotpay - dotpay<br>* sofort - sofort<br>* gcash - Payments made via GCash.<br>* nupay - Payments made via NuPay.<br>* faster_payments - Faster Payments<br>* rakuten_pay - Payments made via Rakuten Pay.<br>* qpay - Payments made via Qpay.<br>* online_banking_poland - Online Banking Poland<br>* klarna - Payments made via Klarna.<br>* swish - Payments made via Swish<br>* kbc_payment_button - KBC Payment Button<br>* bancontact - bancontact<br>* trustly - Trustly<br>* fpx - Payments made via FPX.<br>* paypay - PayPay<br>* kakao_pay - Payments made via Kakao Pay.<br>* boleto - boleto<br>* revolut_pay - Payments made via Revolut Pay.<br>* naver_pay - Payments made via Naver Pay.<br>* electronic_payment_standard - Electronic Payment Standard<br>* p24 - Payments made via Przelewy24 (P24).<br>* thai_qr - Payments made via Thai QR.<br>* pay_by_bank - This attribute is omitted when no preference is stored.<br><br>* `card`: Options for card payments.<br>  * `three_d_secure`: Options for 3DS authentication.<br>    * `challenge_preference`: The preferred 3DS flow. Applicable only when `payment_method_type` is `card` and 3DS is enabled for the gateway account. Supported for Stripe, Adyen, and BlueSnap; ignored for other gateways. The gateway or card issuer can override the preference.<br>      * `no_preference`: Chargebee, the gateway, and the issuer decide the 3DS flow.<br>      * `no_challenge`: A frictionless flow without a challenge is requested.<br>      * `challenge`: A challenge flow is requested.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_PaymentReferenceNumber">PaymentReferenceNumber</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapaymentreferencenumber"></a>
<a id="schema_PaymentReferenceNumber"></a>
<a id="tocSpaymentreferencenumber"></a>
<a id="tocspaymentreferencenumber"></a>

```json
null
```

Using this resource you can create reference numbers for Payment Instructions at the invoice level, allowing for multiple payment information and payment reference numbers to be associated with a single invoice. However, only one PRN is generated for each payment method.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|The `id`<br>of the `payment_reference_number`<br>resource is a unique identifier assigned to the PRN to track and reference in systems.<br>|
|type|string|true|none|This attribute helps `type`<br>field in the API, specifies how to reconcile offline payments, and generate `payment_reference_number`<br>on invoices based on country-specific rules. Setting the `type`<br>field generates `payment_reference_number`<br>for the respective country and includes them on the invoice for correct reconciliation.<br><br>* frn - The reference number printed on invoices in Finland is utilized by buyers for payment via bank transfer, facilitating the association of payments with invoices.<br>* fik - Denmark based number calculated using recursive MOD 10 algorithm.<br>* kid - The KID number (kundeidentifikasjon) in Norway is an abbreviation for "Customer identification". It is used to associate payments with the customer and invoice.<br>* ocr - A OCR-based payment, contains an OCR reference, which is used to identify the vendor and the purchase document in connection with a payment. Swedish reference number can contain customer ID and/or invoice number to identify customer and invoice.<br>|
|number|string|true|none|A number is generated based on the configuration type of the PRN during the invoice creation process.<br>|
|invoice_id|string|false|none|The `invoice_id`<br>of the payment reference number (PRN) resource is the unique identifier assigned to the invoice that the PRN is associated with.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|kid|
|type|ocr|
|type|frn|
|type|fik|
|type|swiss_reference|

<h2 id="tocS_PaymentSchedule">PaymentSchedule</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapaymentschedule"></a>
<a id="schema_PaymentSchedule"></a>
<a id="tocSpaymentschedule"></a>
<a id="tocspaymentschedule"></a>

```json
null
```

Payment schedules for an invoice refer to a payment structure where the `amount_due`
on an invoice is divided into smaller, more manageable parts, each of which is paid over a specified period.

`reference_transactions[]` lists the payment attempts referenced against those installments.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|An auto-generated unique identifier for the payment schedule.<br>|
|scheme_id|string|true|none|The identifier of the `payment_schedule_scheme`<br>, used to create the payment schedules.<br>|
|entity_type|string|true|none|Specifies the types of entity this payment schedule is based on.<br><br>* invoice - Indicates the invoice entity type<br>|
|entity_id|string|true|none|The identifier of the entity this payment schedule is based on.<br>|
|amount|integer(int64)|false|none|The part of the `invoice.amount_due`<br>to be distributed across the payment schedules. If not specified, the entire `invoice.amount_due`<br>is considered by default.<br>|
|created_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|The timestamp at which the `payment_schedule`<br>was created.<br>|
|resource_version|integer(int64)|false|none|Version number of this resource. The `resource_version`<br>is updated with a new timestamp in milliseconds for every change made to the resource. This attribute will be present only if the resource has been updated after 2016-09-28.<br>|
|updated_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Specifies when these payment schedules are updated recently.<br>|
|currency_code|string|false|none|The currency code (ISO 4217 format) of the transaction amount.<br>|
|schedule_entries|[object]|false|none|List of schedule entries<br>|
|reference_transactions|[object]|false|none|The list of transactions referenced against the schedule entries of this payment schedule, most recent first. A transaction referenced against more than one schedule entry appears once per entry.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|entity_type|invoice|

<a id="tocspaymentschedulescheme"></a>

```json
null
```

Payment schedules for an invoice refer to a payment structure where the `amount_due`
on an invoice is divided into smaller, more manageable parts, each of which is paid over a specified period. Payment schedule scheme is a configuration or set of rules for creating payment schedules. After creating a payment schedule scheme, you can use it to generate payment schedules for multiple invoices.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|An auto-generated unique identifier for the payment schedule scheme.<br>|
|name|string|false|none|The name of a payment schedule scheme.<br>|
|description|string|false|none|A brief description for this payment schedule scheme.<br>|
|number_of_schedules|integer(int32)|true|none|Specifies the total number of payment schedules for the invoice. The maximum `number_of_schedules`<br>varies based on the `period_unit`<br>: - **Day**: Up to 30 schedules<br><br>* **Week**: Up to 52 schedules<br>* **Month**: Up to 12 schedules<br>|
|period_unit|string|true|none|Defines the time unit for intervals between payment schedules. Possible values are: day, week, and month.<br><br>* month - When the time unit for intervals between payment schedules is set as month<br>* week - When the time unit for intervals between payment schedules is set as week<br>* day - When the time unit for intervals between payment schedules is set as day<br>|
|period|integer(int32)|false|none|The time period between the effective dates of two consecutive payment schedules, expressed in period_units. Use this parameter to have fixed intervals between payment schedules. The maximum `period`<br>varies based on the `period_unit`<br>: - **Day**: Up to 30 days<br><br>* **Week**: Up to 6 weeks<br>* **Month**: Up to 6 months<br>|
|created_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|The timestamp at which the `payment_schedule_scheme`<br>was created.<br>|
|resource_version|integer(int64)|false|none|Version number of this resource. The `resource_version`<br>is updated with a new timestamp in milliseconds for every change made to the resource. This attribute will be present only if the resource has been updated after 2016-09-28.<br>|
|updated_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Defines the timestamp when the config was last updated<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|period_unit|day|
|period_unit|week|
|period_unit|month|

**Updates**

This API obsoletes the [Cards API](/docs/api/cards)
in Chargebee.

Represents the payment source for the customer. Specific types of payment source (Card, Direct Debit, Paypal Express Checkout, etc.) is defined as sub-resource in the response object. You can find the list of supported payment sources and the expected input parameters [here](/docs/api/payment_parameters). See [Payment source attributes](/docs/api/payment_sources/payment-source-object) for a descriptive list of attributes and payment source types.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|Identifier of the payment source<br>|
|resource_version|integer(int64)|false|none|Version number of this resource. The `resource_version`<br>is updated with a new timestamp in milliseconds for every change made to the resource. This attribute will be present only if the resource has been updated after 2016-09-28.<br>|
|updated_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Timestamp indicating when this payment source resource was last updated.<br>|
|created_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Timestamp indicating when this payment source resource is created.<br>|
|customer_id|string|true|none|Identifier of the customer with whom this payment source is associated.<br>|
|type|string|true|none|Type of payment source<br><br>* direct_debit - Represents bank account for which the direct debit or ACH agreement/mandate is created.<br>* unionpay - Payments made via UnionPay.<br>* mercado_pago - Payments made via Mercado Pago.<br>* sepa_instant_transfer - Payments made via Sepa Instant Transfer<br>* dotpay - Payments made via Dotpay.<br>* klarna - Payments made via Klarna.<br>* giropay - Payments made via giropay.<br>* grab_pay - Payments made via GrabPay<br>* stablecoin - Payments made via Stablecoin.<br>* p24 - Payments made via Przelewy24 (P24).<br>* nupay - Payments made via NuPay.<br>* picpay - Payments made via PicPay.<br>* bancontact - Payments made via Bancontact Card.<br>* nequi - Payments made via Nequi.<br>* amazon_payments - Payments made via Amazon Payments.<br>* pay_by_bank - Pay By Bank<br>* online_banking_poland - Payments made via Online Banking Poland<br>* touch_n_go - Payments made via Touch 'n Go.<br>* after_pay - Payments made via Afterpay<br>* momo - Payments made via MoMo.<br>* fpx - Payments made via FPX.<br>* paypay - Payments made via PayPay<br>* generic - Payments made via Generic Payment Method.<br>* twint - Payments made via Twint<br>* automated_bank_transfer - Represents virtual bank account using which the payment will be done.<br>* paypal_express_checkout - Payments made via PayPal Express Checkout.<br>* trustly - Trustly<br>* upi - UPI Payments.<br>* cash_app_pay - Payments made via Cash App Pay.<br>* south_korean_cards - Payments made via South Korean Cards<br>* qpay - Payments made via Qpay.<br>* affirm_pay - <h2 id="tocS_PaymentVoucher">PaymentVoucher</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapaymentvoucher"></a>
<a id="schema_PaymentVoucher"></a>
<a id="tocSpaymentvoucher"></a>
<a id="tocspaymentvoucher"></a>

```json
null
```

The Payment Voucher resource represents a voucher that has been created for a customer to initiate voucher-based payment. This resource contains relevant details such as the voucher URL, the amount of the voucher, the status of the voucher, and more. Currently, the only supported voucher-based payment source is Boleto. Boleto is a payment method in Brazil that is regulated by the Central Bank of Brazil and is considered an official form of payment. This is also a popular voucher-based payment method in Brazil.  
**Note:**
This resource can be extended in the future to support other types of payment sources for vouchers.

|id_at_gateway|string|false|none|The id with which this voucher is referred in gateway.<br>|
|payment_voucher_type|string|true|none|Type of the payment source.<br><br>* boleto - Boleto<br>|
|expires_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Timestamp indicating when the Voucher will expire if left unconsumed.<br>|
|status|string|false|none|Current status of the payment voucher.<br><br>* consumed - Consumed for a transaction and cannot be used again<br>* expired - Expired before consumed and cannot be used again<br>* active - Active and ready to be consumed<br>* failure - Failed to create the voucher due to gateway rejection<br>|
|subscription_id|string|false|none|Identifier of the subscription for which this payment voucher is made.<br>|
|currency_code|string|true|none|The currency code (ISO 4217 format) for the voucher.<br>|
|amount|integer(int64)|false|none|Amount for this payment voucher.<br>|
|gateway_account_id|string|false|none|The gateway account used for this voucher<br>|
|payment_source_id|string|false|none|Identifier of the payment source for which this payment voucher is created<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_PersonalizedOffer">PersonalizedOffer</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapersonalizedoffer"></a>
<a id="schema_PersonalizedOffer"></a>
<a id="tocSpersonalizedoffer"></a>
<a id="tocspersonalizedoffer"></a>

```json
null
```

A Personalized Offer represents the best possible offer for a subscriber at a given moment in their lifecycle. It is generated by combining subscriber profile, subscription details, and contextual signals with the plays configured by Growth Managers in the Chargebee Growth dashboard. Learn more about [Growth Solutions](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/retention/getting-started-guide/chargebee-growth-solutions).
Growth Managers define strategic plays that guide customer engagement. Developers then use the Personalized Offers API to fetch and surface these offers within the subscriber experience; whether in an app, portal, checkout flow, websites or communications like email and SMS. Some common plays include:

* `Acquire`: Incentivize trial users or prospects to subscribe.
* `Expand`: Encourage existing subscribers to purchase higher-value products or add-ons.
* `Retain`: Engage at-risk subscribers with targeted winbacks or discounts.

**Note:** Growth solutions are currently in **Early Access** and available only for Chargebee Billing customers at no additional cost during the EAP period. This API is also part of the Early Access Program (EAP). To request access, go to the [Chargebee Growth Early Access](https://app.chargebee.com/login?forward=https://app.chargebee.com/request_access/chargebee-growth&ref=feature) page in Chargebee Billing.

**Features of this object**

The Personalized Offers object enables you to:

* Fetch context-aware offers generated by the Growth system.
* Display offer content (title and description) to subscribers.
* Provide subscribers with options they can act on.
* Attribute offers to the correct brand (for multi-brand merchants).
* Respect time-bound validity with the expires_at attribute.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|A unique and immutable identifier for the personalized offer.<br>|
|offer_id|string|true|none|ID of the base offer configured. This ID is immutable and always refers to the core offer and its latest published version.<br>|
|content|object|true|none|The offer content to display to the user, includes title and description. \*\*Tip\*\* The content is formatted in HTML and can be rendered safely in the DOM. However, the code may contain empty \`  <br>\` elements of the form \`  <br>\`. Replace these with one or two newlines to preserve the intended line breaks.<br>|
|options|[object]|true|none|List of offer options (choices or call-to-action buttons) in this offer.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_PortalSession">PortalSession</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaportalsession"></a>
<a id="schema_PortalSession"></a>
<a id="tocSportalsession"></a>
<a id="tocsportalsession"></a>

```json
null
```

Customer Portal lets your customers to manage their account and billing themselves. Chargebee supports Single Sign-on (SSO) to access the customer portal. If you already have your own authentication for your website, it allows your authenticated customers to access their portal without having to login again.

**Note:** You can instead allow your customers to access the portal via login page provided by Chargebee. [Read more](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/inapp-self-serve-portal.html).

Please follow the below steps for supporting portal access via SSO:

1. To enable the "Allow access to customer portal via API", click **Settings** \> **Configure Chargebee** \> **Customer Facing Essentials** \> **Checkout and Self Serve Portal** \> **Portal**.
2. Provide a link in your website/application which your authenticated customers can use to access the portal (For example, `{your_website_url}/portal_link`).
3. Handle the link request in your server code and create a portal session for the customer by calling Chargebee's "Create a portal session" API
4. Forward the user to the access URL present in the "Portal Session" resource returned by the above API call.

**Notes about access URL:**

* The access URL should be accessed by the customer within one hour from the time it was created.
* Once accessed, the session is valid until the user logs out from the portal UI or logout API is called from your application for this session.
* Once accessed, the access url cannot be reused. Hence do not persist this URL. Whenever you need to provide access to the portal, you need to create a new portal session.  
Using Chargebee's authentication  
**Note:** This feature is not supported in [in-app](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/inapp-self-serve-portal.html) portal.
Chargebee allows you to integrate your website by building user authentication on top of Chargebee. You can also use the portal login to provide authenticated access for your customers to your website pages.
**Workflow:**

Users should be redirected to the portal login URL - **https://yourdomain.chargebeeportal.com/portal/login** by passing the following parameters:

* **return_url** - URL the users should be redirected to upon successful authentication.
* **cancel_url** - URL the users should be redirected to when they want to go back to your website during login. The domain name used in the Return/Cancel URL should be added as a 'Whitelisted Domain' in Chargebee. Add just the domain name in Chargebee and not the entire URL: E.g. yourdomain.com.

Upon successful authentication, a session is created for the user and Chargebee redirects the user to the return_url along with the following parameters:

* **auth_session_id** - Identifier to the authenticated session.
* **auth_session_token** - Token for the session which should be sent later to activate this session. Using the **auth_session_id** \& **auth_session_token** , you should call [Activate a Portal Session](/docs/api/portal_sessions/activate-a-portal-session) API to validate the session details and create a session for that user in your website. **Note:** The process of setting up the portal account will take place along with the authentication process.  
Scheduled subscription changes  
* When [Ramps](ramps) are disabled, the customer can view and edit the single scheduled change if it exists.

* When [Ramps](ramps) are enabled with compatibility mode:

  * The customer can view and edit the first ramp if it exists.
  * If they edit the subscription, the impacts are the same as those described in the documentation for [`changes_scheduled_at`](subscriptions#update_subscription_for_items_changes_scheduled_at) parameter in the Update subscription API.

  For more details, see [Ramps API compatibility mode](subscriptions#ramps-compat-mode).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the portal session.<br>|
|token|string|true|none|Unique pre-authenticated portal session token to access customer portal directly.<br>|
|access_url|string|true|none|Unique URL for accessing the customer portal. Once accessed, this cannot be reused.<br>|
|redirect_url|string|false|none|URL to redirect when the user logs out from the portal.<br>|
|status|string|true|none|Indicates the current status of the portal session.<br><br>* not_yet_activated - Indicates that the portal session is created and not yet activated for the customer to allow access to your website. This is applicable when you use Chargebee's authentication for your website<br>* activated - Indicates that the portal session is activated for the customer to allow access to your website. This is applicable when you use Chargebee's authentication for your website.<br>* logged_in - Indicates that the portal session URL has been accessed by the user and the session is active.<br>* created - Indicates that the portal session is just created and not yet accessed by the user.<br>* logged_out - Indicates that the portal session is logged out either by user or via API.<br>|
|created_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Timestamp indicating when this portal session was generated.<br>|
|expires_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Specifies when the portal session URL expires. After this time, it is no longer accessible. The expiration time is set to 1 hour after the portal session is created.<br>|
|customer_id|string|true|none|Identifier of the customer.<br>|
|login_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Timestamp indicating when this portal session URL was accessed by the user.<br>|
|logout_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Timestamp indicating when this portal session was logged out either by user or via API.<br>|
|login_ipaddress|string|false|none|IP Address from which the portal session URL was accessed.<br>|
|logout_ipaddress|string|false|none|IP Address from which the portal session was logged out either by user or via API.<br>|
|linked_customers|[object]|false|none|The list of customers for this session<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|created|
|status|logged_in|
|status|logged_out|
|status|not_yet_activated|
|status|activated|

<h2 id="tocS_PriceRamp">PriceRamp</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapriceramp"></a>
<a id="schema_PriceRamp"></a>
<a id="tocSpriceramp"></a>
<a id="tocspriceramp"></a>

```json
null
```

Price ramp resource lets you define a stepped pricing schedule on an [item price](/docs/api/item_prices) in the Product Catalog. Each ramp is an ordered list of `ramp_intervals` that set the price for contiguous ranges of billing cycles, so new subscriptions inherit introductory or stepped pricing without custom per-subscription logic.

Here's an example to show how you can use ramp pricing:

A media streaming company offers a **Basic** monthly plan with a catalog price of $9.99. To grow acquisitions, they configure a price ramp so new subscribers start on an introductory price, then step up to full price.  

|----------|--------------|---------------|-------------------|
| **Plan** | **Currency** | **Frequency** | **Catalog price** |
| Basic    | USD          | Monthly       | $9.99             |

|--------------------|-------------------|-------------------------|
| **Billing cycles** | **Price charged** | **Price type**          |
| Month 1            | $0.99             | Introductory ramp price |
| Months 2--4        | $4.99             | Introductory ramp price |
| Month 5 onwards    | $9.99             | Catalog price           |

Every new subscription on this Basic USD Monthly item price inherits the ramp automatically. In this example the final interval uses the catalog price, so the subscriber stays on $9.99 from month 5 onward. The catalog price continues only when that final interval sets `apply_catalog_price` to `true`. A final interval that sets `price` and omits `ending_billing_cycle` keeps that fixed price for the remaining billing cycles.

An interval that uses the item price's catalog price returns `apply_catalog_price` as `true`. The resolved price for every interval is always available in `price` (in the [minor unit of the currency](/docs/api/currencies)) and, when [multi-decimal pricing](/docs/api/currencies) is enabled, in `price_in_decimal`.  
When a price ramp is linked to an item price, the `price_ramp_id` is exposed on the corresponding [item price](/docs/api/item_prices) object.  
**See also:**
For a more detailed understanding of Price Ramps, including how to configure and manage them, as well as their impact on other features, follow these resources:

* [Price Ramps](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/product-catalog/price-ramps)
* [Configuring a Price Ramp](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/product-catalog/price-ramps-configure)
* [How Ramp Pricing works with Create Subscription](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/product-catalog/price-ramps-create-subscription)
* [How Ramp Pricing works with Hosted Checkout](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/product-catalog/price-ramps-hosted-checkout)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|A unique and immutable ID for the price ramp. It is auto-generated when the price ramp is created.<br>|
|item_price_id|string|true|none|The ID of the<br>[item price](/docs/api/item_prices)<br>whose price changes according to this ramp. An item price can be linked to at most one price ramp.<br>|
|status|string|true|none|The current status of the price ramp.<br><br>* active - The price ramp is active and its ramp intervals apply to the linked item price.<br>* deleted - The price ramp has been deleted and its link to the item price has been removed.<br>* archived - The price ramp has been archived and no longer applies to the linked item price.<br>|
|created_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Timestamp (UTC, in seconds) indicating when this price ramp was created.<br>|
|resource_version|integer(int64)|false|none|Version number of this resource. The `resource_version`<br>is updated with a new timestamp in milliseconds for every change made to the resource.<br>|
|updated_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Timestamp (UTC, in seconds) indicating when this price ramp was last updated.<br>|
|archived_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Timestamp (UTC, in seconds) indicating when this price ramp was archived. Present only when `status`<br>is `archived`.<br>|
|business_entity_id|string|false|none|The unique ID of the<br>[business entity](/docs/api/business_entities)<br>of this `price_ramp`.<br>This is applicable only when multiple business entities have been created for the site. The value of this attribute indicates that the resource is specific to the given business entity.<br>|
|ramp_intervals|[object]|false|none|The ordered list of intervals that make up the price ramp. Each interval defines the price that applies for a contiguous range of billing cycles. Adjacent intervals with the same pricing are stored as a single interval. Up to 3 intervals. The first interval starts at billing cycle `1`.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|active|
|status|archived|
|status|deleted|

Price variant resource offers businesses the flexibility to manage pricing for multiple variations of an [item](/docs/api/items) (plan, addon, or charge) in the Product Catalog. It enables the creation of diverse pricing structures based on variables such as geography, partners, versions, and more.  
**See also:**
For a more detailed understanding of Price Variants, including how to enable, configure, and manage them, as well as their impact on other features, follow these resources:

* [Price Variant Overview](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/variant-pricing-overview.html)
* [Enabling Price Variant](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/variant-pricing-enable.html)
* [Configuring Price Variant](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/variant-pricing-config.html)
* [Impacted Features by Price Variant](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/variant-pricing-impacted-features.html)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|The unique and immutable identifier of the price variant.<br>|
|name|string|true|none|A unique name of the price variant.<br>|
|external_name|string|false|none|A unique display name for the price variant.<br>|
|variant_group|string|false|none|The `variant_group`<br>organizes similar [price_variants](/docs/api/price_variants)<br>to optimize strategies such as bundling, geo-based pricing experiments, and campaign-specific pricing like `cb-atomic-pricing-`<br>for effective grouping. The `variant_group`<br>provides greater flexibility and precision in your pricing models.<br>|
|description|string|false|none|Description of the price variant.<br>|
|status|string|false|none|Status of a price variant.<br><br>* active -<br>  Active price variant. This price variant can be attached to [item prices](/docs/api/item_prices)<br>  .<br>* deleted -<br>  Deleted price variant. The `id`<br>  and `name`<br>  of the deleted price variant can be reused.<br>* archived -<br>  Archived price variant. This price variant is no longer `active`<br>  and cannot be attached to new [item prices](/docs/api/item_prices).<br>  Existing item prices that already have this price variant attached will continue to remain as is.<br>|
|created_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Timestamp indicating when this price variant is created.<br>|
|resource_version|integer(int64)|false|none|The version number of this resource. For every change made to the resource, `resource_version`<br>is updated with a new timestamp in milliseconds.<br>|
|updated_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Timestamp indicating when this price variant was last updated.<br>|
|archived_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Timestamp indicating when this price variant was archived.<br>|
|business_entity_id|string|false|none|The unique ID of the<br>[business entity](/docs/api/business_entities)<br>of this `price_variant`.<br>This is applicable only when multiple business entities have been created for the site. The value of this attribute indicates that the resource is specific to the given business entity.<br>|
|deleted|boolean|true|none|Indicates whether the price variant has been deleted or not.<br>|
|attributes|[object]|false|none|The list of price variant attribute values.<br>Attributes can be used to store additional information about the price variant. For example, for a price variant called 'Germany', the attributes can be 'Country':'Germany', 'City':'Berlin' and so on.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|active|
|status|archived|
|status|deleted|

The `pricing_page_session`
resource allows you to create a pricing page that incorporates customer and subscription details. This page helps customers choose a plan, start a new subscription, or modify an existing one. Each session is distinct and has a limited duration, ensuring a unique and time-sensitive experience.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|Unique identifier generated for each pricing page session requested.<br>|
|url|string|false|none|Unique URL for the pricing page that can be included in your website.<br>|
|created_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Indicates when this pricing page session is generated.<br>|
|expires_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Indicates when this pricing page session will expire. After this, the pricing page cannot be accessed.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_Product">Product</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaproduct"></a>

<a id="tocSproduct"></a>
<a id="tocsproduct"></a>

```json

```

Products are offerings that can be sold to customers either as one-time purchases or as recurring subscriptions. These products could include physical items, digital goods, or services that are delivered over a period of time. Chargebee's API allows developers to interact with and manipulate product data, enabling businesses to seamlessly integrate their product offerings into their subscription management workflows.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|The immutable unique identifier of the product.<br>|
|name|string|true|none|A unique display name for the product. This is visible only in Chargebee.<br>|
|external_name|string|true|none|This is a unique name appears for each product to the end user.<br>|
|description|string|false|none|Description of the product.<br>|
|has_variant|boolean|true|none|Whether the product has variants or not.<br>|
|status|string|true|none|Status of the product.<br><br>* active - The active products are visible on the storefront, subscription, or checkout.<br>* inactive - The inactive products are not visible on the storefront, subscription, or checkout.<br>|
|shippable|boolean|true|none|Whether a product is shippable or not.<br>|
|sku|string|false|none|A unique identifier code a seller assigns to each product or item. Retailers and merchants use SKUs to keep track of inventory and sales data and help organize products within a store or warehouse. SKUs can include a combination of letters, numbers, and symbols and can vary in length depending on the seller's needs.<br>|
|created_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Timestamp when the product was created.<br>|
|resource_version|integer(int64)|false|none|Version number of this resource. The `resource_version`<br>is updated with a new timestamp in milliseconds for every change made to the resource. This attribute will be present only if the resource has been updated after 2016-09-28.<br>|
|updated_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Timestamp indicating when this product was last updated<br>|
|deleted|boolean|true|none|Determines if the product is deleted or not. If the value is `true`<br>then the product has been deleted else it exists. Once the product is deleted, you can reuse the product `id`<br>and `name`<br>.<br>|
|metadata|object|false|none|A collection of key-value pairs that provides extra information about the product.  <br>**Note:**<br>There's a character limit of 65,535.<br><br>[Learn more](/docs/api/advanced-features#metadata)<br>.<br>|
|options|[object]|false|none|Array of option list which helps in the product variant creation.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|active|
|status|inactive|

|closing_balance|integer(int64)|true|none|Closing balance as on end date.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_Purchase">Purchase</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapurchase"></a>
<a id="schema_Purchase"></a>
<a id="tocSpurchase"></a>
<a id="tocspurchase"></a>

```json
null
```

The `purchase` resource represents a collection of [item prices](/docs/api/item_prices) bought together. A purchase can contain one or more of the following:

* subscriptions (a [subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions) resource consists of item prices such that at least one of the item prices belongs to an [item](/docs/api/items) of `type` `plan`.)
* group of one-time charges (aka [charge item prices](/docs/api/item_prices))

**Prerequisite**

Purchases must be enabled explicitly for the site. If not already enabled, contact eap@chargebee.com. Purchases require the following features to work so they're automatically enabled along with them:

* [Consolidated Invoicing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html)
* [Manual discounts](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/subscription-manual-discounts.html)
* [Multiple coupon support](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/coupons.html#applying-multiple-coupons-to-a-subscription)
* [Multi-decimal pricing and quantities](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/multi-decimal-support.html)  
**Note**

Once created, Chargebee never modifies a `purchase` resource; it cannot be modified via API either. Change the subscriptions it created with the [subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions) operations.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|The unique identifier of the purchase resource. This is always autogenerated.<br>|
|customer_id|string|true|none|The unique identifier of the [customer](/docs/api/customers)<br>that made this purchase.<br>|
|created_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|The time at which this purchase was created.<br>|
|modified_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|The time at which the purchase was modified.<br>|
|subscription_ids|[string]|false|none|The unique identifiers of the [subscriptions](/docs/api/subscriptions)<br>that are created as part of this purchase. These IDs remain even when the associated subscriptions have been deleted.<br>|
|invoice_ids|[string]|false|none|The unique identifiers of the [invoices](/docs/api/invoices)<br>created immediately as part of this purchase. This list is empty when the purchase raises no invoiceable charges, such as a trial-only purchase. When [consolidated invoicing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html) is enabled for the customer, charges are consolidated where the subscriptions allow it. Subscription differences can still leave more than one invoice in this list. When consolidated invoicing is disabled, each subscription with invoiceable charges has its own invoice.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_Quote">Quote</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaquote"></a>
<a id="schema_Quote"></a>
<a id="tocSquote"></a>
<a id="tocsquote"></a>

```json
null
```

A quote is an estimate of the invoice with the charges likely to occur when customers buy an item. A quote can be converted to a regular invoice once the customer accepts it.

The line items of a quote are grouped by charge events and are available as a separate [resource](/docs/api/quote_line_groups). This resource can be retrieved using the [List quote line groups](/docs/api/quotes/list-quote-line-groups) endpoint. Note that the first quote line group is available within the quote resource itself and parsing the quote line groups object is not required.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|The quote number. Acts as a identifier for quote and typically generated sequentially.<br>|
|name|string|false|none|The quote name will be used as the pdf name of the quote.<br>|
|po_number|string|false|none|Purchase Order Number<br>|
|customer_id|string|true|none|The identifier of the customer this quote belongs to.<br>|
|subscription_id|string|false|none|The identifier of the subscription this quote belongs to.<br>|
|invoice_id|string|false|none|The identifier of the invoice generated while converting this quote.<br>|
|status|string|true|none|Current status of this quote.<br><br>* open - The quote is either newly created, or has been approved but not yet sent to the customer.<br>* invoiced - The accepted quote has been converted into a subscription or one-time charge and invoiced through Chargebee.<br>* voided -<br>  The quote has been invalidated and can no longer be acted upon.  <br>  **Note**<br><br>  Applicable only when Chargebee CPQ is enabled. To request access, contact [Chargebee Support](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/kb/getting-started/how-to-contact-chargebees-support-team?utm_source=docs_api&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=support).<br>* accepted - The customer has accepted the quote.<br>* closed -<br>  The quote has been marked as closed.  <br>  **Note**<br><br>  Not applicable when Chargebee CPQ is enabled.<br>* declined - The customer declined/rejected the quote.<br>* proposed -<br>  The quote has been shared with the customer via email or e-signature and is awaiting their response.  <br>  **Note**<br><br>  Applicable only when Chargebee CPQ is enabled. To request access, contact [Chargebee Support](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/kb/getting-started/how-to-contact-chargebees-support-team?utm_source=docs_api&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=support).<br>* expired -<br>  The quote has passed its expiration date and is no longer valid.  <br>  **Note**<br><br>  Applicable only when Chargebee CPQ is enabled. To request access, contact [Chargebee Support](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/kb/getting-started/how-to-contact-chargebees-support-team?utm_source=docs_api&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=support).<br>* approval_rejected -<br>  The quote was rejected with comments, allowing for revisions.  <br>  **Note**<br><br>  Applicable only when Chargebee CPQ is enabled. To request access, contact [Chargebee Support](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/kb/getting-started/how-to-contact-chargebees-support-team?utm_source=docs_api&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=support).<br>* pending_approval -<br>  The quote has been submitted for internal approval and is awaiting review.  <br>  **Note**<br><br>  Applicable only when Chargebee CPQ is enabled. To request access, contact [Chargebee Support](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/kb/getting-started/how-to-contact-chargebees-support-team?utm_source=docs_api&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=support).<br>|
|operation_type|string|true|none|Operation Type<br><br>* onetime_invoice - onetime_invoice<br>* create_subscription_for_customer - create_subscription_for_customer<br>* change_subscription - change_subscription<br>* renew_subscription - renew_subscription<br>|
|vat_number|string|false|none|VAT/ Tax registration number of the customer. [Learn more](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/tax.html#capture-tax-registration-number)<br>|
|price_type|string|true|none|The price type of the quote.<br><br>* tax_inclusive - All amounts in the document are inclusive of tax.<br>* tax_exclusive - All amounts in the document are exclusive of tax.<br>|
|valid_till|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Quote will be valid till this date. After this date quote will be marked as closed.<br>|
|date|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Creation date of the quote. Typically this is the date on which quote is generated.<br>|
|total_payable|integer(int64)|false|none|Total contract value. Applicable when multi billing cycle quote is enabled.<br>|
|charge_on_acceptance|integer(int64)|false|none|Charge on acceptance. Applicable when multi billing cycle quote is enabled.<br>|
|sub_total|integer(int64)|true|none|Subtotal (in cents) of the first quote line group.<br>|
|total|integer(int64)|false|none|Total (in cents) of the first quote line group.<br>|
|credits_applied|integer(int64)|false|none|Credits applied (in cents) for the first quote line group.<br>|
|amount_paid|integer(int64)|false|none|Existing outstanding payments (in cents) if any, applied to the first quote line group.<br>|
|amount_due|integer(int64)|false|none|Amount due (in cents) for the first quote line group.<br>|
|version|integer(int32)|false|none|Version of the quote.<br>|
|resource_version|integer(int64)|false|none|Version number of this resource. The `resource_version`<br>is updated with a new timestamp in milliseconds for every change made to the resource. This attribute will be present only if the resource has been updated after 2016-09-28.<br>|
|updated_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Timestamp indicating when this quote was last updated.<br>|
|vat_number_prefix|string|false|none|An overridden value for the first two characters of the [full VAT number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VAT_identification_number).<br>Only applicable specifically for customers with [billing_address](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#billing_address)<br><br>`country`<br>as `XI`<br>(which is **United Kingdom - Northern Ireland**<br>).<br><br>When you have enabled [EU VAT](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/eu-vat.html)<br>in 2021 or have [manually enabled](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/brexit.html#what-needs-to-be-done-in-chargebee)<br>the Brexit configuration, you have the option of setting [billing_address](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#billing_address)<br><br>`country`<br>as `XI`.<br>That's the code for **United Kingdom - Northern Ireland** .<br>The first two characters of the VAT number in such a case is<br>`XI`<br>by default. However, if the VAT number was registered in UK, the value should be `GB`.<br>Set<br>`vat_number_prefix`<br>to `GB`<br>for such cases.<br>|
|tax_category|string|false|none|Specifies the customer's category for the Goods and Services Tax (GST). This field is returned only if you've configured GST for the India region.<br>|
|currency_code|string|true|none|The currency code (ISO 4217 format) of the quote.<br>|
|notes|[object]|false|none|List of notes associated with this quotes.<br>|
|contract_term_start|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Specifies the contract term's start date.<br>|
|contract_term_end|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Specifies the contract term's end date. It indicates when the action set in `action_at_term_end`<br>gets triggered.<br>|
|contract_term_termination_fee|integer(int64)|false|none|Specifies the charge to be applied for terminating the contract term.<br>|
|business_entity_id|string|false|none|The unique ID of the [business entity](/docs/api/advanced-features)<br>of this quote.<br>|
|deleted|boolean|true|none|Indicates that this resource has been deleted when the value is `true`<br>.<br>|
|total_contract_value|integer(int64)|false|none|The total contract value of the quote.<br><br>**Note:** This parameter applies only when Chargebee CPQ is enabled. To request access, please contact [support](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/kb/getting-started/how-to-contact-chargebees-support-team?utm_source=docs_api&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=support)<br>|
|total_discount|integer(int64)|false|none|The total discount value of the quote for the contract period.<br><br>**Note:** This parameter applies only when Chargebee CPQ is enabled. To request access, please contact [support](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/kb/getting-started/how-to-contact-chargebees-support-team?utm_source=docs_api&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=support)<br>|
|has_entitlements|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether this quote has entitlement records associated with it.<br>|
|line_items|[object]|false|none|The list of line items for this quote.<br>|
|line_item_tiers|[object]|false|none|The list of tiers applicable for the various line items in this quote.<br>|
|line_item_discounts|[object]|false|none|The list of deductions applied for each line item of this quote.<br>|
|line_item_taxes|[object]|false|none|The list of taxes applied on the line items of this quote.<br>|
|discounts|[object]|false|none|The list of all deductions applied to the quote.<br>|
|taxes|[object]|false|none|The list of taxes applicable for this quote.<br>|
|shipping_address|object|false|none|Shipping address for the quote.<br>|
|billing_address|object|false|none|Billing address for the quote.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_QuoteEntitlement">QuoteEntitlement</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaquoteentitlement"></a>
<a id="schema_QuoteEntitlement"></a>
<a id="tocSquoteentitlement"></a>
<a id="tocsquoteentitlement"></a>

```json
null
```

Overview
--------

The quote entitlement object represents the entitlement a [quote](/docs/api/quotes) holds for a [feature](/docs/api/features). A quote can have several quote entitlements, each tied to a specific feature and to an entity on the quote (such as a plan price, addon price, or charge price).

How quote entitlements are determined
-------------------------------------

Quote entitlements are based on the [entitlements](/docs/api/entitlements) linked to the [item prices](/docs/api/item_prices) on the quote. If an item price lacks an entitlement record for a particular feature, Chargebee considers the entitlement (when available) of its parent [item](/docs/api/items).

You can further customize entitlements by passing `entitlement_overrides` when creating or editing item-based quotes. When an entitlement has been explicitly overridden on the quote, `is_overridden` is `true` and the entitlement takes on the override `value`.

The method used to derive entitlement levels follows the same rules determined by the feature [type](/docs/api/features/feature-object#type) as described for [subscription entitlements](/docs/api/subscription_entitlements).

Use the [List Quote Entitlements](/docs/api/quote_entitlements/list-quote-entitlements) API to retrieve the entitlements associated with a quote.  
**Note**
Applicable only when Chargebee CPQ and Entitlements are enabled. To request access, contact [Chargebee Support](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/kb/getting-started/how-to-contact-chargebees-support-team?utm_source=docs_api&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=support).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|entity_id|string|true|none|The `id` of the entity on the quote whose entitlement this record represents.<br>|
|entity_type|string|true|none|The type of the entity on the quote for which this entitlement applies.<br><br>* charge_price - Indicates that the entity is an `item_price` with [`item_type`](/docs/api/item_prices/item-price-object#item_type) set to `charge`.<br>* addon_price - Indicates that the entity is an `item_price` with [`item_type`](/docs/api/item_prices/item-price-object#item_type) set to `addon`.<br>* plan_price - Indicates that the entity is an `item_price` with [`item_type`](/docs/api/item_prices/item-price-object#item_type) set to `plan`.<br>|
|feature_id|string|true|none|The unique identifier of the [feature](/docs/api/features)<br>.<br>|
|value|string|false|none|The level of entitlement that the quote entity has towards the feature. The possible values depend on the value of `feature.type`<br>:<br><br>* When `feature.type` is `custom`: The value can be any one of `levels[].value`.<br><br>* When `feature.type` is `switch`: This value is `true` when the feature is available; it is `false` when the feature is unavailable.<br><br>* When `feature.type` is `quantity`:<br><br>* When `levels[].is_unlimited` is not `true`: The value can be any one of `levels[].value`.<br><br>* When `levels[].is_unlimited` is `true`: The value can also be any one of `levels[].value` or it can be `unlimited` (case-insensitive), indicating unlimited entitlement.<br><br>* When `feature.type` is `range`:<br><br>* When `levels[].is_unlimited` is not `true`: The value can be any whole number between `levels[0].value` and `levels[1].value` (inclusive).<br><br>* When `levels[].is_unlimited` is `true`: The value can be any whole number equal to or greater than `levels[0].value` or it can be `unlimited` (case-insensitive), indicating unlimited entitlement.<br><br>**See also:**<br>[How quote entitlements are determined](/docs/api/quote_entitlements).<br>|
|is_enabled|boolean|true|none|Indicates whether the entitlement for the feature is enabled for the entity on the quote.<br>|
|start_date|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Start date (UTC timestamp) of this entitlement on the quote. Used with `end_date` for ramp-scoped entitlements.<br>|
|end_date|integer(unix-time)|false|none|End date (UTC timestamp) of this entitlement on the quote. Used with `start_date` for ramp-scoped entitlements.<br>|
|created_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Timestamp indicating when this quote entitlement record was created.<br>|
|modified_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Timestamp indicating when this quote entitlement record was last modified.<br>|
|is_overridden|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether the entitlement held by the quote entity for the feature is overridden via an `entitlement_overrides` record on the quote.<br>|
|feature_name|string|false|none|The [name of the feature](/docs/api/features/feature-object#name)<br>.<br>|
|feature_unit|string|false|none|[The unit of measure](/docs/api/features/feature-object#unit)<br>for the feature when its `type`<br>is either `quantity`<br>or `range`<br>.<br>|
|feature_type|string|false|none|Specifies the [type of the feature](/docs/api/features/feature-object#type)<br>associated with the granted quote entitlement.<br>|
|name|string|false|none|The display name of the entitlement level that the quote entity holds for the feature. It is derived based on the `type`<br>of feature as follows:<br><br>* When `feature.type` is `range` or `quantity`: the `name` is the space-separated concatenation of `value` and the pluralized form of `feature_unit`. For example, if `value` is `20` and `feature_unit` is `user`, then `name` becomes `20 users`.<br>* When `feature.type` is `custom`: the `name` is the same as `value`.<br>* When `feature.type` is `switch`: `name` is set to `Available` when `value` is `true`; it's set to `Not Available` when `value` is `false`.<br>|
|metered|boolean|false|none|Indicates if the feature is a metered feature.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|entity_type|plan_price|
|entity_type|addon_price|
|entity_type|charge_price|

<h2 id="tocS_QuoteLineGroup">QuoteLineGroup</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaquotelinegroup"></a>
<a id="schema_QuoteLineGroup"></a>
<a id="tocSquotelinegroup"></a>
<a id="tocsquotelinegroup"></a>

```json
null
```

The line items of a quote are grouped by charge event. Each of these groups is called a quote line group. A quote would have at least one quote line group. Let's look at an example.

Consider the following:

* A monthly plan A for $500 per month.
* A non-recurring addon B for $50. Now consider a quote that is created for 3 billing cycles of the plan with the addon applied immediately. This quote would be associated with a list of quote line groups: one for each charge event as shown below:

#### Quote Line group 1

**Plan A:**
$500

**Addon B:**
$50

**Total:**
$550

#### Quote Line group 2

**Plan A:**
$500

**Total:**
$500

#### Quote Line group 3

**Plan A:**
$500

**Total:**
$500

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|version|integer(int32)|false|none|Version of the quote line group.<br>|
|id|string|false|none|Uniquely identifies a quote line group.<br>|
|sub_total|integer(int64)|true|none|Subtotal in cents.<br>|
|total|integer(int64)|false|none|Total in cents.<br>|
|credits_applied|integer(int64)|false|none|Credits (in cents) applied to this quote line group.<br>|
|amount_paid|integer(int64)|false|none|Existing outstanding payments (in cents) if any, applied to this quote line group.<br>|
|amount_due|integer(int64)|false|none|Amount due in cents<br>|
|charge_event|string|false|none|Describes the time in the subscription lifecycle when the charge is to occur.<br><br>* subscription_creation - Subscription Creation<br>* trial_start - Trial Start<br>* subscription_renewal - Subscription Renewal<br>* subscription_change - Subscription Change<br>* subscription_cancel - Subscription Cancel<br>* immediate - Immediate<br>|

When a [quote](/docs/api/quotes) is created, it generates the `quoted_subscription` resource. This captures most of the details of the subscription that would eventually be created once the quote is invoiced. This resource is returned along with the quote for most of the associated operations.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|A unique and immutable identifier for the subscription. If not provided, it is autogenerated.<br>|
|billing_period|integer(int32)|false|none|none|
|billing_period_unit|string|false|none|none|
|start_date|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Applicable only when `operation_type`<br>of the quote is `create_subscription_for_customer`.<br>For subscriptions in the `future`<br>`status`<br>, this is the date/time when the subscription is set to start. The quote can be converted on a date/time after this date. This is called backdating the subscription creation. Backdating is performed when the subscription has already been provisioned but the conversion action has been delayed. Backdating is allowed only when the following prerequisites are met:<br><br>* Backdating is enabled for subscription creation operations.<br>* The current day of the month does not exceed the limit set in Chargebee for backdating such operations. This day is typically the day of the month by which the accounting for the previous month must be closed.<br>* The date is not more than duration X into the past where X is the billing period of the plan. For example, if the period of the subscription's plan is 2 months and today is 14th April, the `start_date` cannot be earlier than 14th February.<br>|
|trial_end|integer(unix-time)|false|none|End of the trial period for the subscription. Presence of this value for 'future' subscription implies the subscription will go into 'in_trial' state when it starts.<br>|
|remaining_billing_cycles|integer(int32)|false|none|* When the subscription is not on a contract term: this value is the number of billing cycles remaining after the current cycle, at the end of which, the subscription cancels.<br>* When the subscription is on a [contract term](/docs/api/contract_terms): this value is the number of billing cycles remaining in the contract term after the current billing cycle.<br>|
|po_number|string|false|none|Purchase order number for this subscription.<br>|
|auto_collection|string|false|none|none|
|plan_quantity_in_decimal|string|false|none|The decimal representation of the quantity of the plan purchased. Returned for quantity-based plans when [multi-decimal pricing](/docs/api/currencies)<br>is enabled.<br>|
|plan_unit_price_in_decimal|string|false|none|The decimal representation of the price or per-unit price of the plan. The value is in major units of the currency. Always returned when [multi-decimal pricing](/docs/api/currencies)<br>is enabled.<br>|
|changes_scheduled_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Applicable only when `operation_type`<br>of the quote is `change_subscription`.<br>When `change_option`<br>is set to `specific_date`<br>, then this is the date/time at which the subscription change is scheduled to occur. The quote can be converted on a date/time after this date. This is called backdating the subscription change and performed when the subscription change has already been provisioned but the conversion action has been delayed. Backdating is allowed only when the following prerequisites are met:<br><br>* Backdating must be enabled for subscription change operations.<br><br>* Only the following changes can be backdated:<br><br>* Changes in the recurring items or their prices.<br><br>* Addition of non-recurring items.<br><br>* Subscription `status` is `active`, `cancelled`, or `non_renewing`.<br><br>* The current day of the month does not exceed the limit set in Chargebee for backdating subscription change. This limit is the day of the month by which the accounting for the previous month must be closed.<br><br>* The date is on or after `current_term_start`.<br><br>* The date is on or after the last date/time any of the following changes were made:<br><br>* Changes in the recurring items or their prices.<br><br>* Addition of non-recurring items.<br><br>* The date is not more than duration X into the past where X is the billing period of the plan. For example, if the period of the subscription's plan is 2 months and today is 14th April, `changes_scheduled_at` cannot be earlier than 14th February.<br><br>|
|change_option|string|false|none|Applicable only when `operation_type`<br>of the quote is `change_subscription`.<br>When the quote is converted, this attribute determines the date/time as of when the subscription change is to be carried out.<br><br>* end_of_term - The change is scheduled to be carried out at the end of the billing cycle of the subscription.<br>* specific_date -<br>  The change is carried out as of `changes_scheduled_at`<br>  .<br>* immediately - The change is carried out immediately upon quote conversion.<br>|
|free_period|integer(int32)|false|none|The period of time by which the first term of the subscription is extended free of charge. The value is expressed in the time unit specified by `free_period_unit`. For example, `3` with `free_period_unit` = `month` means 3 free months are added to the first term.  <br>**Constraints**<br><br>* Applicable only when `operation_type` is `create_subscription_for_customer`.<br>* Applicable only when Chargebee CPQ is enabled. To request access, [contact Chargebee Support](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/kb/getting-started/how-to-contact-chargebees-support-team?utm_source=docs_api&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=support)<br>|
|free_period_unit|string|false|none|The time unit for `free_period`.  <br>**Constraints**<br><br>* Applicable only when `operation_type` is `create_subscription_for_customer`.<br>* Applicable only when Chargebee CPQ is enabled. To request access, [contact Chargebee Support](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/kb/getting-started/how-to-contact-chargebees-support-team?utm_source=docs_api&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=support)<br><br>* week - Charge based on week(s)<br>* month - Charge based on month(s)<br>* day - Charge based on day(s)<br>* year - Charge based on year(s)<br>|
|contract_term_billing_cycle_on_renewal|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of billing cycles the new contract term should run for, on contract renewal. The default value is the same as `billing_cycles`<br>or a custom value depending on the [site configuration](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/contract-terms.html#configuring-contract-terms)<br>.<br>|
|coupons|[object]|false|none|List of coupons for this subscription<br>|
|discounts|[object]|false|none|List of discounts for this quoted subscription.<br>|
|subscription_items|[object]|false|none|Details of individual [item prices](/docs/api/item_prices)<br>that are part of this subscription<br>|
|item_tiers|[object]|false|none|List of item tier.<br>|
|quoted_contract_term|object|false|none|The details of the contract term to be created when this quote is invoiced.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|---|---|

|billing_period_unit|week|
|billing_period_unit|month|
|billing_period_unit|year|
|auto_collection|on|
|auto_collection|off|

|change_option|specific_date|
|change_option|immediately|

<h2 id="tocS_Ramp">Ramp</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaramp"></a>
<a id="schema_Ramp"></a>
<a id="tocSramp"></a>
<a id="tocsramp"></a>

```json
null
```

A `ramp` resource, or subscription ramp, represents a planned change to a [`subscription`](/docs/api/subscriptions) that occurs at a future date. Use this resource to define and schedule subscription modifications, such as updating pricing, altering quantity, or transitioning to a different plan, without immediately applying them.  
**Note**

* **Upcoming ramps limit** : A subscription can have a maximum of 12 upcoming ramps at any given time, excluding deleted ramps. Upcoming ramps are ramps with `status` as [`scheduled`](/docs/api/ramps/ramp-object#status).
* **Total ramps limit**: A subscription can have a maximum of 100 ramps at any given time, excluding deleted ramps.  

#### Auto-draft conditions

When you create or update a ramp, Chargebee automatically moves any existing ramps scheduled after that ramp to `draft` status if either of the following conditions is met:

* The new or updated ramp changes the subscription [term end date](subscriptions#subscription_current_term_end).
* The new or updated ramp changes the subscription billing frequency. That is, either of the following [attributes](subscriptions#subscription_items) is changed:
  * `subscription_items[i].billing_period`
  * `subscription_items[i].billing_period_unit`
  * where `i` is the index where `subscription_items[i].item_type` is `plan`.
* The new or updated ramp introduces an [addon](item_prices#item_price_item_type) that is not [applicable](attached_items) to the plan in one or more of the subsequent ramps.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|A unique and immutable identifier for the ramp.<br>|
|description|string|false|none|A brief summary of the pricing changes applied with this ramp.<br>|
|subscription_id|string|true|none|The ID of the subscription for which this ramp was created.<br>|
|effective_from|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Specifies the time when the changes to the subscription will be applied by executing the ramp.<br>|
|status|string|true|none|The execution status of the ramp<br><br>* succeeded - The ramp completed successfully.<br>* scheduled -<br>  The ramp has been created and scheduled for execution.  <br>  **Note**<br>  Excluding deleted ramps, a subscription can have a maximum of 12 ramps in the `scheduled` `status`.<br>* draft -<br>  The ramp is moved to `draft`<br>  status when the associated subscription is updated. The reason for the draft status can be explained in the [status_transition_reason](/docs/api/ramps/ramp-object#status_transition_reason)  <br>  **Note**<br>  Ramps in draft state will not be executed.<br>* failed - The ramp did not complete because of an error.<br>|
|created_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Timestamp indicating when this resource was created.<br>|
|resource_version|integer(int64)|false|none|Version number of this resource. The `resource_version`<br>is updated with a new timestamp in milliseconds for every change made to the resource.<br>|
|updated_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Timestamp indicating when this resource was last updated.<br>|
|items_to_remove|[string]|false|none|List of [item prices](/docs/api/item_prices)<br>removed from the subscription through this ramp.<br>|
|coupons_to_remove|[string]|false|none|List of [coupons](/docs/api/coupons)<br>removed from the subscription through this ramp.<br>|
|discounts_to_remove|[string]|false|none|List of [discounts](/docs/api/discounts)<br>removed from the subscription through this ramp.<br>|
|deleted|boolean|true|none|Indicates if the ramp is marked as deleted. To retrieve deleted ramps, use the [List subscription ramps](/docs/api/ramps/list-ramps)<br>endpoint with [include_deleted](/docs/api/ramps/list-ramps)<br>set to `true`<br>.<br>|
|items_to_add|[object]|false|none|Details about the [item prices](/docs/api/item_prices)<br>added to the subscription through this ramp.<br>|
|items_to_update|[object]|false|none|Details about the [item prices](/docs/api/item_prices)<br>updated in the subscription through this ramp.<br>|
|coupons_to_add|[object]|false|none|Details about the [coupons](/docs/api/coupons)<br>added to the subscription through this ramp.<br>|
|discounts_to_add|[object]|false|none|Details about the [discounts](/docs/api/discounts)<br>added to the subscription through this ramp.<br>|
|item_tiers|[object]|false|none|**Note**<br>Allowed only when both of these conditions are met:<br><br>* [Price overriding](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/price-override.html) is enabled for the site.<br>* `pricing_model` of the item price is either `tiered`, `volume`, or `stairstep`.<br><br>Overrides the [item_tiers](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object#item_tiers) for specific `item_prices` of the subscription.<br>|
|contract_term|object|false|none|An object that specifies the contract term details.<br>|
|billing_configuration|object|false|none|Billing-related settings to update when this ramp is executed.<br>|
|status_transition_reason|object|false|none|Detailed reason for the status transition of a ramp to [draft](/docs/api/ramps/ramp-object#status)<br>and [failed](/docs/api/ramps/ramp-object#status)<br>status.<br>|
|entitlement_overrides_to_add|[object]|false|none|none|
|entitlement_overrides_to_update|[object]|false|none|none|
|entitlement_overrides_to_remove|[object]|false|none|none|
|credit_unit_grants_to_add|[object]|false|none|none|
|credit_unit_grants_to_update|[object]|false|none|none|
|credit_unit_grants_to_remove|[object]|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|scheduled|
|status|succeeded|
|status|failed|
|status|draft|

<h2 id="tocS_RecordedPurchase">RecordedPurchase</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarecordedpurchase"></a>
<a id="schema_RecordedPurchase"></a>
<a id="tocSrecordedpurchase"></a>
<a id="tocsrecordedpurchase"></a>

```json
null
```

**Important**

* Handle the **synchronous** API response first. Record a Purchase can fail immediately (for example, an incorrect `app_id`, a malformed URL or request, or recording a purchase that already belongs to a different customer) before a job is created---treat these as standard API errors (`4xx`). To reassign an existing omnichannel subscription to another customer, use [Move an omnichannel subscription](/docs/api/omnichannel_subscriptions/move-an-omnichannel-subscription) instead of re-recording the purchase.
* After the call is accepted, purchase validation with Apple or Google is **asynchronous** . Track the job with `status` (`in_process` → `completed`, `failed`, or `ignored`). Omnichannel subscription or one-time order creation happens only after successful async completion.
* This resource is applicable for Apple App Store and Google Play Store.

The recorded purchase resource represents a background job that syncs in-app purchases made through Apple App Store and Google Play Store with Chargebee. The [status](/docs/api/recorded_purchases/recorded_purchase-object#status) (`in_process`, `completed`, `failed`, and `ignored`) attribute represents the current status of the background job.

### Record Apple and Google in-app purchases and retrieve linked omnichannel resources

You can record subscription and one-time-order purchases made on Apple App Store or Google Play Store, then retrieve the resulting omnichannel resources.

To record a purchase and retrieve details, follow these steps:

1. Use the [Record a Purchase API](/docs/api/recorded_purchases/record-a-purchase) with `app_id`, `customer[id]`, and exactly one store payload:

   * **Apple App Store (preferred)** : `apple_app_store[transaction_id]` for a new subscription, expired re-purchase, or one-time product.

   * **Apple App Store (receipt path)** : `apple_app_store[receipt]` and `apple_app_store[product_id]`.

   * **Google Play Store (preferred)** : `google_play_store[order_id]` for a subscription or one-time order.

   * **Google Play Store (subscription token path)** : `google_play_store[purchase_token]`.

   * **Google Play Store (one-time order token path)** : `google_play_store[purchase_token]` and `google_play_store[product_id]`.

2. The API response includes a `recorded_purchase` object with the [status](/docs/api/recorded_purchases/recorded_purchase-object#status) of the job.

3. When recording completes successfully, `status` updates from `in_process` to `completed` and Chargebee sets `omnichannel_transaction_id` plus either:

   * **Subscription** : `linked_omnichannel_subscriptions`, with webhook [`omnichannel_subscription_created`](/docs/api/events/webhook/omnichannel_subscription_created) (or [`omnichannel_subscription_imported`](/docs/api/events/webhook/omnichannel_subscription_imported)).
   * **One-time order** : `linked_omnichannel_one_time_orders`, with webhook [`omnichannel_one_time_order_created`](/docs/api/events/webhook/omnichannel_one_time_order_created).
4. In addition to webhooks, retrieve the job by the `recorded_purchase` [id](/docs/api/recorded_purchases/recorded_purchase-object#id) returned when you record the purchase.

If `status` is `failed`, review [error_detail](/docs/api/recorded_purchases/recorded_purchase-object#error_detail) and see [`record_purchase_failed`](/docs/api/events/webhook/record_purchase_failed).

If `status` is `ignored`, the purchase was already recorded in Chargebee as an omnichannel subscription or one-time order. Chargebee does not create a new linked resource for this job---use the existing omnichannel subscription or one-time order. Linked IDs and `omnichannel_transaction_id` are populated when `status` is `completed`, not for `ignored`.

See also [omnichannel events](/docs/api/omnichannel_events).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|A unique ID generated by Chargebee for the recorded purchase job.<br>|
|customer_id|string|true|none|The `id`<br>of the [customer](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#id)<br>object associated with this purchase. If the `customer_id`<br>is not present in Chargebee when the [record_a_purchase](/docs/api/recorded_purchases/record-a-purchase)<br>API request is made, Chargebee automatically creates the customer using the details provided in the request.<br>|
|app_id|string|true|none|App Identifier in Chargebee. This is the handle created by Chargebee for your app. To get the `app_id`:<br><br>* For **Apple** , follow [these steps](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/mobile-subscriptions/omnichannel-app-store#create-an-omnichannel-subscription-for-in-app-purchases).<br>* For **Google** , follow [these steps](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/mobile-subscriptions/omnichannel-play-store#connect-google-app-to-chargebee-to-generate-unique-app-id-and-notifications-url).<br>|
|source|string|true|none|The source where the purchase is originally made and managed.<br><br>* google_play_store - The purchase originated from the Google Play Store.<br>* apple_app_store - The purchase originated from the Apple App Store.<br>|
|status|string|true|none|Current status of the recorded purchase operation.<br><br>* completed - The purchase recording job completed successfully. You receive `omnichannel_transaction_id` and either `linked_omnichannel_subscriptions` (subscription purchase) or `linked_omnichannel_one_time_orders` (one-time order purchase).<br>* ignored -<br>  Terminal status when the purchase was already recorded in Chargebee as an omnichannel subscription or one-time order (same store purchase / customer association).<br>  Chargebee does **not** create a new linked resource for this job. Use the existing omnichannel subscription or one-time order in Chargebee rather than treating this job as a new successful recording.<br>  `linked_omnichannel_subscriptions` / `linked_omnichannel_one_time_orders` and `omnichannel_transaction_id` are returned when `status` is `completed`, not for `ignored`.<br>* failed -<br>  The purchase recording job failed. You do **not** receive `omnichannel_transaction_id` or linked subscription / one-time-order objects. Check the [error_detail](/docs/api/recorded_purchases/recorded_purchase-object#error_detail)<br>  attribute for the failure reason. Chargebee may also emit [`record_purchase_failed`](/docs/api/events/webhook/record_purchase_failed).<br>* in_process - The purchase recording job is in progress. You do **not** yet receive `omnichannel_transaction_id` or linked subscription / one-time-order objects.<br>|
|omnichannel_transaction_id|string|false|none|The `id`<br>of the [omnichannel transaction](/docs/api/omnichannel_transactions/omnichannel_transaction-object#id)<br>object associated with the purchase. Present when `status` is `completed`.<br>|
|created_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Timestamp when the `recorded_purchase` resource was created in Chargebee.<br>|
|resource_version|integer(int64)|false|none|Version number of this resource. The `resource_version`<br>is updated with a new timestamp in milliseconds for every change made to the resource.<br>|
|linked_omnichannel_subscriptions|[object]|false|none|The list of omnichannel subscriptions created for this purchase. Applicable when the recorded purchase is a subscription. Present when `status` is `completed`.<br>|
|linked_omnichannel_one_time_orders|[object]|false|none|The list of omnichannel one-time orders created for this purchase. Applicable when the recorded purchase is a one-time order. Present when `status` is `completed`.<br>|
|error_detail|object|false|none|Applicable only for recorded purchases where the job status is `failed`.<br>It provides more details about the failure.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|source|apple_app_store|
|source|google_play_store|
|source|roku|
|source|amazon_app_store|
|status|in_process|
|status|completed|
|status|failed|
|status|ignored|
