<h2 id="tocS_SalesOrder">SalesOrder</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasalesorder"></a>
<a id="schema_SalesOrder"></a>
<a id="tocSsalesorder"></a>
<a id="tocssalesorder"></a>

```json
null
```

Sales orders represent the contractual agreement and commitment for services between a seller and a buyer. They act as a seamless interface connecting any sales system (such as CPQ, CRM, or Customer Portal) with Chargebee Billing. The sales order captures the following essential components

* Order Line Items including discounts and ramps
* Billing and payment configuration
* Contract terms and conditions
* Customer information including billing and shipping contacts
* Meta data

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|External identifier of the sales order.<br>|
|version|integer(int32)|true|none|Version of the sales order.<br>|
|renewed_from_order_id|string|false|none|The unique identifier of the original sales order from which this order was renewed. This field is used to track renewal orders and link them to their previous sales transactions.<br>|
|updated_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Indicates the timestamp at which this sales order was last updated.<br>|
|created_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Timestamp indicating sales order created.<br>|
|po_number|string|false|none|Buyer's purchase order reference number.<br>|
|meta_data|string|false|none|A set of key-value pairs stored as additional information for the subscription. [Learn more](/docs/api/sales_orders)<br>.<br>|
|quote_id|string|false|none|Primary quote id for which the order was placed.<br>|
|effective_date|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Effective start date of the order signifies when the contract is signed and becomes legally binding.<br>|
|end_date|integer(unix-time)|false|none|The date when the order is considered completed, cancelled, or no longer valid.<br>|
|business_entity_id|string|false|none|The unique ID of the<br>[business entity](/docs/api/getting-started)<br>of this sales order.<br>|
|customer_id|string|true|none|The unique ID of the customer to which this sales order belongs.<br>|
|subscription_id|string|true|none|none|
|currency_code|string|true|none|The currency code (ISO 4217 format) of the sales order.<br>|
|subscription_ids|[string]|false|none|The unique identifiers of the [subscriptions](/docs/api/subscriptions)<br>that are bundled as part of this sales order.<br>|
|status|string|true|none|Status of the sales order.<br><br>* completed - completed<br>* active - active<br>|
|deleted|boolean|true|none|none|
|line_items|[object]|false|none|Line items of this sales order<br>|
|billing_addresses|[object]|false|none|Billing address for a customer.<br>|
|discounts|[object]|false|none|List of discounts for this subscription<br>|
|shipping_addresses|[object]|false|none|Shipping address for the subscription.<br>|
|line_item_tiers|[object]|false|none|The pricing details of `line_items`<br>which have `pricing_model`<br>as `tiered`<br>, `volume`<br>or `stairstep`.<br>[Learn more](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/plans.html#pricing-models)<br>about pricing models.<br>|
|payment_configuration|object|false|none|Payment configuration of this sales order<br>|
|billing_configuration|object|false|none|Configurations controlling billing behavior and invoice generation workflows.<br>|
|renewal_term|object|false|none|Renewal term for this sales order.<br>|
|credit_lines|[object]|false|none|none|
|entitlement_overrides|[object]|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|active|
|status|completed|

<h2 id="tocS_Subscription">Subscription</h2>

A Chargebee subscription connects a customer record to products/services. It describes what the customer has signed up for and how often they're charged for it. The essential components of a subscription are:

* A [plan-item price](/docs/api/item_prices).
* Any addon- and charge-item prices applied to the subscription.
* Any [coupons](/docs/api/coupons) applied.
* Any [discounts](/docs/api/discounts) applied.

The charges in a subscription are billed via invoices.  
**Note:**
The maximum number of subscriptions for any given [customer](/docs/api/customers)
([active](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object#status)
or not) is 900.  

#### Subscription billing frequencies

Chargebee offers two billing frequency options for subscriptions:

* **Plan-based billing** (`default`): Subscriptions are billed based on the billing period defined for the item price of the `item_type` `plan`. [Learn more](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/subscriptions#plan-based-billing).

* **Multi-frequency billing** : Subscriptions are billed according to the billing period of each recurring item price within the subscription. [Learn more](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/multi-frequency-billing).

  **Important**

  [Limitations](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/subscriptions/multi-frequency-billing#limitations) of Multi-frequency billing.

The selection of the billing frequency preference is configured at the site level.  

#### Item price compatibility in a subscription

When creating or updating a subscription, one of the item prices specified under subscription_items must be a plan-item price. The remaining must be compatible addon- or charge-item prices. An item price is compatible with a plan-item price if their currencies are the same. Additionally, an addon-item price is compatible with a plan-item price only if their billing frequencies meet the following conditions:  

| `period_unit` for plan-item price | Compatible `period_unit` for addon-item price |                                                                                                                                                                                                Compatible period for addon-item price                                                                                                                                                                                                |
|-----------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `day`                             | `day`                                         | The `period` of the plan-item price should be divisible by the `period` of the addon-item price. **Example** If the `period` of the plan-item price is `10`, then the period of the addon-item price can be `10`, `5`, `2`, or `1`.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `week`                            | `week` or `day`                               | The `period` (in days) of the plan-item price should be divisible by the `period` of the addon-item price. **Example** If the `period` of the plan-item price is `2`, then the period of the addon-item price can be as follows depending on the value of `period_unit`: * for `period_unit` as `week`, `period` can be `2` or `1`. * for `period_unit` as `day`, `period` can be `14`, `7`, `2`, or `1`.                            |
| `month`                           | `month`                                       | The `period` of the plan-item price should be divisible by the `period` of the addon-item price. **Example** If the `period` of the plan-item price is `6`, then the `period` of the addon-item price can be `6`, `3`, `2`, or `1`.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `year`                            | `year` or `month`                             | The `period` (in months) of the plan-item price should be divisible by the `period` of the addon-item price. **Example** If the `period` of the plan-item price is `2`, then the `period` of the addon-item price can be as follows depending on the value of `period_unit`: * for `period_unit` as `year`, `period` can be `2` or `1`. * for `period_unit` as `month`, `period` can be `24`, `12`, `8`, `6`, `4`, `3`, `2`, or `1`. |

#### Ramps API compatibility mode

If you want to schedule changes on a subscription, use the [Ramps API](/docs/api/ramps).

If you are currently scheduling changes through the [Update subscription API](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items), migrate to the Ramps API. To get started, [request access for Subscription Ramps](https://app.chargebee.com/login?forward=https://app.chargebee.com/request_access/subscription-ramps&ref=feature). Chargebee will enable Ramps compatibility mode for your site. Once enabled, you can test the Ramps API without impacting your existing integrations.

The following parts of the Billing API have subtle differences in behavior when the Ramps feature is disabled versus when it is enabled with compatibility mode. (Follow the links to learn more.)

* The value of the [`subscription.has_scheduled_changes`](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object#has_scheduled_changes) attribute.
* [Update subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items#impact-scheduled-changes)
* [Create Checkout for updating a subscription](/docs/api/hosted_pages/create-checkout-to-update-a-subscription#impact-scheduled-changes)
* [Remove scheduled changes](/docs/api/subscriptions/remove-scheduled-changes)
* [Retrieve with scheduled changes](/docs/api/subscriptions/retrieve-with-scheduled-changes)
* [Create a quote for updating a subscription](/docs/api/quotes/create-a-quote-for-update-subscription-items)
* [Edit a quote for updating a subscription](/docs/api/quotes/edit-update-subscription-quote-for-items)
* [Portal sessions](/docs/api/portal_sessions#scheduled-subscription-changes)

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|The unique identifier of the `subscription`<br>resource. You have the option to specify this value when creating a customer. If not specified, Chargebee automatically generates a unique identifier.  <br>**Note**<br>In the event that the subscription resource is [transferred](/docs/api/business_entities/transfer-resources-to-another-business-entity) along with its associated [customer](/docs/api/customers) resource to a different business entity, Chargebee assigns a new random value as the `id` for the subscription. The original identifier is preserved for the transferred copy of the `subscription` resource. (See also: [Mechanics of business entity transfer](/docs/api/business_entities).)<br>|
|currency_code|string|true|none|The currency code ([ISO 4217 format](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/supported-currencies.html)<br>) of the subscription<br>|
|billing_period|integer(int32)|false|none|Specifies the length of each billing cycle (or term) of the subscription, expressed in the unit defined by `billing_period_unit`.<br>|
|billing_period_unit|string|false|none|Specifies the unit used to measure the `billing_period`.<br><br>* day - Charge based on day(s)<br>* month - Charge based on month(s)<br>* year - Charge based on year(s)<br>* week - Charge based on week(s)<br>|
|start_date|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Applicable only for 'future' subscriptions. The scheduled start time of the subscription.<br>|
|trial_end|integer(unix-time)|false|none|End of the trial period for the subscription. Presence of this value for 'future' subscription implies the subscription will go into 'in_trial' state when it starts.<br>|
|remaining_billing_cycles|integer(int32)|false|none|* When the subscription is not on a contract term: this value is the number of billing cycles remaining after the current cycle, at the end of which, the subscription cancels.<br>* When the subscription is on a [contract term](/docs/api/contract_terms): this value is the number of billing cycles remaining in the contract term after the current billing cycle.<br>|
|po_number|string|false|none|Purchase order number for this subscription.<br>|
|auto_collection|string|false|none|Defines whether payments need to be collected automatically for this subscription. Overrides customer's auto-collection property.<br><br>* on - Whenever an invoice is created for this subscription, an automatic charge will be attempted on the payment method available.<br>* off - Automatic collection of charges will not be made for this subscription. Use this for offline payments.<br>|
|plan_quantity_in_decimal|string|false|none|The decimal representation of the quantity of the plan purchased. Returned for quantity-based plans when [multi-decimal pricing](/docs/api/currencies)<br>is enabled.<br>|
|plan_unit_price_in_decimal|string|false|none|The decimal representation of the price or per-unit price of the plan. The value is in major units of the currency. Always returned when [multi-decimal pricing](/docs/api/currencies)<br>is enabled.<br>|
|customer_id|string|true|none|Identifier of the customer with whom this subscription is associated.<br>|
|status|string|true|none|Current state of the subscription<br><br>* future - The subscription is scheduled to start at a future date.<br>* non_renewing - The subscription will be canceled at the end of the current term.<br>* active - The subscription is active and will be charged for automatically based on the items in it.<br>* cancelled - The subscription has been canceled and is no longer in service.<br>* transferred -<br>  The `transferred`<br>  status will be reflected on the source business entity's subscription attribute once the [customer transfer](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/mbe-getting-started-with-customer-transfer.html)<br>  activity is completed successfully.<br>* in_trial - The subscription is in trial.<br>* paused -<br>  The subscription is [paused](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/pause-subscription.html).<br>  The subscription will not renew while in this state.<br>|
|trial_start|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Start of the trial period for the subscription. Presence of this value for `future`<br>subscription implies the subscription will go into `in_trial`<br>state when it starts.<br>|
|trial_end_action|string|false|none|Applicable only when [End-of-trial Action](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/trial_periods_hidden.html#how-to-define-the-end-of-trial-actions-for-subscriptions)<br>has been enabled for the site. Whenever the subscription has a trial period, this attribute (parameter) is returned (required) and specifies the operation to be carried out for the subscription once the trial ends.<br><br>* activate_subscription - The subscription activates and charges are raised for non-metered items.<br>* cancel_subscription - The subscription cancels.<br>* plan_default -<br>  The action [configured for the site](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/trial_periods_hidden.html#how-to-define-the-end-of-trial-actions-for-subscriptions)<br>  at the time when the trial ends, takes effect.<br>* site_default -<br>  This is the default value. The action [configured for the site](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/trial_periods_hidden.html#how-to-define-the-end-of-trial-actions-for-subscriptions)<br>  at the time when the trial ends, takes effect.<br>|
|current_term_start|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Start of the current billing period of the subscription.<br>|
|current_term_end|integer(unix-time)|false|none|End of the current billing period of the subscription. Subscription is renewed immediately after this.<br>|
|next_billing_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|The date/time at which the next billing for the subscription happens. This is usually right after `current_term_end`<br>unless multiple subscription terms were invoiced in advance using the `terms_to_charge`<br>parameter.<br>|
|created_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|The time at which the subscription was created.<br>|
|started_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Time at which the subscription was started. Is `null`<br>for `future`<br>subscriptions as it is yet to be started.<br>|
|activated_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Time at which the subscription `status`<br>last changed to<br>`active`.<br>For example, this value is updated when an `in_trial`<br>or<br>`cancelled`<br>subscription activates.<br>|

|invoice_notes|string|false|none|A customer-facing note added to all invoices associated with this subscription. This note is one among [all the notes](/docs/api/invoices/invoice-object#notes)<br>displayed on the invoice PDF.<br>|
|meta_data|object|false|none|A collection of key-value pairs that provides extra information about the subscription.  <br>**Note:**<br>There's a character limit of 65,535.<br><br>[Learn more](/docs/api/advanced-features#metadata)<br>.<br>|
|deleted|boolean|true|none|Indicates that the subscription has been deleted when the value is `true`.<br>You can retrieve a deleted subscription using the [list operation](/docs/api/subscriptions/list-subscriptions)<br>.<br>|
|changes_scheduled_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|The date-time at which the subscription change is scheduled to happen.  <br>**Note**<br>This attribute is not returned when the change is scheduled to happen at the end of the current term.<br>|
|cancel_reason_code|string|false|none|Reason code for canceling the subscription. Must be one from a list of reason codes set in the Chargebee app in **Settings \> Configure Chargebee \> Reason Codes \> Subscriptions \> Subscription Cancellation**.<br>Must be passed if set as mandatory in the app. The codes are case-sensitive<br>|
|free_period|integer(int32)|false|none|The period of time by which the first term of the subscription is extended free of charge. The value is expressed in the time unit specified by `free_period_unit`. For example, `3` with `free_period_unit` = `month` means 3 free months are added to the first term.<br>|
|free_period_unit|string|false|none|The time unit for `free_period`.<br><br>* week - Charge based on week(s)<br>* month - Charge based on month(s)<br>* day - Charge based on day(s)<br>* year - Charge based on year(s)<br>|
|create_pending_invoices|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether the invoices for this subscription are generated with a `pending` `status`. This attribute is set to `true` automatically when the subscription has item prices that belong to `metered` items.<br>You can also set this to `true` explicitly using the [create](/docs/api/subscriptions/create-subscription-for-items#create_pending_invoices)/[update](/docs/api/subscriptions/update-subscription-for-items#create_pending_invoices) subscription operations. This is useful in the following scenarios:<br><br>* When tracking usages and calculating usage-based charges on your end. You can then add them to the subscription as a [one-time charge](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/charges.html) at the end of the billing term.<br>* When you need to inspect all charges before closing invoices for this subscription. Applicable only when [Metered Billing](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/metered_billing.html) is enabled for the site<br>|
|auto_close_invoices|boolean|false|none|Set to `false`<br>to override for this subscription, the [site-level setting](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/usage-based-billing/metered_billing#configuring-metered-billing)<br>for auto-closing invoices. Only applicable when auto-closing invoices has been enabled for the site. This attribute has a higher precedence than the same attribute at the [customer level](/docs/api/customers/customer-object#auto_close_invoices)<br>.<br>|
|business_entity_id|string|false|none|The unique ID of the [business entity](/docs/api/advanced-features)<br>of this subscription. This is always the same as the [business entity](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object#customer_id)<br>of the customer.<br>|
|decommissioned|boolean|true|none|Indicates whether the subscription has been [decommissioned](/docs/api/subscriptions/cancel-subscription-for-items#decommissioned). If set to `true` all subscription operations are disabled except deletion.  <br>**Note** : Decommission operation is irreversible. Once set to `true` it cannot be updated to `false` and thus subscription will remain decommissioned permanently.<br>|
|brand_id|string|false|none|The unique ID of the [brand](/docs/api/brands) this subscription belongs to. This is the brand of the customer the subscription was created for, unless a different brand was specified in the create request.<br>|
|subscription_items|[object]|false|none|Details of individual [item prices](/docs/api/item_prices)<br>that are part of this subscription.<br>|
|item_tiers|[object]|false|none|The pricing details of `subscription_items`<br>which have [pricing_model](/docs/api/item_prices/item_price-object#pricing_model)<br>as<br>`tiered`<br>, `volume`<br>or `stairstep`<br>.<br>|
|charged_items|[object]|false|none|List of event based charge items that have already been charged.<br>|
|coupons|[object]|false|none|List of coupons for this subscription<br>|
|shipping_address|object|false|none|Shipping address for the subscription.<br>|
|referral_info|object|false|none|Referral details if exists for the subscription<br>|
|billing_override|object|false|none|Specify limits on how credits and excess payments are applied to individual invoices for the subscription.  <br>**Prerequisite**<br><br>* [Credit flexibility](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/invoices-credit-notes-and-quotes/credit-notes#credits-flexibility) must be enabled for the site.  <br>**Constraints**<br><br>* These limits do not apply to [consolidated invoices](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/consolidated-invoicing.html).<br>|
|contract_term|object|false|none|Contract terms for this subscription<br>|
|discounts|[object]|false|none|List of [discounts](/docs/api/discounts)<br>currently attached to the subscription.  <br>**Note**<br><br>* Discounts of [duration_type](/docs/api/discounts/discount-object#duration_type) `one_time` are removed from the list after a single application to the subscription.<br>* Discounts of `duration_type` `limited_period` are removed from the list once the specified [period](/docs/api/discounts/discount-object#period) expires since their attachment to the subscription.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_SubscriptionEntitlement">SubscriptionEntitlement</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasubscriptionentitlement"></a>
<a id="schema_SubscriptionEntitlement"></a>
<a id="tocSsubscriptionentitlement"></a>
<a id="tocssubscriptionentitlement"></a>

```json
null
```

Overview
--------

The subscription entitlement object represents the entitlement a [subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions) holds for a [feature](/docs/api/features). A subscription can have several subscription entitlements, each tied to a specific feature.

How subscription entitlements are determined
--------------------------------------------

### With subscription-level entitlement override

When an [entitlement override](/docs/api/entitlement_overrides) with `entity_type` set to `subscription` is set for a subscription related to a feature, the subscription entitlement takes on the [value](/docs/api/entitlement_overrides/entitlement_override-object#value) of that override.  

### Without entitlement overrides

If there is no entitlement override for the subscription and feature, the subscription entitlement is based on the [entitlements](/docs/api/entitlements) linked to the [item prices](/docs/api/item_prices) within the [subscription items](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object#subscription_items). If an item price lacks an entitlement record for a particular feature, we consider the entitlement (when available) of its parent [item](/docs/api/items).

The method used to derive the subscription entitlement from these entitlements follows specific rules determined by the feature [type](/docs/api/features/feature-object#type). We outline and provide examples of these rules in the sections below:  
Switch feature  

#### Summary {#switch-content}

Consider a feature of type `switch`. Consider also a subscription whose subscription items correspond to item prices (or items) that have entitlements to the feature. Looking at these entitlements, we first determine the entitlement value held by each subscription item for this feature.

If the entitlement value for the feature held by **any** of the subscription items is `true`, then the subscription entitlement value is also set to `true`. Otherwise, the subscription entitlement value is set to `false`.

#### Example

##### 1. Feature record

Consider the following [feature](/docs/api/features) record:  

|        `id`        |  `type`  |                   `description`                   |
|--------------------|----------|---------------------------------------------------|
| `xero-integration` | `switch` | An integration with the Xero accounting software. |
[Table 1: Feature records.]

##### 2. Entitlement records

Consider the following [entitlement](/docs/api/entitlements) records for the `xero-integration` feature:  

|      `entity_id`      | `entity_type` | `value` |
|-----------------------|---------------|---------|
| `starter`             | `plan`        | `true`  |
| `starter-monthly-usd` | `plan_price`  | `false` |
| `plus`                | `addon`       | `true`  |
[Table 2: Entitlement records for the `xero-integration` feature.]

##### 3. Subscription-items records

Consider that a [subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions) with ID `AzZjAiTl1btqS2lEj` has the following `subscription_items[]` records:  

| Index |    `item_price_id`    | `quantity` |
|-------|-----------------------|------------|
| `0`   | `starter-monthly-usd` | `1`        |
| `1`   | `plus-monthly-usd`    | `1`        |
| `2`   | `installation-usd`    | `2`        |
[Table 3: Subscription-items records.]

##### 4. Subscription-item entitlements

Chargebee Billing now determines the entitlement held by each subscription item based on the entitlements defined in Table 2. This is shown in Table 4. For clarity, we've omitted the `quantity` column because it doesn't affect features with type `switch`.  

| Index |    `item_price_id`    |                         Entitlement value (determined from Table 2)                          |
|-------|-----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `0`   | `starter-monthly-usd` | `false` (Matches the value of the plan price.)                                               |
| `1`   | `plus-monthly-usd`    | `true` (Inherited from the addon `plus`, as no entitlement is defined for this addon price.) |
| `2`   | `installation-usd`    | None (No entitlement defined for the charge item.)                                           |
[Table 4: Entitlement values for subscription-items.]

##### 5. Determining final subscription entitlements

###### Case 1: Absence of a subscription-level override

In this scenario, the **final entitlement** (`subscription_entitlement.value`) for the `xero-integration` feature is set to `true` because at least one subscription-item entitlement value is `true`.

###### Case 2: With subscription-level override

Suppose there's an [entitlement override](/docs/api/entitlement_overrides) added to the subscription for the feature, as shown below:  

|     `entity_id`     | `entity_type`  |    `feature_id`    | `value` |
|---------------------|----------------|--------------------|---------|
| `AzZjAiTl1btqS2lEj` | `subscription` | `xero-integration` | `false` |
[Table 5: Entitlement override record for the subscription and feature.]

Given this override, the subscription's final entitlement value for the `xero-integration` feature is set to `false`.  
Quantity feature  

#### Summary {#quantity-content}

Consider a feature of type `quantity`. Consider also a subscription whose subscription items correspond to item prices (or items) that have entitlements to the feature. Looking at these entitlements, we first determine the entitlement value held by each subscription item for this feature.

If the entitlement value for the feature held by any of the subscription items is `unlimited`, then the subscription entitlement value is also `unlimited`. Otherwise, the subscription entitlement value is the sum of all the entitlement values of the subscription items.

#### Example

##### 1. Feature record

Consider the following feature record:  

|      `id`       |   `type`   |             `description`             |
|-----------------|------------|---------------------------------------|
| `user_licenses` | `quantity` | The number of user licenses provided. |
[Table 6: Feature records.]

Suppose that the feature has `feature.levels[]` records as follows:  

| `level` | `value`  | `is_unlimited` |
|---------|----------|----------------|
| `0`     | `5`      | `false`        |
| `1`     | `10`     | `false`        |
| `2`     | `20`     | `false`        |
| `3`     | Not set. | `true`         |
[Table 7: Feature levels records.]

##### 2. Entitlement records

Consider the following entitlement records for the `user_licenses` feature:  

|      `entity_id`      | `entity_type` |   `value`   |
|-----------------------|---------------|-------------|
| `starter`             | `plan`        | `10`        |
| `starter-monthly-usd` | `plan_price`  | `unlimited` |
| `plus`                | `addon`       | `5`         |
| `one-time`            | `charge`      | `5`         |
[Table 8: Entitlement records for the `user_licenses` feature.]

##### 3. Subscription-items records

Consider that a subscription with ID `AzZjAiTl1btqS2lEj` has the following `subscription_items[]` records:  

| Index |    `item_price_id`    | `quantity` |
|-------|-----------------------|------------|
| `0`   | `starter-monthly-usd` | `5`        |
| `1`   | `plus-monthly-usd`    | `10`       |
| `2`   | `one-time-usd`        | `1`        |
[Table 9: Subscription-items records.]

##### 4. Subscription-item entitlements

Chargebee Billing now determines the entitlement held by each subscription item based on the entitlements defined in Table 8. This is shown in Table 10.  

| Index |    `item_price_id`    | `quantity` |                        Entitlement value (determined from Table 8)                        | Entitlement value subtotal (Entitlement value × `quantity`) |
|-------|-----------------------|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| `0`   | `starter-monthly-usd` | `5`        | `unlimited` (Matches the value of the plan price.)                                        | `unlimited` (unlimited x 5)                                 |
| `1`   | `plus-monthly-usd`    | `10`       | `5` (Inherited from the addon `plus`, as no entitlement is defined for this addon price.) | `50` (5 x 10)                                               |
| `2`   | `one-time-usd`        | `1`        | `5` (Inherited from the charge `one-time`.)                                               | `5` (5 x 1)                                                 |
[Table 10: Entitlement values for subscription-items.]

##### 5. Determining final subscription entitlements

###### Case 1: Absence of a subscription-level override

In this scenario, the **final entitlement value** (`subscription_entitlement.value`) for the `user_licenses` feature is the total entitlement value from the last column in Table 10, which amounts to (unlimited + 50 + 5) = `unlimited`.

###### Case 2: With subscription-level override

Suppose there's an entitlement override added to the subscription for the feature, as shown below:  

|     `entity_id`     | `entity_type`  |  `feature_id`   | `value` |
|---------------------|----------------|-----------------|---------|
| `AzZjAiTl1btqS2lEj` | `subscription` | `user_licenses` | `20`    |
[Table 11: Entitlement override record for the subscription and feature.]

Given this override, the subscription's **final entitlement value** for the `user_licenses` feature is set to `20`.  
Range feature  

#### Summary {#range-content}

Consider a feature of type `range`. Consider also a subscription whose subscription items correspond to item prices (or items) that have entitlements to the feature. Looking at these entitlements, we first determine the entitlement value held by each subscription item for this feature.

If the entitlement value for the feature held by any of the subscription items is `unlimited`, then the subscription entitlement value is also `unlimited`. Otherwise, one of two scenarios are possible:

* If `feature.levels[1].is_unlimited` is `true`, the subscription entitlement value equals the sum of all entitlement values of the subscription items.

* If `feature.levels[1].is_unlimited` is `false`, the subscription entitlement value equals the sum of all entitlement values of the subscription items without exceeding the maximum value of `feature.level[1].value`.

#### Example

##### 1. Feature record

Consider the following feature record:  

|       `id`       | `type`  |                     `description`                      |
|------------------|---------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `api_rate_limit` | `range` | The maximum number of API requests allowed per minute. |
[Table 12: Feature records.]

Suppose that the feature has `feature.levels[]` records as follows:  

| `level` | `value` | `is_unlimited` |
|---------|---------|----------------|
| `0`     | `100`   | `false`        |
| `1`     | `1000`  | `false`        |
[Table 13: Feature levels records.]

##### 2. Entitlement records

Consider the following entitlement records for the `api_rate_limit` feature:  

|      `entity_id`      | `entity_type` | `value` |
|-----------------------|---------------|---------|
| `premium`             | `plan`        | `450`   |
| `premium-monthly-usd` | `plan_price`  | `400`   |
| `plus`                | `addon`       | `150`   |
[Table 14: Entitlement records for the `api_rate_limit` feature.]

##### 3. Subscription-items records

Consider that a subscription with ID `AzZjAiTl1btqS2lEj` has the following `subscription_items[]` records:  

| Index |    `item_price_id`    | `quantity` |
|-------|-----------------------|------------|
| `0`   | `premium-monthly-usd` | `2`        |
| `1`   | `plus-monthly-usd`    | `2`        |
[Table 15: Subscription-items records.]

##### 4. Subscription-item entitlements

Chargebee Billing now determines the entitlement held by each subscription item based on the entitlements defined in Table 14. This is shown in Table 16.  

| `subscription_items[]` index |    `item_price_id`    | `quantity` |                        Entitlement value (determined from Table 14)                         | Entitlement value subtotal (Entitlement value x `quantity`) |
|------------------------------|-----------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| `0`                          | `premium-monthly-usd` | `2`        | `400` (Matches the value of the plan price.)                                                | `800` (400 x 2)                                             |
| `1`                          | `plus-monthly-usd`    | `2`        | `150` (Inherited from the addon `plus`, as no entitlement is defined for this addon price.) | `300` (150 x 2)                                             |
[Table 16: Entitlement values for subscription-items.]

##### 5. Determining final subscription entitlements

###### Case 1: `feature.levels[1].is_unlimited` is `false`

In this scenario, the **final entitlement value** (`subscription_entitlement.value`) for the `api_rate_limit` feature is the total entitlement value from the last column in Table 16, capped at `feature.levels[1].value`. The total entitlement value is 800 + 300 = 1100. However, `feature.levels[1].value` is `1000`, which is less than 1100. Therefore, the final entitlement is `1000`.

###### Case 2: `feature.levels[1].is_unlimited` is `true`

In this scenario, `feature.levels[1].value` is disregarded, and the **final entitlement value** is not capped. In other words, the final entitlement value is `1100`.  
Custom feature  

#### Summary {#custom-content}

Consider a feature of type `custom`. Consider also a subscription whose subscription items correspond to item prices (or items) that have entitlements to the feature.

Looking at these entitlements, we first determine the entitlement value held by each subscription item for this feature. The subscription entitlement value is then set to the highest of these identified values.

#### Example

##### 1. Feature record

Consider the following feature record:  

|   `id`    |  `type`  |                        `description`                        |
|-----------|----------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| `support` | `custom` | `The form of after-sales support provided to the customer.` |
[Table 17: Feature records.]

Suppose that the feature has `feature.levels[]` records as follows:  

| `level` | `value` |
|---------|---------|
| `0`     | `email` |
| `1`     | `chat`  |
| `2`     | `call`  |
[Table 18: Feature levels records.]

##### 2. Entitlement records

Consider the following entitlement records for the `support` feature:  

|      `entity_id`      | `entity_type` | `value` |
|-----------------------|---------------|---------|
| `starter`             | `plan`        | `chat`  |
| `starter-monthly-usd` | `plan_price`  | `email` |
| `plus`                | `addon`       | `call`  |
[Table 19: Entitlement records for the `api_rate_limit` feature.]

##### 3. Subscription-items records

Consider that a subscription with ID `AzZjAiTl1btqS2lEj` has the following `subscription_items[]` records:  

| Index |    `item_price_id`    | `quantity` |
|-------|-----------------------|------------|
| `0`   | `starter-monthly-usd` | `2`        |
| `1`   | `plus-monthly-usd`    | `2`        |
[Table 20: Subscription-items records.]

##### 4. Subscription-item entitlements

Chargebee Billing now determines the entitlement held by each subscription item based on the entitlements defined in Table 19. This is shown in Table 21. For clarity, we've omitted the `quantity` column because it doesn't affect features with type `custom`.  

| Index |    `item_price_id`    |                 Subscription-Item Entitlement Value (determined from Table )                 |
|-------|-----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `0`   | `starter-monthly-usd` | `email` (Matches the value of the plan price.)                                               |
| `1`   | `plus-monthly-usd`    | `call` (Inherited from the addon `plus`, as no entitlement is defined for this addon price.) |
[Table 21: Entitlement values for subscription-items.]

##### 5. Determining final subscription entitlements

###### Case 1: Absence of a subscription-level override

In this scenario, the **final entitlement** for the `support` feature is the **highest** of all the subscription-item entitlement values, which in this case is `call`.

###### Case 2: With subscription-level override

Suppose there's an entitlement override added to the subscription for the feature, as shown below:  

|     `entity_id`     | `entity_type`  | `feature_id` | `value` |                         `expires_at`                          |
|---------------------|----------------|--------------|---------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| `AzZjAiTl1btqS2lEj` | `subscription` | `support`    | `chat`  | `1695884985` (7 days from now, assuming today is 2023-09-21.) |
[Table 22: Entitlement override record for the subscription and feature.]

Given this override, the subscription's **final entitlement value** for the `support` feature will be `chat` until 2023-09-21 and `call` thereafter.  

### With other entity-level entitlement overrides

When an [entitlement override](/docs/api/entitlement_overrides) with `entity_type` set to `plan_price`, `addon_price`, or `charge` is set for a subscription, the override affects the entitlement value used for that specific entity when calculating subscription-item entitlements. If an entitlement override exists for a plan price, addon price, or charge entity, its value is used instead of the regular [entitlement](/docs/api/entitlements) value for that entity.

The method used to derive the subscription entitlement from these overridden values follows the same rules determined by the feature [type](/docs/api/features/feature-object#type) as described in the sections above. We outline and provide examples of these rules in the sections below:  
Switch feature  

#### Summary {#switch-entity-override-content}

When calculating subscription-item entitlements for a feature of type `switch`, if an entitlement override exists for a plan price, addon price, or charge entity, the override's value is used instead of the regular entitlement value for that entity. The final subscription entitlement value is then determined using the same logic as described in the [Switch feature section](#switch): if the entitlement value for the feature held by **any** of the subscription items is `true`, then the subscription entitlement value is also set to `true`. Otherwise, the subscription entitlement value is set to `false`.

#### Example

##### 1. Feature record

Consider the following [feature](/docs/api/features) record:  

|        `id`        |  `type`  |                    `description`                    |
|--------------------|----------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| `xero-integration` | `switch` | `An integration with the Xero accounting software.` |
[Table 23: Feature records.]

##### 2. Entitlement records

Consider the following [entitlement](/docs/api/entitlements) records for the `xero-integration` feature:  

|      `entity_id`      | `entity_type` | `value` |
|-----------------------|---------------|---------|
| `starter`             | `plan`        | `true`  |
| `starter-monthly-usd` | `plan_price`  | `false` |
| `plus`                | `addon`       | `false` |
[Table 24: Entitlement records for the `xero-integration` feature.]

##### 3. Subscription-items records

Consider that a [subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions) with ID `AzZjAiTl1btqS2lEj` has the following `subscription_items[]` records:  

| Index |    `item_price_id`    | `quantity` |
|-------|-----------------------|------------|
| `0`   | `starter-monthly-usd` | `1`        |
| `1`   | `plus-monthly-usd`    | `1`        |
[Table 25: Subscription-items records.]

##### 4. Entitlement override records

Suppose there's an [entitlement override](/docs/api/entitlement_overrides) added to the subscription for the `plus-monthly-usd` addon price, as shown below:  

|    `entity_id`     | `entity_type` |    `feature_id`    | `value` |
|--------------------|---------------|--------------------|---------|
| `plus-monthly-usd` | `addon_price` | `xero-integration` | `true`  |
[Table 26: Entitlement override record for the addon price and feature.]

##### 5. Subscription-item entitlements

Chargebee Billing now determines the entitlement held by each subscription item based on the entitlements defined in Table 24, but uses the override value from Table 26 for the `plus-monthly-usd` addon price. This is shown in Table 27. For clarity, we've omitted the `quantity` column because it doesn't affect features with type `switch`.  

| Index |    `item_price_id`    |                                          Entitlement value                                          |
|-------|-----------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `0`   | `starter-monthly-usd` | `false` (Matches the value of the plan price entitlement.)                                          |
| `1`   | `plus-monthly-usd`    | `true` (Uses the override value from Table 26 instead of inheriting `false` from the addon `plus`.) |
[Table 27: Entitlement values for subscription-items.]

##### 6. Determining final subscription entitlements

In this scenario, the **final entitlement** for the `xero-integration` feature is set to `true` because at least one subscription-item entitlement value is `true` (the overridden value for `plus-monthly-usd`).  
Quantity feature  

#### Summary {#quantity-entity-override-content}

When calculating subscription-item entitlements for a feature of type `quantity`, if an entitlement override exists for a plan price, addon price, or charge entity, the override's value is used instead of the regular entitlement value for that entity. The final subscription entitlement value is then determined using the same logic as described in the [Quantity feature section](#quantity): if the entitlement value for the feature held by any of the subscription items is `unlimited`, then the subscription entitlement value is also `unlimited`. Otherwise, the subscription entitlement value is the sum of all the entitlement values of the subscription items.

#### Example

##### 1. Feature record

Consider the following feature record:  

|      `id`       |   `type`   |             `description`             |
|-----------------|------------|---------------------------------------|
| `user_licenses` | `quantity` | The number of user licenses provided. |

Suppose that the feature has `feature.levels[]` records as follows:  

| `level` | `value` | `is_unlimited` |
|---------|---------|----------------|

| `1`     | `10`    | `false`        |
| `2`     | `20`    | `false`        |
[Table 29: Feature levels records.]

##### 2. Entitlement records

Consider the following entitlement records for the `user_licenses` feature:  

|      `entity_id`      | `entity_type` | `value` |
|-----------------------|---------------|---------|
| `starter`             | `plan`        | `10`    |
| `starter-monthly-usd` | `plan_price`  | `5`     |
| `plus`                | `addon`       | `5`     |
| `one-time`            | `charge`      | `5`     |
[Table 30: Entitlement records for the `user_licenses` feature.]

##### 3. Subscription-items records

Consider that a subscription with ID `AzZjAiTl1btqS2lEj` has the following `subscription_items[]` records:  

| Index |    `item_price_id`    | `quantity` |
|-------|-----------------------|------------|
| `0`   | `starter-monthly-usd` | `2`        |
| `1`   | `plus-monthly-usd`    | `3`        |
| `2`   | `one-time-usd`        | `1`        |
[Table 31: Subscription-items records.]

##### 4. Entitlement override records

Suppose there are [entitlement override](/docs/api/entitlement_overrides) records added to the subscription for the plan price and charge, as shown below:  

|      `entity_id`      | `entity_type` |  `feature_id`   | `value` |
|-----------------------|---------------|-----------------|---------|
| `starter-monthly-usd` | `plan_price`  | `user_licenses` | `10`    |
| `one-time`            | `charge`      | `user_licenses` | `10`    |
[Table 32: Entitlement override records for the plan price and charge.]

##### 5. Subscription-item entitlements

Chargebee Billing now determines the entitlement held by each subscription item based on the entitlements defined in Table 30, but uses the override values from Table 32 for the `starter-monthly-usd` plan price and `one-time` charge. This is shown in Table 33.  

| Index |    `item_price_id`    | `quantity` |                                                Entitlement value                                                 | Entitlement value subtotal (Entitlement value × `quantity`) |
|-------|-----------------------|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| `0`   | `starter-monthly-usd` | `2`        | `10` (Uses the override value from Table 32 instead of the plan price entitlement value of `5`.)                 | `20` (10 x 2)                                               |
| `1`   | `plus-monthly-usd`    | `3`        | `5` (Inherited from the addon `plus`, as no entitlement is defined for this addon price and no override exists.) | `15` (5 x 3)                                                |
| `2`   | `one-time-usd`        | `1`        | `10` (Uses the override value from Table 32 instead of the charge entitlement value of `5`.)                     | `10` (10 x 1)                                               |
[Table 33: Entitlement values for subscription-items.]

##### 6. Determining final subscription entitlements

In this scenario, the **final entitlement value** for the `user_licenses` feature is the total entitlement value from the last column in Table 33, which amounts to (20 + 15 + 10) = `45`.

| `0`   | `starter-monthly-usd` | `2`        |
| `1`   | `plus-monthly-usd`    | `2`        |
[Table 43: Subscription-items records.]

##### 4. Entitlement override records

Suppose there's an [entitlement override](/docs/api/entitlement_overrides) added to the subscription for the addon price, as shown below:  

|    `entity_id`     | `entity_type` | `feature_id` | `value` |
|--------------------|---------------|--------------|---------|
| `plus-monthly-usd` | `addon_price` | `support`    | `call`  |
[Table 44: Entitlement override record for the addon price and feature.]

##### 5. Subscription-item entitlements

Chargebee Billing now determines the entitlement held by each subscription item based on the entitlements defined in Table 42, but uses the override value from Table 44 for the `plus-monthly-usd` addon price. This is shown in Table 45. For clarity, we've omitted the `quantity` column because it doesn't affect features with type `custom`.  

| Index |    `item_price_id`    |                                 Subscription-Item Entitlement Value                                 |
|-------|-----------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `0`   | `starter-monthly-usd` | `email` (Matches the value of the plan price.)                                                      |
| `1`   | `plus-monthly-usd`    | `call` (Uses the override value from Table 44 instead of inheriting `email` from the addon `plus`.) |
[Table 45: Entitlement values for subscription-items.]

##### 6. Determining final subscription entitlements

In this scenario, the **final entitlement** for the `support` feature is the **highest** of all the subscription-item entitlement values, which in this case is `call` (the overridden value for `plus-monthly-usd`).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subscription_id|string|true|none|The unique identifier of the [subscription](/docs/api/subscriptions)<br>.<br>|
|feature_id|string|false|none|The unique identifier of the [feature](/docs/api/features)<br>.<br>|
|feature_name|string|false|none|The [name of the feature](/docs/api/features/feature-object#name)<br>.<br>|
|feature_unit|string|false|none|[The unit of measure](/docs/api/features/feature-object#unit)<br>for the feature when its `type`<br>is either `quantity`<br>or `range`<br>.<br>|
|feature_type|string|false|none|Specifies the [type of the feature](/docs/api/features/feature-object#type)<br>associated with the granted subscription entitlement.<br>|
|value|string|false|none|The value denoting the final entitlement level that the subscription holds for the feature.  <br>**See also:**<br>[How subscription entitlements are determined](/docs/api/subscription_entitlements).<br>|
|name|string|false|none|The display name of the final entitlement level that the subscription holds for the feature. It is derived based on the `type`<br>of feature as follows: - When `feature.type` is `range` or `quantity`: the `name` is the space-separated concatenation of `value` and the pluralized form of `feature_unit`. For example, if `value` is `20` and `feature_unit` is `user`, then `name` becomes `20 users`.<br><br>* When `feature.type` is `custom`: the `name` is the same as `value`.<br>* When `feature.type` is `switch`: `name` is set to `Available` when `value` is `true`; it's set to `Not Available` when `value` is `false`.<br>|
|is_overridden|boolean|true|none|Indicates whether the entitlement held by the subscription for the feature is overridden via an [entitlement_overrides](/docs/api/entitlement_overrides)<br>record.<br>|
|is_enabled|boolean|true|none|Indicates that `components.is_enabled`<br>exists.<br>|
|expires_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Timestamp when the subscription entitlements are going to expire.<br>|
|components|object|false|none|The component entitlements that constitute this `subscription_entitlement`.<br>The effective entitlement [value](/docs/api/subscription_entitlements/subscription_entitlement-object#value)<br>and [name](/docs/api/subscription_entitlements/subscription_entitlement-object#name)<br>are determined from these component entitlements.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_TaxWithheld">TaxWithheld</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemataxwithheld"></a>
<a id="schema_TaxWithheld"></a>
<a id="tocStaxwithheld"></a>
<a id="tocstaxwithheld"></a>

```json
null
```

Tax regulations in many countries allow taxes to be deducted by the buyer while making payments for products and services. The buyer then pays this tax to the taxation authority. The `tax_withheld` resource captures the details of such tax deductions.  
**Note:**

* This resource is available as the `linked_taxes_withheld` sub-resource under `invoice`s.
* Whenever refunds are provided against this resource, they are available as `linked_tax_withheld_refunds` sub-resource under `credit_note`s.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|An auto-generated unique identifier for the tax withheld. The value starts with the prefix `tax_wh_`.<br>For example, `tax_wh_16BdDXSlbu4uV1Ee6`<br>.<br>|
|reference_number|string|false|none|A unique external reference number for the tax withheld. Typically, this is the reference number used by the system you are integrating the API with. Depending on your integration, this could be the reference number issued by the taxation authority to identify the customer or the specific tax transaction.<br>|
|description|string|false|none|The description for this tax withheld.<br>|
|date|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Date or time associated with the tax withheld.<br>|
|amount|integer(int64)|false|none|The amount withheld by the customer as tax from the invoice. The unit depends on the [type of currency](/docs/api/getting-started)<br>.<br>|
|resource_version|integer(int64)|false|none|none|
|updated_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_ThirdPartyPaymentMethod">ThirdPartyPaymentMethod</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemathirdpartypaymentmethod"></a>
<a id="schema_ThirdPartyPaymentMethod"></a>
<a id="tocSthirdpartypaymentmethod"></a>
<a id="tocsthirdpartypaymentmethod"></a>

```json
null
```

Used when you want to copy card information between two gateways (such as copying cards between Authorize.Net and Stripe). Will contain details of the payment method type (card, Amazon Payments, etc.), name of the gateway, and the reference ID that the gateway uses to identify the specific card.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|Type of the payment method.<br><br>* direct_debit - Represents bank account for which the direct debit or ACH agreement/mandate is created.<br>* unionpay - Payments made via UnionPay.<br>* ovo - Payments made via OVO.<br>* google_pay - Payments made via Google Pay.<br>* mercado_pago - Payments made via Mercado Pago.<br>* sepa_instant_transfer - Payments made via Sepa Instant Transfer<br>* dotpay - Payments made via Dotpay.<br>* pay_to - Payments made via PayTo<br>* klarna - Payments made via Klarna.<br>* revolut_pay - Payments made via Revolut Pay.<br>* thai_qr - Payments made via Thai QR.<br>* naver_pay - Payments made via Naver Pay.<br>* giropay - Payments made via giropay.<br>* grab_pay - Payments made via GrabPay<br>* rakuten_pay - Payments made via Rakuten Pay.<br>* blik - Payments made via BLIK.<br>* stablecoin - Payments made via Stablecoin.<br>* alipay -<br>  Payments made via Alipay.  <br>  This payment source is deprecated.<br>* kakao_pay - Payments made via Kakao Pay.<br>* sofort - Payments made via Sofort.<br>* gcash - Payments made via GCash.<br>* dana - Payments made via Dana.<br>* pix - Payments made via Pix<br>* p24 - Payments made via Przelewy24 (P24).<br>* pay_co - Payments made via PayCo<br>* wechat_pay -<br>  Payments made via WeChat Pay.  <br>  This payment source is deprecated.<br>* netbanking_emandates - Netbanking (eMandates) Payments.<br>* nupay - Payments made via NuPay.<br>* picpay - Payments made via PicPay.<br>* bancontact - Payments made via Bancontact Card.<br>* go_pay - Payments made via GoPay<br>* nequi - Payments made via Nequi.<br>* card - Card based payment including credit cards and debit cards. <h2 id="tocS_ThunkingPlan">ThunkingPlan</h2>

```json
null
```

This resource is used to return thunking plan.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|The identifier for the item price. It is unique and immutable.<br>|
|name|string|true|none|A unique display name for the item price in the Chargebee UI. If `external_name`<br>is not provided, this is also used in customer-facing pages and documents such as [invoices](/docs/api/invoices)<br>and [hosted pages](/docs/api/hosted_pages)<br>.<br>|
|item_id|string|false|none|The id of the item that the item price belongs to.<br>|
|description|string|false|none|Description of the item price.<br>|
|status|string|false|none|The status of the item price.<br><br>* archived - The item price is no longer active and cannot be used in new subscriptions or added to existing ones. Existing subscriptions that already have this item price will continue to renew with the item price.<br>* active - The item price can be used in subscriptions.<br>* deleted -<br>  Indicates that the item price has been deleted. The `id`<br>  and `name`<br>  can be reused.<br>|
|external_name|string|false|none|The name of the item price used in customer-facing pages and documents. These include [invoices](/docs/api/invoices)<br>and [hosted pages](/docs/api/hosted_pages).<br>If not provided, then `name`<br>is used<br>|
|price_variant_id|string|false|none|none|
|price_ramp_id|string|false|none|none|
|proration_type|string|false|none|none|
|pricing_model|string|true|none|The [pricing scheme](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/plans.html#pricing-models) for this item price. If subscriptions, invoices or [differential prices](/docs/api/differential_prices) exist for this item price, `pricing_model` cannot be changed.<br><br>* tiered - There are quantity tiers for which per unit prices are set. Quantities are purchased from successive tiers.<br>* per_unit - A fixed price per unit quantity.<br>* flat_fee - A fixed price that is not quantity-based.<br>* volume - The per unit price is based on the tier that the total quantity falls in.<br>* stairstep - A quantity-based pricing scheme. The item is charged a fixed price based on the tier that the total quantity falls in.<br>|
|price|integer(int64)|false|none|The cost of the item price when the pricing model is `flat_fee`.<br>When the pricing model is `per_unit`<br>, it is the price per unit quantity of the item. |price_in_decimal|string|false|none|The price of the item when the pricing_model is `flat_fee`.<br>When the pricing model is `per_unit`<br>, it is the price per unit quantity of the item. Not applicable for the other pricing models. The value is in decimal and in major units of the currency. Also, this is only applicable when [multi-decimal pricing](/docs/api/getting-started)<br>is enabled.<br>|
|period|integer(int32)|false|none|* When the item `type` is `plan`: The billing period of the plan in `period_unit`s. For example, create an addon with a 2 month `period` by providing period as 2 and `period_unit` as `month`. The period of an addon is the duration for which its `price` applies. When attached to a plan, the addon is billed for the billing period of the plan. [Learn more.](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/addons-billingcycle.html)<br><br>If subscriptions or invoices exist for this item price, `period`<br>cannot be changed. |period_unit|string|false|none|The unit of time for `period`.<br>If subscriptions or invoices exist for this item price, `period_unit`<br>cannot be changed. The `period_unit`<br>is mandatory when the item `type`<br>is `plan`<br>or `addon`<br><br>* month - A period of 1 calendar month.<br>* day - A period of 24 hours.<br>* week - A period of 7 days.<br>* year - A period of 1 calendar year.<br>|
|trial_period|integer(int32)|false|none|The trial period of the plan in `trial_period_unit`<br>s. |trial_period_unit|string|false|none|The unit of time for `trial_period`<br>.<br><br>* month - A period of 1 calendar month.<br>* day - A period of 24 hours.<br>|
|trial_end_action|string|false|none|Applicable only when [End-of-trial Action](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/trial_periods_hidden.html#how-to-define-the-end-of-trial-actions-for-subscriptions)<br>has been enabled for the site. Specifies the operation to be carried out for the subscription once the trial ends. Whenever the `item.type`<br>is `plan`<br>and a trial period is defined for this item price, this attribute (parameter) is returned (required). This can be overridden at the [subscription-level](/docs/api/subscriptions/subscription-object#trial_end_action)<br>.<br><br>* cancel_subscription - The subscription cancels.<br>* activate_subscription - The subscription activates and charges are raised for non-metered items.<br>* site_default -<br>  The action [configured for the site](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/trial_periods_hidden.html#how-to-define-the-end-of-trial-actions-for-subscriptions)<br>  at the time when the trial ends, takes effect.<br>|

|free_quantity|integer(int32)|true|none|Free quantity the subscriptions of this **plan** `item_price` will have. |channel|string|false|none|The subscription channel this object originated from and is maintained in.<br><br>* web - The object was created (and is maintained) for the web channel directly in Chargebee via API or UI.<br>* app_store -<br>  The object data is synchronized with data from [in-app subscription(s)](/docs/api/in_app_subscriptions)<br>  created in Apple App Store. Direct manipulation of this object via UI or API is disallowed.<br>* play_store -<br>  The object data is synchronized with data from [in-app subscription(s)](/docs/api/in_app_subscriptions)<br>  created in Google Play Store. Direct manipulation of this object via UI or API is disallowed.<br>|

|created_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Timestamp indicating when this item price was created<br>|
|usage_accumulation_reset_frequency|string|false|none|none|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the item.<br><br>* plan - An essential component of a subscription. Every subscription has exactly one plan. Use the format: `: ....` For example, `Region: South`<br>* [**QuickBooks:**](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/quickbooks.html ) If you've categorized your product sales in QuickBooks according to Location, provide the Location name here. Use the following format: `::....` For example: `Location: North America: Canada`<br>* [**NetSuite:**](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/netsuite.html ) If you've categorized your products in NetSuite under Locations, provide the location name here. Use the following format `: : ....` For example: `NA:US:CA`<br>* [**Intacct:**](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/2.0/intacct.html ) If you've classified your products in Intacct under Dimensions, provide the value of the Dimension here.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_TimeMachine">TimeMachine</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematimemachine"></a>
<a id="schema_TimeMachine"></a>
<a id="tocStimemachine"></a>
<a id="tocstimemachine"></a>

```json
null
```

Time Machine is a simulation feature which imitates the key characteristics, behaviours and functions of the billing configurations. It is a virtual time travelling tool which facilitates the integration testing process by carrying out subscription renewals, dunning, webhooks etc on a hypothetical time frame.

You can use Time Machine in the test site to verify if the billing rules configured in your site adhere to your expectations before executing them in real time. This feature can be used in both API and UI versions.

View this [doc](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/time-machine.html) for more details.

**Note:** In order to use Time Machine via API , you need to first "enable" the Time Travel option which is available under **Settings** \> **Configure Chargebee** \> **Time Machine**.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the time machine. Currently only **delorean**<br>is allowed<br>|
|time_travel_status|string|true|none|The current status of time travel<br><br>* succeeded - Time travel has succeeded.<br>* not_enabled - Time travel has not been enabled for the site<br>* failed -<br>  Time travel has failed. Check the failure code and failure reason attributes for further details.<br>  **Note:**<br>  The time machine needs to be reset by starting afresh again.<br>* in_progress - Time travel is in progress<br>|
|genesis_time|integer(unix-time)|true|none|The start time of the time machine. Specified when 'starting afresh'<br>|
|destination_time|integer(unix-time)|true|none|The destination time to which the time machine is travelling (or has traveled)<br>|
|failure_code|string|false|none|The failure code. This will follow the api error code convention<br>|
|failure_reason|string|false|none|The more descriptive failure reason.<br>|
|error_json|string|false|none|The failure details as error json.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|time_travel_status|not_enabled|
|time_travel_status|in_progress|
|time_travel_status|succeeded|
|time_travel_status|failed|

PayPal Payflow Pro is a payment gateway.<br>* razorpay - Razorpay is a fast growing payment service provider in India working with all leading banks and support for major local payment methods including Netbanking, UPI etc.<br>* global_payments - Global Payments is a payment service provider.<br>* not_applicable - Indicates that payment gateway is not applicable for this resource.<br>* checkout_com - Checkout.com is a payment gateway.<br>* adyen - Adyen is a payment gateway.<br>* braintree - Braintree is a payment gateway.<br>* nmi - NMI is a payment gateway.<br>* worldpay - WorldPay is a payment gateway<br>* moneris_us - Moneris USA is a payment gateway.<br>* pin - Pin is a payment gateway<br>* authorize_net - Authorize.net is a payment gateway<br>* stripe - Stripe is a payment gateway.<br>* moneris - Moneris is a payment gateway.<br>* chargebee - Chargebee test gateway.<br>* cybersource - CyberSource is a payment gateway.<br>* first_data_global - First Data Global Gateway Virtual Terminal Account<br>* exact - Exact Payments is a payment gateway.<br>* eway - eWAY Account is a payment gateway.<br>* payu - PayU is a payment gateway that enables secure card payment acceptance via PaymentsOS.<br>* amazon_payments - Amazon Payments is a payment service provider.<br>* quickbooks - Intuit QuickBooks Payments gateway<br>* wepay - Elavon Virtual Merchant is a payment solution.<br>* paypal_pro - PayPal Pro Account is a payment gateway.<br>* orbital - Chase Paymentech(Orbital) is a payment gateway.<br>* paypal - PayPal Commerce is a payment gateway.<br>* beanstream - Bambora(formerly known as Beanstream) is a payment gateway.<br>* hdfc - HDFC Account is a payment gateway.<br>* ingenico_direct - Worldline Online Payments is a payment gateway.<br>* ogone - Ingenico ePayments (formerly known as Ogone) is a payment gateway.<br>* migs - Details about the card can be obtained from the card resource.<br>* affirm_pay - Payments made via Affirm Pay.<br>* p24 - Payments made via Przelewy24 (P24).<br>* thai_qr - Payments made via Thai QR.<br>* pay_by_bank - Pay By Bank<br>* go_pay - Payments made via GoPay<br>* generic - Payments made via Generic Payment Method.<br>* payme - Payments made via PayMe<br>* google_pay - Payments made via Google Pay.<br>* pay_co - Payments made via PayCo<br>* ovo - Payments made via OVO.<br>* unionpay - Payments made via UnionPay.<br>* ideal - Payments made via iDEAL.<br>* nequi - Payments made via Nequi.<br>* alipay -<br>  Payments made via Alipay.  <br>  This payment source is deprecated.<br>* picpay - Payments made via PicPay.<br>* dotpay - Payments made via Dotpay.<br>* sofort - Payments made via Sofort.<br>* gcash - Payments made via GCash.<br>* mercado_pago - Payments made via Mercado Pago.<br>* nupay - Payments made via NuPay.<br>* direct_debit - Represents bank account for which the direct debit or ACH agreement/mandate is created.<br>* rakuten_pay - Payments made via Rakuten Pay.<br>* qpay - Payments made via Qpay.<br>* upi - UPI Payments.<br>* wero - Payments made via Wero.<br>* swish - Payments made via Swish<br>* twint - Payments made via Twint<br>* wechat_pay -<br>  Payments made via WeChat Pay.  <br>  This payment source is deprecated.<br>* kbc_payment_button - KBC Payment Button<br>|

|date|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Indicates when this transaction occurred.<br>|
|settled_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Indicates the time at which the final status of the transaction has been marked.<br>|
|exchange_rate|number(decimal)|false|none|Exchange rate used for base currency conversion<br>|
|currency_code|string|true|none|The currency code (ISO 4217 format) for the transaction.<br>|
|amount|integer(int64)|false|none|Amount for this transaction.<br>|
|id_at_gateway|string|false|none|The id with which this transaction is referred in gateway.<br>|
|status|string|false|none|The status of this transaction.<br><br>* in_progress -<br>  Transaction is being processed by the gateway. This typically happens for [direct debit transactions](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/direct-debit-payments.html)<br>  or, in case of cards, refund transactions. Such transactions can take 2-7 days to complete, depending on the gateway and payment method.<br>* timeout - Transaction failed because of Gateway not accepting the connection.<br>* success - The transaction is successful.<br>* voided - The transaction got voided or authorization expired at gateway.<br>* needs_attention -<br>  When connection with the Gateway gets terminated abruptly. For `needs_attention`<br>  status Chargebee automatically reconcile the transaction for few gateways, for rest of the gateways you have to use the [Reconcile transaction API](/docs/api/transactions/reconcile-transaction).<br>  You can use this API to update the `id_at_gateway`<br>  (Gateway Transaction ID) and `status`<br>  for a [`needs_attention`](/docs/api/transactions/transaction-object#status)<br>  transaction to be reconciled at par with the gateway.  <br>  [Learn more](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/payments/2.0/needs-attention-transactions.html)<br>  about `needs_attention`<br>  transaction status<br>* late_failure - Indicates that a successful payment transaction has failed now due to a late failure notification from the payment gateway, typically caused by issues like insufficient funds or a closed bank account.<br>* failure - Transaction failed. Refer the 'error_code' and 'error_text' fields to know the reason for failure<br>|
|fraud_flag|string|false|none|Indicates whether or not the transaction has been [identified as fraudulent](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/payments/2.0/fraud-management/chargebee-fraud-management).<br><br>* suspicious - The transaction has been identified as potentially fraudulent by the gateway<br>* safe - The transaction has been marked as safe<br>* fraudulent - The transaction has been marked as fraudulent<br>|
|initiator_type|string|false|none|Marker for on-session payments (3DS). null indicates 'merchant'.<br><br>* merchant - Payment initiated on stored payment method by the merchant<br>* customer - Customer initiated 3DS payment<br>|
|three_d_secure|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether this transaction has gone through 3DS. Applicable only for 'on-session' payments \& verifications.If 3DS is not enforced by the gateway/bank or if the customers' card is not enrolled, this will be false.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_UnbilledCharge">UnbilledCharge</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaunbilledcharge"></a>
<a id="schema_UnbilledCharge"></a>
<a id="tocSunbilledcharge"></a>
<a id="tocsunbilledcharge"></a>

```json
null
```

Unbilled charge represents the charges that are held by passing `invoice_immediately` in various operations such as update subscription, add charge, create subscription, etc. [Learn more.](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/unbilled-charges.html)

If any invoice is to be created for a subscription all the unbilled charges associated with the subscription will be included in that invoice.

If any invoice is to be created for a customer, all the unbilled charges associated with its subscriptions will be included in that invoice.

Any automatic invoice creation like renewal, activation, etc., will include the unbilled charges.

Subscriptions are invoiced at the start of every term based on the recurring items and charged immediately against the customer's credit card if 'auto_collection' is turned 'on', otherwise the resulting invoice will be created as 'Payment Due'.

If consolidated invoicing is enabled, the charges during the subscription renewals/activations will be held and consolidated at the last renewal/activation that takes place on that particular day.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|Uniquely identifies an unbilled charge.<br>|
|customer_id|string|false|none|A unique identifier for the customer being charged.<br>|
|subscription_id|string|false|none|A unique identifier for the subscription this charge belongs to.<br>|
|date_from|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Start date of this charge.<br>|
|date_to|integer(unix-time)|false|none|End date of this charge.<br>|
|unit_amount|integer(int64)|false|none|Unit amount of the charge item.<br>|
|pricing_model|string|false|none|The pricing scheme for this line item.<br><br>* tiered - There are quantity tiers for which per unit prices are set. Quantities are purchased from successive tiers.<br>* volume - The per unit price is based on the tier that the total quantity falls in.<br>* per_unit - A fixed price per unit quantity.<br>* flat_fee - A fixed price that is not quantity-based.<br>* stairstep - A quantity-based pricing scheme. The item is charged a fixed price based on the tier that the total quantity falls in.<br>|
|quantity|integer(int32)|false|none|Quantity of the item which is represented by this charge.<br>|
|amount|integer(int64)|false|none|Total amount of this charge. Typically equals to unit amount x quantity.<br>|
|currency_code|string|true|none|The currency code (ISO 4217 format) for the charge.<br>|
|discount_amount|integer(int64)|false|none|Total discounts for this charge.<br>|
|description|string|false|none|Detailed description about this charge.<br>|
|entity_type|string|true|none|Specifies the modelled entity this line item is based on.<br><br>* charge_item_price - Indicates that this line item is based on charge Item Price<br>* addon_item_price - Indicates that this line item is based on addon Item Price<br>* plan_item_price - Indicates that this line item is based on plan Item Price<br>* adhoc - Indicates that this lineitem is not modelled. i.e created adhoc. So the 'entity_id' attribute will be null in this case<br>|
|entity_id|string|false|none|The identifier of the modelled entity this charge is based on. Will be null for 'adhoc' entity type.<br>|
|is_voided|boolean|true|none|Will be true if the charge has been voided. Usually the unbilled charge will be voided and revised to different charges(s) during proration.<br>|
|voided_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Timestamp indicating the date and time this charge got voided.<br>|
|unit_amount_in_decimal|string|false|none|The decimal representation of the unit amount for the entity. The value is in major units of the currency. Returned when the entity is quantity-based and [multi-decimal pricing](/docs/api/currencies)<br>is enabled.<br>|
|quantity_in_decimal|string|false|none|The decimal representation of the quantity of this entity. Returned when the entity is quantity-based and [multi-decimal pricing](/docs/api/currencies)<br>is enabled.<br>|
|amount_in_decimal|string|false|none|The decimal representation of the amount for the charge, in major units of the currency. Typically equals to `unit_amount_in_decimal`<br>x `quantity_in_decimal`.<br>Returned when [multi-decimal pricing](/docs/api/currencies)<br>is enabled.<br>|
|created_at|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Timestamp indicating when the unbilled charge was created.<br>|
|updated_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Timestamp indicating when the unbilled charge was last updated<br>|
|is_advance_charge|boolean|false|none|The value of this parameter will be true if it is a recurring unbilled charge for a future term.<br>|
|business_entity_id|string|false|none|The unique ID of the [business entity](/docs/api/advanced-features)<br>of this unbilled charge. This is always the same as the [business entity](/docs/api/unbilled_charges/unbilled_charge-object#customer_id)<br>of the customer.<br>|
|deleted|boolean|true|none|Indicates that this resource has been deleted.<br>|
|tiers|[object]|false|none|The list of tiers applicable for this line item<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_Usage">Usage</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
